title: INTEGROS® Architecture Map
text: OOF™ INTEGROS® Architecture Map INTEGROS® Architecture Map Integrity Governance Architecture — Integrity Governance Layer Official Integrity Governance Reference Map for AI Systems, Autonomous Systems, Digital Assets, Organizations, Critical Infrastructure, and Future Operational Environments INTEGROS® serves as the official OOF® integrity governance reference map used to identify, define, classify, navigate, validate, and understand governable integrity spaces across AI systems, autonomous systems, digital assets, organizations, critical infrastructure, and future operational environments. The purpose of INTEGROS® is not to define the technical implementation of a system. The purpose of INTEGROS® is to identify, define, separate, and map the governable spaces through which integrity is established, evaluated, protected, restored, and continuously assured. INTEGROS® serves as the official integrity governance reference map for: AI Systems Autonomous Systems Autonomous Agents Digital Assets Digital Identity Environments Enterprise Systems Government Systems Healthcare Infrastructure Financial Infrastructure Industrial Systems Critical Infrastructure Multi-System Environments Future Operational Ecosystems Core Architectural Principle Every integrity governance space answers one primary governance question. No integrity governance space duplicates the purpose of another integrity governance space. Every integrity governance space has a defined beginning, a defined operational purpose, and a defined governance boundary. Every integrity governance space begins where the preceding integrity governance requirement has been sufficiently established. Together, these integrity governance spaces form the official integrity governance reference map of INTEGROS®. Official Integrity Governance Flow Integrity Definition → Integrity Structure → Integrity Conditions → Integrity Measurement → Integrity State → Integrity Deviation → Integrity Breach → Integrity Response → Integrity Restoration → Integrity Assurance 1. Integrity Definition Standard (INDS) Governed Space: Integrity Definition Core Question How can integrity be formally defined as a governable operational reality? Canonical Definition Integrity Definition Standard (INDS) defines the governance conditions under which integrity is formally identified, described, bounded, classified, documented, and established as a governable operational concept for a specific governed entity. Governance Boundary Begins when a governed entity requires a formal and operationally usable definition of integrity. Ends when integrity has been sufficiently defined, bounded, classified, and documented to support structural governance. 2. Integrity Structure Standard (STIS) Governed Space: Integrity Structure Core Question How should integrity be structurally organized so that it can be consistently governed? Canonical Definition Integrity Structure Standard (STIS) defines the governance conditions under which the components, relationships, dependencies, layers, and structural elements constituting integrity are identified, organized, validated, and documented. Governance Boundary Begins when the formally defined concept of integrity requires a structural model. Ends when the components and relationships constituting integrity have been sufficiently organized and validated to support the definition of integrity conditions. 3. Integrity Conditions Standard (ICS) Governed Space: Integrity Conditions Core Question Under which governed conditions can integrity legitimately exist, be preserved, and remain operationally valid? Canonical Definition Integrity Conditions Standard (ICS) defines the governance conditions, requirements, dependencies, thresholds, and operational circumstances under which integrity may legitimately exist, remain valid, and be preserved. Governance Boundary Begins when the structure of integrity has been established and the conditions required for its valid existence must be defined. Ends when the required integrity conditions have been identified, validated, documented, and made suitable for objective measurement. 4. Integrity Measurement Standard (IMS) Governed Space: Integrity Measurement Core Question How can integrity be objectively measured, evaluated, and demonstrated? Canonical Definition Integrity Measurement Standard (IMS) defines the governance conditions under which integrity indicators, metrics, thresholds, measurement methods, evidence sources, and evaluation procedures are established and applied. Governance Boundary Begins when approved integrity conditions require objective measurement. Ends when valid measurement methods and sufficient measurement results exist to determine the integrity state of a governed entity. 5. Integrity State Standard (ISS) Governed Space: Integrity State Core Question What is the current integrity state of a governed entity, and how can that state be objectively determined? Canonical Definition Integrity State Standard (ISS) defines the governance conditions under which the current integrity state of a governed entity is assessed, classified, validated, monitored, and documented through approved integrity measurements and evidence. Governance Boundary Begins when sufficient integrity measurements exist to determine the current state of integrity. Ends when the integrity state has been objectively assessed, classified, validated, and made available for ongoing governance evaluation. 6. Integrity Deviation Standard (IDS) Governed Space: Integrity Deviation Core Question When does integrity begin to deviate from approved conditions, and how can that deviation be governed before it becomes a breach? Canonical Definition Integrity Deviation Standard (IDS) defines the governance conditions under which departures from approved integrity conditions are identified, assessed, validated, monitored, classified, and documented before or without automatically constituting a formal integrity breach. Governance Boundary Begins when the observed or measured integrity state no longer fully conforms to approved integrity conditions. Ends when the deviation has been resolved, accepted under governed conditions, or formally determined to constitute an integrity breach. 7. Integrity Breach Standard (IBS) Governed Space: Integrity Breach Core Question When does an integrity deviation become a governed integrity breach requiring formal governance intervention? Canonical Definition Integrity Breach Standard (IBS) defines the governance conditions under which an integrity deviation is formally identified, validated, assessed, classified, documented, and recognized as an integrity breach requiring governed intervention. Governance Boundary Begins when an integrity deviation reaches an approved breach condition, threshold, severity, or governance significance. Ends when the breach has been formally validated, classified, documented, and transferred into the governed integrity response process. 8. Integrity Response Standard (IRS) Governed Space: Integrity Response Core Question How should verified integrity breaches be governed, contained, and managed to minimize operational impact? Canonical Definition Integrity Response Standard (IRS) defines the governance conditions under which verified integrity breaches are authorized for intervention, coordinated, contained, escalated, managed, executed, and documented through an accountable response process. Governance Boundary Begins when an integrity breach has been formally validated and requires governance action. Ends when the immediate effects of the breach have been contained, response actions have been completed, and the governed entity is ready to enter integrity restoration. 9. Integrity Restoration Standard (IRRS) Governed Space: Integrity Restoration Core Question How can integrity be objectively restored after a verified breach while preserving governance accountability and evidence? Canonical Definition Integrity Restoration Standard (IRRS) defines the governance conditions under which integrity is planned for restoration, operationally re-established, validated, evidenced, approved, and documented after a verified integrity breach and governed response. Governance Boundary Begins when the immediate integrity response has been completed and restoration of approved integrity conditions becomes possible. Ends when approved integrity conditions have been demonstrably re-established, validated, evidenced, documented, and formally accepted. 10. Integrity Assurance Standard (IAS) Governed Space: Integrity Assurance Core Question How can restored integrity remain continuously verified, demonstrable, and governably assured throughout the complete operational lifecycle? Canonical Definition Integrity Assurance Standard (IAS) defines the governance conditions under which integrity is continuously monitored, validated, evidenced, reported, supervised, and maintained after restoration or initial integrity establishment. Governance Boundary Begins when integrity has been formally established or successfully restored and requires continuous assurance. Continues throughout the remaining operational lifecycle of the governed entity while integrity must remain verifiable, demonstrable, and governably maintained. Core Governed Integrity Spaces Integrity Definition Integrity Structure Integrity Conditions Integrity Measurement Integrity State Integrity Deviation Integrity Breach Integrity Response Integrity Restoration Integrity Assurance Architectural Position INTEGROS® governs the complete integrity governance lifecycle. The architecture progresses through: Integrity Definition → Integrity Structure → Integrity Conditions → Integrity Measurement → Integrity State → Integrity Deviation → Integrity Breach → Integrity Response → Integrity Restoration → Integrity Assurance Together, these integrity governance spaces govern how integrity is formally defined, structurally organized, conditionally established, objectively measured, operationally determined, monitored for deviation, classified when breached, governed through response, re-established through restoration, and continuously maintained through assurance. INTEGROS® therefore provides a complete governance path from the first definition of integrity to its continuous operational preservation. What INTEGROS® Defines INTEGROS® defines: where the governance of integrity begins how integrity is formally defined which structural elements constitute integrity which conditions must exist for integrity to remain valid how integrity is objectively measured how the current integrity state is determined where integrity deviation begins when a deviation becomes a formal integrity breach how verified integrity breaches enter governed response how integrity is objectively restored how restored integrity is continuously assured. INTEGROS® provides the official integrity governance language used for integrity-space identification, integrity lifecycle navigation, governance classification, structural diagnosis, and integrity architecture design across complex operational environments. Compatible OOF® Architectures GOA™ — Governance Architecture ORA™ — Operational Reality Architecture OBIDENITY® — Origin-Bound Identity Governance Architecture AGA™ — Accountability Governance Architecture AIG® — AI Governance Architecture CLIA® — Cognitive Governance Intelligence Architecture MGIA™ — Memory Governance Intelligence Architecture ASGA™ — Autonomous Systems Governance Architecture ART™ — Audit in Real Time Architecture Canonical Principle INTEGROS® does not define system functionality, software implementation, organizational performance, behavioral legitimacy, or governance authority. INTEGROS® governs the integrity conditions under which governed entities remain formally defined, structurally coherent, objectively measurable, operationally verifiable, recoverable after breach, and continuously assured throughout their complete lifecycle. Canonical Closing Statement INTEGROS® serves as the official integrity governance reference map for AI systems, autonomous systems, digital assets, organizations, critical infrastructure, and future operational environments. By defining the primary governable spaces of integrity, INTEGROS® provides the architecture used to identify, classify, navigate, measure, validate, protect, restore, and continuously assure integrity throughout the complete lifecycle of every governed entity.

text: OOF™ INTEGROS® Integrity Governance Architecture — Integrity Governance Layer INTEGROS® Integrity Governance Architecture (INTEGROS®) — Integrity Governance Layer Official Integrity Governance Architecture for AI Systems, Autonomous Systems, Digital Assets, Organizations, Critical Infrastructure, and Future Operational Environments INTEGROS® serves as the official OOF® integrity governance architecture used for integrity governance design, integrity space identification, integrity validation, integrity assessment, integrity restoration, integrity assurance, and integrity governance navigation across AI systems, autonomous systems, organizations, digital assets, critical infrastructure, and future operational environments. Core Question How can integrity remain continuously defined, measurable, governable, recoverable, and assured throughout the complete operational lifecycle? title: Integrity Response Authorization Module (IRAM)
text: OOF™ Integrity Response Authorization Module (IRAM) Integrity Response Authorization Module (IRAM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-IRS-IRAM-2026-07-21-0001 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Integrity Response Standard (IRS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Integrity Response Authorization Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 21 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Integrity Response Authorization Canonical Definition Integrity Response Authorization Module (IRAM) defines the governance framework for authorizing responses to verified integrity breaches. It establishes the authorization criteria, decision authorities, approval mechanisms, accountability requirements, and governance controls required to ensure that every integrity response is initiated by appropriately authorized entities and executed under approved governance conditions throughout the complete lifecycle of a governed entity. Operational Role IRAM governs the authorization layer of integrity response management by ensuring that no integrity response is initiated without documented authority, approved governance conditions, and accountable decision-making. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define Response Authorization Criteria Identify the governance conditions, breach classifications, severity thresholds, and operational circumstances that require authorization before response activities may begin. 2. Define Authorization Authorities Establish who is authorized to approve, reject, delegate, or escalate integrity response activities and under which governance conditions those authorities may act. 3. Define Authorization Validation Logic Define how response authorizations are verified for legitimacy, completeness, accountability, policy compliance, and consistency with the approved governance methodology. 4. Define Governance Response Establish governance actions for approved authorizations, denied requests, delegated authority, emergency authorizations, authorization conflicts, and escalation procedures. 5. Preserve Authorization Records Maintain authorization decisions, approvals, delegations, supporting evidence, timestamps, governance justifications, and audit documentation throughout the complete lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — Enterprise AI Governance Scenario A verified integrity breach requires the immediate suspension of autonomous decision-making within a production AI platform. Application IRAM determines the authorized decision-makers, validates emergency authority, records the approval, and authorizes containment actions according to the organization's governance policies. Result The response begins under documented authority with complete accountability and auditability. Use Case 2 — Critical Infrastructure Operations Scenario A verified integrity breach affects operational control systems within a national power grid. Application IRAM authorizes emergency response actions, validates executive authority, records governance approvals, and ensures that containment measures are initiated only by authorized personnel. Result Critical response activities are executed under controlled governance, preserving operational integrity, accountability, and regulatory compliance. Canonical Closing Statement Integrity Response Authorization Module establishes the canonical governance framework for authorizing integrity responses through documented authority, accountable decision-making, and approved governance conditions. It ensures that every integrity response begins with legitimate authorization, preserving governance integrity, operational control, and full auditability throughout the complete lifecycle of every governed entity.

title: Integrity Response Coordination Module (IRCM)
text: OOF™ Integrity Response Coordination Module (IRCM) Integrity Response Coordination Module (IRCM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-IRS-IRCM-2026-07-21-0002 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Integrity Response Standard (IRS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Integrity Response Coordination Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 21 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Integrity Response Coordination Canonical Definition Integrity Response Coordination Module (IRCM) defines the governance framework for coordinating integrity response activities across responsible individuals, teams, systems, organizations, and operational environments. It establishes the coordination principles, communication mechanisms, role assignments, synchronization requirements, and governance controls required to ensure that every integrity response is executed consistently, efficiently, and under unified governance throughout the complete lifecycle of a governed entity. Operational Role IRCM governs the coordination layer of integrity response management by ensuring that all authorized response activities remain synchronized, accountable, transparent, and operationally aligned. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define Response Coordination Requirements Identify the operational participants, governance responsibilities, communication channels, dependencies, and coordination rules required during integrity response activities. 2. Define Coordination Methodology Establish standardized coordination procedures, role assignments, decision synchronization, task allocation, reporting mechanisms, and cross-functional collaboration requirements. 3. Define Coordination Validation Logic Define how coordination activities are evaluated for consistency, completeness, timeliness, accountability, operational alignment, and compliance with approved governance methodology. 4. Define Governance Response Establish governance actions for coordination failures, communication breakdowns, conflicting decisions, resource conflicts, delayed execution, and escalation procedures. 5. Preserve Coordination Records Maintain coordination plans, communication records, task assignments, governance decisions, synchronization logs, escalation history, and audit documentation throughout the complete lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — Multi-Agent AI Environment Scenario A verified integrity breach affects several autonomous AI agents operating across multiple services. Application IRCM coordinates the activities of governance teams, AI operators, security personnel, and system administrators to ensure synchronized containment and response execution. Result All response actions remain coordinated under a single governance framework, minimizing operational disruption and preventing conflicting actions. Use Case 2 — International Manufacturing Network Scenario An integrity breach impacts production facilities operating in multiple countries. Application IRCM synchronizes operational response activities, executive decisions, regulatory communication, and local response teams across all affected facilities. Result The global response is executed consistently, transparently, and under unified governance despite distributed operational environments. Canonical Closing Statement Integrity Response Coordination Module establishes the canonical governance framework for synchronizing integrity response activities across people, systems, organizations, and operational environments. title: Integrity State Monitoring Module (ISMM)
text: OOF™ Integrity State Monitoring Module (ISMM) Integrity State Monitoring Module (ISMM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-ISS-ISMM-2026-07-21-0004 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Integrity State Standard (ISS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Integrity State Monitoring Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 21 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Integrity State Monitoring Canonical Definition Integrity State Monitoring Module (ISMM) defines the governance framework for continuously observing, tracking, and supervising the operational state of integrity. It establishes the monitoring mechanisms, observation criteria, reporting rules, and governance controls required to detect integrity state changes and maintain continuous awareness throughout the complete lifecycle of a governed entity. Operational Role ISMM governs the monitoring layer of integrity state management by providing continuous visibility into the current integrity state and detecting changes that may require governance intervention. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define Monitoring Scope Identify the integrity states, operational activities, governance events, measurements, and environmental conditions that require continuous monitoring. 2. Define Monitoring Requirements Establish monitoring frequency, observation methods, reporting intervals, alert thresholds, evidence collection requirements, and governance responsibilities. 3. Define Monitoring Validation Logic Define how monitoring results are verified for accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, and compliance with approved governance methodology. 4. Define Governance Response Establish governance actions for detected state changes, monitoring alerts, abnormal conditions, missing observations, escalations, and corrective interventions. 5. Preserve Monitoring Records Maintain monitoring logs, state histories, alerts, evidence, governance decisions, observation reports, and audit documentation throughout the complete lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — Autonomous AI Operations Scenario An autonomous AI platform continuously operates across multiple business environments where integrity conditions may change in real time. Application ISMM continuously monitors the integrity state, detects changes, generates governance alerts, and supports timely operational oversight. Result Integrity remains continuously observable, enabling rapid governance responses before operational risks escalate. Use Case 2 — Industrial Control System Scenario A manufacturing facility continuously monitors the integrity of production systems, safety controls, and operational processes. Application ISMM supervises integrity states in real time and identifies operational changes that require governance review or intervention. Result Continuous integrity monitoring improves operational reliability, reduces governance blind spots, and supports proactive integrity management. Canonical Closing Statement Integrity governance requires continuous awareness, not periodic observation. Integrity State Monitoring Module establishes the canonical framework for continuously monitoring integrity states, enabling early detection of operational changes, timely governance intervention, and sustained integrity throughout the complete lifecycle of every governed entity.

title: Integrity Scope Module (ISPM)
text: OOF™ Integrity Scope Module (ISPM) Integrity Scope Module (ISPM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-INDS-ISPM-2026-07-17-0005 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Integrity Definition Standard (INDS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Integrity Scope Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 17 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Integrity Scope Canonical Definition Integrity Scope Module (ISPM) defines the extent of integrity governance by specifying which entities, components, processes, relationships, and lifecycle stages are subject to integrity requirements. It establishes the formal scope within which integrity governance is applied and enforced. Module Purpose ISPM ensures that the application of integrity governance is explicit, complete, and consistently bounded. It prevents uncertainty by defining exactly what falls within the governed integrity space and what remains outside its intended application. Without a clearly defined scope, integrity governance may become incomplete, inconsistent, or incorrectly applied. Operational Role ISPM establishes the official scope of integrity governance, ensuring that every integrity definition, measurement, evaluation, restoration, and assurance activity applies only to the intended governed space. Operational Space ISPM governs: integrity scope scope boundaries governed entities lifecycle coverage applicability rules. Minimum Implementation Framework An implementation of ISPM should define: governed entities covered components covered lifecycle stages exclusions scope modification rules. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — Autonomous Systems Define whether integrity governance applies only to the autonomous agent itself or also to its training data, decision models, external interfaces, and runtime operations. Use Case 2 — Supply Chain Governance Specify which organizations, assets, operational processes, and transfer events are included within the governed integrity scope. Canonical Closing Statement Integrity governance is effective only when its scope is explicitly defined. Integrity Scope Module establishes the formal extent of integrity governance, ensuring that every integrity obligation, evaluation, and assurance activity is applied consistently across the intended governed space throughout the complete lifecycle of the entity.

title: Integrity State Reporting Module (ISRM)
text: OOF™ Integrity State Reporting Module (ISRM) Integrity State Reporting Module (ISRM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-ISS-ISRM-2026-07-21-0005 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Integrity State Standard (ISS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Integrity State Reporting Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 21 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Integrity State Reporting Canonical Definition Integrity State Reporting Module (ISRM) defines the governance framework for communicating the current integrity state of a governed entity. It establishes the reporting structure, content requirements, evidence references, communication rules, and governance controls required to ensure that integrity states are reported accurately, consistently, and transparently throughout the complete lifecycle. Operational Role ISRM governs the reporting layer of integrity state management by transforming validated integrity state information into standardized governance reports for operational, regulatory, audit, and executive decision-making. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define Reporting Requirements Identify which integrity states must be reported, who receives the reports, reporting frequency, required evidence, and governance objectives. 2. Define Reporting Structure Establish standardized report formats, mandatory reporting elements, classification terminology, evidence references, and documentation requirements. 3. Define Reporting Validation Logic Define how integrity reports are verified for accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, and compliance before publication or distribution. 4. Define Governance Response Establish governance actions for critical reports, reporting exceptions, delayed reporting, reporting errors, escalation procedures, and corrective reporting activities. 5. Preserve Reporting Records Maintain published reports, reporting history, supporting evidence, approvals, revisions, distribution records, and audit documentation throughout the complete lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — AI Governance Oversight Scenario An enterprise periodically reports the integrity state of its AI systems to executive management and regulatory stakeholders. Application ISRM governs the preparation, validation, and publication of standardized integrity state reports supported by objective evidence. Result Decision-makers receive consistent and transparent integrity information that supports governance, risk management, and regulatory compliance. Use Case 2 — Critical Infrastructure Authority Scenario A national infrastructure operator reports the integrity state of critical operational systems to supervisory authorities and internal governance committees. Application ISRM standardizes the reporting process, ensuring every reported integrity state is evidence-based and consistently communicated. Result Integrity reporting becomes transparent, comparable, auditable, and suitable for operational, regulatory, and public accountability. Canonical Closing Statement Integrity governance is effective only when integrity states are communicated consistently and supported by objective evidence. Integrity State Reporting Module establishes the canonical framework for standardized integrity state reporting, enabling transparent communication, informed governance decisions, regulatory accountability, and continuous integrity oversight throughout the complete lifecycle of every governed entity.

title: Integrity State Transition Module (ISTM)
text: OOF™ Integrity State Transition Module (ISTM) Integrity State Transition Module (ISTM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-ISS-ISTM-2026-07-21-0002 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Integrity State Standard (ISS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Integrity State Transitions Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 21 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Integrity State Transitions Canonical Definition Integrity State Transition Module (ISTM) defines the governance framework for controlling how integrity moves from one operational state to another. It establishes the transition rules, authorization requirements, validation criteria, and governance controls required to ensure that every integrity state change is legitimate, traceable, and consistently governed throughout the complete lifecycle of a governed entity. Operational Role ISTM governs the transition layer of integrity state management by ensuring that integrity state changes occur only through validated governance processes rather than arbitrary or uncontrolled events. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define State Transition Rules Identify all permitted integrity state transitions and define the governance conditions under which each transition is allowed. 2. Define Transition Requirements Establish authorization requirements, validation criteria, supporting evidence, approvals, and operational prerequisites required before any integrity state transition may occur. 3. Define Transition Validation Logic Define how transition requests are verified for legitimacy, completeness, consistency, evidence sufficiency, and governance compliance before execution. 4. Define Governance Response Establish governance actions for approved transitions, rejected transitions, unauthorized state changes, emergency transitions, rollback procedures, and escalation. 5. Preserve Transition Records Maintain transition requests, approvals, supporting evidence, state histories, authorization records, timestamps, and audit documentation throughout the complete lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — Autonomous AI Governance Scenario An autonomous AI system changes from Maintained Integrity to Degraded Integrity after repeated policy violations exceed approved governance thresholds. Application ISTM validates that the transition satisfies all governance rules before officially changing the integrity state. Result Integrity state changes remain fully governed, authorized, and auditable rather than occurring automatically without governance oversight. Use Case 2 — Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Scenario A production facility changes from Operational Integrity to Suspended Integrity after a failed quality validation. Application ISTM governs the transition process by verifying evidence, authorizations, and regulatory requirements before the state change becomes official. Result Integrity transitions remain transparent, traceable, and compliant with governance and regulatory obligations. Canonical Closing Statement Integrity governance requires controlled evolution of operational conditions. Integrity State Transition Module establishes the canonical framework for governing integrity state changes, ensuring that every transition is authorized, validated, traceable, and consistently managed throughout the complete lifecycle of every governed entity.

title: Integrity State Validation Module (ISVM)
text: OOF™ Integrity State Validation Module (ISVM) Integrity State Validation Module (ISVM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-ISS-ISVM-2026-07-21-0003 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Integrity State Standard (ISS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Integrity State Validation Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 21 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Integrity State Validation Canonical Definition Integrity State Validation Module (ISVM) defines the governance framework for validating the correctness of an assigned integrity state. It establishes the validation procedures, evidence requirements, verification rules, and governance controls required to confirm that the current integrity state accurately reflects the actual operational condition of a governed entity throughout its complete lifecycle. Operational Role ISVM governs the validation layer of integrity state management by ensuring that every assigned integrity state is supported by objective evidence, consistent evaluation, and approved governance methodology. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define State Validation Requirements Identify the evidence, measurements, indicators, thresholds, and governance conditions required to validate every integrity state. 2. Define Validation Methodology Establish standardized validation procedures, verification criteria, evidence quality requirements, review methods, and governance approval processes. 3. Define Validation Logic Define how integrity state assignments are verified for accuracy, consistency, completeness, repeatability, and compliance with approved governance rules. 4. Define Governance Response Establish governance actions for validated states, disputed states, failed validations, reclassification, escalation, and corrective governance actions. 5. Preserve Validation Records Maintain validation procedures, supporting evidence, review decisions, validation history, approvals, exceptions, and audit records throughout the complete lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — AI Governance Platform Scenario An enterprise AI system is classified as operating with Maintained Integrity based on continuous governance monitoring. Application ISVM validates that the assigned integrity state is supported by sufficient evidence, approved measurements, and standardized governance methodology. Result The integrity state is confirmed as objective, reliable, and defensible during internal audits and regulatory reviews. Use Case 2 — Financial Compliance System Scenario A financial institution assigns an integrity state to its transaction monitoring platform following periodic governance evaluations. Application ISVM verifies that the assigned state accurately reflects operational reality before it is accepted as the official integrity condition. Result Integrity state classifications remain evidence-based, consistent, and fully auditable across the governance lifecycle. Canonical Closing Statement An integrity state is trustworthy only when it has been objectively validated. Integrity State Validation Module establishes the canonical governance framework for confirming the accuracy, consistency, and evidentiary support of integrity state classifications, ensuring reliable governance throughout the complete lifecycle of every governed entity.

title: Integrity Threshold Module (ITM)
text: OOF™ Integrity Threshold Module (ITM) Integrity Threshold Module (ITM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-IMS-ITM-2026-07-17-0003 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Integrity Measurement Standard (IMS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Integrity Thresholds Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 17 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Integrity Thresholds Canonical Definition Integrity Threshold Module (ITM) defines the governance thresholds that determine the acceptable limits of integrity measurements. It establishes the quantitative and qualitative boundary values used to distinguish acceptable integrity from degraded, compromised, or unacceptable integrity conditions throughout the complete lifecycle of a governed entity. Operational Role ITM governs the threshold layer of integrity measurement by defining the decision boundaries used to classify integrity measurements and trigger appropriate governance actions. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define Integrity Thresholds Identify the threshold values that separate acceptable, warning, critical, and unacceptable integrity conditions. 2. Define Threshold Requirements Establish threshold criteria, tolerance ranges, escalation levels, review requirements, and governance approval procedures for each integrity threshold. 3. Define Threshold Evaluation Logic Define how integrity measurements are evaluated against approved thresholds and how threshold crossings are detected, validated, and classified. 4. Define Governance Response Establish governance actions for warning conditions, threshold exceedances, critical integrity degradation, emergency intervention, and operational recovery. 5. Preserve Threshold Records Maintain threshold definitions, revisions, approvals, historical changes, evaluation results, governance decisions, and supporting evidence throughout the complete lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — AI Safety Governance Scenario An AI platform defines thresholds for hallucination rate, policy compliance, unsafe outputs, and autonomous decision confidence. Application ITM governs these thresholds and continuously evaluates operational measurements against approved governance limits. Result Integrity degradation is detected immediately when predefined governance thresholds are exceeded, allowing timely intervention. Use Case 2 — Medical Device Monitoring Scenario A medical device continuously monitors calibration accuracy, sensor reliability, operational stability, and patient safety indicators. Application ITM establishes the approved integrity thresholds and automatically detects when operational measurements exceed safe limits. Result The device maintains operational integrity by triggering governance actions before integrity degradation becomes a safety risk. Canonical Closing Statement Integrity measurements become operationally meaningful only when evaluated against governed thresholds. Integrity Threshold Module establishes the canonical governance boundaries that distinguish acceptable integrity from degradation, enabling consistent classification, timely intervention, and objective governance throughout the complete lifecycle of every governed entity.

title: Structural Coherence Module (SCCM)
text: OOF™ Structural Coherence Module (SCCM) Structural Coherence Module (SCCM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-STIS-SCCM-2026-07-17-0005 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Structural Integrity Standard (STIS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Structural Coherence Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 17 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Structural Coherence Canonical Definition Structural Coherence Module (SCCM) defines the governance conditions required to ensure that all structural components, relationships, dependencies, and organizational elements operate as one coherent, consistent, and governable structure. It preserves the overall unity of the governed entity throughout its complete lifecycle. Operational Role SCCM governs the coherence of the complete structural architecture. While previous modules govern individual structural elements, SCCM ensures that the entire structure functions as a unified and internally consistent whole capable of preserving integrity. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define Structural Coherence Objectives Identify the structural characteristics required for the governed entity to operate as a coherent architecture. Define the expected consistency between components, relationships, dependencies, organizational hierarchy, and governance structure. 2. Define Structural Coherence Requirements Establish the governance conditions required to maintain structural consistency, architectural alignment, interoperability, coordination, stability, and overall structural harmony throughout the complete lifecycle. 3. Define Structural Incoherence Logic Identify the conditions under which structural fragmentation, conflicting relationships, inconsistent dependencies, architectural misalignment, or organizational contradictions compromise structural coherence. 4. Define Governance Response Define governance actions for resolving structural inconsistencies, restoring architectural alignment, restructuring relationships, correcting dependencies, or approving structural modifications necessary to preserve coherence. 5. Preserve Structural Coherence Records Preserve structural assessments, coherence evaluations, governance decisions, architectural revisions, validation records, and supporting evidence demonstrating that structural coherence has been maintained throughout the lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — Government Digital Infrastructure Scenario A national digital government platform integrates identity services, taxation, healthcare, licensing, justice, and public administration into a unified governance ecosystem. Application SCCM evaluates whether all participating systems remain architecturally aligned, structurally consistent, and capable of operating as one coherent governance environment despite continuous evolution. Result The government preserves a unified digital governance architecture where structural inconsistencies are identified and resolved before they undermine system-wide integrity. Use Case 2 — Enterprise AI Governance Platform Scenario An enterprise deploys multiple AI systems responsible for customer service, finance, compliance, cybersecurity, and operational decision-making across different business units. Application SCCM validates that every AI system, governance policy, operational dependency, and organizational relationship remains structurally aligned with the enterprise architecture. Result The enterprise maintains a coherent AI governance architecture where all governed systems operate consistently, preserving structural integrity across the entire organization. Canonical Closing Statement Structural integrity reaches its highest form when every governed component, relationship, dependency, and organizational element operates as one coherent whole. Structural Coherence Module preserves this unity, ensuring that the complete architecture remains consistent, resilient, and governable throughout the lifecycle of every governed entity.

title: Structural Component Integrity Module (SCIM)
text: OOF™ Structural Component Integrity Module (SCIM) Structural Component Integrity Module (SCIM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-STIS-SCIM-2026-07-17-0002 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Structural Integrity Standard (STIS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Structural Component Integrity Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 17 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Structural Component Integrity Canonical Definition Structural Component Integrity Module (SCIM) defines the governance conditions required to ensure that every structural component of a governed entity maintains its integrity individually while remaining consistent with the integrity of the overall structure throughout the complete lifecycle. Operational Role SCIM governs the integrity of individual structural components before the integrity of the complete structure is evaluated. It ensures that every governed component satisfies the structural requirements necessary to contribute to the integrity of the whole. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define Structural Components Identify every structural component that belongs to the governed entity. Define each component's purpose, responsibilities, governance role, and contribution to the overall structural integrity. 2. Define Component Integrity Requirements Establish the structural conditions, quality requirements, dependencies, interfaces, and governance rules that every component must satisfy to preserve its individual integrity. 3. Define Component Failure Logic Identify the conditions under which a component becomes incomplete, inconsistent, corrupted, unavailable, unauthorized, or otherwise incapable of preserving its structural integrity. 4. Define Governance Response Define governance actions for validating, correcting, replacing, isolating, repairing, or reapproving structural components whose integrity no longer satisfies the required governance conditions. 5. Preserve Component Records Preserve component definitions, governance approvals, integrity assessments, change history, dependency information, maintenance activities, and supporting evidence throughout the complete lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — Enterprise Information System Scenario An organization operates a governance platform consisting of identity services, audit services, authorization services, and policy management components. Application SCIM evaluates each component individually to verify that it satisfies its structural integrity requirements before the integrity of the overall platform is assessed. Result Every structural component maintains its governed integrity, increasing the reliability, stability, and resilience of the complete governance system. Use Case 2 — Autonomous AI Platform Scenario An autonomous AI system contains separate modules for reasoning, planning, memory, identity, safety, and runtime governance. Application SCIM validates that each module independently satisfies its structural integrity requirements and that no compromised component weakens the integrity of the complete AI architecture. Result The AI platform preserves structural integrity at the component level, providing a stable foundation for trustworthy autonomous operation and long-term governance. Canonical Closing Statement The integrity of a structure depends upon the integrity of its components. Structural Component Integrity Module ensures that every governed component preserves its individual integrity while strengthening the resilience, consistency, and governability of the complete structural architecture.

title: Structural Dependency Integrity Module (SDIM)
text: OOF™ Structural Dependency Integrity Module (SDIM) Structural Dependency Integrity Module (SDIM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-STIS-SDIM-2026-07-17-0004 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Structural Integrity Standard (STIS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Structural Dependency Integrity Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 17 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Structural Dependency Integrity Canonical Definition Structural Dependency Integrity Module (SDIM) defines the governance conditions required to identify, validate, monitor, and preserve the integrity of dependencies between structural components. It ensures that every dependency remains legitimate, transparent, resilient, and governable throughout the complete lifecycle of a governed entity. Operational Role SDIM governs the dependency layer of structural integrity. It ensures that every governed dependency is explicitly identified, continuously validated, and managed so that changes or failures in one component do not compromise the integrity of the overall structure. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define Structural Dependencies Identify every dependency between structural components, including functional, operational, organizational, technical, governance, and external dependencies that influence structural integrity. 2. Define Dependency Integrity Requirements Establish the governance conditions that every dependency must satisfy, including legitimacy, availability, consistency, traceability, resilience, and continuity. 3. Define Dependency Failure Logic Identify the conditions under which a dependency becomes unavailable, invalid, inconsistent, broken, unauthorized, obsolete, or otherwise incapable of supporting structural integrity. 4. Define Governance Response Define governance actions for validating, replacing, mitigating, removing, restructuring, or approving dependency changes whenever dependency integrity is compromised. 5. Preserve Dependency Records Preserve dependency maps, governance approvals, dependency changes, validation history, supporting evidence, and lifecycle records necessary to demonstrate dependency integrity. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — Financial Services Platform Scenario A financial institution operates multiple interconnected services, including customer identity, transaction processing, fraud detection, and regulatory reporting, all of which depend on one another. Application SDIM identifies and governs every dependency between these services, ensuring that changes to one service do not unintentionally compromise the structural integrity of the entire platform. Result The institution maintains resilient and transparent service dependencies, reducing operational risk while preserving structural integrity across the complete financial ecosystem. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Multi-Agent System Scenario A fleet of autonomous agents depends on shared memory services, identity infrastructure, orchestration components, external sensors, and governance policies to coordinate operations. Application SDIM maps and continuously validates every operational and governance dependency, ensuring that dependency failures are detected and managed before they affect the integrity of the system. Result The autonomous ecosystem maintains dependable structural relationships, allowing agents to operate safely and consistently despite changes in individual components or supporting infrastructure. Canonical Closing Statement Integrity depends not only on components and relationships, but also on the dependencies that connect them. Structural Dependency Integrity Module ensures that every governed dependency remains visible, resilient, and continuously governable, preserving the structural integrity of the complete governed entity throughout its lifecycle.

title: Structural Relationship Integrity Module (SRIM)
text: OOF™ Structural Relationship Integrity Module (SRIM) Structural Relationship Integrity Module (SRIM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-STIS-SRIM-2026-07-17-0003 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Structural Integrity Standard (STIS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Structural Relationship Integrity Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 17 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Structural Relationship Integrity Canonical Definition Structural Relationship Integrity Module (SRIM) defines the governance conditions required to preserve the integrity of relationships between structural components. It ensures that dependencies, interactions, authority paths, information flows, and organizational connections remain complete, consistent, valid, and governable throughout the complete lifecycle of a governed entity. Operational Role SRIM governs the integrity of relationships connecting structural components. It ensures that the overall structure remains coherent by preserving the legitimacy, consistency, and continuity of every governed relationship. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define Structural Relationships Identify every governed relationship between structural components, including dependencies, authority relationships, communication paths, operational interactions, and information flows. 2. Define Relationship Integrity Requirements Establish the governance conditions that every structural relationship must satisfy, including consistency, validity, traceability, authorization, continuity, and dependency integrity. 3. Define Relationship Failure Logic Identify the conditions under which a structural relationship becomes invalid, inconsistent, broken, unauthorized, ambiguous, incomplete, or incapable of preserving structural integrity. 4. Define Governance Response Define governance actions for validating, correcting, restoring, replacing, removing, or reauthorizing structural relationships whenever integrity is compromised. 5. Preserve Relationship Records Preserve relationship definitions, dependency records, governance approvals, structural revisions, validation history, and supporting evidence necessary to demonstrate relationship integrity throughout the complete lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — Corporate Governance Scenario A multinational organization restructures its reporting hierarchy, changing governance relationships between executive leadership, regional management, and operational departments. Application SRIM validates every new reporting relationship, authority chain, and governance dependency to ensure that the organizational structure continues to preserve structural integrity. Result The restructured organization maintains consistent governance relationships without introducing ambiguity, broken authority chains, or structural inconsistencies. Use Case 2 — Autonomous AI Ecosystem Scenario An autonomous AI ecosystem contains multiple agents that exchange information, delegate tasks, coordinate decisions, and share operational resources. Application SRIM governs the integrity of communication paths, coordination relationships, authority delegation, and operational dependencies between agents before the system enters production. Result The AI ecosystem preserves trustworthy structural relationships, ensuring coordinated, governable, and structurally consistent autonomous operation throughout its lifecycle. Canonical Closing Statement A structure is only as strong as the relationships that connect it. Structural Relationship Integrity Module preserves the legitimacy, consistency, and continuity of every governed relationship, ensuring that structural integrity extends beyond individual components to the complete governed architecture.

title: Structure Mapping Module (STMM)
text: OOF™ Structure Mapping Module (STMM) Structure Mapping Module (STMM) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority OriginID: OOF-OID-INTEGROS-STIS-STMM-2026-07-17-0001 Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture Parent Standard: Structural Integrity Standard (STIS) Operational Layer: Meta-Integrity Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Integrity Governance Type: Parent Standard Module Governed Space: Structural Mapping Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Module Origin Date: 17 July 2026 Compatibility: OOF Methodology OS · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · ART™ · ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP™ — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: English (UCL) Governed Space Structural Mapping Canonical Definition Structure Mapping Module (STMM) defines the canonical structural representation of a governed entity by identifying its components, relationships, dependencies, hierarchy, and organizational arrangement. It establishes the structural reference required to preserve, evaluate, and govern integrity throughout the complete lifecycle of the entity. Operational Role STMM establishes the official structural map upon which every subsequent structural integrity activity depends. It provides the governed representation of how the entity is organized before structural integrity can be measured, monitored, evaluated, or assured. Minimum Implementation Framework 1. Define the Governed Structure Identify the governed entity and define every structural component that forms its integrity architecture. All components, organizational units, assets, services, processes, or functional elements requiring integrity governance shall be explicitly identified and documented. 2. Define Structural Relationships Establish the relationships, dependencies, hierarchy, interactions, and organizational connections between structural components. The structural map shall accurately represent how components interact and collectively preserve structural integrity. 3. Define Structural Failure Logic Identify the conditions under which the structural model becomes incomplete, inconsistent, fragmented, ambiguous, obsolete, or incapable of preserving integrity. Define how structural weaknesses and missing relationships are detected. 4. Define Governance Response Define governance actions for validating, updating, correcting, restructuring, approving, or rejecting structural changes whenever modifications affect the governed integrity structure. 5. Preserve Structural Records Preserve structural maps, governance approvals, dependency records, relationship definitions, structural revisions, version history, and supporting evidence required to demonstrate structural integrity throughout the complete lifecycle. Example Use Cases Use Case 1 — Corporate Governance Scenario An organization prepares for an enterprise-wide governance assessment and must establish a complete representation of its governance structure before evaluating structural integrity. Application STMM maps all governance bodies, organizational units, reporting relationships, operational processes, critical assets, and structural dependencies into a single governed structural model. Result The organization obtains a complete structural reference that enables consistent structural integrity assessment, governance analysis, and controlled structural evolution. Use Case 2 — Autonomous AI System Scenario An autonomous AI platform contains multiple decision engines, memory services, identity services, governance controls, external interfaces, and runtime components that operate together. Application STMM creates the canonical structural map of the complete AI architecture by documenting every governed component, dependency, hierarchy, and interaction before structural integrity is evaluated. Result The AI system becomes structurally governable, allowing integrity assessments, governance decisions, and future architectural changes to be performed against a complete and continuously maintained structural reference. Canonical Closing Statement Integrity can only be preserved when the underlying structure is fully understood. Structure Mapping Module establishes the canonical structural representation that enables every structural integrity assessment, governance decision, and assurance activity throughout the complete lifecycle of a governed entity.
