title: Value Emergence Determination Module (VEDM)
text: Value Emergence Determination Module (VEDM) Value Emergence Determination Module (VEDM) Value Emergence Determination Module (VEDM) Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture Parent Standard: Value Emergence Standard (VES) Module: VEDM — Value Emergence Determination Module Operational Layer: Value Emergence Determination Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Value Lifecycle Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value Emergence Determination Origin ID: VFM-VES-VEDM-003.4 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 24 August 2026 Compatibility: OOF® Methodology OS™ · GOA™ · ORA™ · INTEGROS® · CLA™ · ADIT® · VALIDOS® · SIMULOS® · OBIDENITY® AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition Value Emergence Determination Module (VEDM) is the fourth Core Module of the Value Emergence Standard (VES) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture. VEDM governs the formal determination of whether potential value has actually become existent value within the defined Value Context. The Module receives the governed emergence conditions, emergence threshold, and emergence event established through the preceding modules and determines whether their combined basis is sufficient to establish the transition: Potential Value → Existing Value VEDM therefore creates the decisive methodological gate between: a value that could exist and a value that has emerged. It does not determine whether that value is legally recognized, owned, marketable, taxable, validated, correctly priced, economically beneficial to every stakeholder, or universally accepted. It determines one narrower question: Has the governed value actually emerged? Architectural Position VEDM is the fourth module within the Value Emergence Standard. It follows: VEEM — Value Emergence Event Module and precedes: VERM — Value Emergence Record Module. The internal sequence is: Emergence Conditions → Emergence Threshold → Emergence Event → Emergence Determination → Emergence Record The modules perform distinct functions: VECM establishes the conditions under which value may emerge. VETM establishes when those conditions become sufficient for emergence. VEEM identifies what materially occurred at the emergence boundary. VEDM determines whether the governed basis establishes that value has actually emerged. VERM preserves that determination as a governed lifecycle record. Internal Value Flow Defined Value Context → Identified Value Origin → Potential Value → Emergence Conditions → Emergence Threshold → Emergence Event → Determination Basis Assembly → Context Consistency Check → Threshold–Event Relationship Assessment → Value Existence Assessment → Uncertainty Assessment → Emergence Determination → Existing Value / Value Not Established / Conditional State → Emergence Record VEDM is therefore the point where the architecture can legitimately say: This value now exists. Governance Flow Position Within the complete VFM® governance flow: Value Context → Value Origin → Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change → Value Development / Value Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration / Value Extinction VEDM operates at the final determination stage inside Value Emergence, immediately before the result is formally recorded. It establishes whether the lifecycle may proceed from: Value Emergence to: Value Recognition. Operational Purpose Organizations routinely assume that value exists because something else exists. Examples include: Money Spent → therefore Value Created Asset Built → therefore Value Created Technology Deployed → therefore Value Created Project Completed → therefore Value Created Product Delivered → therefore Value Created Capability Available → therefore Value Created Revenue Generated → therefore Value Created VEDM prevents these automatic equivalences. Each may provide evidence relevant to value emergence. None establishes value emergence independently unless it satisfies the governed Value Context and emergence basis. VEDM therefore introduces an explicit Value Existence Determination rather than allowing value to be inferred from activity, expenditure, ownership, output, or institutional assertion. Determination Basis A Value Emergence Determination should be based upon a reconstructable relationship between: Governed Value Context Value Origin Emergence Conditions Emergence Threshold Emergence Event Material Evidence Remaining Uncertainty The exact evidential requirement may vary according to the value being governed. VEDM does not impose one universal formula for all value. It requires the determination basis to be explicit. Value Existence Test At minimum, VEDM should establish whether: 1. the governed value remains the same value identified through the Value Context; 2. a relevant Value Origin exists; 3. required emergence conditions were materially satisfied; 4. the applicable emergence threshold was reached; 5. a qualifying emergence event occurred; 6. the event materially relates to the governed value; 7. the claimed value is distinguishable from the resources consumed to produce it; 8. material uncertainty does not make the existence claim unsupported; 9. no known contradiction defeats the determination; 10. the available basis supports an explicit emergence state. Only then should the architecture establish: Existing Value. Value Existence ≠ Value Amount VEDM determines whether value exists. It does not necessarily determine: how much value exists. This distinction is essential. A new capability may clearly create value while the exact economic magnitude of that value remains uncertain. Therefore: Value Existence Determination ≠ Value Quantification and: Unknown Value Amount ≠ No Value A legitimate Value Emergence Determination may exist even when precise monetary valuation is impossible. Value Existence ≠ Price Market price may provide information concerning value. Price does not define value existence under VFM®. An object may: have value without an observable market price; have a price while the governed value being assessed has not emerged; have multiple prices across markets; temporarily have no liquid market; provide operational, strategic, scientific, social, infrastructural, or capability value without a direct market price. Therefore: Price ≠ Value Existence VEDM protects the architecture from reducing value to market pricing. Value Existence ≠ Cost Cost establishes resource consumption. VEDM establishes value emergence. The two may be related, but they are not equivalent. CHF 100 million invested does not establish: CHF 100 million of value created. Equally: CHF 1 million invested does not prevent: CHF 100 million of value from emerging. This separation allows VFM® to analyze value independently from the accounting history of the resources used to create it. Value Existence ≠ Revenue Revenue may result from value, market position, contractual structure, scarcity, pricing power, regulation, transfer, speculation, or other mechanisms. VEDM does not automatically treat revenue as proof that the specific governed value has emerged. Likewise, value may emerge before revenue exists. Therefore: Revenue ≠ Value Emergence and No Revenue ≠ No Value. Value Existence ≠ Asset Completion A completed asset may remain only a potential value source. Examples include: an unused factory; unused infrastructure; dormant intellectual property; an undeployed algorithm; an unutilized production capability; an unused satellite capability; an empty logistics facility; an installed but ineffective technology. Asset completion may therefore precede value emergence. VEDM requires the architecture to determine whether the defined value actually crossed into existence. Value Existence ≠ Value Recognition VEDM establishes whether value exists. The subsequent Value Recognition Standard (VRS) governs whether that existing value may be recognized within a defined governance context. This produces a critical VFM® distinction: Value may exist before it is recognized. Therefore: Emergence Determination → Existing Value → Recognition Governance not: Recognition → Value Existence. Recognition does not create the underlying value merely by declaring it. Positive Emergence Determination A Positive Emergence Determination is established where the governed basis sufficiently supports that the identified value has moved from potential to existent value. The resulting state is: Existing Value This state becomes eligible to enter the Value Recognition Standard. A positive determination should identify: the value determined to exist; the applicable Value Context; relevant Value Origin; satisfied conditions; threshold basis; emergence event; determination time; material limitations; uncertainty; applicable context. Negative Emergence Determination A Negative Emergence Determination establishes that the available basis does not support the conclusion that the governed value has emerged. This does not necessarily mean: the value can never emerge. It means: Value Emergence Not Established under the current basis. The value may remain: Potential Value and later undergo a new emergence pathway. Conditional Emergence Determination Some value may be determined to exist only under defined conditions. For example: Value exists for beneficiary group A under operational condition B, but has not been established outside that context. VEDM therefore permits: Conditional Emergence Determination. Conditional existence must remain explicitly bounded. It must not silently become universal value existence. Indeterminate Emergence Where the available basis is insufficient to support either a positive or negative determination, VEDM should permit: Emergence Indeterminate. This is important because methodological governance must not force certainty where certainty does not exist. The correct outcome may be: insufficient basis to determine whether value has emerged. This can trigger: further observation; additional evidence; renewed emergence event assessment; threshold reassessment; clarification of Value Context. Emergence Determination States VEDM may assign at least the following states: 1. Not Assessed No formal emergence determination has yet occurred. 2. Emergence Not Established The current basis does not establish that value has emerged. 3. Emergence Indeterminate The available basis does not permit a sufficiently supported determination. 4. Conditionally Emerged Value existence is established only within explicitly defined conditions. 5. Emerged The governed basis supports that the identified value exists. 6. Determination Suspended A previously issued determination requires reassessment because a material problem affecting its basis has arisen. 7. Determination Superseded A later governed determination replaces the previous determination. These states make value emergence machine-governable rather than dependent upon unstructured narrative claims. Determination Time VEDM should establish when the emergence determination becomes effective. This time may differ from: the time the Value Origin was created; the time expenditure occurred; the time an asset was completed; the time the threshold was reached; the time the emergence event began; the time evidence was reviewed; the time the determination was formally documented. Where possible, VEDM should distinguish: Emergence Event Time from Emergence Determination Time. This supports later lifecycle reconstruction. Retroactive Determination Value may have emerged before the organization formally recognized or assessed that emergence. VEDM may therefore support a retroactive determination where sufficient evidence exists. For example: Value Emerged at T1 but Value Emergence Determination issued at T2. The architecture must preserve both timestamps. This becomes especially important for accounting, investment analysis, public policy, economic measurement, project evaluation, and future tax-governance interfaces. Determination Scope A Value Emergence Determination must remain connected to its defined scope. Value may be established: for one beneficiary but not another; in one jurisdictional or operational context but not another; for one purpose but not another; under one configuration but not another; during one period but not another; for one value dimension but not another. VEDM therefore rejects the assumption: Value Exists Somewhere → Value Exists Universally. Partial Emergence Some value structures may emerge progressively. VEDM may therefore determine that only a defined part, dimension, capability, beneficiary relationship, or portion of the governed value has emerged. This should not be confused with Value Development. Partial Emergence means the original emergence process is incomplete. Value Development means already-existing value subsequently increases, strengthens, matures, compounds, or develops. The distinction is: Incomplete emergence ≠ development of existing value. Composite Value Emergence A governed value may depend upon multiple constituent value components. VEDM may determine: Component A Emerged Component B Emerged Component C Not Established while the composite value remains: Not Yet Fully Emerged. This enables VFM® to govern complex infrastructure, industrial, technological, financial, scientific, and mission systems without forcing binary simplification. Contradictory Evidence VEDM must account for materially contradictory evidence. A Value Emergence Determination must not be based solely upon evidence supporting the preferred conclusion. Contradictory evidence may: prevent positive determination; produce an indeterminate state; narrow the determination scope; create conditional emergence; trigger reassessment of the emergence event; require additional evidence. Preferred outcome ≠ governed determination. Uncertainty Uncertainty does not automatically prevent Value Emergence Determination. VEDM distinguishes between: uncertainty about the exact magnitude of value and uncertainty about whether value exists at all. The first may permit a positive determination. The second may require conditional or indeterminate status. This distinction allows VFM® to operate in environments where precise valuation is impossible but value existence is nevertheless materially demonstrable. Determination Reassessment A Value Emergence Determination may require reassessment where: material evidence changes; the Value Context was incorrectly defined; the emergence event was misidentified; threshold satisfaction is challenged; contradictory evidence emerges; fraud or data error is discovered; the beneficiary relationship was misunderstood; the claimed value was actually a different value; the determination was based upon an invalid dependency. VEDM must therefore support controlled reassessment. Emergence Determination ≠ Validation Determination VEDM does not replace VALIDOS®. The distinction is: VEDM: Has the specifically governed value emerged according to the VFM® emergence structure? VALIDOS®: Can a defined Validation Object or claim legitimately receive a Validation Determination under the applicable validation criteria, method, evidence, and reliance conditions? A Value Emergence Determination may itself later become a Validation Object. The two governance questions remain distinct. Emergence Determination ≠ Accounting Recognition VEDM does not determine whether value must appear on: a balance sheet; income statement; financial report; regulatory filing; accounting ledger. Accounting recognition is a separate governance and regulatory question. VFM® can provide an upstream value-lifecycle structure that accounting systems may later reference. This distinction is strategically important: Value may exist even where existing accounting rules do not recognize it as an accounting asset. Emergence Determination ≠ Taxable Event A determination that value exists does not establish that tax is due. Taxation may depend upon: realization; transfer; jurisdiction; legal classification; taxable event; taxpayer status; statutory rules; exemptions; timing. Therefore: Value Emergence ≠ Tax Liability. A future tax-governance architecture may use VFM® value states and transitions as inputs without VFM® becoming a tax system. Emergence Determination ≠ Ownership VEDM determines whether value exists. It does not determine who owns that value. The underlying object, capability, right, or value relationship may involve separate identity, ownership, authority, provenance, or transfer governance. Therefore: Value Existence ≠ Value Ownership. Determination Integrity A Value Emergence Determination should be: context-linked; origin-linked; threshold-linked; event-linked; evidence-aware; uncertainty-aware; scope-bounded; temporally identifiable; reconstructable; capable of reassessment. The determination should not exist merely as an unsupported statement: “Value was created.” VEDM converts that assertion into a governable methodological conclusion. Determination Logic A minimum operational logic may be: Value Context valid? ↓ Value Origin identified? ↓ Emergence Conditions satisfied? ↓ Emergence Threshold reached? ↓ Qualifying Emergence Event occurred? ↓ Event materially connected to governed value? ↓ Contradictory evidence assessed? ↓ Material uncertainty acceptable for determination? ↓ YES → Emerged / Conditionally Emerged NO → Emergence Not Established / Indeterminate This logic may be implemented manually, computationally, or through AI-supported governance systems. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum VEDM implementation should establish: 1. Governed Value Confirmation Confirm the exact value whose emergence is being determined. 2. Context Confirmation Confirm the relevant Value Context, object, beneficiary, purpose, and reference framework. 3. Origin Confirmation Confirm the governed Value Origin supporting the emergence pathway. 4. Conditions and Threshold Review Confirm the applicable emergence conditions and threshold state. 5. Emergence Event Review Confirm the event or composite event forming the immediate emergence basis. 6. Evidence Review Identify the material evidence supporting and challenging emergence. 7. Uncertainty Assessment Determine whether remaining uncertainty affects existence, magnitude, scope, or only downstream recognition. 8. Determination Assign the appropriate Value Emergence Determination state. 9. Scope and Time Definition Define the context and temporal boundary within which the determination applies. 10. Transfer to Record Transfer the governed determination to VERM for preservation. Governance Outputs VEDM may produce: Value Emergence Determination Value Existence Determination Value Emergence Determination State Value Emergence Basis Value Emergence Evidence Basis Value Emergence Contradiction Record Value Emergence Uncertainty Statement Conditional Emergence Statement Partial Emergence Determination Composite Value Emergence Determination Value Emergence Scope Statement Value Emergence Effective Time Value Emergence Determination Time Value Emergence Reassessment Trigger Governed Existing Value These outputs become the governed input for: VERM — Value Emergence Record Module. Use Case 1 — Banking & Infrastructure Finance: Has the Investment Actually Created Value? A banking consortium finances a CHF 1.2 billion infrastructure project. Construction is completed. The asset exists physically. The financing has been deployed. The project appears operational. Traditional reporting may show: Capital Deployed → Asset Completed → Project Operational But the financing institutions need to answer a different question: Has the value for which the capital was deployed actually emerged? Suppose the governed value is: a transport capability capable of sustainably moving the required passenger volume while reducing defined network congestion. VFM® separates: CHF 1.2bn Expenditure → Infrastructure Asset → Potential Value → Emergence Conditions → Emergence Threshold → Operational Emergence Event → VEDM Determination If the infrastructure operates but does not achieve the minimum capability required by the defined Value Context, VEDM may determine: Emergence Not Established or: Conditionally Emerged. If the governed basis demonstrates that the required capability exists, VEDM may establish: Emerged. The bank can therefore distinguish between: money deployed asset completed asset operational and value actually emerged. That distinction can materially improve project finance monitoring, restructuring decisions, investment governance, portfolio analysis, public-private financing, and post-investment evaluation. Use Case 2 — AI / Space Mission: Capability Success vs. Actual Mission Value A space organization develops an AI-enabled autonomous navigation system for a planetary mission. Billions are spent on research, simulation, hardware, launch, and mission operations. The spacecraft reaches the target. The navigation system activates successfully. Technically, the project has achieved major milestones. But suppose the governed value is: autonomous navigation capability that materially increases mission access to scientifically valuable locations unavailable under the previous control architecture. VFM® does not infer value merely from: R&D expenditure launch success system deployment or technical activation. The emergence pathway may instead be: Navigation Capability Source → Potential Mission Value → Defined Emergence Conditions → Performance Threshold → Autonomous Navigation Event → Successful Access to Previously Unreachable Scientific Target → VEDM Determination VEDM may then establish: Emerged for the governed mission value. The organization can now distinguish: technology exists from technology works from technology created the value for which it was developed. This makes VFM® applicable not merely to financial valuation, but to mission governance, AI investment, scientific programs, infrastructure, public spending, industrial development, and other environments where enormous resource expenditure does not itself prove value creation. Foundational Principles Potential value is not existing value. Threshold satisfaction is not automatically value existence. An emergence event is not automatically a positive emergence determination. Value existence is not value amount. Value is not reducible to price. Cost is not value. Revenue is not value. Asset completion is not value emergence. Capability existence is not necessarily value emergence. Value may exist before it is recognized. Value may exist without being owned, priced, taxed, traded, or recognized in accounting. Uncertainty about value magnitude does not automatically mean uncertainty about value existence. A Value Emergence Determination must remain connected to the Value Context, Value Origin, emergence conditions, threshold, event, evidence, scope, and uncertainty that support it. VEDM establishes whether potential value has crossed into existence; it does not determine what every external system must subsequently do with that value. Canonical Closing Statement Value Emergence Determination Module establishes the decisive existence gate within the Value Emergence Standard by determining whether the governed value has legitimately transitioned from potential value into existing value. Through explicit linkage of Value Context, Value Origin, emergence conditions, emergence thresholds, emergence events, evidence, contradictions, uncertainty, scope, and temporal position, VEDM prevents expenditure, asset completion, technical deployment, transactions, revenue, institutional assertion, or operational activity from being automatically interpreted as value creation. By separating value existence from value magnitude, price, accounting recognition, ownership, taxation, validation, and subsequent recognition, VEDM creates a distinct governable determination that can be used across banking, investment, infrastructure, industry, science, AI, public finance, mission systems, and other value-bearing environments. VEDM therefore establishes the methodological point at which VFM® may legitimately state that potential value has become existent value, while preserving the conditions and boundaries required for that value to proceed into formal Value Recognition and the subsequent value lifecycle. title: Value Emergence Event Module (VEEM)
text: Value Emergence Event Module (VEEM) Value Emergence Event Module (VEEM) Value Emergence Event Module (VEEM) Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture Parent Standard: Value Emergence Standard (VES) Module: VEEM — Value Emergence Event Module Operational Layer: Value Emergence Event Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Value Lifecycle Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value Emergence Event Origin ID: VFM-VES-VEEM-003.3 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 24 August 2026 Compatibility: OOF® Methodology OS™ · GOA™ · ORA™ · INTEGROS® · CLA™ · ADIT® · VALIDOS® · SIMULOS® · OBIDENITY® AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition Value Emergence Event Module (VEEM) is the third Core Module of the Value Emergence Standard (VES) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture. VEEM governs the identification, definition, structuring, temporal localization, contextualization, and documentation of the event, occurrence, transition, activation, realization, or materially identifiable change through which threshold- satisfied potential value moves into an emergence event capable of supporting a subsequent Value Emergence Determination. The Module establishes the governed transition between: Emergence-Ready Value and Value whose emergence has materially occurred and can now be evaluated. VEEM does not determine conclusively that value exists. That responsibility belongs to: VEDM — Value Emergence Determination Module. VEEM governs what happened at the point of emergence. VEDM governs whether what happened is sufficient to determine that value has emerged. Architectural Position VEEM is the third module within the Value Emergence Standard. It follows: VETM — Value Emergence Threshold Module and precedes: VEDM — Value Emergence Determination Module. The internal sequence is: Emergence Conditions → Emergence Threshold → Emergence Event → Emergence Determination → Emergence Record VECM establishes: What conditions must exist? VETM establishes: When are those conditions sufficient? VEEM establishes: What materially occurred when the emergence boundary was crossed? VEDM establishes: Does that occurrence legitimately establish that value emerged? VERM preserves: What emergence was ultimately established and on what basis? Internal Value Flow Potential Value → Emergence Conditions → Threshold Satisfaction → Threshold Crossing → Emergence-Ready Value → Emergence Event Candidate → Event Identification → Event Context → Event Temporal Position → Event-to-Value Relationship → Event State → Governed Value Emergence Event → Value Emergence Determination This flow prevents value existence from being declared merely because a threshold was theoretically satisfied. Something must materially occur that connects the satisfied emergence conditions to the claimed emergence of value. Governance Flow Position Within the complete VFM® governance flow: Value Context → Value Origin → Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change → Value Development / Value Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration / Value Extinction Within Value Emergence: VECM — Value Emergence Conditions → VETM — Value Emergence Threshold → VEEM — Value Emergence Event → VEDM — Value Emergence Determination → VERM — Value Emergence Record VEEM therefore occupies the exact transition point between: sufficient conditions for emergence and formal determination that value now exists. Operational Purpose Value does not necessarily emerge simply because: money was invested; an asset was created; a product was completed; infrastructure became available; a capability became technically operational; a transaction occurred; a service was launched; a resource was consumed; a project reached completion; a threshold was theoretically satisfied. These events may be related to value. They are not automatically Value Emergence Events. VEEM requires the relevant occurrence to be connected to the specific governed value established through the Value Context Standard. The Module therefore asks: What actually happened that may mark the transition from potential value toward existing value? Value Emergence Event A Value Emergence Event is a materially identifiable occurrence, transition, activation, realization, interaction, outcome, state change, or other governed event through which threshold-satisfied potential value manifests in a form capable of being evaluated as existent value. A Value Emergence Event must be connected to: Governed Value Context Value Origin Emergence Conditions Emergence Threshold Relevant Occurrence The event is therefore not an isolated operational event. It is an event interpreted specifically within the governed value lifecycle. Operational Event ≠ Value Emergence Event An operational event may occur without creating value. For example: Factory starts production. That is an operational event. Whether it constitutes a Value Emergence Event depends upon the governed value. If the governed value is: production capability, the event may be highly relevant. If the governed value is: reduction of customer delivery time, production startup alone may not yet establish emergence. If the governed value is: reduction of manufacturing cost, production startup may even occur before any relevant value has emerged. Therefore: Operational Event ≠ Value Emergence Event unless the event is materially connected to the defined value context. Transaction ≠ Value Emergence Event A transaction may transfer money, assets, rights, obligations, or resources. It does not automatically establish that value has emerged. For example: Investor pays CHF 10 million does not establish: CHF 10 million of value emerged. The payment may finance a potential value source. VEEM separates: resource movement from value emergence. This distinction is fundamental for banking, investment, public finance, accounting, infrastructure, and economic analysis. Cost ≠ Value Emergence Resources consumed in creating potential value must not automatically be interpreted as value created. Therefore: Cost Incurred ≠ Value Emerged Capital Deployed ≠ Value Emerged Budget Spent ≠ Value Emerged Asset Completed ≠ Value Emerged Technology Deployed ≠ Value Emerged The relevant Value Emergence Event must demonstrate a material connection between the potential value and the occurrence through which that value begins to exist. Event Identification VEEM requires the emergence event to be identifiable. Identification may include: event identity; event type; event source; event time; event location or environment where relevant; participating entities; affected value object; beneficiary relationship; originating value source; applicable emergence conditions; applicable threshold; resulting observable change; event evidence; uncertainty. The exact implementation may vary. The governance requirement remains: the emergence event must be reconstructable sufficiently to support downstream determination. Event Types Value may emerge through different types of events. VEEM may govern: Activation Event A capability becomes materially usable. Utilization Event A previously available capability is actually used in a value-producing context. Delivery Event A value-bearing outcome reaches the relevant beneficiary. Performance Event A capability produces the defined performance associated with the governed value. Conversion Event A potential value source produces a materially different value-bearing result. Interaction Event Value emerges through interaction between multiple actors, systems, resources, or capabilities. Availability Event A resource or capability becomes materially available where availability itself constitutes the governed value. Outcome Event The defined outcome associated with the governed value occurs. Realization Event Previously potential value becomes materially realized. Composite Emergence Event Several events together establish the relevant emergence occurrence. VFM® does not require all value to emerge through one universal event type. Single Event vs. Composite Event Some value may emerge through one identifiable event. Example: a service successfully delivered to a beneficiary. Other value may require a sequence or combination of events. Example: technology activation + sustained operation + beneficiary utilization + measurable outcome. VEEM therefore distinguishes: Single Emergence Event from Composite Emergence Event. A composite event must preserve the relationship between its constituent occurrences. Instantaneous vs. Progressive Emergence Value may emerge: instantaneously or progressively. An instantaneous emergence event may occur at a specific moment. A progressive emergence event may develop across: multiple interactions; repeated outputs; sustained utilization; cumulative performance; continuous availability; gradual realization. VEEM must therefore permit an emergence event to have: Event Start Event Progression Event Completion where the governed value requires it. Temporal Localization VEEM establishes the temporal position of the emergence event. Where possible, the Module should distinguish: Before Emergence Event During Emergence Event After Emergence Event This enables downstream VFM® governance to identify when value entered existence and subsequently distinguish: Value Emergence from Value Development or Value Degradation. Without temporal localization, later value changes may be incorrectly treated as part of original value creation. Emergence Event Boundary VEEM must identify where the emergence event begins and where it ends. This is especially important for progressive or composite value emergence. The boundary may be based upon: activation; first qualifying use; delivery; threshold crossing; outcome occurrence; sustained performance; beneficiary realization; completion of an event sequence; other context-specific conditions. The event boundary must correspond to the governed value rather than an arbitrary project milestone. Event-to-Value Relationship The existence of an event does not establish that the event caused or produced the governed value. VEEM therefore requires an explicit relationship between: Emergence Event and Governed Value. The relationship may be: direct; enabling; contributory; composite; conditional; dependent; uncertain. This relationship must remain visible for VEDM. Direct Emergence Direct emergence occurs where the event itself produces or manifests the governed value with minimal intermediate dependency. Example: A transportation service successfully moves the beneficiary from the defined origin to destination. Where the governed value is: successful transportation delivery the completion event may have a direct relationship to value emergence. Enabling Event An event may enable value without itself establishing that value has emerged. Example: A hospital installs a new diagnostic system. Installation creates capability. If the governed value is: improved diagnostic outcome installation alone is an enabling event, not necessarily the Value Emergence Event. This distinction prevents: Capability Creation from being silently transformed into: Value Creation. Contributory Event Some events contribute to value emergence without independently establishing it. Several contributory events may together form a Composite Emergence Event. VEEM should therefore preserve: Event A + Event B + Event C → Composite Emergence Basis where appropriate. Beneficiary Relationship Where value depends upon a beneficiary, VEEM should preserve the relationship between the emergence event and that beneficiary. A capability may exist. An output may exist. A product may exist. But where the governed value depends upon beneficiary realization, value may not emerge until the relevant beneficiary relationship becomes operationally meaningful. This does not mean all value requires a human beneficiary. The beneficiary may be: individual; organization; system; ecosystem; infrastructure; public institution; economy; mission; operational process; future capability. The relevant beneficiary is inherited from the governed Value Context. Event Materiality Not every occurrence related to potential value should become a Value Emergence Event. VEEM therefore requires materiality. An event is materially relevant where it changes the governed value lifecycle sufficiently to justify progression toward Value Emergence Determination. Materiality may depend upon: value purpose; beneficiary; scale; duration; consequence; threshold relationship; operational significance; persistence; context. Event Evidence A Value Emergence Event should have an identifiable evidential basis proportionate to its significance. Evidence may include: operational records; system outputs; delivery records; utilization data; performance measurements; beneficiary interaction; transaction records; physical observation; sensor data; production data; mission data; financial data; documented outcomes. VEEM governs the event relationship. It does not replace broader evidence governance under ADIT®, integrity governance under INTEGROS®, or validation governance under VALIDOS®. Event Uncertainty Not every emergence event will be perfectly observable. VEEM therefore allows uncertainty concerning: event timing; event completeness; event causality; event materiality; event-to-value relationship; beneficiary effect; event persistence; composite event completion. Where material uncertainty exists, it must remain visible when the event proceeds to VEDM. Event States VEEM may assign governed event states including: No Emergence Event No materially relevant event has been identified. Event Candidate A potentially relevant emergence event has been identified. Event In Progress A progressive or composite emergence event has begun but is not complete. Event Occurred The governed emergence event has materially occurred. Event Uncertain The available basis does not support reliable characterization of the event. Event Failed The expected emergence event did not complete sufficiently. Event Reversed An event occurred but was materially reversed before emergence could be determined. Event Superseded A later event replaces the earlier event as the relevant emergence basis. These states support complex and dynamic value environments. Failed Emergence Event A threshold may be crossed while the subsequent emergence event fails. For example: production capability exists but the first intended production process fails to produce usable output. The lifecycle may therefore become: Threshold Crossed → Emergence Event Attempted → Emergence Event Failed → Value Remains Potential This is an important architectural distinction. Emergence Readiness ≠ Successful Emergence. Reversed Emergence Event An emergence event may begin but reverse before a legitimate emergence determination is possible. Example: A digital service becomes operational but immediately fails before any material value can be realized. VEEM allows: Event Initiation → Event Reversal without forcing the architecture to declare that value existed merely because activation briefly occurred. Repeated Emergence Events Some value may emerge repeatedly. Examples include: repeated service delivery; recurring energy generation; repeated transportation; recurring computation; repeated financial benefit; repeated scientific output. VEEM must distinguish: Initial Value Emergence from Repeated Value-Producing Events. Once the governed value already exists, later events may belong to: Value State Value Change or Value Development rather than constituting new emergence of the same value. This prevents repeated production from being counted repeatedly as original value creation. New Value from Existing Value A later event may create a genuinely new value even where another value already exists. Example: A dataset already has operational value. A new analytical capability later produces a new predictive value from that dataset. The new value requires its own governed Value Context and emergence pathway. Therefore: Existing Value + New Capability ≠ Automatically Same Value A new value may require: New Value Context → New Value Origin → New Value Emergence. Event Attribution Boundary VEEM identifies the relationship between an event and value emergence. It does not determine legal responsibility, ownership, entitlement, accountability, or compensation for that value. Those questions remain outside the Module. Therefore: Value Emergence Event ≠ Ownership Event Value Emergence Event ≠ Taxable Event Value Emergence Event ≠ Payment Event Value Emergence Event ≠ Legal Recognition Event Value Emergence Event ≠ Accountability Determination This separation is critical if VFM® is later combined with accounting, taxation, banking, payment, or economic governance architectures. Internal Value Flow Control VEEM acts as the event gate between threshold satisfaction and formal emergence determination. The operational logic is: No Event → Remain Emergence-Ready Event Candidate → Assess Event Event In Progress → Continue Observation Event Uncertain → Hold / Clarify Event Failed → Return to Potential / Emergence-Ready State as applicable Event Reversed → Reassess Emergence Basis Event Occurred → Transfer to VEDM This makes VEEM usable as an operational governance mechanism. Governance Outputs VEEM may produce: Value Emergence Event Candidate Value Emergence Event Definition Value Emergence Event Identity Value Emergence Event Type Value Emergence Event Context Value Emergence Event Timeline Value Emergence Event Boundary Value Emergence Event-to-Value Relationship Composite Emergence Event Map Value Emergence Event Materiality Assessment Value Emergence Event Evidence Basis Value Emergence Event Uncertainty Record Value Emergence Event State Failed Emergence Event Record Reversed Emergence Event Record Governed Value Emergence Event These outputs provide the governed basis for: VEDM — Value Emergence Determination Module. Use Case 1 — Banking & Project Finance: Investment Completion vs. Value Emergence A bank finances a large industrial project. The borrower completes construction. The facility appears on the balance sheet. Equipment is installed. The project is officially declared operational. These facts may demonstrate that capital has been deployed and an asset exists. They do not automatically demonstrate that the expected value has emerged. VFM® may establish the governed value as: sustained productive capability capable of generating the defined economic output. VECM identifies the conditions. VETM establishes the emergence threshold. VEEM then identifies the actual emergence event. That event may require: Operational Activation → Successful Production → Usable Output → Commercially Relevant Delivery rather than merely: Construction Completed. The bank can therefore distinguish: Capital Expenditure → Completed Asset → Potential Value → Emergence Threshold → Emergence Event → Value Emergence Determination This gives lenders, investors, restructuring teams, and public financing bodies a governed way to detect projects where: money has been spent and assets exist, but the intended value has not yet emerged. Use Case 2 — Space Mission: Mission Activity vs. Scientific Value Emergence A space agency launches a scientific mission. The spacecraft reaches its destination. The instruments activate successfully. From a traditional project perspective, multiple major milestones have been achieved. But suppose the governed value is: usable scientific knowledge concerning a defined planetary phenomenon. Then: Launch Success ≠ Scientific Value Emergence Orbital Arrival ≠ Scientific Value Emergence Instrument Activation ≠ Scientific Value Emergence Those events create or activate the potential value source. VEEM identifies the materially relevant emergence event. The sequence may be: Instrument Activation → Observation → Data Acquisition → Successful Transmission → Ground Reception → Usable Scientific Dataset Produced Only then may the relevant occurrence proceed to VEDM for determination of whether the governed scientific value has actually emerged. This allows mission governance to distinguish: Mission Expenditure from Mission Capability from Mission Activity from Mission Value. That distinction can support mission evaluation, portfolio prioritization, continuation decisions, cost control, scientific program assessment, and comparison of alternative mission architectures. Foundational Principles Threshold satisfaction is not automatically value emergence. An operational event is not automatically a Value Emergence Event. A transaction is not automatically a Value Emergence Event. Cost incurred is not value emerged. Capital deployed is not value emerged. Asset completion is not value emerged. Capability activation is not automatically value realization. An emergence event must remain connected to the specific governed value context. A Value Emergence Event may be instantaneous, progressive, composite, conditional, failed, uncertain, or reversed. The occurrence of an event must remain distinguishable from the determination of what that event means for value existence. VEEM governs what happened at the emergence boundary; VEDM governs whether what happened establishes that value emerged. Canonical Closing Statement Value Emergence Event Module establishes the governed event layer through which threshold-satisfied potential value may transition toward existent value. By identifying and structuring the occurrence, activation, realization, interaction, outcome, or state change associated with value emergence, VEEM separates operational activity, transactions, expenditure, asset completion, capability creation, and technical activation from the materially relevant event through which the governed value may actually emerge. Through event identification, temporal localization, event boundaries, event-to-value relationships, materiality, beneficiary relationships, composite events, progressive emergence, uncertainty, failed events, reversals, and event-state governance, VEEM creates the evidentially identifiable transition required before Value Emergence Determination can occur. In doing so, VEEM prevents activity from being mistaken for value, cost from being mistaken for value creation, and technical completion from being mistaken for value realization, while establishing the governed bridge between emergence readiness and legitimate determination of value existence within VFM®.
