title: Value Recognition Criteria Module (VRCM)
text: Value Recognition Criteria Module (VRCM) Value Recognition Criteria Module (VRCM) VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria Module Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture Parent Standard: Value Recognition Standard (VRS) Module: VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria Module Operational Layer: Value Recognition Criteria Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Value Lifecycle Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value Recognition Criteria Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 24 August 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition Value Recognition Criteria Module (VRCM) is the first Core Module of the Value Recognition Standard (VRS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture. VRCM governs the explicit criteria under which already existing value may become eligible for formal recognition within a defined value governance context. The Module establishes what conditions must be satisfied before an existing value can proceed toward a governed recognition determination. Its purpose is not to determine whether value exists. Value existence has already been established through the preceding Value Emergence Standard (VES). VRCM asks the next question: What must be true for that existing value to become eligible for recognition within this specific context? This creates a controlled methodological boundary between: Existing Value → Recognition Eligibility Architectural Position VRCM operates within the fourth governed space of the VFM® lifecycle: Value Context → Value Origin → Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change → Value Development / Value Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration / Value Extinction Within Value Recognition, VRCM is the entry module. It receives an established existing value from the preceding lifecycle stage and establishes the recognition criteria against which that value can subsequently be assessed. Internal Module Flow Existing Value → VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria → VRBM — Value Recognition Basis → VRDM — Value Recognition Determination → VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation → VRRM — Value Recognition Record → Recognized Value VRCM therefore governs the rules of recognition before recognition is decided. Operational Space VRCM governs the identification, definition, structuring, applicability, and documentation of criteria used to determine whether existing value is eligible for recognition. Recognition criteria may concern: relevance; materiality; beneficiary relationship; purpose relationship; contextual applicability; usability; accessibility; capability contribution; operational contribution; economic contribution; strategic contribution; resource contribution; temporal relevance; measurable effect; attributable benefit; cost avoidance; efficiency contribution; capability preservation; future utility where the context permits it. The criteria used depend upon the value context established under the Value Context Standard (VCXS). VRCM does not impose one universal definition of valuable. It governs how the recognition criteria must be made explicit. Recognition Criteria Principle Value recognition must not occur through an undefined intuition that something is “valuable.” A recognition system must be capable of identifying the criteria under which recognition is possible. The methodological relationship is: Existing Value + Defined Recognition Context + Applicable Recognition Criteria → Recognition Eligibility Without explicit criteria, recognition becomes difficult to compare, reproduce, challenge, govern, or automate. Context-Specific Recognition Recognition criteria are context-dependent. A capability may satisfy recognition criteria for one purpose while failing them for another. For example, a proprietary dataset may have: high operational relevance but no current collateral recognition. A technological capability may have: strategic value recognition without current accounting recognition. A reduction in energy consumption may satisfy: operational efficiency recognition criteria without automatically satisfying: financial asset recognition criteria. These are not contradictions. They are different recognition contexts. VRCM makes those contexts explicit. Recognition Criteria ≠ Value Existence VRCM enforces a critical architectural distinction: Failure to satisfy recognition criteria does not establish that value does not exist. It establishes only that the value does not currently satisfy the defined criteria for recognition within the specified context. Therefore: Existing Value + Criteria Not Satisfied → Unrecognized Existing Value not: Criteria Not Satisfied → No Value This distinction protects the VFM® lifecycle from allowing external recognition systems to redefine value existence. Recognition Criteria ≠ Value Measurement Recognition criteria establish whether value may qualify for recognition. They do not necessarily quantify how much value exists. For example: Does this capability materially reduce operational resource consumption? may be a recognition criterion. Determining the magnitude of that value is a different governance question. Therefore: Recognition Eligibility ≠ Value Magnitude Recognition Criteria ≠ Market Price Market price may be relevant to a particular recognition context. It is not a universal recognition criterion. Value may exist and be recognized even where: no market exists; no transaction has occurred; no price has been established; the value is internally consumed; the value consists of avoided cost; the value represents preserved capability; the value benefits a public system rather than a buyer; the value cannot presently be exchanged. VFM® therefore does not reduce recognition to monetization. Recognition Criteria Structure A governed recognition criterion should identify, where relevant: Criterion Identity → What criterion is being applied? Recognition Context → Within what context does it apply? Value Relationship → What characteristic or effect of the existing value does it examine? Beneficiary Relationship → For whom or what is the value relevant? Threshold or Condition → What must be demonstrated? Applicability → To which value objects or situations does the criterion apply? Temporal Condition → For what period does the criterion remain relevant? Exclusions → What does the criterion explicitly not establish? This creates recognition criteria that can be interpreted independently of the person or system that originally created them. Recognition Eligibility VRCM may establish recognition eligibility states such as: Eligible The existing value satisfies the applicable criteria sufficiently to proceed toward recognition determination. Conditionally Eligible The criteria are satisfied only under explicitly defined conditions. Insufficiently Established The available basis does not yet establish whether the criteria are satisfied. Not Eligible in Context The existing value does not satisfy the applicable recognition criteria within the defined context. These are recognition-governance states. They are not statements about whether the underlying value exists. Multiple Recognition Contexts The same existing value may be assessed simultaneously against multiple recognition criteria frameworks. For example: Operational Recognition Criteria → Eligible Strategic Recognition Criteria → Eligible Financial Recognition Criteria → Conditionally Eligible Collateral Recognition Criteria → Not Eligible This enables VFM® to represent value without forcing all institutions and systems to adopt one universal recognition model. The value remains one governed value. Its recognition relationships may be multiple. Criteria Stability and Change Recognition criteria may change over time. Changes may result from: organizational priorities; technology; operational conditions; available capabilities; resource scarcity; market conditions; institutional requirements; new knowledge; beneficiary needs; environmental conditions. VRCM requires material criteria changes to remain distinguishable from changes in the underlying value. Therefore: Recognition Criteria Change ≠ Value Change A value may remain unchanged while its eligibility for recognition changes. Machine-Readable Recognition Explicit recognition criteria create an important foundation for machine-readable value governance. A machine-readable implementation may represent: Value ID → Recognition Context ID → Criterion Set → Criterion Conditions → Eligibility State → Recognition Basis → Recognition Determination This can allow different systems to determine not merely whether something has been labelled valuable, but why it is eligible for recognition within a particular context. Boundary with Value Emergence The Value Emergence Standard (VES) determines when potential value becomes existent value. VRCM begins only after value existence has been established. Therefore: VES: Does the value exist? VRCM: What criteria must that existing value satisfy to become eligible for recognition here? Emergence ≠ Recognition Eligibility Boundary with Value Recognition Basis VRCM establishes the criteria that must be satisfied. VRBM — Value Recognition Basis Module governs the basis used to demonstrate or support satisfaction of those criteria. Therefore: Criteria → What must be demonstrated Basis → What supports the assessment This separation prevents criteria from being silently rewritten according to whatever information happens to be available. Boundary with Value Recognition Determination VRCM does not issue the final recognition determination. It establishes the criteria against which that determination will later be made. VRDM — Value Recognition Determination Module governs the actual determination. Therefore: Criteria ≠ Determination Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum VRCM implementation should establish: 1. Existing Value Reference Identify the existing value entering recognition governance. 2. Recognition Context Define the context within which recognition is being considered. 3. Recognition Purpose Identify why recognition is required. 4. Applicable Criteria Define the criteria that must be satisfied. 5. Criterion Meaning Specify what each criterion actually tests. 6. Applicability Conditions Define where each criterion applies. 7. Thresholds or Conditions Establish any relevant threshold, condition, or qualifying requirement. 8. Exclusions Identify what satisfying the criterion does not establish. 9. Eligibility Assessment Determine whether the value is eligible to proceed through the recognition process. 10. Criteria Record Preserve the applicable criteria and eligibility state for downstream recognition governance. Governance Outputs VRCM may produce: Value Recognition Criteria Set Recognition Context Record Recognition Purpose Statement Recognition Criterion Record Recognition Applicability Record Recognition Threshold Record Recognition Exclusion Record Recognition Eligibility Assessment Recognition Eligibility State Value Recognition Criteria Record These outputs provide the governed input for VRBM — Value Recognition Basis Module. Use Case 1 — Banking and Enterprise Capability A bank evaluates a technology company containing significant operational capabilities, proprietary datasets, specialized systems, intellectual resources, and internal infrastructure. Some of these resources may generate existing value even though conventional accounting or collateral systems do not recognize them in the same manner. VRCM allows the bank to establish explicit criteria for a particular analytical context. For strategic enterprise assessment, the criteria might examine whether a capability: materially contributes to revenue generation; reduces operating cost; creates defensible capability; can continue producing benefit; contributes materially to future operations. A capability may satisfy those criteria and become: Eligible for Strategic Value Recognition without automatically becoming: Recognized Accounting Asset or: Eligible Collateral. The bank can therefore govern multiple forms of recognition without confusing them with one another. Use Case 2 — Space Mission Resource Optimization A space organization introduces a mission-planning capability that reduces fuel requirements, simulation workload, engineering time, hardware testing, or mission risk. The organization wants to determine whether these effects should be recognized as value within its mission-efficiency framework. VRCM can define criteria such as: measurable resource reduction; preserved mission capability; avoided operational expenditure; increased mission capacity; reduced engineering workload; improved resource utilization. If the existing benefit satisfies the criteria, it may proceed as: Eligible Mission-Efficiency Value for formal recognition. This does not determine its market price, accounting treatment, or tax consequence. It establishes that the existing value meets the defined criteria for recognition within the mission context. Enterprise Application VRCM enables organizations to replace implicit value recognition with explicit recognition logic. This can support banking, investment, government, infrastructure, industrial operations, AI systems, energy systems, scientific programs, public administration, digital ecosystems, and resource optimization. Its deeper importance is methodological. Two organizations may disagree about whether they recognize the same value. With VRCM, that disagreement can be decomposed into: different contexts → different criteria → different eligibility outcomes rather than being reduced to an undefined disagreement over whether something “has value.” That makes value recognition more transparent, comparable, auditable, interoperable, and machine-readable. Foundational Principles Value recognition requires explicit criteria. Recognition criteria do not create value. Failure to satisfy recognition criteria does not prove absence of value. Recognition criteria are context-specific, not universally absolute. Recognition eligibility is not value magnitude. Market price is not a universal recognition criterion. Different recognition contexts may legitimately produce different recognition outcomes for the same existing value. A change in recognition criteria does not necessarily represent a change in value. Canonical Closing Statement Value Recognition Criteria Module establishes the first governed control point within the Value Recognition Standard by defining the explicit criteria under which already existing value may become eligible for recognition within a specified context. By separating value existence from recognition eligibility, recognition criteria from recognition basis, and recognition eligibility from final recognition determination, VRCM prevents institutional, financial, market, technological, or organizational recognition systems from silently becoming definitions of value itself. It enables recognition decisions to become explicit, contextual, comparable, traceable, interoperable, and machine-readable while preserving the foundational VFM® distinction that value may exist independently of whether any particular system chooses or is able to recognize it. title: Value Recognition Determination Module (VRDM)
text: Value Recognition Determination Module (VRDM) Value Recognition Determination Module (VRDM) VRDM — Value Recognition Determination Module Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture Parent Standard: Value Recognition Standard (VRS) Module: VRDM — Value Recognition Determination Module Operational Layer: Value Recognition Determination Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Value Lifecycle Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value Recognition Determination Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 24 August 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition Value Recognition Determination Module (VRDM) is the third Core Module of the Value Recognition Standard (VRS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture. VRDM governs the formal determination of whether existing value is recognized within a defined value context by applying the recognition criteria established through VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria Module to the recognition basis established through VRBM — Value Recognition Basis Module. Its purpose is to transform an established recognition basis into an explicit, reproducible, bounded, and governable recognition outcome. VRDM does not determine whether value originally existed. It does not create value. It does not determine market price, ownership, legality, accounting treatment, taxation, validation status, or universal acceptance. Its function is precise: to determine whether existing value qualifies for recognition within the defined recognition context. The governing relationship is: Existing Value + Recognition Context + Recognition Criteria + Recognition Basis → Value Recognition Determination Architectural Position VRDM operates within the fourth governed space of the VFM® lifecycle: Value Context → Value Origin → Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change → Value Development / Value Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration / Value Extinction Within the Value Recognition Standard, VRDM occupies the decision point between the recognition basis and the limitations attached to the resulting recognition. Internal Module Flow Existing Value → VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria → VRBM — Value Recognition Basis → VRDM — Value Recognition Determination → VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation → VRRM — Value Recognition Record → Recognized Value VRDM therefore answers the decisive question in the internal recognition flow: Given these criteria and this basis, what recognition outcome legitimately follows? Operational Space VRDM governs: recognition determination initiation; recognition context confirmation; criterion applicability confirmation; recognition basis consideration; criterion-to-basis assessment; supporting basis treatment; contradictory basis treatment; conditional recognition; partial recognition; non-recognition; indeterminate recognition; recognition determination reasoning; recognition state assignment; determination consistency; determination reproducibility; determination uncertainty; determination conditions; determination review triggers; machine-readable recognition outcomes. The Module converts recognition analysis into a governed determination. Recognition Determination Principle Recognition must not arise merely because an institution, organization, model, analyst, or automated system labels something valuable. A governed recognition determination requires an identifiable methodological chain: Defined Value → Defined Recognition Context → Applicable Recognition Criteria → Applicable Recognition Basis → Recognition Assessment → Recognition Determination This makes the outcome reconstructable. A downstream user should be able to determine not merely: “This value was recognized.” but: “This value was recognized under these criteria, on this basis, within this context, subject to these conditions.” Determination ≠ Value Creation VRDM enforces one of the most important boundaries in VFM®: Recognition does not create the underlying value. Value must already exist before it enters the Value Recognition Standard. Therefore: Existing Value → Recognition not: Recognition → Value Existence An institution may recognize value that already exists. It may fail to recognize value that already exists. It may change its recognition determination without changing the underlying value. This prevents institutional recognition systems from silently becoming definitions of value itself. Determination ≠ Universal Recognition A VRDM determination applies only within its defined recognition context. Therefore: Recognized in Context A ≠ Universally Recognized For example, a capability may be: Recognized as Operational Value while remaining: Not Recognized as Accounting Value Not Recognized as Collateral Value and Conditionally Recognized as Strategic Value. These outcomes may coexist without contradiction. They describe different recognition relationships to the same existing value. Criterion-to-Basis Determination VRDM requires each material recognition criterion to be considered against the relevant recognition basis. The determination chain may be represented as: Criterion A → Basis A → Assessment A Criterion B → Basis B → Assessment B Criterion C → Basis C → Assessment C ↓ Combined Recognition Determination This prevents recognition from being based upon a general impression when explicit criteria have already been established. Supporting and Contradictory Basis VRDM must consider materially relevant basis that: supports recognition; weakens recognition; contradicts recognition; conditions recognition; limits recognition; leaves recognition unresolved. A recognition determination that considers only favorable basis is methodologically incomplete. Therefore: Recognition Determination ≠ Selection of Supporting Information VRDM requires material conflicts identified by VRBM to remain visible in the determination. Recognition Determination States VRDM may establish a minimum canonical state model. 1. Recognized The applicable criteria are sufficiently satisfied by the governed recognition basis within the defined context. 2. Conditionally Recognized Recognition is legitimate only where explicitly defined conditions remain satisfied. 3. Partially Recognized Only a defined portion, dimension, capability, benefit, period, application, or value relationship satisfies the applicable recognition requirements. 4. Not Recognized The applicable criteria are not sufficiently satisfied within the defined recognition context. 5. Indeterminate The available basis does not permit a sufficiently supported recognition or non-recognition determination. 6. Recognition Suspended A previous recognition determination cannot presently be relied upon because a material change, unresolved contradiction, missing basis, or review condition requires reassessment. These are recognition states, not value-existence states. Non-Recognition Principle VRDM makes a critical distinction: Not Recognized ≠ No Value Non-recognition means: the existing value does not currently satisfy the applicable recognition requirements within this defined context. It does not establish: the value does not exist. This distinction is particularly important where conventional systems recognize only a limited subset of value. A technological capability, avoided cost, operational advantage, public benefit, strategic resource, unused capacity, or future-use capability may exist as value even where a specific institutional recognition framework does not recognize it. Indeterminate Recognition VRDM must permit an indeterminate outcome. Without an indeterminate state, recognition systems may be forced into false binary conclusions: Recognized / Not Recognized even where the available basis is insufficient. An indeterminate state allows the system to state: the recognition question remains unresolved on the current basis. This is methodologically stronger than manufacturing certainty where none exists. Conditional Recognition Recognition may depend upon conditions. Examples include: continued availability of a capability; continued beneficiary relevance; defined operating conditions; specified technological configuration; defined market conditions; continued resource scarcity; maintained performance; temporal validity; defined regulatory context; continued accessibility. VRDM must preserve those conditions within the recognition determination. If a condition disappears, the recognition determination may require reassessment. Partial Recognition Some value objects may contain multiple value dimensions. A single object may provide: operational value; strategic value; financial value; technological value; resource value; public value; future-use value. VRDM may therefore recognize one value dimension without recognizing another. Similarly, only part of a claimed value may be sufficiently supported. This permits: Partial Recognition without forcing the entire value claim into one binary state. Recognition Across Multiple Beneficiaries Value may be recognized differently depending upon the beneficiary established through the Value Context Standard (VCXS). For example, the same infrastructure may create: Value for Operator Value for Customer Value for Government Value for Community Value for Future Users The recognition determination must remain linked to the relevant beneficiary where beneficiary identity materially affects recognition. Therefore: Recognition for Beneficiary A ≠ Recognition for Beneficiary B unless the applicable basis supports both. Temporal Recognition Recognition exists in time. A value recognized today may not remain recognizable indefinitely. Recognition may change because: the beneficiary changes; the purpose changes; the capability becomes obsolete; technology advances; resources become more or less scarce; operating conditions change; the recognition basis changes; recognition criteria change; the underlying value changes. VRDM therefore requires recognition determinations to support temporal applicability and reassessment. Recognition Change ≠ Value Change A recognition determination may change even when the underlying value remains unchanged. For example: Year 1: value exists but is not institutionally recognized. Year 2: recognition criteria expand. Year 3: the same existing value becomes recognized. The value itself may not have changed. The recognition relationship changed. Therefore: Recognition State Change ≠ Value State Change This distinction becomes essential when VFM® is used across institutional, economic, technological, governmental, or accounting systems. Recognition Determination ≠ Valuation VRDM determines whether value is recognized. It does not determine the magnitude of that value. Therefore: Recognized Value ≠ Valued Amount A determination such as: Recognized as Operational Value does not itself establish: CHF 10 million of value. Valuation or value magnitude may require separate methodology. VRDM protects the architecture from collapsing recognition into pricing. Recognition Determination ≠ Accounting Recognition Accounting systems may use recognition rules appropriate to financial reporting. VRDM is broader. It may govern recognition of value in contexts including: operations; strategy; infrastructure; public systems; science; technology; resource efficiency; resilience; capability; investment analysis; mission planning; digital systems. Accounting recognition may therefore be one external recognition context. It is not the universal definition of VFM® value recognition. Recognition Determination ≠ Market Acceptance A market may recognize value through demand, exchange, pricing, or liquidity. But value recognition under VFM® does not depend upon the existence of a market. A value may be recognized where: it is internally consumed; it avoids cost; it preserves capability; it reduces resource use; it increases resilience; it creates strategic optionality; it benefits a public system; it cannot be transferred; no market currently exists. Therefore: No Market ≠ No Recognizable Value Recognition Determination ≠ Legal or Tax Determination VRDM does not determine whether recognized value: constitutes property; creates ownership rights; is legally enforceable; is taxable; creates taxable income; creates a taxable event; qualifies as a regulated asset; may be transferred; may be used as collateral. Those questions belong to their relevant legal, tax, governance, or external architectural systems. VFM® governs the value lifecycle. Determination Reproducibility A governed recognition determination should be capable of reconstruction. A reviewer should be able to identify: Value Reference → Recognition Context → Recognition Criteria → Recognition Basis → Criterion Assessments → Material Conflicts → Conditions → Recognition Determination This does not require every evaluator to reach the same conclusion under every methodology. It requires the reasoning pathway to be explicit enough to understand how the determination was reached. Determination Consistency Where materially equivalent value contexts, criteria, and bases are assessed differently, the difference should be identifiable. VRDM therefore supports consistency analysis across recognition determinations. This can expose: inconsistent institutional recognition; undocumented exceptions; criteria drift; arbitrary recognition; algorithmic inconsistency; human decision inconsistency; changes in recognition policy. Consistency does not require identical outcomes where material facts differ. It requires differences to have an identifiable basis. Human and Machine Determination VRDM may support recognition determinations performed by: humans; committees; institutions; AI systems; automated rules; hybrid human-machine processes. The governance requirement remains the same: the determination must remain connected to the governed criteria, basis, context, conditions, and outcome. An AI-generated recognition decision does not become governed merely because it is computationally produced. Machine-Readable Recognition Determination A machine-readable VRDM implementation may represent: Value ID → Recognition Context ID → Beneficiary ID / Reference → Criterion Set ID → Recognition Basis ID → Criterion Assessment States → Conflict State → Recognition Conditions → Recognition Determination State → Temporal Applicability → VRLM Limitation Interface → VRRM Record Interface This allows recognition determinations to become portable across systems without reducing them to a binary label. Recognition Review Triggers A recognition determination may require review where there is material change to: value context; beneficiary; purpose; recognition criteria; recognition basis; underlying capability; resource conditions; technological conditions; operational conditions; temporal relevance; material contradictory information. Review does not automatically change recognition. It reopens the determination where its existing basis may no longer be sufficient. Boundary with VRCM VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria Module determines: What must be satisfied for recognition? VRDM determines: Given the applicable criteria and basis, what recognition outcome follows? Therefore: Criteria ≠ Determination Boundary with VRBM VRBM — Value Recognition Basis Module establishes: What supports the recognition assessment? VRDM evaluates that basis against the applicable criteria. Therefore: Basis ≠ Determination The same basis may produce different legitimate determinations under different recognition contexts or criteria. Boundary with VRLM VRDM determines the recognition outcome. VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation Module subsequently determines the limitations, boundaries, exclusions, and conditions governing how that recognition may legitimately be interpreted or used. Therefore: Recognition Determination ≠ Unlimited Recognition Boundary with VRRM VRDM produces the recognition determination. VRRM — Value Recognition Record Module preserves the recognition outcome and its governed basis as a durable recognition record. Therefore: Determination ≠ Record Boundary with Value State Standard Recognition is not itself the complete state of value. The subsequent Value State Standard (VSS) governs the state of the value within the broader VFM® lifecycle. VRDM must therefore not collapse: Recognition State into: Value State A value can be recognized while later becoming degraded, nullified, restored, or extinct. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum VRDM implementation should establish: 1. Value Reference Identify the existing value subject to recognition determination. 2. Recognition Context Confirmation Confirm the context, beneficiary, and purpose within which recognition is being determined. 3. Applicable Criteria Receive the applicable recognition criteria from VRCM. 4. Recognition Basis Receive the governed recognition basis from VRBM. 5. Criterion Assessment Assess each material criterion against the relevant basis. 6. Conflict Assessment Consider materially supporting, contradictory, conditional, and limiting basis. 7. Recognition Determination Determine the legitimate recognition outcome. 8. Recognition State Assignment Assign the appropriate recognition state. 9. Conditions and Temporal Applicability Identify conditions and temporal boundaries affecting the determination. 10. Determination Basis Preserve the reasoning necessary for VRLM and VRRM to govern the resulting recognition. Governance Outputs VRDM may produce: Value Recognition Determination Recognition Determination State Criterion Assessment Record Recognition Context Confirmation Recognition Beneficiary Relationship Recognition Conflict Assessment Conditional Recognition Statement Partial Recognition Statement Non-Recognition Determination Indeterminate Recognition Determination Recognition Suspension State Recognition Temporal Applicability Recognition Review Trigger Recognition Determination Basis These outputs provide the governed input for VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation Module. Use Case 1 — Banking: Recognition Beyond the Balance Sheet A bank evaluates a technology company possessing proprietary software, operational datasets, automation capabilities, specialized processes, and internal technological infrastructure. The relevant value has already emerged. VRCM establishes criteria for strategic enterprise value recognition. VRBM establishes basis including: recurring cost reductions; production improvements; customer retention effects; demonstrated internal dependence; measurable productivity gains; technological capability. VRDM applies the criteria to that basis. The outcome might be: Strategic Value → Recognized Operational Value → Recognized Future Capability Value → Conditionally Recognized Collateral Value → Not Determined within this recognition context The bank has not magically converted software into collateral. It has done something methodologically different: it has established which forms of existing value can legitimately be recognized for the defined analytical purpose. This enables richer enterprise assessment without confusing strategic recognition with accounting, legal, or collateral status. Use Case 2 — Space Mission: Recognition of Avoided Resource Consumption A space organization deploys a mission-optimization capability. The capability does not create a new physical asset. Instead, it reduces: engineering hours; simulation executions; physical testing; fuel requirements; hardware consumption; mission preparation time. The value already exists through these resource effects. VRCM establishes criteria for Mission Resource Efficiency Value. VRBM provides the basis: 8,000 engineering hours avoided 35% reduction in computational workload two physical testing campaigns avoided measurable fuel requirement reduction VRDM determines whether those effects satisfy the recognition criteria. The result may be: Mission Resource Efficiency Value → Recognized with specified conditions concerning mission configuration, measurement period, and comparison baseline. This demonstrates an important VFM® capability: value can be formally recognized even where its manifestation is not a new asset or new revenue, but resources that no longer need to be consumed. Enterprise Application VRDM gives organizations a controlled mechanism for transforming value-related information into explicit recognition determinations. It can support banking, investment, government, public finance, enterprise management, infrastructure, technology, AI, energy, manufacturing, scientific programs, resource optimization, mission planning, and other environments where organizations need to distinguish: value that exists from value that a particular system recognizes. This distinction becomes especially powerful where conventional systems recognize only narrow forms of value. VRDM enables multiple recognition contexts to coexist without forcing operational, strategic, financial, social, technological, resource, and other forms of value into one universal recognition model. Foundational Principles Recognition does not create value. Value may exist before recognition. Recognition must be based on explicit criteria and an identifiable basis. Recognition is contextual, not automatically universal. Not recognized does not mean no value exists. Indeterminate recognition is legitimate where the basis does not support certainty. Recognition state is not value state. Recognition determination is not valuation. Recognition determination is not accounting treatment. Recognition determination is not market acceptance. Recognition determination is not legal or tax determination. The same existing value may legitimately have different recognition outcomes in different contexts. A governed recognition determination must be reconstructable from the context, criteria, basis, assessment, and resulting recognition state. Canonical Closing Statement **Value Recognition Determination Module establishes the decision layer of the Value Recognition Standard by converting explicit recognition criteria and governed recognition basis into a formal, contextual, conditional, reproducible, and machine-readable recognition outcome. Through governance of criterion assessment, supporting and contradictory basis, recognition states, conditional and partial recognition, non-recognition, indeterminate outcomes, temporal applicability, beneficiary relationships, consistency, review triggers, and determination traceability, VRDM prevents institutional recognition from being confused with value existence itself. By separating recognition determination from value creation, valuation, accounting treatment, market acceptance, legal status, taxation, value state, and downstream recognition limitations, VRDM enables organizations and intelligent systems to state not merely that value is recognized, but precisely what value is recognized, for whom, within what context, against what criteria, on what basis, under what conditions, and with what determination outcome. title: Value Recognition Limitation Module (VRLM)
text: Value Recognition Limitation Module (VRLM) Value Recognition Limitation Module (VRLM) VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation Module Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture Parent Standard: Value Recognition Standard (VRS) Module: VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation Module Operational Layer: Value Recognition Limitation Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Value Lifecycle Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value Recognition Limitation Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 24 August 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition Value Recognition Limitation Module (VRLM) is the fourth Core Module of the Value Recognition Standard (VRS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture. VRLM governs the explicit boundaries, conditions, exclusions, restrictions, dependencies, uncertainties, temporal limits, beneficiary limits, contextual limits, and prohibited interpretations attached to a Value Recognition Determination. Its purpose is to prevent legitimate recognition within one defined context from being silently expanded into recognition that the underlying determination does not support. VRLM does not determine whether value exists. It does not establish recognition criteria, create the recognition basis, or issue the recognition determination. Its function begins after a recognition outcome has been established through VRDM — Value Recognition Determination Module. Its governing function is: to determine what the recognition determination does not establish, where its legitimate meaning ends, and under what conditions it remains applicable. The governing relationship is: Recognition Determination → Recognition Boundary → Recognition Conditions → Recognition Limitations → Bounded Recognition Architectural Position VRLM operates within the fourth governed space of the VFM® lifecycle: Value Context → Value Origin → Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change → Value Development / Value Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration / Value Extinction Within the Value Recognition Standard, VRLM follows the recognition determination and precedes the formal recognition record. Internal Module Flow Existing Value → VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria → VRBM — Value Recognition Basis → VRDM — Value Recognition Determination → VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation → VRRM — Value Recognition Record → Bounded and Recorded Recognized Value The internal logic is: What must be satisfied → what supports the assessment → what recognition outcome follows → where that recognition applies and stops → how the complete recognition is recorded VRLM therefore establishes the boundary between: legitimate recognition and unsupported recognition expansion. Operational Space VRLM governs limitations affecting the legitimate interpretation and downstream use of recognition. These may include: recognition-context limitations; beneficiary limitations; purpose limitations; value-dimension limitations; object limitations; capability limitations; geographic limitations; temporal limitations; operational limitations; technological limitations; dependency limitations; assumption limitations; measurement limitations; evidence limitations; uncertainty limitations; comparability limitations; transfer limitations; institutional limitations; downstream-use limitations; prohibited recognition interpretations. The objective is not to weaken recognition. It is to preserve its legitimate meaning. Recognition Limitation Principle Every recognition determination exists within a boundary. If the determination establishes: “Value X is recognized within Context A for Beneficiary B and Purpose C.” VRLM prevents that statement from silently becoming: “Value X is universally recognized for every beneficiary and every purpose.” Therefore: Recognition ≠ Unlimited Recognition and: Recognition Expansion Requires a Governed Basis Limitation ≠ Non-Recognition A limitation does not mean that value is not recognized. For example: Recognized only for operational efficiency is still a legitimate recognition determination. The limitation merely prevents the recognition from being interpreted as: financial recognition; collateral recognition; accounting recognition; market recognition; legal recognition; tax recognition; universal recognition. Therefore: Bounded Recognition ≠ Weak Recognition A narrow recognition determination may be extremely strong within its legitimate context. Context Limitation Recognition must remain attached to the value context established through the Value Context Standard (VCXS). A recognition determination made within: industrial operational efficiency cannot automatically be transferred into: financial reporting or: taxable economic value. The underlying value may remain the same. The recognition context has changed. A new recognition context may therefore require a new recognition assessment. Beneficiary Limitation Value recognized for one beneficiary may not automatically be recognized for another. For example, a technological system may create substantial value for: the operator while creating limited value for: the customer and potentially negative value for: another affected party. VRLM requires beneficiary boundaries to remain visible where they materially affect recognition. Therefore: Recognition for Beneficiary A ≠ Recognition for Beneficiary B Purpose Limitation Recognition may be valid only for a defined purpose. Examples include: investment analysis; operational planning; strategic assessment; resource allocation; infrastructure planning; technological capability assessment; public-policy analysis; cost optimization; mission planning. Recognition for one purpose does not automatically authorize reliance for another. Value-Dimension Limitation The same underlying value may possess several dimensions. For example: Operational Value Strategic Value Technological Value Financial Value Resource Value Public Value Resilience Value VRLM ensures that recognition of one dimension does not silently establish recognition of all dimensions. Therefore: Recognized Operational Value ≠ Recognized Financial Value unless a separate governed basis establishes that relationship. Object and Capability Limitation Recognition may apply only to a defined object, configuration, capability, version, system, facility, process, technology, resource, or organizational unit. Recognition attached to: Technology Configuration V4 must not automatically be transferred to: Technology Configuration V7 where material changes affect the recognition basis. Similarly, recognition of one capability within a system does not automatically recognize every capability of the system. Temporal Limitation Recognition is not automatically permanent. A recognition determination may remain legitimate only: during a defined period; while specific conditions remain satisfied; while the capability remains operational; while the beneficiary relationship exists; while the recognition basis remains current; until material change occurs; until a defined review date; while external conditions remain materially equivalent. VRLM therefore allows recognition to carry: Temporal Applicability rather than assuming perpetual recognition. Geographic and Jurisdictional Limitation Recognition may depend upon geography or institutional environment. A value recognized within: Region A may not automatically satisfy the recognition requirements of: Region B. Similarly, an institutional recognition determination in one jurisdiction does not automatically create equivalent legal, accounting, regulatory, or tax recognition elsewhere. VRLM preserves this distinction without attempting to govern those external systems. Operational Limitation Recognition may depend upon specific operating conditions. For example, an optimization system may create recognized value only where: production exceeds a certain scale; specific infrastructure exists; particular resources are constrained; required data is available; defined process conditions exist; system integration remains functional. Outside those conditions, the recognition basis may weaken or disappear. Dependency Limitation Recognized value may depend upon another capability, system, resource, infrastructure, relationship, right, dataset, workforce, technology, or condition. VRLM requires material dependencies to remain visible. For example: AI capability value may depend upon: access to proprietary operational data. If access disappears, the recognized value may require reassessment. Therefore: Recognized Value + Critical Dependency ≠ Independently Sustainable Value Assumption Limitation Some recognition determinations rely upon assumptions. These may concern: future demand; resource availability; technological continuity; user behavior; cost structures; operational conditions; market conditions; expected utilization; policy continuity. VRLM requires material assumptions to remain attached to the recognition determination where recognition would materially change if the assumptions fail. Measurement Limitation A recognition determination may rely upon measured effects whose measurement itself is bounded. For example: 18% operating-cost reduction may apply only to: one facility; one production period; one product line; one baseline; one operating configuration. VRLM prevents that measurement from silently becoming evidence of: 18% enterprise-wide permanent cost reduction. Uncertainty Limitation Recognition can remain legitimate even where uncertainty exists. VRLM therefore does not require uncertainty to eliminate recognition. Instead, it requires material uncertainty to constrain the interpretation of recognition where necessary. For example: Strategic Value → Recognized may coexist with: Magnitude uncertain or: Future persistence uncertain. This preserves useful recognition without manufacturing false certainty. Transfer Limitation A recognition determination may not automatically transfer when value moves between: entities; beneficiaries; systems; organizations; environments; jurisdictions; technologies; ownership structures; operating contexts. Transfer of the underlying object does not necessarily transfer the same recognition relationship. Therefore: Value Transfer ≠ Recognition Transfer A new recognition context may require reassessment. Institutional Limitation One institution's recognition does not automatically bind another institution. For example: Company Recognition does not automatically establish: Bank Recognition which does not automatically establish: Accounting Recognition which does not automatically establish: Tax Recognition which does not automatically establish: Regulatory Recognition. These systems may rely upon different criteria and purposes. VRLM preserves those institutional boundaries. Recognition Limitation ≠ Legal Restriction VRLM uses the term limitation methodologically. A Value Recognition Limitation is not automatically: a legal prohibition; regulatory restriction; contractual restriction; ownership restriction; tax limitation. It defines the boundary of the VFM® recognition determination. External legal consequences must be established through the relevant system. Recognition Limitation ≠ Value Limitation VRLM limits the meaning of the recognition determination, not necessarily the underlying value. This distinction is fundamental. For example: Recognition limited to operational use does not establish: the value itself exists only operationally. Other recognition contexts may later identify additional dimensions of the same value. Therefore: Recognition Boundary ≠ Value Boundary Unsupported Recognition Expansion VRLM identifies Unsupported Recognition Expansion where recognition is extended beyond its governed basis. Examples include: Operational Value Recognized → presented as Financial Value Established Strategic Capability Recognized → presented as Market Price Established Cost Avoidance Recognized → presented as Revenue Generated Public Value Recognized → presented as Taxable Value Established Technological Value Recognized → presented as Collateral Eligibility Established Future Capability Recognized → presented as Realized Economic Benefit These transformations may eventually be legitimate. But they require their own governed basis. They cannot be assumed. Recognition Boundary Statement VRLM may produce an explicit Recognition Boundary Statement. A minimum structure may identify: Recognized Value → Recognition Context → Recognized Dimension → Beneficiary → Purpose → Applicable Conditions → Material Dependencies → Temporal Applicability → Exclusions → Unsupported Interpretations This makes the recognition determination portable without detaching it from its legitimate boundary. Recognition Limitation States VRLM may classify recognition limitations using states such as: 1. Unrestricted Within Defined Context No additional material limitation has been identified beyond the established recognition context. 2. Conditionally Limited Recognition remains legitimate only while specified conditions remain satisfied. 3. Scope-Limited Recognition applies only to a defined object, capability, value dimension, beneficiary, purpose, or operational space. 4. Temporally Limited Recognition applies only within a defined period or until a defined trigger occurs. 5. Dependency-Limited Recognition materially depends upon another identified capability, resource, relationship, system, or condition. 6. Uncertainty-Limited Recognition remains legitimate, but material uncertainty constrains its interpretation or downstream use. 7. Transfer-Limited Recognition cannot automatically be transferred to another context, entity, beneficiary, system, or jurisdiction. Multiple limitation states may apply simultaneously. Limitation Combination A recognition determination may carry several limitations at once. For example: Recognized Strategic Value may be: Scope-Limited + Dependency-Limited + Temporally Limited + Transfer-Limited This is not a contradiction. It is a more precise representation of the recognition relationship. Limitation Persistence Principle Material recognition limitations must remain attached to the recognition determination when it is: recorded; transferred; aggregated; reported; analyzed; reused; exported; consumed by AI; used in another decision process; supplied to another organization. A limitation that disappears when the recognition result moves downstream no longer functions as a governance control. Therefore: Recognition + Detached Limitation = Distorted Recognition Machine-Readable Recognition Limitation A machine-readable VRLM implementation may represent: Recognition Determination ID → Value ID → Recognition Context ID → Beneficiary Reference → Recognized Dimension → Purpose → Limitation Type → Limitation Condition → Dependency Reference → Temporal Boundary → Excluded Interpretation → Transfer Condition → Review Trigger → VRRM Record Interface This enables AI and automated systems to consume not merely: “Recognized = Yes” but: “Recognized = Yes, within these explicit boundaries.” Recognition Limitation Review A limitation may require review when: the recognition context changes; the beneficiary changes; the purpose changes; a dependency disappears; a dependency becomes stronger; uncertainty decreases; uncertainty increases; new evidence becomes available; operating conditions change; technology changes; a temporal boundary expires; the underlying value changes. A review may: preserve the limitation; narrow it; expand legitimate recognition; remove it; add new limitations; trigger a new recognition determination. Boundary with VRCM VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria Module determines the criteria required for recognition. VRLM does not modify those criteria after determination. It governs the boundaries attached to the resulting recognition. Boundary with VRBM VRBM — Value Recognition Basis Module establishes the basis supporting recognition. VRLM may use limitations identified in that basis but does not recreate the recognition basis. Boundary with VRDM VRDM — Value Recognition Determination Module determines: whether and how the value is recognized. VRLM determines: where that recognition applies, what constrains it, and where its legitimate interpretation ends. Therefore: Recognition Determination ≠ Recognition Boundary Boundary with VRRM VRLM produces the limitations that must accompany the recognition determination. VRRM — Value Recognition Record Module preserves the complete recognition record. Therefore: Recognition Limitation → Recognition Record Input The limitation must not disappear when the recognition is recorded. Boundary with Value State Standard VRLM does not determine the broader lifecycle state of the underlying value. A recognition limitation may change without the underlying value state changing. Likewise, the value may later develop, degrade, become nullified, or be restored without that lifecycle transition being governed by VRLM. Boundary with VALIDOS® VRLM does not determine whether evidence or a recognition claim has been formally validated. Where validation of a recognition claim is required, VALIDOS® may govern that validation process. VRLM governs the legitimate boundary of the recognition determination itself. Boundary with AGA™ VRLM does not determine who is accountable for making, accepting, communicating, or relying upon a recognition determination. Where accountability is required, AGA™ may govern those relationships. VRLM governs what the recognition means and where that meaning stops. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum VRLM implementation should establish: 1. Recognition Determination Input Receive the recognition determination from VRDM. 2. Context Boundary Identify the recognition context within which the determination applies. 3. Beneficiary and Purpose Boundary Identify who benefits and for what recognition purpose. 4. Scope Boundary Define applicable value dimensions, objects, capabilities, systems, configurations, or operating spaces. 5. Condition and Dependency Assessment Identify conditions and dependencies necessary for recognition to remain legitimate. 6. Temporal Boundary Determine temporal applicability and relevant expiration or review triggers. 7. Uncertainty and Measurement Limits Preserve material uncertainty and measurement limitations affecting interpretation. 8. Excluded Interpretations Identify conclusions that the recognition determination does not establish. 9. Transfer Conditions Determine whether and how recognition may legitimately transfer into another context. 10. Recognition Limitation Record Create the governed limitation package for VRRM. Governance Outputs VRLM may produce: Value Recognition Boundary Statement Value Recognition Limitation Record Recognition Context Limitation Recognition Beneficiary Limitation Recognition Purpose Limitation Recognition Scope Limitation Recognition Dimension Limitation Recognition Dependency Record Recognition Temporal Limitation Recognition Uncertainty Limitation Recognition Transfer Limitation Recognition Exclusion Statement Unsupported Recognition Expansion Record Recognition Review Trigger Bounded Recognition Object These outputs provide the governed input for VRRM — Value Recognition Record Module. Use Case 1 — Banking: Preventing Strategic Value from Becoming Unsupported Collateral Value A bank evaluates a technology company. VRDM determines that the company's proprietary optimization platform has: Recognized Operational Value and: Recognized Strategic Value. The recognition basis includes measurable productivity improvement, recurring cost avoidance, deployment across multiple facilities, and dependence of critical operations upon the platform. Without VRLM, that determination could later be simplified into: “The platform is recognized as valuable.” and subsequently interpreted as: “The platform therefore has established collateral value.” VRLM prevents that jump. It may establish: Recognition Context: enterprise assessment Recognized Dimensions: operational and strategic value Beneficiary: operating company Purpose: enterprise capability assessment Limitation: collateral eligibility not determined Limitation: market price not established Limitation: accounting recognition not established Dependency: continued operational integration and access to required data The bank can therefore use the recognition legitimately without confusing: recognized enterprise value with: bankable collateral value. This allows broader forms of value to enter banking analysis while preserving the boundaries necessary for financial discipline. Use Case 2 — Space Mission: Recognized Resource Value Without False Universalization A space organization recognizes substantial value from a mission-optimization capability. VRDM determines: Mission Resource Efficiency Value → Recognized because the capability reduces engineering hours, simulation workload, physical testing, mission preparation time, and projected resource consumption. VRLM then establishes that the recognition applies only to: defined mission architecture → specified mission configuration → governed comparison baseline → defined simulation and engineering environment → specified resource categories → current mission-planning period It also records: fuel reduction is configuration-dependent engineering-hour savings are baseline-dependent future missions require reassessment avoided resource consumption does not automatically constitute financial revenue The organization therefore preserves the genuine value of resource reduction without transforming it into claims the recognition basis never established. This is particularly important for mission, scientific, infrastructure, and public-sector environments where significant value may exist outside conventional revenue-based measurement. Enterprise Application VRLM enables organizations to use broader concepts of value without allowing those concepts to become methodologically uncontrolled. This is particularly important for VFM® because the architecture may recognize forms of value that conventional systems treat separately or fail to represent adequately. These may include: avoided cost; preserved capability; resource efficiency; strategic optionality; technological capability; resilience; unused productive capacity; public benefit; future-use capability; infrastructure value; knowledge value. The broader the recognition system becomes, the more important recognition boundaries become. VRLM provides that control. It allows organizations to say: “Yes, this value is recognized.” while simultaneously stating: “This is exactly what that recognition means—and exactly what it does not mean.” Foundational Principles Recognition is not unlimited recognition. A limitation does not negate legitimate recognition. Bounded recognition may be stronger than ambiguous recognition. Recognition for one beneficiary does not automatically establish recognition for another. Recognition for one purpose does not automatically authorize another use. Recognition of one value dimension does not establish recognition of every value dimension. Recognition boundary is not value boundary. Value transfer does not automatically transfer recognition. Institutional recognition does not automatically create universal recognition. Operational recognition does not automatically create accounting, tax, market, legal, or collateral recognition. Material recognition limitations must travel with the recognition determination. A recognition determination becomes distorted when its limitations are removed from it. Canonical Closing Statement Value Recognition Limitation Module establishes the boundary-control layer of the Value Recognition Standard by governing the contextual, beneficiary, purpose, dimensional, operational, temporal, dependency, uncertainty, measurement, transfer, institutional, and interpretive limitations attached to a Value Recognition Determination. Through explicit Recognition Boundary Statements, limitation states, dependency controls, excluded interpretations, temporal applicability, transfer conditions, review triggers, and downstream limitation persistence, VRLM prevents legitimate recognition within one governed context from expanding silently into unsupported financial, accounting, market, legal, tax, collateral, institutional, or universal claims. By separating the boundary of recognition from the existence and boundary of value itself, VRLM enables VFM® to recognize broad and unconventional forms of value while preserving methodological precision over exactly what each recognition determination establishes, where it applies, under what conditions it remains legitimate, and where its meaning must stop.
