title: Value State Determination Module (VSDM)
text: Value State Determination Module (VSDM) Value State Determination Module (VSDM) Value State Determination Module (VSDM) Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture Parent Standard: Value State Standard (VSS) Module: VSDM — Value State Determination Module Operational Layer: Value State Determination Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Value Lifecycle Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value State Determination Origin ID: VFM-VSS-VSDM-005.3 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 25 August 2026 Compatibility: OOF® Methodology OS™ · GOA™ · ORA™ · VALIDOS® · INTEGROS® · ADIT® · AGA™ · OBIDENITY® AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition Value State Determination Module (VSDM) is the third Core Module of the Value State Standard (VSS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture. VSDM governs the formal determination of the current governed Value State by evaluating whether a classified Value State Candidate is sufficiently supported, contextually bounded, temporally applicable, and methodologically coherent to become the authoritative state representation of the governed value at the defined reference point. The Module transforms: Classified Value State Candidate → Governed Value State Determination VSDM establishes the point at which a classification ceases to be merely a candidate interpretation and becomes the governed current state used by downstream VFM® processes. Its foundational distinction is: Classification ≠ Determination A value condition may be identified. It may be classified. But it must not become the authoritative governed Value State until the basis for that determination is established. Architectural Position VSDM is the third module within VSS. It follows: VSIM — Value State Identification Module → VSCM — Value State Classification Module and precedes: VSTM — Value State Transition Readiness Module. The internal logic is: Identify the current condition → Classify the condition → Determine the governed Value State → Assess readiness for subsequent state transition VSDM therefore represents the formal determination gate within Value State governance. Internal Module Flow Classified Value State Candidate → Determination Context Confirmation → Classification Basis Review → Supporting Basis Assessment → Contradiction Review → Uncertainty Review → Temporal Applicability Review → Determination Threshold Assessment → Value State Determination → Determination Status Assignment → VSTM — Value State Transition Readiness Module Operational Space VSDM governs the methodological space between: a classified value condition and an authoritative governed Value State. Its operational space includes: determination object; determination context; classification basis review; supporting basis; determination criteria; determination thresholds; contextual applicability; temporal applicability; contradictory information; uncertainty; determination confidence where used; determination limitations; provisional determination; conditional determination; confirmed determination; indeterminate state; determination suspension; determination withdrawal; determination traceability. Determination Object Every VSDM process must identify exactly what is being determined. The determination object should preserve, where applicable: Governed Value Value-Bearing Object Beneficiary Value Context Reference Framework Reference Point Observed Condition Value-State Classification This prevents a state determination from becoming detached from the value relationship that gives it meaning. Determination Basis A Value State Determination must have an identifiable basis. The basis may include: VSIM identification records; VSCM classification records; operational information; technical condition; financial information; utilization information; capability information; market information; contractual information; dependency status; resource information; system telemetry; governed observations; relevant external assessments; other context-appropriate information. VSDM does not require every value type to use the same evidence structure. It requires the basis to be sufficient for the determination being made. Determination Threshold Organizations implementing VSDM should establish the threshold required before a classified candidate becomes a governed Value State. The threshold may depend upon: importance of the value; consequence of incorrect determination; operational significance; financial significance; strategic significance; reversibility; uncertainty; available information; decision context. A low-consequence internal resource may require a relatively simple determination basis. A value state affecting: major financing; public infrastructure; critical industrial capacity; investment; mission capability; systemic financial exposure; strategic assets may require substantially stronger support. VSDM therefore permits proportional determination governance. Determination Status A VSDM implementation may use explicit determination statuses. 1. Indeterminate Available information does not support a sufficiently grounded determination. 2. Provisional A state can be determined temporarily, but material uncertainty or missing information remains. 3. Conditional The determination remains valid only while explicitly defined conditions remain satisfied. 4. Determined The applicable determination threshold has been satisfied and the classified state becomes the governed current Value State. 5. Suspended A previously determined state can no longer be relied upon pending reassessment. 6. Withdrawn The previous determination has ceased to represent the governed current state. These statuses prevent a binary system from forcing: determined or not determined where reality is more complex. Value Asset™ Determination Where the classified value condition satisfies the applicable determination requirements, VSDM may establish a governed state corresponding to: Value Asset™ A Value Asset™ represents value that exists and occupies a positively governed value state within the applicable context. The determination remains tied to: what value for whom in what context at what reference point under what conditions has been determined. The existence of a Value Asset™ under VFM® does not automatically establish: legal ownership; accounting recognition; market price; tax treatment; regulatory classification; transferability. Those questions remain governed by their appropriate systems. ZVA™ — Zero Value Asset™ Determination VSDM provides the formal determination gate for: ZVA™ — Zero Value Asset™ A value-bearing object must not become a governed ZVA™ merely because it is: unused; old; unprofitable; written down; technologically outdated; temporarily inaccessible; non-revenue-producing; operationally inactive. The determination must establish that the governed value has reached a zero-value state within the defined context and reference point. The canonical logic is: Value-Bearing Object Exists → Relevant Value Context Identified → Current Condition Identified → Zero-Value Classification Candidate → Determination Basis Assessed → Zero-Value State Determined → ZVA™ Therefore: ZVA™ ≠ Object Non-Existence and: ZVA™ ≠ Universal Worthlessness Zero-State Determination Protection Because a zero-value determination may trigger significant downstream consequences, VSDM must protect against false zero states. A zero determination should examine whether relevant value remains through: another current use; backup function; strategic capability; recoverability; transferability; component value; knowledge value; data value; contingency value; alternative beneficiary; alternative context; future defined use where relevant to the governed context. This does not mean every hypothetical future possibility prevents a zero-value determination. It means material existing value must not be ignored merely because the primary use has disappeared. Unknown ≠ Zero VSDM preserves one of the most important VSS rules: Insufficient Information ≠ Zero Value If the organization cannot establish whether value exists, the appropriate state may be: Indeterminate rather than: ZVA™ This prevents missing information from becoming a mechanism for manufacturing zero-value determinations. Dormant ≠ Zero A dormant asset may currently generate no operational output. Yet its governed value may remain intact. Examples include: emergency infrastructure; reserve production capacity; backup computing systems; strategic inventories; unused intellectual property; contingency equipment; inactive but recoverable capabilities. VSDM must therefore distinguish: no current utilization from no current value. Recoverable ≠ Zero A capability that has temporarily lost its ability to generate value may remain recoverable. For example: Machine unavailable because one replaceable component failed is fundamentally different from: Machine incapable of producing value within the governed context and with no materially relevant recovery pathway. The first may support a: Recoverable Value State rather than a ZVA™ determination. Negative Value Determination Where the applicable VFM® implementation governs negative-value states, VSDM must distinguish: Zero Value from Negative Value. A value-bearing object may impose more burden than the value it produces through: maintenance; energy; storage; compliance; capital lock-up; operational complexity; environmental burden; risk exposure; disposal obligation. That condition must not be hidden inside a zero-value classification where the distinction is materially relevant. Multi-Context Determination The same object may receive multiple valid Value State Determinations simultaneously. For example: Legacy Data Center may be determined as: Degraded Value — Primary Computing Context Active Value — Backup Capacity Context Conditional Value — Resale Context Strategic Value — Business Continuity Context The determinations are not contradictory where they govern different value relationships. Therefore: One Object ≠ One Universal Value State Multi-Beneficiary Determination Value may also differ by beneficiary. A manufacturing tool may have zero production value to one company while carrying active production value to another. An abandoned technology may have low value to its developer while carrying significant research value to a university. VSDM must preserve the beneficiary relationship where it materially affects the determination. Temporal Determination Every Value State Determination exists relative to a reference point. A determined state is therefore not automatically permanent. The same governed value may move through: Active Value → Degraded Value → Zero Value → Recoverable Value → Active Value as circumstances change. VSDM determines the current state. It does not freeze value into that state indefinitely. State Determination ≠ State Transition VSDM determines: what state value currently occupies. It does not govern: the mechanism by which value moved into that state. That distinction is fundamental. The fact that a machine is currently in a degraded-value state does not require VSDM to govern the technical event that damaged the machine. Likewise, determining that a digital asset has reached zero value does not require VSDM to govern the external market, legal, technological, or operational event responsible for the change. Those external mechanisms remain outside the VSDM governed space. Determination Contradiction Material contradictory information must be addressed before a final determination where it could alter the result. For example: Operations: capability is obsolete. Engineering: capability remains technically deployable. Finance: asset is fully depreciated. Strategy: capability remains essential during transition. VSDM should first determine whether these statements concern: the same governed value or different value contexts. Only genuine contradictions within the same governed value relationship require reconciliation at the determination level. Determination Uncertainty Uncertainty must remain visible where it materially affects the state determination. VSDM may preserve uncertainty relating to: future usability; current capability; dependency availability; market relevance; recoverability; strategic importance; technological condition; beneficiary relevance; data completeness; reference-point accuracy. A determination may remain provisional or conditional where uncertainty does not justify a fully determined state. Determination Expiry A Value State Determination may require expiry or review where the value environment changes rapidly. An implementation may define: Review Date Validity Period Material Change Trigger Reassessment Trigger Examples include: new market conditions; new technology; restoration; deterioration; regulatory change; beneficiary change; operational reconfiguration; dependency restoration; dependency failure; new evidence. A determination that no longer represents the governed reality must not remain authoritative merely because it exists in a record. Determination Authority Organizations should identify who or what may issue a Value State Determination. Depending upon context, this may involve: authorized personnel; defined governance function; automated rules; AI-supported assessment; committee decision; system-generated determination; hybrid human-machine process. VSDM governs the determination structure. Where authority, responsibility, accountability, or delegation itself requires governance, the appropriate governance architecture remains responsible for those questions. Automated Value State Determination VSDM can operate in automated environments. A system may continuously receive: Operational Data → Current Condition → State Classification → Determination Assessment → Current Governed Value State This enables value-state governance to move beyond periodic static reporting. However, automated determination must preserve: criteria; reference context; input basis; uncertainty; determination logic; determination timestamp; applicable limitations; state history. Automation must not turn a contextual Value State into an unexplained label. Determination Traceability A governed Value State should be traceable backward through the VSS process. The minimum chain is: Governed Value State → Determination Basis → State Classification → State Candidate → Observed Condition → Reference Point → Value Context → Governed Value This creates reconstructability of the state without requiring VFM® to take ownership of the external systems that generated the underlying information. Determination ≠ Valuation VSDM does not determine monetary value. It may determine: Active Value Dormant Value Degraded Value Zero Value or another governed state. It does not automatically determine: CHF 4.7 million or another monetary amount. Therefore: Value State Determination ≠ Monetary Valuation A valuation methodology may use the determined state as an input. Determination ≠ Accounting Recognition A VSDM determination does not replace accounting standards. An asset may remain recognized in financial accounts while VSDM determines that its operational value has reached zero within a particular context. Conversely, an organizational capability may have no separately recognized accounting asset while carrying an active strategic Value State. This is precisely why the two governance spaces must remain separate. Determination ≠ Tax Treatment A governed Value State does not itself establish tax liability, deductibility, taxable value, depreciation treatment, or tax recognition. However, a future tax architecture may consume VFM® Value State Determinations as governed inputs where legislation or policy chooses to recognize value-state information. The boundary remains: VFM® determines the governed Value State. The tax system determines the legal tax consequence. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum VSDM implementation should establish: 1. Classified Candidate Input Receive the classified Value State Candidate from VSCM. 2. Determination Context Confirm governed value, object, beneficiary, context, and reference point. 3. Determination Criteria Define what must be established before the classified state may become authoritative. 4. Supporting Basis Review Review the information supporting the classified state. 5. Contradiction Review Identify material conflicting information capable of changing the determination. 6. Uncertainty Review Identify material uncertainty affecting determination legitimacy. 7. Determination Threshold Assessment Determine whether the required threshold has been satisfied. 8. Value State Determination Issue the applicable Value State or preserve an indeterminate, provisional, conditional, suspended, or withdrawn status. 9. Determination Conditions Record material limitations, validity periods, conditions, or review triggers. 10. Determination Record Create the governed determination basis for transfer to VSTM. Governance Outputs VSDM may produce: Value State Determination Value State Determination Status Value State Determination Basis Value State Determination Criteria Record Value State Determination Threshold Record Value State Determination Uncertainty Record Value State Contradiction Record Value State Applicability Statement Value State Validity Period Value State Review Trigger Value Asset™ Determination ZVA™ Determination Value State Determination Record These outputs provide the governed basis for: VSTM — Value State Transition Readiness Module. Use Case 1 — Public Finance and Infrastructure: Determining Which Assets Still Carry Operational Value A government or public infrastructure operator may control thousands of: buildings; roads; facilities; machines; IT systems; land parcels; equipment; licenses; infrastructure components. Traditional asset registers can establish that these objects exist and may assign accounting amounts to them. But they do not necessarily establish the current operational state of the value attached to each object. VSDM allows the organization to formally determine, within defined contexts: Active Value Dormant Value Constrained Value Degraded Value Recoverable Value ZVA™ — Zero Value Asset™ Consider an unused public building. Its non-use does not automatically establish zero value. The building may retain: Emergency Capacity Value Alternative Public-Service Value Rental Value Redevelopment Value or Strategic Land Value. VSDM prevents a simplistic: unused → zero value determination. But where the relevant value contexts have been examined and the applicable determination threshold establishes that a specific governed value has genuinely reached zero, the organization can create an explicit ZVA™ determination. Across a large public asset base, this creates the possibility of identifying where resources remain tied to value-bearing objects whose governed value state no longer justifies their continued treatment as productive capacity. The result can support better: asset management, capital allocation, maintenance prioritization, infrastructure renewal, reuse analysis, and public spending discipline. Use Case 2 — AI and Data-Center Infrastructure: Determining When Computing Capacity Stops Creating Useful Value An organization operates a large AI infrastructure environment containing: GPUs; servers; storage; models; software licenses; datasets; networking capacity; specialized accelerators; legacy computing systems. Physical and accounting existence alone does not reveal whether each resource continues to create useful value. A GPU cluster may remain technically operational while its energy cost, performance profile, software compatibility, workload suitability, or infrastructure requirements make it unsuitable for the governed workload. Another older cluster may appear obsolete for frontier-model training but remain highly valuable for inference, testing, simulation, or lower-complexity workloads. VSDM can determine separate states by context: Cluster A → Active Value — Frontier Training Cluster B → Zero Value — Frontier Training but → Active Value — Batch Inference Cluster C → Recoverable Value — Current Workload Cluster D → Negative Value Candidate — Legacy Infrastructure Context This prevents organizations from making the expensive mistake of equating: technological age with zero value. It also prevents the opposite mistake: physical availability with continued productive value. At infrastructure scale, VSDM can provide a governed state layer showing where computing, energy, capital, cooling, maintenance, and physical space remain attached to resources that no longer create sufficient value within their intended context. That state information can subsequently support VFM® value-change and transition governance and other architectures concerned with resource allocation, efficiency, investment, or operational optimization. Foundational Principles Classification is not determination. A Value State becomes authoritative only through an explicit determination basis. Value State Determination must remain bound to value context, beneficiary, and reference point. Unknown value is not zero value. Dormant value is not zero value. Recoverable value is not zero value. Zero value is not negative value. Zero value does not mean non-existence. Zero value in one context does not establish zero value in every context. One object may legitimately carry multiple Value State Determinations. A Value State Determination is not monetary valuation. A Value State Determination is not accounting recognition. A Value State Determination is not tax treatment. The current Value State must remain revisable when the reality supporting it materially changes. Canonical Closing Statement Value State Determination Module establishes the formal determination gate of the Value State Standard by transforming a classified Value State Candidate into an explicit, context-bound, reference-point-specific, supportable, uncertainty-aware, and reviewable governed Value State. Through governance of determination criteria, supporting basis, thresholds, contradictions, uncertainty, applicability, determination status, temporal validity, authority, traceability, Value Asset™ determination, and ZVA™ — Zero Value Asset™ determination, VSDM prevents classifications, accounting records, physical existence, non-use, technological age, missing information, or assumptions of worthlessness from becoming authoritative statements about the current state of value without a governed basis. By separating Value State Determination from monetary valuation, accounting recognition, tax treatment, external causation, and state transition, VSDM establishes the authoritative current- state layer required before VFM® can determine whether value is ready to move into another governed state. title: Value State Identification Module (VSIM)
text: Value State Identification Module (VSIM) Value State Identification Module (VSIM) Value State Identification Module (VSIM) Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture Parent Standard: Value State Standard (VSS) Module: VSIM — Value State Identification Module Operational Layer: Value State Identification Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Value Lifecycle Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value State Identification Origin ID: VFM-VSS-VSIM-005.1 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 25 August 2026 Compatibility: OOF® Methodology OS™ · GOA™ · ORA™ · VALIDOS® · INTEGROS® · ADIT® · AGA™ · OBIDENITY® AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition Value State Identification Module (VSIM) is the first Core Module of the Value State Standard (VSS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture. VSIM governs the identification of the specific current value condition that must be examined as a Value State Candidate before that condition can be classified, formally determined, assessed for transition readiness, and recorded. The Module establishes the reference relationship between: Governed Value → Value Context → Reference Point → Observed Value Condition → Value State Candidate Its purpose is to ensure that value-state governance begins with an explicitly identified condition rather than an assumed, inherited, outdated, or context-free statement about value. VSIM does not determine the final value state. It establishes what current value condition is being submitted to state governance. Architectural Position VSIM is the first module within VSS. It receives the governed value basis established through the preceding VFM® lifecycle and creates the state candidate required for subsequent classification. It precedes: VSCM — Value State Classification Module The internal sequence begins: Governed Recognized Value → VSIM — Value State Identification → VSCM — Value State Classification The distinction is essential: Identifying the condition to be governed ≠ determining the final state. Internal Module Flow Governed Recognized Value → Value Reference Confirmation → Value Context Confirmation → Reference Point Definition → Current Condition Observation → Condition Boundary Identification → Condition Relevance Assessment → Value State Candidate Identification → Identification Record → VSCM — Value State Classification Module Operational Space VSIM governs the point at which an existing governed value becomes the subject of a current-state examination. Its operational space includes: value reference confirmation; governed value linkage; value-context linkage; current-condition identification; reference-point identification; temporal reference; operational reference; relevant condition identification; state-candidate creation; state-candidate boundary; context separation; condition observability; uncertainty identification; stale-state detection; conflicting-condition identification; identification traceability. VSIM answers neither: “What category does this state belong to?” nor: “What is the formally determined state?” Those questions belong downstream. Value Reference Confirmation State identification must begin with a defined governed value. The Module must therefore establish which value is being examined. This may be value associated with: an asset; a capability; a resource; a technology; a relationship; a right; a process; a system; infrastructure; intellectual property; information; a digital object; an organizational capability; another value-bearing basis. VSIM does not redefine the value. It links the state-identification process to the value already established within the VFM® lifecycle. Value Context Confirmation The same object may carry different values under different contexts. Therefore, VSIM must preserve the value context before identifying the state candidate. For example: Industrial Robot may carry: Production Value Resale Value Spare-Part Value Strategic Capability Value Training Value These are not automatically the same governed value. Consequently, the statement: “The robot has zero value.” is insufficient for governed state identification. VSIM requires the more precise structure: Value Object: Industrial Robot Value Context: Production Capability Reference Point: Current Production Configuration Observed Condition: Cannot perform required production function Only then can the relevant Value State Candidate proceed downstream. Reference Point Definition A current value condition must be anchored to a defined reference point. The reference point may be: current time; reporting date; accounting period; mission phase; production configuration; system version; project phase; contractual state; market condition; operating environment; infrastructure configuration; technological generation; another governed reference condition. Without this reference point, the identified state may already be obsolete when it enters downstream governance. Current Condition Observation VSIM identifies the observable or otherwise supportable condition of the governed value at the applicable reference point. The condition may concern: availability; usability; functionality; demand; utilization; strategic relevance; operational relevance; technological relevance; accessibility; compatibility; recoverability; constraint; inactivity; deterioration; absence of current value; another context-relevant condition. VSIM does not yet translate the condition into a formal state classification. It preserves the condition before classification. Condition ≠ State A central VSIM distinction is: Observed Condition ≠ Governed Value State For example: “Machine is not currently used.” is a condition. It does not automatically mean: ZVA™ — Zero Value Asset™ The machine may remain strategically necessary, readily deployable, valuable as backup capacity, transferable, or useful within another value context. Likewise: “Patent generates no current licensing revenue.” does not automatically establish zero strategic value. VSIM therefore prevents premature state assignment. Value State Candidate A Value State Candidate is the identified current value condition submitted for subsequent classification and determination. A candidate should preserve, where applicable: Governed Value Reference Value Object Reference Value Context Beneficiary Context Reference Point Observed Condition Relevant Dependencies Material Constraints Available Supporting Basis Uncertainty Identification Timestamp The candidate is not yet the authoritative current value state. Context Separation Principle Where the same value-bearing object participates in multiple value contexts, VSIM should identify separate state candidates where materially necessary. For example: Technology Platform may produce: Commercial Value State Candidate and separately: Strategic Technology Value State Candidate and separately: Operational Capability Value State Candidate This prevents one condition from incorrectly propagating across all value contexts. Current State Identification ≠ Historical State Historical information may help identify the present condition. It must not replace it. A previous record showing: High Operational Value does not establish that the same state exists today. VSIM therefore distinguishes: Historical Condition from: Current Condition Candidate. This is particularly important in automated systems where old records may otherwise continue to be treated as current truth. Current State Identification ≠ Predicted State Forecasts may indicate that a value condition is likely to change. VSIM does not convert that forecast into a current-state candidate unless the relevant condition actually exists at the applicable reference point. Therefore: Expected Future Condition ≠ Current Value Condition and: Predicted State ≠ Identified Current State. Conflicting Conditions Value-state identification may encounter conflicting information. For example: Financial Record: asset remains productive while: Operational Record: production capability has been unavailable for six months. VSIM must preserve the conflict rather than silently selecting the more convenient source. A conflicting state candidate may proceed with explicit uncertainty or require additional information before classification. Unknown Condition ≠ Zero Value Where the current condition cannot be established sufficiently, VSIM must permit an unresolved identification state. Therefore: Unknown ≠ Zero Missing Data ≠ Zero Unobserved ≠ Zero Uncertain ≠ ZVA™ This prevents absent information from becoming an artificial zero-value determination. Stale State Detection VSIM should identify situations where a previously recorded state may no longer represent the current condition. Potential stale-state indicators include: expired reference period; material operational change; technology replacement; market change; contract termination; capability degradation; infrastructure change; new evidence; changed value context; changed beneficiary; restoration event; material external event. The purpose is not to determine that the old state is wrong. It is to determine that current-state identification must be performed again. Multi-Level Identification State candidates may exist at different organizational levels. For example: Component → Machine → Production Line → Factory → Enterprise Capability VSIM must prevent a condition observed at one level from automatically becoming the state of another level. A failed component does not automatically mean the production line has zero value. Likewise, a profitable enterprise does not mean every underlying capability is value-producing. Identification Granularity VSIM should identify value conditions at the level necessary for meaningful downstream governance. Excessive aggregation may hide: dormant value; degraded value; zero-value assets; recoverable capabilities; critical dependencies; unused capacity; value concentration. Excessive fragmentation may create unnecessary governance complexity. The identification level should therefore correspond to the intended value-governance purpose. Identification Basis A Value State Candidate may be identified using relevant information such as: operational records; financial information; utilization data; technical condition; system telemetry; market information; contractual information; production data; capability assessments; resource availability; infrastructure status; expert observations; external valuations; governed digital records. VSIM does not take ownership of those information systems. It governs how they are connected to the identification of the current value condition. Identification Uncertainty VSIM must preserve material uncertainty affecting the identified condition. Uncertainty may concern: incomplete information; conflicting information; timing; object configuration; operational availability; market relevance; dependency status; technological condition; context applicability. A state candidate may remain usable with uncertainty attached. The uncertainty must not disappear merely because the candidate moves downstream. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum VSIM implementation should establish: 1. Governed Value Reference Identify the governed value whose current condition is being examined. 2. Value Object Reference Identify the value-bearing object, capability, resource, relationship, system, or other basis associated with the value. 3. Value Context Confirmation Confirm the context within which the current value condition is being identified. 4. Reference Point Definition Establish the temporal, operational, technological, contractual, mission, or other applicable reference point. 5. Current Condition Identification Identify the materially relevant present condition of the governed value. 6. Condition Boundary Determine the level and scope to which the identified condition applies. 7. Supporting Basis Link the condition to available supporting information. 8. Uncertainty Identification Record material uncertainty or conflicting information. 9. State Candidate Creation Create an explicit Value State Candidate without prematurely determining its classification. 10. Identification Record Preserve the candidate and its governing context for transfer to VSCM. Governance Outputs VSIM may produce: Value State Candidate Value Reference Record Value Context Link Value Object Reference Value State Reference Point Current Value Condition Record Condition Boundary Record Supporting Basis Record State Identification Uncertainty Record Conflicting Condition Record Stale State Indicator Value State Identification Record These outputs provide the governed input for: VSCM — Value State Classification Module. Use Case 1 — Banking: Identifying Hidden Value- State Risk Before Credit Exposure A bank has financed an industrial company with a large asset base. The borrower's financial records still contain machinery, production infrastructure, intellectual property, inventories, software systems, and other assets with substantial recorded values. A conventional portfolio view may therefore indicate that significant value remains available. VSIM introduces a different examination. For each materially relevant value-bearing basis, the bank can establish: Governed Value → Credit-Relevant Value Context → Current Reference Point → Observed Current Condition → Value State Candidate A production machine may still exist physically and remain on the borrower's balance sheet while no longer being compatible with the company's current production process. Another machine may be idle but immediately deployable. A patent may produce no revenue but remain strategically important. A production line may be operational but dependent upon a supplier whose critical component is no longer available. VSIM prevents all four conditions from being treated simply as: “assets with value.” It identifies the materially different current conditions before classification and formal state determination occur. This can give the bank an earlier governance signal that the economic condition of the underlying value base may be diverging from its static recorded representation. VSIM does not replace collateral valuation, accounting, credit models, or regulatory capital requirements. It creates the identification layer required to ask a more fundamental question: What is actually happening to the value underlying the exposure now? Use Case 2 — Space Mission: Finding Value That Can Be Removed Without Losing Mission Capability A space mission operates under severe constraints on: mass; energy; computing capacity; storage; communication bandwidth; maintenance capacity; crew time; redundancy; mission cost. As the mission evolves, systems and capabilities that were valuable during one phase may no longer create material value during another. VSIM can continuously identify current value conditions across mission capabilities. For example: Capability A may remain essential. Capability B may be dormant but critical as emergency redundancy. Capability C may no longer contribute to the current or future mission configuration. Capability D may have lost its original function but remain useful for diagnostics or scientific observation. Without explicit value-state identification, all four capabilities may continue consuming mission resources merely because they still exist. VSIM establishes: Mission Value Context → Mission Phase → Capability Reference → Current Condition → Dependency Check → Value State Candidate The downstream VSS modules can then determine whether a capability remains a Value Asset™, occupies another defined state, or may qualify as ZVA™ — Zero Value Asset™ within the relevant mission context. This creates a practical path toward identifying where resources can potentially be removed, reassigned, deactivated, or preserved without confusing physical existence with mission value. In resource-constrained environments, that distinction can translate directly into lower operating burden and better allocation of scarce mission resources. Foundational Principles A value state must be identified before it can be classified. Observed condition is not automatically governed state. Value state identification must remain connected to the governed value context. A historical state is not automatically the current state. A predicted state is not the current state. Unknown condition is not zero value. Physical existence does not establish current value condition. One value-bearing object may require multiple state candidates across different value contexts. State identification must occur at the level at which the relevant value condition actually exists. The first requirement of current-state governance is to identify what condition is actually being governed now. Canonical Closing Statement Value State Identification Module establishes the entry point into Value State governance by identifying the precise current condition of governed value that must be examined before classification, determination, transition-readiness assessment, and state recording can occur. Through explicit linkage of governed value, value-bearing object, value context, reference point, observed condition, scope, supporting basis, uncertainty, stale-state indicators, and multi-context distinctions, VSIM prevents historical records, predictions, accounting classifications, physical existence, missing information, or premature zero-value assumptions from being mistaken for the current governed state of value. By creating an explicit Value State Candidate, VSIM provides the methodological foundation upon which the remaining Value State Standard modules can determine what state value actually occupies. title: Value State Record Module (VSRM)
text: Value State Record Module (VSRM) Value State Record Module (VSRM) Value State Record Module (VSRM) Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture Parent Standard: Value State Standard (VSS) Module: VSRM — Value State Record Module Operational Layer: Value State Record Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Value Lifecycle Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value State Record Origin ID: VFM-VSS-VSRM-005.5 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 25 August 2026 Compatibility: OOF® Methodology OS™ · GOA™ · ORA™ · VALIDOS® · INTEGROS® · ADIT® · AGA™ · OBIDENITY® AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition Value State Record Module (VSRM) is the fifth Core Module of the Value State Standard (VSS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture. VSRM governs the creation, structuring, preservation, linkage, updating, and lifecycle continuity of the governed Value State Record representing the current determined state of value and the material basis upon which that state was established. The Module transforms: Determined Value State + Transition Readiness → Governed Value State Record VSRM ensures that the result of Value State governance does not remain an isolated determination, temporary analytical conclusion, undocumented classification, or context-free label. It establishes a persistent and reconstructable representation of: what value state was determined for what governed value in what context for which beneficiary at what reference point on what basis with what limitations with what transition-readiness status. Its foundational distinction is: Value State ≠ Value State Record The state describes the governed condition of value. The record preserves the governed representation of that condition. Architectural Position VSRM is the fifth and final module within VSS. It follows: VSIM — Value State Identification Module → VSCM — Value State Classification Module → VSDM — Value State Determination Module → VSTM — Value State Transition Readiness Module and completes the internal VSS sequence through: VSRM — Value State Record Module The internal logic is: Identify State → Classify State → Determine State → Assess Transition Readiness → Record State VSRM therefore creates the governed output through which the current Value State can remain available to subsequent VFM® processes. VFM® Governance Flow Position VSRM completes the fifth governed space within the VFM® governance flow: Value Context → Value Origin → Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change The VSRM output forms the reference basis against which subsequent material Value Change can be identified. The architectural bridge is: Governed Value State Record → Observed New Condition → Potential Difference → Value Change Governance This is essential because change cannot be meaningfully established without a governed reference state against which the new condition can be compared. Internal Module Flow Value State Identification → Value State Classification → Value State Determination → Transition Readiness Assessment → Record Object Creation → Context Linkage → Determination Basis Linkage → Reference Point Assignment → Limitation & Uncertainty Preservation → Transition Readiness Linkage → Record Status Assignment → Governed Value State Record → VCS — Value Change Standard Operational Space VSRM governs the methodological space between: a completed Value State determination and a persistent governed representation capable of supporting subsequent value governance. Its operational space includes: Value State record identity; governed-value linkage; value-bearing object linkage; beneficiary linkage; context linkage; reference framework linkage; determined state; determination status; determination basis; temporal reference point; applicability; uncertainty; limitations; transition readiness; transition conditions; record version; record status; supersession; historical continuity; state lineage; downstream VFM® availability. Value State Record Object Every VSRM process should create an identifiable Value State Record Object. The Record Object should establish, where applicable: Record ID Governed Value ID Value-Bearing Object Beneficiary Value Context Reference Framework Reference Point Value State Classification Value State Determination Determination Status Determination Basis Uncertainty Limitations Transition Readiness State Applicable Transition Conditions Record Version Record Status This creates a machine-readable and human-interpretable representation of the governed Value State. Record Context Principle A Value State Record must not detach the state from the context that gives it meaning. A record containing only: Asset X — Zero Value is methodologically insufficient where the actual determination was: Asset X — Zero Value for Beneficiary B within Operational Context C at Reference Point T. The difference is fundamental. Without context preservation, a valid narrow determination may later be interpreted as a universal statement about the object. VSRM therefore requires: State + Context + Reference Point to remain linked. Record Identity Every material Value State Record should be uniquely identifiable. Record identity allows organizations to distinguish: current records; historical records; superseded records; corrected records; parallel context-specific records; beneficiary-specific records; provisional records; conditional records. Record identity is not the same as identity of the underlying asset or object. Therefore: Value State Record Identity ≠ Asset Identity OBIDENITY® or another applicable identity architecture may govern the underlying object identity. VSRM governs the identity of the Value State Record itself. Reference Point Every Value State Record must preserve the temporal or event-based point to which the determination applies. This may be: timestamp; date; reporting period; transaction point; operational event; assessment point; lifecycle milestone; defined condition. Without a reference point, the organization may later confuse: what was true then with what is true now. This becomes particularly important where value changes rapidly. State Record ≠ Permanent Truth A Value State Record represents the governed determination applicable at its reference point. It does not establish permanent value reality. A record may legitimately state: Active Value — 25 August 2026 while a later record states: Degraded Value — 14 October 2026 and another later record states: ZVA™ — 9 January 2027. These records do not invalidate one another where each accurately represents its applicable governed reference state. Together they create: Value State History. Current Record and Historical Record VSRM distinguishes between: Current Value State Record and Historical Value State Record. When a new Value State is legitimately determined, the previous record should normally remain preserved as historical state information rather than being overwritten as though the earlier determination never existed. The logic is: Current Record → Material Change → New Determination → New Current Record while: Previous Current Record → Historical Record This creates state continuity. Record Versioning A Value State Record may require versioning where: information is corrected; uncertainty is updated; limitations change; supporting information changes; determination status changes; transition readiness changes; contextual information is refined. Versioning must distinguish: Record Revision from Value State Change. Correcting a spelling error does not mean value changed. Adding missing documentation does not necessarily mean value changed. Updating transition readiness may not mean the underlying Value State changed. Therefore: Record Change ≠ Value Change Record Supersession Where a new governed Value State replaces the previous current state, VSRM should preserve the supersession relationship. Example: VSR-000145 / Active Value → superseded by → VSR-000186 / Degraded Value → superseded by → VSR-000241 / ZVA™ The chain creates a reconstructable value-state lifecycle. The previous record should not disappear merely because it is no longer current. Parallel Value State Records One value-bearing object may legitimately have multiple simultaneous Value State Records. For example: Industrial Facility may have: Active Value — Production Context Strategic Value — Emergency Capacity Context Degraded Value — Energy Efficiency Context Conditional Value — Redevelopment Context These records are not necessarily contradictory. They represent distinct governed value relationships. VSRM must therefore support: One Object → Multiple Context-Bound Value State Records Beneficiary-Specific Records The same value-bearing object may carry different Value States for different beneficiaries. For example: Legacy Industrial Equipment may represent: ZVA™ — Company A / Current Production Context while simultaneously representing: Active Value — Company B / Secondary Production Context. VSRM must preserve these beneficiary distinctions. Otherwise, a zero-value determination for one beneficiary could incorrectly erase value existing for another. Value Asset™ Record Where VSDM determines a governed state corresponding to: Value Asset™ VSRM preserves that determination as an explicit Value State Record. The record should preserve: why the governed value qualifies as existing positive value and the context within which that determination applies. A Value Asset™ Record does not automatically establish: legal title; accounting asset recognition; market price; tax status; regulatory classification; transfer rights. It records the VFM® Value State. ZVA™ — Zero Value Asset™ Record Where a governed value has legitimately reached: ZVA™ — Zero Value Asset™ VSRM creates a persistent record of that zero-value determination. The record must preserve: what value reached zero for which beneficiary within which context at what reference point on what determination basis subject to what limitations with what recovery or transition conditions where applicable. This prevents: ZVA™ from becoming an unexplained universal label attached permanently to an object. A later state may legitimately move away from ZVA™ where new value emerges, is recognized, and a new state is determined. Unknown-State Record Where VSDM determines that available information is insufficient to establish the current Value State, VSRM may preserve: Indeterminate Value State rather than forcing a positive or zero-value record. This protects the architecture from converting: missing information into false value certainty. Conditional-State Record A conditional determination must preserve its conditions. Example: Conditional Value may depend upon: License Renewal Critical Supplier Availability Network Access Regulatory Approval Energy Availability Restoration Completion If those conditions disappear from the record, downstream systems may incorrectly treat conditional value as unconditional value. VSRM therefore treats conditions as part of the governed record. Uncertainty Preservation Material uncertainty affecting the Value State must remain connected to the record. Relevant uncertainty may concern: capability; utilization; recoverability; beneficiary relevance; market relevance; technical condition; dependency availability; strategic significance; temporal applicability; data completeness. VSRM does not eliminate uncertainty. It ensures that downstream use cannot silently forget it. Limitation Preservation A Value State determination may contain explicit limitations. For example: ZVA™ applies only to the current manufacturing context and does not assess component resale value. That limitation must remain part of the record. Without it, a valid context-specific state can become an invalid universal conclusion. Therefore: State Record without Material Limitations = Incomplete Governance Record where those limitations affect legitimate interpretation. Transition Readiness Record VSRM preserves the transition-readiness result produced through VSTM. The record may therefore contain: Current Value State: Active Value Transition Readiness: Transition-Sensitive or: Current Value State: ZVA™ Transition Readiness: Recovery-Ready This creates a richer state representation than a static value label. It allows downstream systems to know both: where value is now and whether that state is becoming unstable or ready to change. State Lineage VSRM enables the construction of a Value State Lineage. Example: Potential Value → Value Emergence → Recognized Value → Active Value → Degraded Value → ZVA™ → Recoverable Value → Active Value The record lineage does not itself govern all these transitions. It preserves the sequence of governed states and their relationships as they pass through VFM®. This creates the informational foundation required to reconstruct the value lifecycle. Record Continuity Value governance becomes substantially stronger when state records remain continuous across time. A continuous record can answer: What was the value state before the event? What changed? When did it change? What state followed? Was the previous state already transition-sensitive? Was zero value temporary or persistent? Was value later recovered? This is essential for downstream Value Change governance. Record Integrity Boundary VSRM defines what must be represented within the Value State Record. It does not replace general information-integrity governance. Where record integrity, tamper resistance, provenance assurance, authenticity, or broader integrity controls are required, the relevant integrity architecture may govern those properties. The boundary is: VSRM governs what the Value State Record must represent. INTEGROS® may govern whether that record remains trustworthy and intact. Auditability Boundary VSRM creates a reconstructable Value State Record. It does not itself conduct an audit. ADIT® may subsequently examine: whether the record existed; whether supporting information is preserved; whether changes are traceable; whether determinations can be reconstructed; whether state history was altered; whether records correspond to observed evidence. Therefore: Value State Recording ≠ Audit Accounting Boundary A Value State Record is not an accounting ledger entry. The same physical or digital object may have: accounting carrying value and VFM® governed Value State simultaneously. These may differ legitimately because they answer different questions. VSRM must not redefine accounting treatment. However, accounting systems may consume VFM® state information where an organization or future methodology chooses to use it as a governed analytical input. Tax Boundary A Value State Record does not itself create: taxable income; tax liability; deductible loss; depreciation; taxable asset value; tax recognition. A future tax architecture could use VFM® Value State Records as governed inputs into a separate tax determination mechanism. The architectural separation remains: VFM® records the governed state of value. The tax architecture determines the tax consequence. Blockchain and Distributed Ledger Compatibility VSRM can be implemented using conventional databases, enterprise systems, distributed ledgers, blockchain systems, digital asset infrastructures, or future record technologies. A blockchain may preserve: record timestamp; record identity; state version; supersession; provenance reference; state-transition reference. But: Blockchain Record ≠ Governed Value State The technology may preserve the record. VFM® defines the methodological meaning of what the record represents. This distinction allows VSRM to remain technology-neutral. AI and Machine-Readable Value State Records VSRM is designed to support machine-readable implementation. An AI or automated system may consume structured fields such as: Value ID Object ID Beneficiary ID Context ID Reference Point Value State Determination Status Transition Readiness Uncertainty Limitations Record Version This allows Value State governance to become part of automated: asset management; banking; insurance; industrial systems; public finance; digital infrastructure; AI resource allocation; investment systems; operational optimization. Machine readability must not remove contextual meaning. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum VSRM implementation should establish: 1. Record Identity Create a unique Value State Record identifier. 2. Governed Value Link Identify the governed value represented by the record. 3. Context Link Preserve the value-bearing object, beneficiary, context, and applicable reference framework. 4. State Determination Record the determined Value State and determination status. 5. Determination Basis Preserve or link the material basis supporting the state. 6. Reference Point Record the time, period, event, or other reference point to which the state applies. 7. Uncertainty and Limitations Preserve material uncertainty, conditions, and limitations. 8. Transition Readiness Preserve the applicable VSTM readiness state and material transition conditions. 9. Version and Status Identify whether the record is current, historical, provisional, conditional, suspended, superseded, or otherwise governed. 10. Continuity Link Link the record to prior and subsequent Value State Records where applicable. Governance Outputs VSRM may produce: Value State Record Current Value State Record Historical Value State Record Value State Record ID Value State Context Record Value State Determination Link Value State Reference Point Value State Uncertainty Record Value State Limitation Record Value State Transition Readiness Record Value State Version Record Value State Supersession Record Value State History Value State Lineage Value Asset™ Record ZVA™ — Zero Value Asset™ Record These outputs complete the governed output of the Value State Standard (VSS) and establish the reference basis for Value Change Standard (VCS). Use Case 1 — Banking and Collateral: From Static Asset Register to Governed Value-State History A bank holds thousands of loans secured against: industrial machinery; commercial property; infrastructure; vehicles; equipment; intellectual property; digital assets; production capacity. A traditional system may preserve: Asset ID Borrower Original valuation Current accounting amount Collateral category. But the bank may lack a structured record of how the actual governed value condition evolved over time. VSRM allows the bank to preserve: Value State Record 1 → Active Value → production capability strong → transition readiness stable then: Value State Record 2 → Degraded Value → utilization falling → maintenance burden increasing → transition-sensitive then: Value State Record 3 → ZVA™ within Primary Production Context → capability no longer economically usable for that beneficiary while preserving: Secondary Resale Context → Recoverable Value. The bank no longer sees only: “Collateral exists.” It sees: how the governed value attached to that collateral evolved. This can support stronger: credit monitoring collateral governance risk detection restructuring analysis capital allocation and recovery planning. The critical advantage is historical reconstructability. When a major loss occurs, the institution can examine not merely the final state, but the complete governed state path that preceded it. Use Case 2 — Blockchain and Digital Assets: Recording Value State Without Confusing Ownership, Price, and Value A digital infrastructure may contain millions of tokens, digital rights, licenses, data assets, computational resources, digital objects, or blockchain-linked assets. A blockchain can prove that: an object exists a transaction occurred ownership changed or a record was timestamped. But those facts do not necessarily establish: what governed Value State the asset currently occupies. VSRM can create a separate machine-readable Value State layer. For example: Digital Asset A → Active Value → beneficiary: Network X → context: operational utility → reference point: T1 Later: Digital Asset A → Dormant Value → utility temporarily inactive Later: Digital Asset A → ZVA™ → zero operational value within Network X while simultaneously: Digital Asset A → Recoverable Value → secondary interoperability context. The blockchain may preserve the records and their chronology. VFM® defines what those records mean. This separation prevents: token price ownership transaction history and governed value state from being treated as the same concept. It also creates the possibility of portable Value State Records that can be consumed by financial systems, asset- management systems, insurance systems, AI agents, marketplaces, or future value infrastructures without losing their original context. Foundational Principles Value State is not Value State Record. A Value State Record must preserve the context that gives the state meaning. A Value State Record represents a governed reference point, not permanent truth. Historical states must not disappear merely because a new current state exists. Record revision is not automatically Value Change. One object may carry multiple legitimate context-specific Value State Records. One object may carry different Value States for different beneficiaries. ZVA™ in one context does not establish universal zero value. Unknown value must remain distinguishable from zero value. Conditional value must preserve its conditions. Material uncertainty and limitations must travel with the Value State Record. Transition readiness should remain visible alongside the current Value State. Blockchain may preserve a Value State Record; it does not determine the Value State. Accounting value, market price, ownership, tax treatment, and VFM® Value State remain distinct concepts. A governed history of value requires states to remain reconstructable across time. Canonical Closing Statement Value State Record Module completes the Value State Standard by transforming identified, classified, determined, and transition-readiness-assessed value conditions into persistent, context-bound, beneficiary- aware, reference-point-specific, uncertainty-preserving, limitation-aware, versioned, and historically reconstructable Value State Records. Through governance of record identity, state representation, context linkage, determination basis, temporal applicability, conditions, uncertainty, transition readiness, versioning, supersession, parallel states, historical continuity, Value Asset™ records, and ZVA™ — Zero Value Asset™ records, VSRM prevents current value conditions from becoming detached from the circumstances that give them meaning or from overwriting the value history that preceded them. By separating Value State recording from object identity, accounting, taxation, blockchain technology, audit, integrity, and Value Change itself, VSRM creates the persistent reference layer required for VFM® to compare what value was with what value subsequently becomes. A value lifecycle becomes governable only when its states can remain identifiable, contextualized, connected, and reconstructable across time.
