Cross-Border Positive Determination ≠ Jurisdiction Allocation. Multi-Jurisdiction Decision Reuse One governed Determination Decision may support multiple downstream jurisdictional evaluations. The model is: One Governed Event Determination Decision ↓ Multiple Jurisdictional Tax Evaluations This is a core TREGA™ infrastructure function. Jurisdiction-Neutrality EDDM shall preserve a jurisdiction-neutral Decision. The Decision states: This Event is sufficiently governed as Tax-Relevant. It does not state: This jurisdiction may tax it. Jurisdiction-Neutral Determination ≠ Jurisdictional Tax Decision. Decision and Taxability This boundary is absolute. Event Determination Decision ≠ Taxability Determination. Taxability belongs to downstream law. Decision and Tax Jurisdiction Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination. Decision and Taxpayer Event Determination Decision ≠ Taxpayer Determination. Decision and Tax Base Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Base Determination. Decision and Tax Rate Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Rate Determination. Decision and Tax Period Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Period Determination. Decision and Tax Liability Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Liability Determination. Decision and Legal Characterization A jurisdiction may later legally characterize the Event differently from TREGA™ operational terminology. Event Determination Decision ≠ Legal Tax Characterization. Decision State Preservation Every materially relevant Decision state shall remain historically traceable. A later Decision shall not silently erase an earlier one. Decision Supersession ≠ Decision Erasure. Decision Correction Where the Decision itself contains an error that can be corrected without full reconsideration, correction may be recorded. Decision Correction ≠ Silent Replacement. Decision Escalation EDDM may require escalation where: governance basis is materially conflicting; Decision authority is unavailable; conditions are incompatible; automated Decision logic cannot resolve the state; or another governance boundary is reached. Escalation shall preserve the Event and Decision state. Governance States EDDM may represent: Decision Not Initiated Decision Eligible Decision Under Evaluation Decision Basis Complete Decision Basis Qualified Positive Determination Conditional Determination Deferred Determination Rejected Determination Ambiguous Determination Conflicted Determination Decision Escalation Required Decision Correction Required Decision Reconsideration Flagged Decision Finalized Governed Event Determination Decision Established Governance Requirements EDDM implementations shall ensure that: Decision governance begins only after suitable condition governance; Decision eligibility remains distinct from Positive Determination; every Decision has a reconstructable basis; Positive Determination remains distinct from legal taxability; Conditional Determination preserves its qualifications; Deferred Determination remains distinct from Rejected Determination; Rejected Determination does not imply legal non-taxability; ambiguous Decisions remain visible; conflicted Decisions remain visible; conflict is not resolved merely by convenience; Decision rationale remains reconstructable; Decision provenance remains available; Decision authority or process reference remains identifiable; Decision time remains distinct from Event Time; operational finality remains distinct from legal finality; Decision logic remains methodologically consistent; AI or automated Decision proposals remain subject to the same governance requirements; technical system status does not substitute for Determination Decision; accounting, invoice, payment, blockchain, and smart-contract status do not substitute for Decision governance; Merge or Split does not automatically transfer a prior Decision; cross-system duplication does not automatically create multiple Decisions; cross-border Determination remains jurisdiction-neutral; Decision does not determine Tax Jurisdiction; Decision does not determine taxpayer status; Decision does not determine Tax Base; Decision does not determine Tax Rate; Decision does not determine Tax Liability; and the resulting Decision state is suitable for EDUM and downstream TREDS governance. Governance Logic IF EDCM has not established a sufficient Governed Determination Condition State, THEN EDDM shall not issue a Positive Determination. IF materially required conditions are sufficiently satisfied and remaining qualifications do not undermine Event Identity or downstream interpretability, THEN EDDM may issue a Positive Determination. IF the Event is sufficiently governed but bounded qualifications remain, THEN EDDM may issue a Conditional Determination. IF materially necessary governance remains unresolved but may become resolvable, THEN EDDM shall issue a Deferred Determination rather than a Rejected Determination. IF the governed structure does not support existence of a valid Tax-Relevant Event, THEN EDDM may issue a Rejected Determination. IF materially plausible competing Decision outcomes remain unresolved, THEN the Decision shall remain Ambiguous. IF materially authoritative governance inputs support incompatible outcomes, THEN the Decision shall remain Conflicted or be escalated. IF the apparent basis for Decision is a technical status, accounting classification, invoice state, payment state, blockchain finality, or model output alone, THEN that basis shall not be sufficient for a governed EDDM Decision. IF a Merge or Split has materially changed Event structure, THEN the resulting Event shall undergo appropriate Decision governance rather than inherit prior Determination automatically. IF a Positive Determination is issued, THEN it shall mean only that the Event is sufficiently governed for downstream tax evaluation. IF later information materially affects the Decision basis, THEN the Decision may be flagged for reconsideration under EDREM. IF the Decision is sufficiently governed, THEN EDDM shall establish the Governed Event Determination Decision and hand it to EDUM where uncertainty governance is required. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum EDDM implementation should support: Decision Identifier A stable identifier for the Determination Decision. Governed Event Reference The Event under Determination. Readiness State Reference The relevant EDRDM output. Condition State Reference The relevant EDCM output. Decision Eligibility State Whether the Event is eligible for formal Decision. Decision Basis Reference The governance basis supporting the Decision. Decision State Positive, Conditional, Deferred, Rejected, Ambiguous, Conflicted, or Escalation Required. Decision Qualification Any bounded qualification attached to the Decision. Decision Rationale The governed reasoning supporting the selected state. Material Condition Summary The materially relevant conditions supporting or preventing the Decision. Unresolved Condition Reference Any unresolved condition affecting the Decision. Decision Uncertainty State Any uncertainty identified at the Decision stage. Decision Conflict State Any conflict identified at the Decision stage. Decision Authority / Process Reference The human, automated, hybrid, delegated, or rule-governed Decision process. Decision Time The time the Decision was formally established. Decision Provenance Reference The governance lineage supporting the Decision. Decision Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the Decision. Prior Decision Reference Any previous Determination Decision for the Event. Decision Correction Reference Any correction of the Decision. Decision Escalation Reference Any escalation resulting from the Decision process. Reconsideration Flag Whether the Decision requires EDREM review. Jurisdiction-Neutrality State Confirmation that no jurisdiction-specific tax conclusion has been embedded. Taxability Boundary State Confirmation that the Decision does not determine legal taxability. Governance State The current EDDM governance state. Handoff State Whether the Decision may proceed to EDUM or downstream TREDS governance. Governance Outputs EDDM may produce: Decision Eligibility State; Decision Basis Record; Positive Determination; Conditional Determination; Deferred Determination; Rejected Determination; Ambiguous Determination; Conflicted Determination; Decision Qualification; Decision Rationale; Decision Provenance Record; Decision Authority Reference; Decision Traceability Record; Decision Correction; Decision Escalation; Reconsideration Flag; Jurisdiction-Neutral Decision State; and the principal output: Governed Event Determination Decision. Critical Distinctions Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Decision. Decision Initiation ≠ Positive Determination. Decision Eligible ≠ Determination Positive. Decision Output Without Decision Basis ≠ Governed Decision. Positive Event Determination ≠ Positive Tax Determination. Conditional Determination ≠ Unqualified Determination. Deferred Determination ≠ Rejected Determination. Rejected Determination ≠ Legal Non-Taxability. Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Choose the Convenient Decision. Decision Conflict ≠ Decision Discretion without Governance Basis. Operational Decision Finality ≠ Legal Finality. Decision Consistency ≠ Mechanical Uniformity. Decision Provenance ≠ Identity Provenance. Decision Time ≠ Event Time. Decision Sequence ≠ Event Sequence. Low Tax Relevance under Law ≠ TREGA™ Rejection Criterion. Decision ≠ Readiness Assessment. Decision ≠ Condition Evaluation. Decision Uncertainty Recognition ≠ Full Uncertainty Governance. Decision Change ≠ Determination Reconsideration by default. Recognition Decision ≠ Determination Decision. Positive Decision ≠ Formation Authority. Decision ≠ Boundary Redetermination. Event Determination Decision ≠ Legal Tax Point Determination. Positive Determination ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination. Positive Determination ≠ Taxpayer Determination. Positive Determination ≠ Tax Base Determination. Decision ≠ Relationship Governance. Merged Event ≠ Automatically Determined Event. Split Event ≠ Automatically Determined Event. System Status ≠ Governed Event Determination Decision. Accounting Classification ≠ Event Determination Decision. Invoice Status ≠ Event Determination Decision. Payment Completion ≠ Event Determination Decision. Blockchain Finality ≠ Event Determination Decision. Smart-Contract Completion ≠ Event Determination Decision. AI Classification ≠ Governed Determination Decision. Model Confidence ≠ Decision. Automated Decision ≠ Ungoverned Decision. Multiple Records ≠ Multiple Determination Decisions by default. Multiple Organizational Views ≠ Multiple Event Realities. Cross-Border Positive Determination ≠ Jurisdiction Allocation. Jurisdiction-Neutral Determination ≠ Jurisdictional Tax Decision. Event Determination Decision ≠ Taxability Determination. Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination. Event Determination Decision ≠ Taxpayer Determination. Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Base Determination. Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Rate Determination. Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Period Determination. Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Liability Determination. Event Determination Decision ≠ Legal Tax Characterization. Decision Supersession ≠ Decision Erasure. Decision Correction ≠ Silent Replacement. Enterprise Application EDDM provides the formal decision point at which a sufficiently governed Event receives its TREGA™ Determination status. A typical operational path is: EDRDM — Governed Determination Readiness State → EDCM — Governed Determination Condition State → EDDM — Governed Event Determination Decision → EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty Governance → EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration → Determined Tax-Relevant Event This gives enterprises a clear, reviewable answer to whether a governed Event can formally enter downstream tax infrastructure without allowing the Event layer itself to become a tax engine. Use Case 1 — Cross-Border Marketplace Event with Conditional Determination A marketplace Event has completed Readiness governance and its materially necessary Determination Conditions are satisfied. However, one bounded digital Location qualification remains. The uncertainty does not undermine Event Identity, Formation, Boundary, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationships. EDDM issues a Conditional Determination and preserves the Location qualification for downstream processing. The Event becomes eligible for jurisdiction-specific analysis. EDDM does not determine which jurisdiction has taxing authority. Use Case 2 — Machine-Generated Record Rejected as a Tax-Relevant Event An autonomous industrial system generates a technical record every time a machine changes operating state. One record enters TREGA™ because a downstream accounting system incorrectly treats each machine state change as a separate economic event. Upstream governance establishes that the state change is merely part of an already-governed service Event and does not possess independent Event Formation or Boundary. EDDM therefore issues a Rejected Determination for the apparent standalone Event. The rejection does not mean the broader service is non-taxable. It means only that the technical machine-state record does not qualify as an independent Tax-Relevant Event. Canonical Boundary EDDM owns the governance of Decision initiation, Decision eligibility, Decision basis, Positive Determination, Conditional Determination, Deferred Determination, Rejected Determination, Ambiguous Determination, Conflicted Determination, Decision qualification, Decision rationale, Decision consistency, Decision provenance, Decision authority reference, Decision timing, Decision traceability, Decision correction, Decision escalation, and establishment of the Governed Event Determination Decision. EDDM does not perform Determination Readiness governance, Determination Condition governance, full Determination Uncertainty governance, or Determination Reconsideration. It does not perform Event Context, Recognition, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationship governance. It does not determine legal taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, legal tax point, Tax Period, Tax Base, Tax Rate, Tax Liability, exemption, deduction, filing obligation, payment, collection, enforcement, or any other jurisdiction-specific legal tax consequence. Its governance begins when EDCM establishes a Governed Determination Condition State suitable for Decision. Its governance ends when a formal Governed Event Determination Decision has been established for handoff to EDUM and the remaining TREDS process. Canonical Handoff EDCM — Governed Determination Condition State ↓ EDDM — Governed Event Determination Decision ↓ EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty Governance Canonical Closing Statement EDDM converts governed readiness and explicit determination conditions into a formal Event Determination Decision without allowing that decision to become a legal tax conclusion. The decision establishes whether TREGA™ recognizes a sufficiently governed Tax-Relevant Event. It does not decide what any jurisdiction must tax. Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Decision. Positive Event Determination ≠ Positive Tax Determination. TREGA™ governs the event. The jurisdiction governs the tax.

title: OOF™ The Event Determination Readiness Module (EDRDM) governs whether an event
text: OOF™ The Event Determination Readiness Module (EDRDM) governs whether an event The Event Determination Readiness Module (EDRDM) governs whether an event OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ Parent Standard: TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard Module: EDRDM — Event Determination Readiness Module Operational Layer: Event Determination Readiness Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Event Determination Readiness Origin ID: TREGA-TREDS-EDRDM-001 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 2 September 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Event Determination Readiness Module (EDRDM) governs whether an event that has passed through the preceding TREGA™ governance layers is sufficiently prepared to enter formal Tax-Relevant Event Determination. EDRDM evaluates the availability, material completeness, coherence, accessibility, stability, and governance status of the upstream Event structures required for Determination. Its principal transition is: Governed Event Relationship Structure + Upstream Governance States ↓ Determination Readiness Governance ↓ Governed Determination Readiness State EDRDM does not determine whether the event is a Tax-Relevant Event. It determines whether the event is ready for that question to be formally evaluated. The foundational distinction is: Determination Readiness ≠ Event Determination. Operational Role An event should not enter formal Determination merely because a technical record exists or because upstream processing has reached TREDS. Before Determination Conditions can be evaluated, the system must establish whether the necessary Event governance is actually available and sufficiently mature. EDRDM provides this entry control. It prevents formal Determination from beginning where materially necessary upstream governance is: absent; incomplete; inaccessible; structurally inconsistent; materially unstable; unresolved; or not sufficiently traceable. The module therefore functions as the readiness gate of TREDS. Internal Module Flow TREDS operates through: EDRDM — Event Determination Readiness ↓ EDCM — Event Determination Conditions ↓ EDDM — Event Determination Decision ↓ EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty ↓ EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration ↓ Determined Tax-Relevant Event EDRDM is the first Core Module. Its principal output is passed to EDCM. Operational Transition The canonical operational transition is: Governed Event Relationship Structure + Relevant Upstream Governance Outputs ↓ Readiness Evaluation ↓ Governed Determination Readiness State Possible outcomes include: Ready Conditionally Ready Not Ready Readiness Ambiguous Readiness Conflicted Readiness Escalation Required EDRDM does not convert any of these states into a positive Event Determination. Operational Space EDRDM governs: readiness initiation; upstream governance availability; required-input identification; input accessibility; material completeness; governance-state sufficiency; cross-layer coherence screening; unresolved-state screening; upstream conflict screening; upstream uncertainty screening; stability screening; traceability availability; dependency on missing governance; readiness qualification; readiness deferral; readiness ambiguity; readiness conflict; upstream referral; readiness reassessment; and readiness-specific traceability. Operational Scope EDRDM may evaluate readiness for events originating from: enterprise systems; ERP environments; commerce; marketplaces; banking; payments; accounting; logistics; supply chains; digital platforms; blockchain infrastructure; digital assets; smart contracts; AI agents; autonomous systems; industrial infrastructure; energy systems; distributed systems; cross-border operations; machine-to-machine activity; and future machine economies. The readiness principle remains independent of the technology producing the event. Readiness Object The Readiness Object is the governed Event representation submitted for Determination Readiness evaluation together with its relevant upstream governance states. It shall be distinguishable from raw technical records. Technical Record ≠ Readiness Object by default. The Readiness Object represents the governed Event structure, not merely its source data. Readiness Initiation Readiness governance begins when an event has reached the TREDS entry point and materially relevant upstream outputs are available for evaluation. Initiation shall not imply readiness. Readiness Initiation ≠ Readiness Confirmation. Required Governance Inputs EDRDM shall identify which upstream governance outputs are materially necessary for the Event under review. These may include: Event Context; Event Recognition; Event Formation; Event Boundary; Event Timing; Event Location; Event Participation; Value Association; Event Relationship Structure. Not every Event requires identical information depth. The relevant requirement depends on the governed Event structure. Context Readiness EDRDM may evaluate whether sufficient governed Event Context exists for Determination to proceed. It does not recreate Context. TRECS remains authoritative. Context Readiness ≠ Context Determination. Recognition Readiness The event should have a valid Recognition lineage where applicable. EDRDM may identify an unresolved Recognition problem. It does not reperform Event Recognition. Recognition Readiness ≠ Event Recognition. Formation Readiness Event Formation must be sufficiently governed for Determination evaluation. Where it remains materially unclear whether: an Event exists; one or several Events exist; components belong to the same Event; readiness may fail. Formation Uncertainty ≠ Determination Readiness by default. TREFS remains authoritative. Boundary Readiness The Event Boundary shall be sufficiently governed where material. An event whose material scope remains unresolved may not be ready. Boundary Availability ≠ Boundary Readiness. A boundary record may exist while still carrying material unresolved conflict. Timing Readiness Relevant Event Timing shall be sufficiently governed where timing materially affects Event interpretation. EDRDM does not determine Event Time or legal tax point. Timing Readiness ≠ Tax Timing Determination. Location Readiness Relevant Event Location information shall be sufficiently governed where location materially contributes to downstream Event interpretation. EDRDM does not determine Tax Jurisdiction. Location Readiness ≠ Jurisdiction Determination. Participation Readiness Material participants and their Event Participation should be sufficiently represented where required. EDRDM does not determine taxpayer status. Participation Readiness ≠ Taxpayer Determination. Value Association Readiness Where value is materially associated with the Event, the relevant TRVAS governance should be sufficiently available. EDRDM does not determine taxable value or Tax Base. Value Association Readiness ≠ Tax Base Readiness. Relationship Readiness The Governed Event Relationship Structure produced by TRERLS is a principal input to TREDS. EDRDM shall establish whether materially relevant relationships have been sufficiently governed for Determination evaluation. It does not recreate those relationships. Relationship Readiness ≠ Relationship Determination. Input Availability A governance result cannot support readiness if it is unavailable to the Determination process. EDRDM shall therefore distinguish between: governance not performed; governance performed but unavailable; governance available but incomplete; governance available but unresolved; governance sufficiently available. Existing Information ≠ Available Governance. Input Accessibility Required governance information should be accessible in a form usable by the Determination process. Accessibility may be affected by: incompatible systems; inaccessible records; broken references; missing identifiers; unavailable external sources; or failed data exchange. Technical accessibility shall not be confused with substantive sufficiency. Accessible Data ≠ Sufficient Governance. Material Completeness Readiness does not require every possible field or record. It requires materially necessary governance. EDRDM shall distinguish: complete enough for Determination; conditionally complete; materially incomplete; immaterially incomplete. Material Completeness ≠ Total Data Completeness. Missing Information Missing information shall be evaluated according to materiality. If missing information cannot materially alter Event interpretation, it may not prevent readiness. If it could materially alter: Event Identity; Formation; Boundary; Participation; Value Association; Relationship structure; readiness may be blocked. Missing Data ≠ Automatic Readiness Failure. Immaterial Missing Information An event may remain ready where absent information is not necessary for Event Determination. EDRDM should avoid unnecessary governance burden. More Data ≠ Greater Readiness by default. Material Missing Information Materially missing governance shall be identified explicitly. Readiness shall not be declared merely because downstream processing expects an answer. Processing Demand ≠ Readiness. Governance-State Sufficiency An upstream governance output may exist but remain in a state unsuitable for Determination. Examples include: unresolved; conflicted; under reconsideration; structurally incomplete; provisional where finality is materially required. EDRDM evaluates whether the state is sufficient for entry into Determination Conditions governance. Cross-Layer Coherence EDRDM shall screen whether materially relevant upstream outputs are mutually coherent enough to proceed. Examples of potential conflicts include: Formation inconsistent with Boundary; Timing inconsistent with Event Formation; Participant association outside the governed Boundary; Value associated with another Event; Relationship structure inconsistent with Event Identity. EDRDM identifies the readiness impact. It does not assume ownership of the underlying issue. Coherence Failure A material contradiction may produce a Not Ready or Conflicted state. Available Outputs ≠ Coherent Outputs. The existence of every required governance record does not establish readiness if those records materially contradict one another. Upstream Uncertainty Upstream uncertainty shall be evaluated according to its effect on readiness. Bounded uncertainty may permit Conditional Readiness. Material unresolved uncertainty may prevent readiness. Uncertainty ≠ Automatic Not Ready State. Upstream Conflict Material conflict shall remain visible. EDRDM shall not resolve conflicts by selecting whichever result enables Determination. Readiness Pressure ≠ Permission to Ignore Conflict. Readiness Stability The Event structure should be sufficiently stable for formal Determination evaluation. An event undergoing major Formation, Boundary, Merge, Split, or Relationship reconsideration may not yet be ready. Readiness Stability ≠ Permanent Finality. Operationally sufficient stability is enough. Pending Merge or Split Where ERLMM identifies an unresolved Merge or Split Candidate that could materially change Event Identity, the Event may not be ready for Determination. Unresolved Structural Change ≠ Stable Readiness. Correction in Progress A minor correction need not always prevent readiness. The materiality of the correction shall govern the readiness effect. Correction in Progress ≠ Automatic Readiness Failure. Traceability Readiness Sufficient upstream traceability should exist to reconstruct the Event governance relied upon during Determination. EDRDM does not perform full audit governance. However, an Event whose governing basis cannot be reconstructed may not be ready. Governance Result Without Traceability ≠ Reliable Readiness by default. Identifier Continuity The Event and relevant upstream outputs should be sufficiently linked through stable references. Broken or ambiguous identifiers may create readiness problems where they prevent reliable association. Record Proximity ≠ Identity Continuity. Cross-System Readiness An Event may be constructed across multiple systems. Readiness shall depend on the governed Event representation rather than the number of systems involved. Multiple Systems ≠ Reduced Readiness by default. Fragmentation matters only where it prevents sufficient governance. Cross-Organization Readiness An Event may involve multiple organizations. EDRDM may evaluate whether required governance information from those organizations is sufficiently available. It does not determine accountability or taxpayer status. Cross-Border Readiness An Event may span multiple countries. Cross-border complexity may increase governance requirements but does not prevent readiness by itself. Cross-Border Event ≠ Not Ready Event. EDRDM does not determine Tax Jurisdiction. Multi-Jurisdiction Readiness An Event should be capable of supporting downstream jurisdiction-specific evaluation without requiring TREGA™ to select a jurisdiction. The objective is: One Governed Event ↓ One Determination Readiness Assessment ↓ Multiple Potential Jurisdictional Evaluations Multi-Jurisdiction Readiness ≠ Jurisdiction Determination. Blockchain Readiness Blockchain data may provide strong technical traceability while leaving material Event governance unresolved. A transaction hash does not establish readiness. Blockchain Finality ≠ Event Determination Readiness. Off-chain Formation, Participation, Value, or Relationship governance may still be required. Smart-Contract Readiness Completed smart-contract execution does not establish that the resulting Event structure is ready. Execution Completion ≠ Determination Readiness. AI-Agent Readiness An AI agent may produce structured records automatically. Automation does not eliminate governance requirements. Machine-Generated Structure ≠ Governed Readiness. Machine-System Readiness High-frequency machine activity may produce millions of operational records. EDRDM evaluates the governed Event, not record volume. More Machine Records ≠ Greater Readiness. Automated Readiness Assessment Readiness assessment may be partially or fully automated. However, automated processing shall apply the same governance requirements. Automated Readiness Score ≠ Governed Readiness State. A score may support the process but does not replace the governed outcome. Readiness Qualification Where the Event is sufficiently prepared but bounded limitations remain, EDRDM may establish Conditionally Ready. The qualification shall identify the remaining limitation. Conditionally Ready ≠ Fully Ready. Not Ready State An Event shall be Not Ready where materially necessary governance is absent, inaccessible, unstable, incoherent, or unresolved to a degree that prevents meaningful Determination Conditions evaluation. Not Ready ≠ Not Tax-Relevant. It means only that formal Determination cannot yet proceed reliably. Readiness Ambiguity Readiness may be ambiguous where it is unclear whether missing or unresolved governance is materially necessary. The ambiguity shall remain explicit. Readiness Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Assume Readiness. Readiness Conflict Readiness may be conflicted where materially relevant governance sources support incompatible readiness conclusions. The conflict shall remain visible until sufficiently resolved. Upstream Referral Where readiness fails because of an upstream governance issue, EDRDM shall refer the issue to the appropriate Parent Standard. Typical routing includes: Context ↓ TRECS Recognition ↓ TRERS Formation ↓ TREFS Boundary ↓ TREBS Timing ↓ TRETS Location ↓ TRELS Participation ↓ TREPS Value Association ↓ TRVAS Event Relationships ↓ TRERLS EDRDM does not silently repair upstream governance. Readiness Reassessment An Event previously classified Not Ready, Conditionally Ready, Ambiguous, or Conflicted may be reassessed when relevant governance changes. The prior readiness state shall remain traceable. Readiness Reassessment ≠ Historical Erasure. Readiness Expiration Where materially relevant upstream governance changes after readiness was established, the readiness state may cease to be reliable. EDRDM may require reassessment. Prior Readiness ≠ Permanent Readiness. Readiness and Determination Conditions EDRDM determines whether the Event may enter the next module. EDCM then governs whether the actual Determination Conditions are satisfied. This distinction is essential. Ready for Condition Evaluation ≠ Conditions Satisfied. Readiness and Determination Decision EDRDM does not issue: Positive Determination; Rejected Determination; legal tax conclusion; or Taxability Determination. Those functions remain downstream. Ready ≠ Determined. Readiness and Taxability An Event may be fully Ready and later produce no tax consequence under applicable law. Conversely, a potentially taxable activity may remain Not Ready because Event governance is insufficient. Therefore: Determination Readiness ≠ Taxability. Readiness and Tax Jurisdiction Sufficient Location governance may contribute to readiness. EDRDM does not convert Location into Tax Jurisdiction. Location Readiness ≠ Tax Jurisdiction. Readiness and Taxpayer Sufficient Participation governance may contribute to readiness. EDRDM does not identify the taxpayer. Participation Readiness ≠ Taxpayer Readiness. Readiness and Tax Base Sufficient Value Association may contribute to readiness. EDRDM does not establish taxable amount. Value Readiness ≠ Tax Base Determination. Readiness and Legal Tax Point Sufficient Event Timing may contribute to readiness. EDRDM does not establish a legal tax point. Timing Readiness ≠ Legal Tax Point. Governance States EDRDM may represent: Readiness Not Initiated Readiness Governance Initiated Required Inputs Identified Inputs Partially Available Inputs Available Materially Incomplete Conditionally Complete Materially Complete Coherence Review Required Coherence Sufficient Readiness Unstable Readiness Ambiguous Readiness Conflicted Upstream Referral Required Not Ready Conditionally Ready Ready Readiness Under Reassessment Governed Determination Readiness State Established Governance Requirements EDRDM implementations shall ensure that: readiness is evaluated before formal Determination Conditions; readiness remains distinct from Event Determination; materially required upstream governance is identifiable; upstream governance availability is distinguishable from substantive sufficiency; technical accessibility is distinguishable from governance completeness; material completeness is distinguished from total data completeness; immaterial missing information does not automatically block readiness; materially missing governance remains visible; cross-layer coherence is screened; material contradictions are not ignored; upstream uncertainty is evaluated according to material effect; upstream conflict remains visible; unstable Event structures are not automatically declared ready; unresolved Merge or Split issues are considered where material; traceability availability is considered; identifier continuity is considered where necessary; cross-system fragmentation does not automatically prevent readiness; cross-border complexity does not determine Tax Jurisdiction; blockchain finality does not substitute for Event governance; machine-generated information remains subject to the same readiness principles; automated readiness scores do not replace governed readiness states; upstream governance failures are referred to the authoritative layer; readiness reassessment preserves history; readiness remains distinct from Determination Conditions; readiness remains distinct from Determination Decision; and readiness remains distinct from legal taxability. Governance Logic IF materially necessary upstream governance cannot be identified, THEN Determination Readiness shall not be confirmed. IF required upstream governance is materially unavailable, THEN the Event shall remain Not Ready or otherwise qualified. IF required governance exists but contains material unresolved contradiction, THEN readiness shall remain Conflicted, Ambiguous, or Not Ready according to impact. IF missing information is immaterial to Event Determination, THEN its absence shall not automatically prevent readiness. IF missing information could materially alter Event Identity, Formation, Boundary, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationships, THEN readiness shall not be confirmed until the issue is sufficiently governed. IF bounded uncertainty exists but the Event remains sufficiently structured for Determination Conditions evaluation, THEN Conditional Readiness may be established. IF an unresolved Merge or Split Candidate could materially alter Event Identity, THEN readiness shall be withheld or qualified. IF upstream governance is sufficiently available, materially complete, coherent, stable, and traceable, THEN the Event may be classified Ready. IF a readiness failure belongs to an upstream Parent Standard, THEN the issue shall be referred upstream rather than silently resolved inside EDRDM. IF a previously established readiness state is materially affected by new governance information, THEN readiness shall be reassessed. IF the Event reaches a sufficient Governed Determination Readiness State, THEN it shall proceed to EDCM for Event Determination Conditions governance. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum EDRDM implementation should support: Readiness Assessment Identifier A stable identifier for the readiness governance process. Governed Event Reference The Event entering Determination Readiness governance. Event Relationship Structure Reference The TRERLS output supplied to TREDS. Context Governance Reference Relevant TRECS output and governance state. Recognition Governance Reference Relevant TRERS output and governance state. Formation Governance Reference Relevant TREFS output and governance state. Boundary Governance Reference Relevant TREBS output and governance state. Timing Governance Reference Relevant TRETS output and governance state. Location Governance Reference Relevant TRELS output and governance state. Participation Governance Reference Relevant TREPS output and governance state. Value Association Reference Relevant TRVAS output and governance state. Relationship Governance Reference Relevant TRERLS output and governance state. Required Input State Which upstream governance inputs are materially required. Input Availability State Whether those inputs are available. Material Completeness State Whether materially necessary governance is sufficiently complete. Coherence State Whether upstream governance is sufficiently coherent. Stability State Whether Event structure is sufficiently stable. Unresolved Governance State Any material unresolved upstream condition. Upstream Uncertainty State Relevant uncertainty affecting readiness. Upstream Conflict State Relevant conflict affecting readiness. Structural Change State Any material pending Merge, Split, or other structural reconsideration. Traceability Availability State Whether the governance basis can be reconstructed. Upstream Referral Reference Any referral to another TREGA™ Parent Standard. Readiness Qualification Any bounded qualification attached to readiness. Readiness Decision Ready, Conditionally Ready, Not Ready, Ambiguous, Conflicted, or Escalation Required. Prior Readiness Reference Any previous readiness state. Reassessment Reference Any later readiness reassessment. Readiness Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the readiness evaluation. Governance State The current EDRDM governance state. Handoff State Whether the Event may proceed to EDCM. Governance Outputs EDRDM may produce: Required Governance Input Set; Input Availability State; Material Completeness State; Coherence State; Stability State; Upstream Uncertainty State; Upstream Conflict State; Structural Change State; Traceability Readiness State; Upstream Referral; Readiness Qualification; Not Ready Determination; Conditional Readiness State; Ready State; Readiness Ambiguity State; Readiness Conflict State; Readiness Reassessment Record; Readiness Traceability Record; and the principal output: Governed Determination Readiness State. Critical Distinctions Determination Readiness ≠ Event Determination. Technical Record ≠ Readiness Object by default. Readiness Initiation ≠ Readiness Confirmation. Context Readiness ≠ Context Determination. Recognition Readiness ≠ Event Recognition. Formation Uncertainty ≠ Determination Readiness by default. Boundary Availability ≠ Boundary Readiness. Timing Readiness ≠ Tax Timing Determination. Location Readiness ≠ Jurisdiction Determination. Participation Readiness ≠ Taxpayer Determination. Value Association Readiness ≠ Tax Base Readiness. Relationship Readiness ≠ Relationship Determination. Existing Information ≠ Available Governance. Accessible Data ≠ Sufficient Governance. Material Completeness ≠ Total Data Completeness. Missing Data ≠ Automatic Readiness Failure. More Data ≠ Greater Readiness by default. Processing Demand ≠ Readiness. Available Outputs ≠ Coherent Outputs. Uncertainty ≠ Automatic Not Ready State. Readiness Pressure ≠ Permission to Ignore Conflict. Readiness Stability ≠ Permanent Finality. Unresolved Structural Change ≠ Stable Readiness. Governance Result Without Traceability ≠ Reliable Readiness by default. Blockchain Finality ≠ Event Determination Readiness. Execution Completion ≠ Determination Readiness. Machine-Generated Structure ≠ Governed Readiness. Automated Readiness Score ≠ Governed Readiness State. Conditionally Ready ≠ Fully Ready. Not Ready ≠ Not Tax-Relevant. Readiness Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Assume Readiness. Readiness Reassessment ≠ Historical Erasure. Prior Readiness ≠ Permanent Readiness. Ready for Condition Evaluation ≠ Conditions Satisfied. Ready ≠ Determined. Determination Readiness ≠ Taxability. Enterprise Application EDRDM provides the practical entry gate to formal Tax-Relevant Event Determination. A typical operational path is: Operational / Digital Systems → TREGA™ Upstream Event Governance → TRERLS — Governed Event Relationship Structure → EDRDM — Governed Determination Readiness State → EDCM — Event Determination Conditions → EDDM — Event Determination Decision This allows enterprises to identify incomplete or structurally unstable Event representations before they enter formal Determination or downstream tax infrastructure. Use Case 1 — Cross-Border Marketplace Event with Missing Participation Governance A marketplace Event has a governed Context, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Value Association, and Relationship Structure. However, the Event Participation structure remains materially unresolved because two entities may have performed the relevant merchant function. EDRDM identifies Participation as materially necessary for Determination and establishes a Not Ready state. The issue is referred to TREPS. Once Participation governance is sufficiently resolved, EDRDM reassesses the Event and may establish Ready. The module does not determine which participant is legally the taxpayer. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Service Event with Bounded Location Uncertainty An autonomous infrastructure service has governed Formation, Boundary, Timing, machine Participation, Value Association, and Event Relationships. The service spans distributed infrastructure and its exact digital Location contains bounded uncertainty. EDRDM evaluates whether that uncertainty prevents formal Determination Conditions evaluation. Where the uncertainty does not alter Event Identity or prevent meaningful downstream jurisdiction-specific analysis, EDRDM may establish Conditionally Ready while preserving the Location qualification. The module does not determine Tax Jurisdiction. Canonical Boundary EDRDM owns the governance of Determination Readiness initiation, required-input identification, upstream governance availability, material completeness, coherence screening, stability screening, unresolved-state screening, uncertainty and conflict impact on readiness, traceability readiness, upstream referral, readiness qualification, readiness reassessment, and establishment of the Governed Determination Readiness State. EDRDM does not perform Event Context, Recognition, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationship governance itself. It does not determine whether the Event satisfies formal Determination Conditions, does not issue the final Event Determination Decision, and does not determine taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, legal tax point, Tax Base, Tax Rate, Tax Liability, or another jurisdiction-specific legal consequence. Its governance begins when a governed Event and materially relevant upstream TREGA™ outputs are presented for Determination Readiness evaluation. Its governance ends when the Event has received a Governed Determination Readiness State suitable for handoff to EDCM. Canonical Handoff TRERLS — Governed Event Relationship Structure ↓ EDRDM — Governed Determination Readiness State ↓ EDCM — Event Determination Conditions Governance Canonical Closing Statement EDRDM ensures that formal Event Determination begins only when the Event Reality required to support that determination is sufficiently available, coherent, stable, and reconstructable. Readiness opens the door to determination. It does not predetermine what the determination will be. Determination Readiness ≠ Event Determination. Ready ≠ Determined.

title: OOF™ The Event Determination Reconsideration Module (EDREM) governs when and
text: OOF™ The Event Determination Reconsideration Module (EDREM) governs when and The Event Determination Reconsideration Module (EDREM) governs when and OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ Parent Standard: TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard Module: EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration Module Operational Layer: Event Determination Reconsideration Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Event Determination Reconsideration Origin ID: TREGA-TREDS-EDREM-005 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 2 September 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Event Determination Reconsideration Module (EDREM) governs when and how an existing Tax-Relevant Event Determination is reopened for formal review after materially relevant new information, corrected governance, changed Event structure, resolved uncertainty, new conflict, superseding upstream output, or another legitimate reconsideration trigger emerges. EDREM governs the transition from an existing Determination state to a reviewed Determination state while preserving the complete history of the prior Decision. Its principal transition is: Governed Event Determination Decision + Reconsideration Trigger ↓ Reconsideration Governance ↓ Confirmed, Amended, Replaced, Deferred, Rejected, or Superseded Determination State EDREM does not silently rewrite the prior Decision. Its foundational distinction is: Determination Reconsideration ≠ Historical Erasure. Operational Role Tax-Relevant Event Determination occurs at a specific governance state and time. Operational reality may later change or become better understood. Examples include: corrected Event Formation; revised Event Boundary; new participant information; corrected Value Association; resolved Event Relationship conflict; new Merge or Split result; newly available evidence; resolved uncertainty; discovery of duplicate Event representation; or material error in the prior Determination basis. EDREM provides the controlled mechanism for reopening the existing Determination without destroying its historical validity as a prior governance state. The core question is: Does new or changed governance materially affect the existing Determination, and if so, what governed Determination state should replace or qualify it? Internal Module Flow TREDS operates through: EDRDM — Event Determination Readiness ↓ EDCM — Event Determination Conditions ↓ EDDM — Event Determination Decision ↓ EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty ↓ EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration ↓ Determined Tax-Relevant Event EDREM is the final Core Module of TREDS. Its output becomes the final TREDS Determination state for handoff to TREGS. Operational Transition The canonical transition is: Existing Determination State + Material Reconsideration Trigger ↓ Trigger Qualification ↓ Reconsideration Scope ↓ Re-evaluation ↓ Reconsideration Outcome ↓ Final Determination State Possible outcomes include: Determination Confirmed Determination Confirmed with Qualification Determination Amended Determination Replaced Determination Deferred Determination Rejected Determination Superseded Reconsideration Inconclusive Further Upstream Governance Required Operational Space EDREM governs: reconsideration trigger identification; trigger legitimacy; trigger materiality; reconsideration initiation; reconsideration scope; affected Decision dimension; upstream-change impact; Decision-basis change; uncertainty-resolution impact; conflict-resolution impact; correction impact; Merge/Split impact; duplicate-event impact; reconsideration qualification; Determination confirmation; Determination amendment; Determination replacement; Determination deferral; Determination rejection; Determination supersession; reconsideration traceability; prior-state preservation; downstream notification; and final TREDS Determination handoff. Operational Scope EDREM applies to reconsideration of Determination Decisions arising from: commerce; marketplaces; payments; banking; accounting; ERP systems; logistics; supply chains; digital platforms; digital assets; blockchain systems; smart contracts; AI agents; autonomous systems; industrial systems; distributed infrastructure; cross-border operations; machine-to-machine environments; and future machine economies. Its governance logic remains technology-neutral and jurisdiction-neutral. Reconsideration Object The Reconsideration Object is an existing Governed Event Determination Decision whose continued validity has become materially reviewable. The Reconsideration Object shall include: the existing Determination Decision; its Decision basis; relevant qualifications; relevant uncertainty state; the new or changed governance information; the reconsideration trigger. Existing Decision ≠ Immutable Decision. Reconsideration Trigger A Reconsideration Trigger is a materially relevant change or discovery capable of affecting the validity, qualification, or status of an existing Determination. Potential triggers include: corrected upstream governance; newly available information; resolved uncertainty; newly discovered uncertainty; resolved conflict; newly discovered conflict; Event Merge; Event Split; Event correction; duplicate-event discovery; superseded source; materially changed Event Relationship; materially changed Value Association; materially changed Participation; or identified Decision error. New Information ≠ Automatic Reconsideration Trigger. The information must be materially relevant to the existing Determination. Trigger Legitimacy EDREM shall determine whether the reconsideration trigger is methodologically legitimate. A Decision shall not be reopened solely because: a different tax result is desired; reporting becomes inconvenient; commercial preference changes; a jurisdiction produces an unfavorable legal interpretation; a technical system wishes to rewrite history. Preferred Tax Outcome ≠ Reconsideration Basis. Trigger Materiality A trigger is material where it could alter: Event Identity; Event Formation; Event Boundary; Determination Conditions; Determination Decision; Determination qualification; Event count; Participation structure; Value Association; Event Relationships; or downstream usability. Changed Information ≠ Material Change by default. Reconsideration Initiation Reconsideration shall begin only after a legitimate material trigger is established. The prior Decision remains the historical Decision until the reconsideration process produces a governed result. Reconsideration Initiation ≠ Prior Decision Cancellation. Reconsideration Scope EDREM shall define the scope of the reconsideration. The review may affect: one Decision qualification; one governance dependency; one Decision basis element; the complete Determination Decision; or several related Event Determinations. Scope should be no broader than materially necessary. Local Change ≠ Full Determination Reopening by default. Decision-Basis Change Where the basis supporting a prior Decision changes materially, EDREM shall assess whether that change affects the Decision. A changed basis does not automatically require a changed outcome. Changed Basis ≠ Changed Decision by default. Upstream Governance Change An upstream Parent Standard may produce a corrected or superseded governance result. Examples include: revised Formation; revised Boundary; corrected Timing; corrected Location; changed Participation; corrected Value Association; revised Relationship structure. EDREM evaluates the effect on Determination. It does not redo the upstream governance. Formation Reconsideration Impact A materially changed Event Formation may require complete Determination reconsideration. Changed Formation ≠ Automatic Continuity of Prior Determination. TREFS remains authoritative for Formation. Boundary Reconsideration Impact If Event Boundary changes materially, the prior Determination may no longer apply to the same Event structure. Changed Boundary ≠ Same Determination by default. TREBS remains authoritative. Timing Reconsideration Impact A corrected Event Time may or may not affect the Determination. EDREM evaluates material impact. It does not determine legal tax timing. Corrected Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point Reconsideration. Location Reconsideration Impact Changed Location information may affect Event Determination qualification. EDREM does not determine Tax Jurisdiction. Location Reconsideration ≠ Jurisdiction Reconsideration. Participation Reconsideration Impact A corrected Participant structure may materially affect the Determination. EDREM evaluates Determination impact only. Participant Reconsideration ≠ Taxpayer Reconsideration. Value Association Reconsideration Impact Corrected Value Association may require Determination reconsideration. EDREM does not determine taxable value or Tax Base. Value Reconsideration ≠ Tax Base Recalculation. Relationship Reconsideration Impact Corrected Event Relationships may affect whether prior Determination remains valid. Examples include: newly established dependency; changed sequence; revised grouping; Event Merge; Event Split. TRERLS remains authoritative for the relationship structure. Merge Impact Where multiple previously determined Events are governed into one Event through ERLMM, the prior Determination states shall not simply collapse into the new Event. The resulting Event requires appropriate reconsideration. Merged Determinations ≠ One Determination by automatic inheritance. Split Impact Where one previously determined Event is split into multiple governed Events, the prior Decision does not automatically transfer to each resulting Event. One Prior Determination ≠ Multiple Valid Determinations after Split. Duplicate-Event Discovery A previously determined Event may later be identified as a duplicate representation of another governed Event. EDREM may supersede or reject the duplicate Determination while preserving its historical record. Duplicate Determination Correction ≠ Historical Deletion. Uncertainty Resolution Impact EDUM may resolve uncertainty that previously qualified or deferred a Decision. EDREM evaluates whether that resolution justifies: confirmation; removal of qualification; amendment; or replacement. Resolved Uncertainty ≠ Automatic Positive Determination. New Uncertainty Impact New material uncertainty may emerge after Determination. EDREM may reopen the Decision where continued reliance is no longer methodologically justified. Conflict Resolution Impact A conflict may later be resolved. EDREM assesses whether the resolution changes the prior Determination. Conflict Resolution ≠ Automatic Decision Change. New Conflict Impact A new materially authoritative conflict may undermine a previously stable Decision. EDREM may require reconsideration, qualification, deferral, or upstream referral. Known Error If the prior Determination is known to contain a substantive error, EDREM shall distinguish simple correction from full reconsideration. A minor clerical error may not require reopening the Decision. A material governance error may. Clerical Correction ≠ Full Reconsideration by default. Reconsideration Qualification Reconsideration may produce a Determination that remains valid but now carries a new qualification. Any qualification shall remain explicit and traceable. Determination Confirmation The prior Determination may be Confirmed where the new information does not materially alter its basis or outcome. Confirmation should be explicit. Reconsidered and Confirmed ≠ Never Reconsidered. Confirmation with Qualification The prior Determination may remain valid while requiring a new or revised qualification. This creates: Determination Confirmed with Qualification rather than silently altering the original Decision. Determination Amendment A Determination may be Amended where part of the Decision state or qualification changes without replacing the entire Determination. The amendment shall preserve the prior state. Amendment ≠ Historical Replacement. Determination Replacement A Determination may require replacement where the new governance state materially changes the correct Determination outcome. The new Decision shall reference the replaced Decision. Replacement ≠ Erasure. Determination Deferral after Reconsideration A previously positive or conditional Decision may become Deferred where new information creates a material unresolved governance issue. Prior Positive Determination ≠ Permanent Positive Determination. Determination Rejection after Reconsideration A previously determined Event may ultimately be rejected if new governance establishes that the Event representation was invalid. For example: duplicate Event; invalid Formation; invalid standalone Event after Merge; technical operation incorrectly treated as independent Event. Reconsidered Rejection ≠ Legal Non-Taxability. Determination Supersession A new Determination may supersede a prior Decision. Supersession shall preserve: prior Decision; effective sequence; reason for supersession; new Decision; traceability between them. Supersession ≠ Deletion. Reconsideration Inconclusive Where reconsideration cannot establish a sufficiently governed outcome, the state may remain Inconclusive. Further upstream governance or uncertainty resolution may be required. Reconsideration ≠ Mandatory Definitive Outcome. Prior-State Preservation EDREM shall preserve every materially relevant prior Determination state. This enables reconstruction of: What was known ↓ What was determined ↓ What changed ↓ Why reconsideration occurred ↓ What the new Determination became This lifecycle is central to TREGA™ governance integrity. Effective-State Management EDREM shall distinguish: historical Decision state; current effective Determination; pending reconsideration state; superseded Determination. Historical State ≠ Current Effective State. Reconsideration Timing The time of reconsideration shall be distinct from: Event Time; original Decision Time; correction time; legal tax point. Reconsideration Time ≠ Event Time. Reconsideration Sequence Repeated reconsiderations may occur. For example: Initial Determination ↓ First Reconsideration ↓ Amended Determination ↓ Second Reconsideration ↓ Superseded Determination Each material state shall remain traceable. Reconsideration Frequency EDREM shall not reopen Determination unnecessarily. Repeated reconsideration without material trigger may create governance instability. Frequent Review ≠ Stronger Governance by default. Reconsideration Stability After reconsideration, the new Determination should achieve sufficient operational stability for downstream use. Operational stability does not eliminate the possibility of later reconsideration. Downstream Reliance Impact Where downstream systems have already consumed the prior Determination, EDREM should produce a state indicating whether downstream reliance may be affected. Possible states include: No Downstream Impact; Qualification Update Required; Determination Update Required; Prior Determination Withdrawal Required; Downstream Re-evaluation Required. EDREM does not perform jurisdiction-specific tax recalculation. Downstream Notification A material reconsideration outcome should be capable of notifying downstream consumers that the effective TREGA™ Determination has changed. The handoff should identify: prior Decision; new Decision; effective state; reason for change; relevant qualification. Cross-System Reconsideration The same Event may exist across multiple technical systems. A reconsideration shall govern the Event Determination itself rather than create independent contradictory Determinations per system. System Record Update ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default. Cross-Organization Reconsideration Several organizations may consume the same governed Event. EDREM may support distribution of the revised Determination state without deciding each organization's legal tax treatment. Cross-Border Reconsideration New cross-border information may affect Location, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationships. EDREM may reconsider the Event Determination. It does not reconsider Tax Jurisdiction itself. Cross-Border Determination Reconsideration ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Reallocation. Multi-Jurisdiction Continuity A reconsidered TREGA™ Event may continue to support multiple jurisdictional evaluations. The model becomes: One Reconsidered Governed Event ↓ Multiple Updated Jurisdictional Evaluations Each jurisdiction remains responsible for its own legal treatment. Blockchain Reconsideration Immutable ledger records do not make Event Determinations immutable. Off-chain information may reveal: incorrect participant attribution; invalid Event Formation; duplicate Event representation; changed relationship interpretation. Immutable Ledger ≠ Immutable Event Determination. Smart-Contract Reconsideration A smart contract may execute exactly as coded while the governed Event interpretation later changes. Immutable Execution ≠ Immutable Determination. AI-Agent Reconsideration AI-agent Events may require reconsideration where: agent identity mapping changes; execution role is corrected; newly available logs alter Event Formation; Value Association changes; relationship governance is revised. Agent Action History ≠ Determination Finality. Automated Reconsideration EDREM may be automated. Automation shall not permit silent rewriting of prior Determinations. An automated implementation shall preserve: trigger; prior Decision; new governance basis; scope; outcome; effective state; traceability. Automated Reconsideration ≠ Automatic Historical Rewrite. Reconsideration and Readiness A material reconsideration may require return to EDRDM where the revised Event no longer satisfies readiness requirements. EDREM shall not perform EDRDM functions itself. Reconsideration ≠ Readiness Reassessment by default. Reconsideration and Conditions Changed Event governance may require EDCM conditions to be reevaluated. EDREM may trigger that process but does not own condition evaluation. Reconsideration ≠ Condition Re-evaluation Authority. Reconsideration and Decision EDDM owns the formal Determination Decision logic. EDREM owns governance of reopening and transitioning from a prior Decision to a revised governed Decision state. Initial Decision ≠ Reconsideration Decision Process. Reconsideration and Uncertainty EDUM may produce a Reconsideration Required state. EDREM then governs the reconsideration process. Uncertainty Trigger ≠ Reconsideration Outcome. Reconsideration and Lifecycle Governance EDREM governs reconsideration within TREDS. Once the Determination is finalized, TREGS governs the Event Record and TRECLS governs longer-term Event continuity, amendment, correction, supersession, and closure. Determination Reconsideration ≠ Event Lifecycle Governance. Reconsideration and Taxability A tax authority or tax engine may later reinterpret the legal treatment of an Event. That does not automatically require TREGA™ reconsideration unless the underlying Event governance changes. Changed Tax Treatment ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default. Reconsideration and Tax Jurisdiction A jurisdiction may change its legal nexus or sourcing rules. That legal change does not itself alter TREGA™ Event Determination. Tax Jurisdiction Change ≠ Event Determination Change by default. Reconsideration and Taxpayer A legal conclusion about taxpayer identity does not redefine TREGA™ Participation unless new operational facts emerge. Taxpayer Reclassification ≠ Participation Reconsideration by default. Reconsideration and Tax Base A later Tax Base adjustment does not automatically alter Event Determination. Tax Base Adjustment ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default. Governance States EDREM may represent: Reconsideration Not Initiated Potential Trigger Identified Trigger Under Review Trigger Not Material Material Trigger Confirmed Reconsideration Initiated Reconsideration Scope Defined Upstream Review Required Determination Under Reconsideration Determination Confirmed Determination Confirmed with Qualification Determination Amended Determination Replaced Determination Deferred Determination Rejected Determination Superseded Reconsideration Inconclusive Further Governance Required Downstream Update Required Reconsideration Completed Final TREDS Determination State Established Governance Requirements EDREM implementations shall ensure that: reconsideration begins only from an existing Determination; triggers are distinguishable from ordinary new information; triggers are evaluated for legitimacy and materiality; preferred tax outcome is not a valid reconsideration basis; reconsideration initiation does not cancel the prior historical Decision; reconsideration scope is bounded to materially affected areas; changed upstream governance remains governed by its authoritative Parent Standard; Merge and Split do not automatically transfer prior Determinations; duplicate-event correction preserves history; resolved uncertainty does not automatically produce Positive Determination; newly material uncertainty can reopen a Decision; conflict resolution does not automatically require Decision change; clerical correction remains distinct from full reconsideration; confirmation, amendment, replacement, deferral, rejection, and supersession remain distinct states; prior Decision history is preserved; current effective state remains distinguishable from historical state; reconsideration time remains distinct from Event Time; repeated reconsideration requires material basis; downstream impact can be represented; downstream consumers can receive updated Determination state; immutable technical infrastructure does not make Event Determination immutable; automated reconsideration does not silently rewrite history; EDRDM, EDCM, EDDM, and EDUM ownership boundaries remain preserved; tax-law changes do not automatically trigger TREGA™ reconsideration; and the final reconsidered Determination is suitable for handoff to TREGS. Governance Logic IF no existing Governed Event Determination Decision exists, THEN EDREM shall not initiate reconsideration. IF new information is not materially relevant to the existing Determination, THEN reconsideration shall not be required. IF a proposed trigger exists only because a different tax outcome is preferred, THEN the trigger shall be rejected. IF a material upstream governance change could alter the Determination basis, THEN EDREM shall initiate or require reconsideration. IF the new information confirms the original Decision basis, THEN the Determination may be Confirmed. IF the original Decision remains valid but requires a bounded qualification, THEN the Determination may be Confirmed with Qualification. IF part of the Decision must change while the Determination remains substantially continuous, THEN the Determination may be Amended. IF the original Decision no longer represents the governed Event correctly, THEN a Replacement Determination shall be established. IF material governance remains unresolved, THEN the reconsidered Determination may become Deferred. IF new governance establishes that the apparent Event should not have been determined as a standalone Tax-Relevant Event, THEN the Determination may be Rejected or Superseded as appropriate. IF a Merge or Split materially changes Event structure, THEN prior Determinations shall not transfer automatically. IF reconsideration cannot establish a sufficiently governed outcome, THEN the state shall remain Inconclusive or Further Governance Required. IF a new Determination supersedes a prior Decision, THEN the historical Decision shall remain traceable. IF downstream systems relied on the prior Decision and the reconsidered outcome materially changes it, THEN Downstream Update Required shall be established. IF reconsideration is completed, THEN EDREM shall establish the Final TREDS Determination State for TREGS. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum EDREM implementation should support: Reconsideration Identifier A stable identifier for the reconsideration process. Governed Event Reference The Event whose Determination is under reconsideration. Existing Determination Reference The prior EDDM/TREDS Determination Decision. Existing Determination State The effective Decision before reconsideration. Reconsideration Trigger Identifier A stable reference to the triggering change or discovery. Trigger Type Correction, New Information, Uncertainty Resolution, New Uncertainty, Conflict Resolution, New Conflict, Merge, Split, Duplicate Discovery, Upstream Change, Decision Error, or other governed type. Trigger Source Reference The governance layer, system, Event, or source producing the trigger. Trigger Legitimacy State Valid, Invalid, or Under Review. Trigger Materiality State Immaterial, Material, Critical, or Unresolved. Reconsideration Scope The Decision dimension or Event structure affected. Affected Governance Layer Any upstream TREGA™ Parent Standard affected. Prior Readiness Reference Relevant EDRDM state where required. Prior Condition Reference Relevant EDCM state where required. Prior Decision Basis Reference The basis of the earlier EDDM Decision. Prior Uncertainty Reference Relevant EDUM uncertainty state. Updated Governance Reference The new or corrected governance information. Merge / Split Reference Where structural Event transformation triggered reconsideration. Duplicate Event Reference Where duplicate representation is involved. Reconsideration Outcome Confirmed, Confirmed with Qualification, Amended, Replaced, Deferred, Rejected, Superseded, Inconclusive, or Further Governance Required. Updated Determination Qualification Any qualification attached to the reconsidered state. Reconsideration Rationale The governance basis for the outcome. Prior State Preservation Reference The record linking the reconsidered state to historical Determination. Effective Determination State The currently operative TREDS Determination after reconsideration. Supersession Reference The relationship between prior and superseding Determinations. Downstream Impact State No Impact, Qualification Update Required, Determination Update Required, Withdrawal Required, or Downstream Re-evaluation Required. Downstream Notification State Whether relevant consumers have been notified of the changed Determination. Reconsideration Time The time the reconsideration outcome was established. Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the full reconsideration process. Governance State The current EDREM governance state. Handoff State Whether the final TREDS Determination is ready for TREGS. Governance Outputs EDREM may produce: Reconsideration Trigger Record; Trigger Legitimacy State; Trigger Materiality State; Reconsideration Scope; Updated Governance Reference; Determination Confirmation; Confirmation with Qualification; Determination Amendment; Determination Replacement; Determination Deferral; Determination Rejection; Determination Supersession; Reconsideration Inconclusive State; Further Governance Requirement; Prior-State Preservation Record; Effective Determination State; Downstream Impact State; Downstream Update Requirement; Reconsideration Traceability Record; and the principal output: Final TREDS Determination State. Critical Distinctions Determination Reconsideration ≠ Historical Erasure. Existing Decision ≠ Immutable Decision. New Information ≠ Automatic Reconsideration Trigger. Preferred Tax Outcome ≠ Reconsideration Basis. Changed Information ≠ Material Change by default. Reconsideration Initiation ≠ Prior Decision Cancellation. Local Change ≠ Full Determination Reopening by default. Changed Basis ≠ Changed Decision by default. Changed Formation ≠ Automatic Continuity of Prior Determination. Changed Boundary ≠ Same Determination by default. Corrected Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point Reconsideration. Location Reconsideration ≠ Jurisdiction Reconsideration. Participant Reconsideration ≠ Taxpayer Reconsideration. Value Reconsideration ≠ Tax Base Recalculation. Merged Determinations ≠ One Determination by automatic inheritance. One Prior Determination ≠ Multiple Valid Determinations after Split. Duplicate Determination Correction ≠ Historical Deletion. Resolved Uncertainty ≠ Automatic Positive Determination. Conflict Resolution ≠ Automatic Decision Change. Clerical Correction ≠ Full Reconsideration by default. Reconsidered and Confirmed ≠ Never Reconsidered. Amendment ≠ Historical Replacement. Replacement ≠ Erasure. Prior Positive Determination ≠ Permanent Positive Determination. Reconsidered Rejection ≠ Legal Non-Taxability. Supersession ≠ Deletion. Reconsideration ≠ Mandatory Definitive Outcome. Historical State ≠ Current Effective State. Reconsideration Time ≠ Event Time. Frequent Review ≠ Stronger Governance by default. System Record Update ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default. Cross-Border Determination Reconsideration ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Reallocation. Immutable Ledger ≠ Immutable Event Determination. Immutable Execution ≠ Immutable Determination. Automated Reconsideration ≠ Automatic Historical Rewrite. Reconsideration ≠ Readiness Reassessment by default. Reconsideration ≠ Condition Re-evaluation Authority. Initial Decision ≠ Reconsideration Decision Process. Uncertainty Trigger ≠ Reconsideration Outcome. Determination Reconsideration ≠ Event Lifecycle Governance. Changed Tax Treatment ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default. Tax Jurisdiction Change ≠ Event Determination Change by default. Taxpayer Reclassification ≠ Participation Reconsideration by default. Tax Base Adjustment ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default. Enterprise Application EDREM provides the controlled mechanism for maintaining Determination integrity when reality, evidence, or upstream governance changes after a Decision has already been issued. The canonical operational path is: EDDM — Governed Event Determination Decision → EDUM — Governed Determination Uncertainty State → EDREM — Final TREDS Determination State → TREGS — Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record This allows organizations to correct Determination without destroying historical governance or confusing Event reconsideration with retroactive tax-law reinterpretation. Use Case 1 — Marketplace Event Reconsidered After Event Merge A marketplace originally governs two separate Events and EDDM issues a Positive Determination for each. Later, additional operational evidence establishes that the two apparent Events were technical fragments of one economic Event. TRERLS and ERLMM govern the Merge and create a revised Event structure. EDREM identifies the Merge as a material reconsideration trigger. The two earlier Determinations are preserved historically and superseded. The merged Event is routed through the necessary TREDS governance and receives a new effective Determination state. The prior Determinations are not deleted and are not automatically inherited by the merged Event. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Service Determination Confirmed After Uncertainty Resolution An autonomous service Event received a Conditional Determination because the identity of one machine participant remained uncertain. EDUM preserved the uncertainty and triggered reconsideration once new authenticated execution records became available. TREPS updates the governed Participation state. EDREM evaluates the change and determines that the new information confirms the original Event structure while removing the prior qualification. The Determination becomes Confirmed without the previous Participation qualification. The earlier Conditional Determination remains preserved in the Event's governance history. Canonical Boundary EDREM owns the governance of Determination reconsideration triggers, trigger legitimacy, materiality, reconsideration initiation, scope, upstream-change impact, uncertainty-resolution impact, conflict-resolution impact, correction impact, Merge/Split impact, confirmation, qualification, amendment, replacement, deferral, rejection, supersession, prior-state preservation, effective-state management, downstream impact, downstream update requirements, reconsideration traceability, and establishment of the Final TREDS Determination State. EDREM does not perform Event Context, Recognition, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, Value Association, or Relationship governance. It does not independently perform Determination Readiness, Determination Conditions, initial Determination Decision, or Determination Uncertainty governance. It does not govern the broader Event lifecycle after TREDS; TREGS and TRECLS remain authoritative for Event Record Governance and Event Lifecycle & Continuity. It does not determine legal taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, Tax Base, Tax Rate, legal tax point, Tax Period, exemption, deduction, Tax Liability, filing obligation, collection, enforcement, or any other jurisdiction-specific legal tax consequence. Its governance begins when a materially legitimate trigger places an existing Determination under reconsideration. Its governance ends when the effective Final TREDS Determination State is established and ready for handoff to TREGS. Canonical Handoff EDUM — Governed Determination Uncertainty State ↓ EDREM — Final TREDS Determination State ↓ TREGS — Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record Canonical Closing Statement EDREM ensures that a Tax-Relevant Event Determination can evolve when governed reality changes without allowing the history of prior decisions to disappear. A Determination may be confirmed, amended, replaced, deferred, rejected, or superseded — but every material transition must remain reconstructable. Determination Reconsideration ≠ Historical Erasure. Supersession ≠ Deletion. Changed Tax Treatment ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default.

title: OOF™ The Event Determination Uncertainty Module (EDUM) governs how uncertainty
