text: OOF™ The Event Record Linkage Module (ERLKM) governs how a structurally The Event Record Linkage Module (ERLKM) governs how a structurally OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ Parent Standard: TREGS — Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance Standard Module: ERLKM — Event Record Linkage Module Operational Layer: Event Record Linkage Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Event Record Linkage Primary Governed Object: Governed Event Record Linkage State Origin ID: TREGA-TREGS-ERLKM-003 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 3 September 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Event Record Linkage Module (ERLKM) governs how a structurally governed Tax-Relevant Event Record is linked to the Event, related Event Records, upstream governance states, supporting records, predecessor or successor representations, and other materially relevant references required to preserve reconstructability and downstream usability. Its principal transition is: Governed Event Record Structure ↓ Event Record Linkage Governance ↓ Governed Event Record Linkage State ERLKM governs the relationship between records and references. It does not recreate the substantive Event Relationships governed by TRERLS. Its foundational distinction is: Record Linkage ≠ Event Relationship Governance. Operational Role A structurally complete Event Record may still be operationally weak if it cannot be reliably connected to the objects and governance states that give it meaning. ERLKM answers: Which records, Events, governance states, and materially relevant references must this Event Record remain linked to in order to preserve its governed meaning? Its role is to prevent: isolated records; broken Event references; lost predecessor or successor relationships; detached Determination states; disconnected supporting records; ungoverned duplicate links; ambiguous cross-system associations; and silent link loss during transformation. Internal Module Flow TREGS operates through: ERIDM — Event Record Identification ↓ ERSTM — Event Record Structure ↓ ERLKM — Event Record Linkage ↓ ERTM — Event Record Traceability ↓ ERINM — Event Record Interoperability ↓ Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record ERLKM receives: Governed Event Record Structure and produces: Governed Event Record Linkage State for ERTM. Operational Transition The canonical transition is: Governed Event Record Structure ↓ Link Requirement Identification ↓ Link Establishment ↓ Link Qualification ↓ Link Validation State ↓ Governed Event Record Linkage State Operational Space ERLKM governs: Event-to-Record linkage; Record-to-Record linkage; upstream governance references; Determination references; qualification references; uncertainty references; reconsideration references; predecessor links; successor links; related-record links; supporting-record links; duplicate-record associations; Merge/Split references; cross-system references; link type; link direction; link scope; link materiality; link validity state; link continuity; link conflict; link correction; link supersession; and linkage handoff. Operational Scope ERLKM may govern Record Linkage across: ERP systems; commerce platforms; accounting systems; banking infrastructure; payment systems; marketplaces; logistics; tax infrastructure; blockchain systems; smart contracts; AI agents; autonomous systems; distributed platforms; industrial systems; machine-to-machine environments; cross-border infrastructures; and future machine economies. The linkage logic remains technology-neutral and jurisdiction-neutral. Linkage Object The linkage object is a governed association between the Event Record and another materially relevant governed object or reference. A link may connect the Record to: the underlying Event; another Event Record; an upstream governance result; a supporting technical record; a predecessor representation; a successor representation; or another relevant reference. Link Object ≠ Event Relationship by default. Link Requirement Identification ERLKM shall identify which links are materially required for the Event Record to remain reconstructable and usable. Not every available connection belongs in the canonical Record linkage layer. Available Connection ≠ Required Governed Link. Event-to-Record Link The Record shall remain linked to the Determined Tax-Relevant Event it represents. This link is foundational. It allows downstream systems to move from: Record ↓ Governed Event without reconstructing Event identity independently. Event-to-Record Link ≠ Record Identity itself. ERIDM owns Record identity. Record-to-Record Link Event Records may require association with other governed Event Records. Examples include: predecessor/successor Record relationships; duplicate representations; derived representations; superseding Records; records corresponding to related Events. ERLKM governs these associations at the Record layer. Upstream Governance Linkage The Record may preserve links to relevant upstream TREGA™ outputs, including: TRECS Context; TRERS Recognition; TREFS Formation; TREBS Boundary; TRETS Timing; TRELS Location; TREPS Participation; TRVAS Value Association; TRERLS Event Relationships; TREDS Determination. ERLKM does not reproduce these governance functions. Determination Linkage The Event Record shall remain linked to the applicable TREDS Determination result. Where reconsideration has occurred, linkage should support identification of: prior Determination; reconsideration process; current effective Determination. Determination Link ≠ Determination Decision. Qualification Linkage Material qualifications may be linked directly or through governed references. The Record shall not lose qualification merely because the underlying qualification is stored elsewhere. Referenced Qualification ≠ Missing Qualification. Uncertainty Linkage Where material uncertainty remains relevant to downstream reliance, ERLKM shall support a durable link to the governed uncertainty state. Uncertainty Link ≠ Uncertainty Governance. EDUM remains authoritative. Reconsideration Linkage Where EDREM changes the effective Determination, the Event Record should preserve relevant linkage between: Prior Determination ↓ Reconsideration ↓ Current Determination Detailed chronological reconstruction belongs to ERTM. Predecessor Link A Record may require linkage to an earlier representation from which it developed. Predecessor linkage supports continuity without implying that both records represent different Events. Predecessor Record ≠ Prior Event by default. Successor Link A Record may link to a later representation that replaces or supersedes it. This linkage preserves continuity while keeping identities distinct where required. Successor Record ≠ Same Record by default. Supporting Record Linkage A canonical Event Record may link to supporting technical records such as: invoices; payment records; ledger entries; logs; sensor records; contracts; API messages; transaction receipts. These support or represent aspects of the Event. They do not automatically become governed Event Records. Supporting Record ≠ Canonical Event Record. Invoice Linkage An invoice may be linked to a governed Event Record where materially relevant. This does not make the invoice authoritative over the Event. Invoice Link ≠ Event Definition. Payment Linkage A payment record may be linked to the Event Record. The payment may represent: settlement; consideration; transfer; or partial execution. Payment Link ≠ Event Identity. Blockchain Linkage A blockchain transaction may be linked as a supporting or operational representation. A transaction hash may provide strong technical reference quality without defining the Event itself. Blockchain Link ≠ Event Equivalence. Smart-Contract Linkage A smart-contract execution log may be linked where relevant. The link preserves technical execution association. It does not determine full Event meaning. Machine-Generated Linkage Autonomous systems may create large numbers of technical references. ERLKM shall avoid creating canonical links merely because records are technically adjacent. Machine Correlation ≠ Governed Linkage by default. Link Type Every material governed link should possess a distinguishable type. Possible link types include: Represents; Supports; Derived From; References; Supersedes; Precedes; Succeeds; Corresponds To; Duplicate Of; Qualification Reference; Determination Reference; Uncertainty Reference; Governance State Reference. Link semantics should remain explicit. Link Direction Where direction matters, the governed Record should distinguish source and target. For example: Record B Supersedes Record A is not equivalent to: Record A Supersedes Record B. Link Presence ≠ Directional Meaning. Link Scope A link may apply to: the entire Record; one Record component; one Determination state; one qualification; one supporting object; or one lifecycle transition. The scope should be explicit where material. Link Materiality Not every link requires canonical preservation. A link is materially relevant where its absence could impair: Event reconstruction; Record meaning; Determination interpretation; downstream reliance; lifecycle continuity; or auditability. More Links ≠ Better Governance by default. Link Validity ERLKM shall represent whether a link is: Proposed; Established; Qualified; Ambiguous; Conflicted; Invalid; Superseded; or Closed. A stored reference is not necessarily a valid governed link. Stored Reference ≠ Governed Link. Link Qualification A link may exist with qualification. For example: probable source association; bounded duplicate association; unresolved cross-system mapping. Qualification shall remain visible. Link Conflict Link conflict exists where materially relevant sources support incompatible associations. Examples include: one Record linked to two mutually exclusive Events; conflicting predecessor references; incompatible duplicate-record conclusions; inconsistent Determination references. Link Conflict ≠ Permission to Preserve Both as Equally Valid without Qualification. Link Ambiguity Ambiguous linkage exists where the correct association cannot be established sufficiently. Ambiguous links should remain explicitly governed rather than silently treated as established. Duplicate Linkage Where multiple technical records represent the same governed Event Record, ERLKM may establish duplicate or corresponding-record associations. This supports deduplication and traceability. Duplicate Representation ≠ Duplicate Event. Merge Linkage Where TRERLS establishes an Event Merge, TREGS Records may require links among: pre-Merge Event Records; merged Event; resulting governed Record. ERLKM represents these associations. It does not govern the Merge itself. Merge Linkage ≠ Merge Decision. Split Linkage Where an Event is split, Record linkage may preserve association between: original Event Record; resulting Event Records; Split governance reference. Split Linkage ≠ Split Governance. Record Supersession Linkage Where one Record supersedes another, ERLKM shall preserve explicit linkage. Supersession linkage should support: prior Record identity; successor Record identity; effective transition; reason reference. TRECLS owns broader lifecycle supersession. Correction Linkage Where a corrected Record exists, ERLKM may preserve the association between prior and corrected representations. Correction Link ≠ Event Correction Decision. Cross-System Linkage Different systems may maintain independent local representations associated with the same governed Record. ERLKM may link these representations through the canonical Record identity. Cross-System Link ≠ Full Interoperability. ERINM governs interoperability. Cross-Organization Linkage Where several organizations exchange or consume the same Event Record, linkage may preserve associations among: canonical Record; local organizational representation; downstream processing object. This supports continuity without requiring identical local schemas. Cross-Border Linkage Cross-border Event Records may link to several jurisdiction-specific evaluations. These downstream links shall remain distinguishable from the canonical Event Record. Jurisdictional Evaluation Link ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination. Multi-Jurisdiction Linkage The same Event Record may support: Governed Event Record ↓ Jurisdiction A Evaluation Governed Event Record ↓ Jurisdiction B Evaluation Governed Event Record ↓ Jurisdiction C Evaluation Each downstream evaluation may be linked without becoming part of the canonical Event definition. Linkage Cardinality ERLKM shall support one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, and where necessary many-to-many Record associations. Cardinality shall reflect governed reality rather than database convenience. Database Relationship Type ≠ Governed Linkage Meaning. Linkage Persistence Material links should persist as long as they are necessary for reconstructability or lifecycle continuity. Deletion of a technical reference shall not automatically erase a materially relevant governed linkage. Linkage Continuity Links may remain continuous across: Record transformation; system migration; identifier change; schema change; lifecycle state change. Continuity shall preserve semantic meaning. Linkage Change A link may change because: a prior association was incorrect; a new supporting record appeared; a Record was superseded; a Duplicate was resolved; Merge/Split changed Event structure. Material changes should remain governable and traceable. Linkage Correction Where a link is known to be incorrect, it may be corrected. Correction shall preserve prior link state where materially relevant. Link Correction ≠ Silent Historical Rewrite. Linkage Supersession A newer link may supersede an older link. Superseded links should remain reconstructable where materially necessary. Linkage Closure Some links may cease to be operationally active while remaining historically relevant. Closed linkage does not mean the association never existed. Closed Link ≠ Erased Link. Linkage and Traceability ERLKM establishes governed associations. ERTM uses those associations to reconstruct lineage and governance history. Therefore: Linkage ≠ Traceability. A network of links may exist without sufficient traceability logic. Linkage and Interoperability ERLKM establishes what is linked. ERINM governs whether those links and their meanings remain usable across systems. Linkage ≠ Interoperability. Linkage and Event Relationships TRERLS governs substantive relationships among Events. ERLKM may represent those relationships at the Record level. It does not create, merge, split, sequence, group, or dependency-govern Events. Record Relationship Representation ≠ Event Relationship Determination. Linkage and Identity ERIDM establishes Record identity. ERLKM may use that identity to establish links. It does not re-identify the Record. Link Establishment ≠ Record Identification. Linkage and Structure ERSTM establishes structural capacity for links. ERLKM governs actual linkage. Link Field ≠ Governed Link. Linkage and Tax Law Links to jurisdictional evaluations, assessments, returns, or filings do not cause TREGA™ to own those legal outcomes. Tax Assessment Link ≠ Tax Assessment Governance. Governance States ERLKM may represent: Linkage Governance Not Initiated Link Requirement Identified Link Candidate Identified Link Under Evaluation Link Established Link Qualified Link Ambiguous Link Conflicted Link Invalid Duplicate Link Established Predecessor Link Established Successor Link Established Supersession Link Established Correction Link Established Cross-System Link Established Link Superseded Link Closed Linkage Sufficient Governed Event Record Linkage State Established Ready for Traceability Governance Governance Requirements ERLKM implementations shall ensure that: a valid Governed Event Record Structure exists; materially required links are identified; Event-to-Record linkage remains preserved; Record Linkage remains distinct from Event Relationship governance; upstream governance references can be maintained where material; Determination, qualification, uncertainty, and reconsideration references remain governable; predecessor and successor links remain distinguishable; supporting technical records remain distinct from canonical Event Records; link type is explicit where material; link direction is preserved where relevant; link scope is identifiable; link materiality is assessed; stored references do not automatically become governed links; ambiguous and conflicted links remain visible; Duplicate representations do not become duplicate Events; Merge/Split links do not recreate Merge/Split governance; correction and supersession links preserve materially relevant prior states; cross-system linkage remains distinct from interoperability; jurisdiction-specific evaluation links remain downstream; materially relevant links persist sufficiently for reconstructability; link changes remain traceable; and the resulting Governed Event Record Linkage State is suitable for ERTM. Governance Logic IF no valid Governed Event Record Structure exists, THEN ERLKM shall not establish canonical Record Linkage. IF a link is materially necessary to reconstruct or interpret the Event Record, THEN the link shall be represented or reliably referenced. IF a connection is technically present but has no governed semantic meaning, THEN it shall not automatically qualify as a canonical Record Link. IF multiple technical records correspond to the same canonical Record, THEN duplicate or corresponding-record linkage may be established without creating multiple Events. IF a link is materially ambiguous, THEN it shall remain qualified or unresolved rather than treated as established. IF materially authoritative sources support incompatible links, THEN Link Conflict shall be established and governed explicitly. IF one Record supersedes another, THEN predecessor/successor or supersession linkage shall preserve continuity. IF a link changes because of correction, Merge, Split, or reconsideration, THEN prior materially relevant linkage shall remain reconstructable. IF a jurisdiction-specific evaluation is linked, THEN the linkage shall not redefine the canonical Event Record. IF materially required links are sufficiently established and qualified, THEN ERLKM shall produce the Governed Event Record Linkage State for ERTM. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum ERLKM implementation should support: Linkage Governance ID A stable identifier for the ERLKM governance process. Canonical Record Identifier The ERIDM-established Record identity. Record Structure Reference The ERSTM-governed Record Structure. Link Identifier A stable identifier for each governed link. Link Type Represents, Supports, References, Derived From, Precedes, Succeeds, Supersedes, Duplicate Of, Qualification Reference, Determination Reference, Uncertainty Reference, or other governed type. Source Object Reference The source side of the link. Target Object Reference The target side of the link. Link Direction The governed directional meaning where relevant. Link Scope Record-wide, Component-Level, Determination-Level, Qualification-Level, Lifecycle-Level, or other governed scope. Link Materiality State Immaterial, Material, Critical, or Unresolved. Link Validity State Proposed, Established, Qualified, Ambiguous, Conflicted, Invalid, Superseded, or Closed. Event Reference Link The canonical association to the governed Event. Determination Link Reference The applicable TREDS Determination link. Qualification Link Reference Any material qualification link. Uncertainty Link Reference Any EDUM uncertainty link. Reconsideration Link Reference Any EDREM reconsideration association. Predecessor Record Reference Any prior Record representation. Successor Record Reference Any later Record representation. Supporting Record Reference(s) Invoices, payments, ledger records, logs, contracts, or other supporting objects. Duplicate Representation Reference Any governed duplicate or corresponding technical representation. Merge / Split Reference Any relevant TRERLS structural transition. Cross-System Reference Any materially relevant local-system representation. Cross-Organization Reference Any organizational representation associated with the Record. Jurisdictional Evaluation Reference Any downstream tax evaluation linked to the canonical Record. Prior Link State The previous materially relevant link state. Link Correction Reference Any governed link correction. Link Supersession Reference Any superseding linkage. Link Qualification Any limitation attached to the link. Link Conflict State Whether materially incompatible link conclusions exist. Link Trace Reference Minimum reference required for later ERTM reconstruction. Governance State The current ERLKM governance state. Handoff State Whether linkage is sufficiently governed for ERTM. Governance Outputs ERLKM may produce: Event-to-Record Link; Record-to-Record Link; Determination Link; Qualification Link; Uncertainty Link; Reconsideration Link; Predecessor Link; Successor Link; Supporting Record Link; Duplicate Representation Link; Merge/Split Reference; Cross-System Link; Cross-Organization Link; Jurisdictional Evaluation Link; Link Validity State; Link Materiality State; Link Conflict State; Link Correction State; Link Supersession State; Link Continuity State; and the principal output: Governed Event Record Linkage State. Critical Distinctions Record Linkage ≠ Event Relationship Governance. Link Object ≠ Event Relationship by default. Available Connection ≠ Required Governed Link. Event-to-Record Link ≠ Record Identity itself. Determination Link ≠ Determination Decision. Referenced Qualification ≠ Missing Qualification. Uncertainty Link ≠ Uncertainty Governance. Predecessor Record ≠ Prior Event by default. Successor Record ≠ Same Record by default. Supporting Record ≠ Canonical Event Record. Invoice Link ≠ Event Definition. Payment Link ≠ Event Identity. Blockchain Link ≠ Event Equivalence. Machine Correlation ≠ Governed Linkage by default. Link Presence ≠ Directional Meaning. More Links ≠ Better Governance by default. Stored Reference ≠ Governed Link. Link Conflict ≠ Permission to Preserve Both as Equally Valid without Qualification. Duplicate Representation ≠ Duplicate Event. Merge Linkage ≠ Merge Decision. Split Linkage ≠ Split Governance. Correction Link ≠ Event Correction Decision. Cross-System Link ≠ Full Interoperability. Jurisdictional Evaluation Link ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination. Database Relationship Type ≠ Governed Linkage Meaning. Link Correction ≠ Silent Historical Rewrite. Closed Link ≠ Erased Link. Linkage ≠ Traceability. Linkage ≠ Interoperability. Record Relationship Representation ≠ Event Relationship Determination. Link Establishment ≠ Record Identification. Link Field ≠ Governed Link. Tax Assessment Link ≠ Tax Assessment Governance. Enterprise Application ERLKM creates the governed association layer that allows a canonical Event Record to remain connected to the Event, its governance basis, related representations, and downstream processing objects. The canonical enterprise path is: ERIDM — Governed Event Record Identity → ERSTM — Governed Event Record Structure → ERLKM — Governed Event Record Linkage State → ERTM — Governed Event Record Traceability → ERINM — Governed Event Record Interoperability → Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record This prevents the Event Record from becoming an isolated data object after it enters complex system infrastructure. Use Case 1 — Cross-Border Marketplace Event Linked Across Commerce, Payment, and Tax Systems A marketplace Event has one canonical Governed Event Record. The marketplace maintains an order record, the payment provider maintains a settlement record, the ERP maintains an accounting object, and three jurisdictions later create separate tax-evaluation objects. ERLKM links the canonical Event Record to the relevant supporting technical records and downstream jurisdictional evaluations while preserving their distinct roles. The payment record does not become the Event. The tax evaluations do not redefine the canonical Record. One governed Record remains the common reference across the infrastructure. Use Case 2 — Event Record Supersession After Merge Two Events previously possessed separate governed Event Records. TRERLS later determines that the Events must be merged into one governed Event. TREDS produces the appropriate reconsidered Determination, and a resulting Event Record is created. ERLKM preserves links from the new Record to the predecessor Records and the relevant Merge governance reference. The prior Records remain historically reconstructable while the new Record becomes the effective canonical representation. Record continuity is preserved without pretending that supersession erased the prior Record state. Canonical Boundary ERLKM owns the governance of Event-to-Record links, Record-to-Record links, upstream governance references, Determination/qualification/uncertainty/reconsideration links, predecessor and successor links, supporting-record associations, duplicate-representation links, Merge/Split references, link type, direction, scope, materiality, validity, ambiguity, conflict, continuity, correction, supersession, and establishment of the Governed Event Record Linkage State. ERLKM does not establish Record identity; ERIDM owns that space. It does not define Record Structure; ERSTM owns that space. It does not govern full Record lineage reconstruction; ERTM owns Traceability. It does not govern semantic preservation across systems; ERINM owns Interoperability. It does not recreate Event Relationships; TRERLS owns Event Relationship Governance. It does not govern Event lifecycle amendment, correction, supersession, or closure; TRECLS owns those lifecycle functions. It does not determine legal taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, Tax Base, Tax Rate, legal tax point, Tax Period, Tax Liability, or other jurisdiction-specific tax consequences. Its governance begins when a valid Governed Event Record Structure exists. Its governance ends when materially required Record links are sufficiently governed and the Governed Event Record Linkage State is ready for Traceability Governance. Canonical Handoff ERSTM — Governed Event Record Structure ↓ ERLKM — Governed Event Record Linkage State ↓ ERTM — Event Record Traceability Governance Canonical Closing Statement ERLKM ensures that a governed Event Record remains connected to the Event, governance states, records, and representations that give it operational meaning without confusing those links with the Event relationships themselves. A Record can be richly connected and still remain one canonical representation of one governed Event. Record Linkage ≠ Event Relationship Governance. Linkage ≠ Traceability.

title: OOF™ The Event Relationship Merge & Split Module (ERLMM) governs how
text: OOF™ The Event Relationship Merge & Split Module (ERLMM) governs how The Event Relationship Merge & Split Module (ERLMM) governs how OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ Parent Standard: TRERLS — Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard Module: ERLMM — Event Relationship Merge & Split Module Operational Layer: Event Relationship Merge & Split Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Event Relationship Merge & Split Governance Origin ID: TREGA-TRERLS-ERLMM-005 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 1 September 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Event Relationship Merge & Split Module (ERLMM) governs how already-related Tax-Relevant Events are evaluated for justified consolidation into one governed Event representation or separation into multiple governed Event representations when accumulated relationship governance reveals that the existing Event structure no longer faithfully represents operational reality. ERLMM governs the conditions, justification, decision path, historical preservation, and downstream relationship consequences of Event Merge and Event Split. Its principal transition is: Governed Event Group Structure ↓ Merge & Split Governance ↓ Governed Event Relationship Structure ERLMM does not create Event Formation or Event Boundary authority independently. Where a Merge or Split changes what the event itself is, ERLMM coordinates the relationship-level restructuring with the authoritative upstream governance of TREFS — Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard and TREBS — Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard. The foundational distinction is: Relationship Convenience ≠ Permission to Merge or Split Events. Operational Role Event structures may initially appear correct and later prove incomplete, fragmented, duplicated, over-aggregated, or incorrectly bounded. Several records may have been treated as separate events even though subsequent governance establishes that they represent one materially coherent event. Conversely, one governed event may later prove to contain several independently meaningful events. ERLMM provides a controlled mechanism for addressing those situations. Its role is not to optimize the Event structure for: tax outcome; reporting convenience; database architecture; billing convenience; system migration; reconciliation convenience; or computational simplicity. Its role is to preserve the most faithful governed representation of operational reality. Internal Module Flow TRERLS operates through: ERLIM — Event Relationship Identification ↓ ERLDM — Event Relationship Dependency ↓ ERLSM — Event Relationship Sequence ↓ ERLGM — Event Relationship Grouping ↓ ERLMM — Event Relationship Merge & Split ↓ Governed Event Relationship Structure ERLMM is the final Core Module within TRERLS. It receives the Governed Event Group Structure and produces the final Governed Event Relationship Structure for handoff to TREDS. Operational Transition The canonical transition is: Governed Event Group Structure + Formation Evidence + Boundary Evidence + Relationship History ↓ Merge & Split Governance ↓ Governed Event Relationship Structure ERLMM may determine that: no structural change is required; Merge review is required; Split review is required; a Merge is justified; a Split is justified; the issue must be referred upstream; or the structure remains unresolved. Operational Space ERLMM governs: Merge candidate identification; Split candidate identification; Merge qualification; Split qualification; Merge justification; Split justification; Merge decision; Split decision; Event preservation during Merge; Event preservation during Split; source-event mapping; resulting-event mapping; historical relationship preservation; Merge lineage; Split lineage; partial Merge; partial Split; duplicate-event consolidation; artificial-fragmentation correction; artificial-aggregation correction; relationship reassignment; group restructuring; Event Chain restructuring; Event Network restructuring; Merge uncertainty; Split uncertainty; Merge conflict; Split conflict; reconsideration; supersession; and Merge/Split-specific traceability. Operational Scope ERLMM may operate across: enterprise transactions; commerce; payments; banking; accounting; marketplaces; logistics; supply chains; ERP environments; digital platforms; distributed systems; blockchain infrastructures; digital assets; AI agents; autonomous machines; industrial systems; energy systems; cross-border operations; and future machine economies. Merge Candidate A Merge Candidate exists where two or more governed Event representations may in fact represent one materially coherent Tax-Relevant Event. A candidate does not authorize Merge. Merge Candidate ≠ Governed Event Merge. The candidate shall be evaluated against Formation, Boundary, Relationship, and historical information. Split Candidate A Split Candidate exists where one governed Event representation may contain two or more materially independent events. A candidate does not authorize Split. Split Candidate ≠ Governed Event Split. Merge Purpose Event Merge exists to correct structural over-fragmentation where several Event representations incorrectly represent what governance establishes as one event. Merge is therefore corrective, not convenient. Merge ≠ Aggregation for Convenience. Split Purpose Event Split exists to correct structural over-aggregation where one Event representation incorrectly contains several independently meaningful events. Split is therefore corrective, not a mechanism for generating preferred downstream results. Split ≠ Fragmentation for Convenience. Merge Preconditions A Merge shall require sufficient governed basis indicating that separate Event representations should not remain independently constituted. Relevant considerations may include: common Event Formation; overlapping or identical Event Boundary; inseparable operational substance; duplicated Event representation; duplicate technical capture; relationship evidence indicating one underlying occurrence; shared participant structure where materially relevant; integrated Value Association; and consistent historical reconstruction. No single indicator establishes Merge automatically. Split Preconditions A Split shall require sufficient governed basis indicating that one Event representation contains materially distinct Event structures. Relevant considerations may include: independently formed occurrences; separable Event Boundaries; independent participants; independent Value Associations; materially distinct timing; materially distinct location; independent operational purpose; independent dependency or sequence paths; or materially independent downstream relationships. Again: Additional Detail ≠ Split Requirement by default. Duplicate Event Consolidation Two records may represent the same governed event because of: duplicate ingestion; system synchronization; mirrored infrastructure; replicated ledger entries; platform duplication; or migration artifacts. ERLMM may govern consolidation of duplicate Event representations. Duplicate Record ≠ Additional Event. Artificial Fragmentation Artificial fragmentation occurs when one materially coherent event is represented as multiple events without sufficient Event Formation or Boundary justification. Examples may arise from: technical process steps; API calls; accounting line items; blockchain operations; machine instructions; internal workflow stages. ERLMM shall prevent technical structure from becoming Event structure by default. Technical Fragmentation ≠ Economic Event Fragmentation. Artificial Aggregation Artificial aggregation occurs when several independently meaningful events are represented as one event merely because they share: one contract; one invoice; one payment; one participant; one platform; one settlement; one technical workflow; or one reporting record. ERLMM shall prevent convenience-based Event collapse. Shared Record ≠ Permission to Merge. Merge Basis A valid Merge basis shall arise from governed Event reality. It shall not arise solely from: desired tax treatment; desired accounting treatment; lower reporting complexity; database design; reconciliation preference; system limitations. Desired Outcome ≠ Merge Basis. Split Basis A valid Split basis shall likewise arise from governed Event reality. It shall not be created solely because separating the event produces: preferred tax rates; different jurisdictional treatment; different taxable periods; exemptions; reduced tax exposure; reporting convenience. Desired Outcome ≠ Split Basis. Tax Advantage and Merge ERLMM shall explicitly reject tax advantage as an Event Merge criterion. Tax Advantage ≠ Event Merge Criterion. Whether tax law later aggregates events is a separate downstream legal question. Tax Exposure and Split Likewise: Tax Exposure ≠ Event Split Criterion. Event structure shall not be redesigned merely because different representation changes potential tax liability. Merge and Event Formation A Merge may reveal that multiple Event records resulted from one underlying Event Formation. TREFS remains authoritative for Event Formation. ERLMM shall not silently override TREFS. Where Formation must be reconsidered, the issue shall be referred upstream. Event Merge ≠ Independent Formation Authority. Split and Event Formation A Split may reveal that one original representation contained several independently formed events. Where this changes Event Formation, TREFS authority applies. Event Split ≠ Independent Formation Authority. Merge and Event Boundary Merge may require reconsideration of individual Event Boundaries. TREBS remains authoritative. ERLMM governs the relationship-level restructuring resulting from that determination. Event Merge ≠ Independent Boundary Authority. Split and Event Boundary A Split may require creation of distinct governed Event Boundaries. TREBS remains authoritative for those boundaries. Event Split ≠ Independent Boundary Authority. Merge Direction A Merge may combine: Event A + Event B ↓ Event AB or: Event A + Event B + Event C ↓ Event ABC The resulting representation must preserve traceability to all contributing Event representations. Split Direction A Split may produce: Event A ↓ Event A1 + Event A2 or a broader structure where several new Event representations emerge from one previously over-aggregated record. Each resulting event shall remain traceable to the pre-Split representation. Many-to-One Merge Several Event representations may merge into one governed Event representation. Many-to-One Representation ≠ Automatic Merge Justification. The Merge requires substantive governance basis. One-to-Many Split One Event representation may split into several governed events. One-to-Many Representation ≠ Automatic Split Justification. Partial Merge Only part of an Event structure may require consolidation. Where supported, ERLMM may govern a partial Merge without collapsing unrelated Event structure. Partial Relationship Overlap ≠ Full Merge by default. Partial Split Only one portion of an event may prove independently constituted. A partial Split may be required while the remaining event continues. Partial Independence ≠ Full Event Split by default. Merge and Event Identity A governed Merge changes how Event Identity is represented. The original source records shall not disappear from history. They become traceably associated with the resulting governed event. Event Merge ≠ Historical Erasure. Split and Event Identity A governed Split creates or recognizes multiple independently governed Event representations. The prior representation shall remain part of the historical lineage. Event Split ≠ Historical Erasure. Source Event Preservation All events participating in Merge or Split governance shall remain historically referenceable. Historical records may be marked as: merged; superseded; split; replaced; reconstituted; or otherwise structurally transformed. They shall not simply disappear. Resulting Event Preservation Each resulting Event representation shall receive sufficient identity and traceability to support future governance. The resulting structure shall clearly indicate its relationship to predecessor representations. Merge Lineage Merge lineage shall preserve: Source Event(s) ↓ Merge Decision ↓ Resulting Event The basis, decision, authority, and transformation history shall remain reconstructable. Split Lineage Split lineage shall preserve: Source Event ↓ Split Decision ↓ Resulting Event(s) Relationship Reassignment Merge or Split may require existing relationships to be reassigned. For example: dependencies; sequences; group memberships; settlement links; reversal links; Value Associations. Reassignment shall be explicit. Structural Change ≠ Permission to Lose Relationship History. Dependency After Merge Where events merge, prior dependency relationships may become internal to the resulting event or may cease to represent relationships between independent events. ERLMM shall preserve the historical distinction. ERLDM remains authoritative for dependency itself. Dependency After Split A Split may reveal new dependencies among the resulting events. Those dependencies may require renewed ERLDM governance. Split Result ≠ Automatically Governed Dependency. Sequence After Merge Merge may alter how prior Event Sequences are represented. Historic sequence shall remain reconstructable even where several earlier event records become one Event representation. Sequence After Split Split may create multiple events requiring distinct sequence relationships. Those relationships shall be governed through ERLSM where necessary. Grouping After Merge A merged Event representation may replace several group members. Group membership shall be updated without losing prior history. Grouping After Split A Split may create several new group members or may distribute resulting events across different Event Groups. ERLGM authority remains applicable. Event Chain Restructuring Merge or Split may alter an Event Chain. For example: A ↓ B ↓ C may become: AB ↓ C or: A ↓ B1 ↓ B2 ↓ C ERLMM shall preserve structural lineage. Event Network Restructuring Complex Event Networks may require relationship-edge reassignment after Merge or Split. No relationship should disappear merely because Event representation changes. Reversal and Merge A reversal event shall not normally be merged into the original event merely because it reverses it. Reversal Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement. The events may remain separately governed and related. Refund and Merge A refund may remain a separate event related to an earlier purchase or payment. Refund Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement. Correction and Merge A correction record may or may not constitute an independent event. ERLMM shall not assume Merge or independence solely from the label “correction.” Replacement and Merge A replacement event may remain separate from the original event while preserving a replacement relationship. Replacement Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement. Continuation and Split A long-running event shall not be split merely because it contains several operational phases. Operational Phases ≠ Multiple Events by default. TRECLS remains authoritative for lifecycle continuity. System Migration Migration from one platform to another may create duplicate Event representations. This may justify duplicate consolidation. However: System Migration ≠ New Event Formation. and: System Migration ≠ Event Split. Database Consolidation Combining database records does not establish Event Merge. Database Consolidation ≠ Event Merge. Likewise, separating a database record does not establish Event Split. Database Separation ≠ Event Split. Accounting Structure Accounting systems may aggregate or separate activity according to ledger requirements. Those structures do not automatically define TREGA™ Event structure. Accounting Aggregation ≠ Event Merge. Accounting Disaggregation ≠ Event Split. Invoice Structure Several events may appear on one invoice. One event may span several invoice lines or documents. Therefore: Invoice Consolidation ≠ Event Merge. Invoice Separation ≠ Event Split. Payment Structure One payment may settle multiple events, and several payments may relate to one event. Therefore: Payment Aggregation ≠ Event Merge. Multiple Payments ≠ Event Split. Blockchain Merge & Split Blockchain infrastructure may represent one economic activity through several technical transactions or combine many operations inside one transaction. ERLMM shall not derive Merge or Split mechanically from ledger structure. Multiple Blockchain Transactions ≠ Event Split Requirement. Single Blockchain Transaction ≠ Event Merge Requirement. Smart-Contract Structure One smart contract may execute several independent events. Several contracts may participate in one event. Therefore: Smart-Contract Boundary ≠ Event Boundary. AI-Agent Workflow An AI agent may generate hundreds of technical actions in executing one governed event or several independent events within one workflow. ERLMM shall rely on Event governance rather than agent workflow structure. One Agent Workflow ≠ One Event by default. Machine Operations Machine systems may generate high-frequency technical actions. Those operations shall not be split into independent Tax-Relevant Events without appropriate Formation and Boundary governance. Machine Operation Count ≠ Event Count. Cross-System Merge Records from several systems may represent the same event. ERLMM may govern consolidation where Event Formation and Boundary support one Event Identity. Different Systems ≠ Different Events by default. Cross-Organization Merge Different organizations may hold records referring to the same governed event. Their separate records do not automatically mean separate events. However, separate organizational participation also does not automatically justify Merge. Cross-Border Merge & Split An event may cross national borders. Geographic distribution does not by itself justify Event Split. Likewise, shared jurisdiction does not justify Event Merge. Multiple Countries ≠ Multiple Events by default. One Country ≠ One Event by default. Multi-Jurisdiction Neutrality ERLMM shall preserve a jurisdiction-neutral Event structure. Different tax systems may later aggregate or separate the events differently for legal purposes. The TREGA™ representation shall remain stable unless Event reality itself changes. Jurisdictional Tax Treatment ≠ TREGA™ Merge/Split Authority. Merge Uncertainty Available information may suggest Merge without providing sufficient basis. ERLMM shall preserve that uncertainty. Merge Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Merge. Split Uncertainty Likewise: Split Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Split. Merge Conflict Different systems or governance sources may disagree on whether events constitute one event. ERLMM shall preserve the conflict. Merge Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Consolidation. Split Conflict Conflicting evidence regarding Event independence shall remain explicit. Split Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Fragmentation. Merge Reconsideration A prior Merge may later be reconsidered if materially relevant information changes. Historical Merge state shall remain reconstructable. Split Reconsideration A prior Split may likewise be reconsidered. Reconsideration shall not erase previous governance states. Supersession A new Event representation resulting from Merge or Split may supersede prior Event representations for current governance purposes. However: Supersession ≠ Historical Deletion. Governance States ERLMM may represent: Merge & Split Governance Ready Merge & Split Under Governance No Structural Change Required Merge Candidate Split Candidate Merge Qualification Required Split Qualification Required Merge Qualified Split Qualified Merge Rejected Split Rejected Merge Referred Upstream Split Referred Upstream Merge Approved Split Approved Partial Merge Partial Split Duplicate Event Consolidation Artificial Fragmentation Corrected Artificial Aggregation Corrected Merge Ambiguous Split Ambiguous Merge Conflicted Split Conflicted Merge Under Reconsideration Split Under Reconsideration Relationship Structure Reconstituted Governed Event Relationship Structure Established Governance Requirements ERLMM implementations shall ensure that: Merge and Split operate only on governed Event structures; Merge Candidate remains distinct from Merge Decision; Split Candidate remains distinct from Split Decision; Event Merge is supported by substantive Event governance; Event Split is supported by substantive Event governance; technical fragmentation does not automatically create Split; technical aggregation does not automatically create Merge; duplicate records can be distinguished from separate events; desired tax outcome does not govern Merge or Split; tax advantage is not a Merge criterion; tax exposure is not a Split criterion; Event Formation authority remains under TREFS; Event Boundary authority remains under TREBS; source Event representations remain historically traceable; resulting Event representations remain traceable to source events; Merge lineage can be reconstructed; Split lineage can be reconstructed; dependency relationships can be reassigned where necessary; sequence relationships can be reassigned where necessary; group memberships can be updated where necessary; Event Chains can be restructured without losing history; Event Networks can be restructured without losing history; ambiguity remains visible; conflict remains visible; reconsideration remains traceable; supersession does not erase historical states; system migration does not redefine Event structure automatically; accounting, invoicing, payment, blockchain, AI-agent, and machine-system structures do not independently determine Merge or Split; and jurisdiction-specific tax aggregation remains downstream. Governance Logic IF several governed Event representations appear to represent one materially coherent event, THEN ERLMM shall establish a Merge Candidate rather than automatically merging them. IF one governed Event representation appears to contain several materially independent events, THEN ERLMM shall establish a Split Candidate rather than automatically splitting it. IF Merge would alter Event Formation or Event Boundary, THEN the relevant matter shall be coordinated with TREFS and TREBS before final structural change. IF Split would alter Event Formation or Event Boundary, THEN the relevant matter shall be coordinated with TREFS and TREBS before final structural change. IF records are merely technical duplicates of one governed event, THEN duplicate consolidation may be performed while preserving source lineage. IF several technical operations belong to one materially coherent event, THEN technical fragmentation alone shall not justify multiple Event Identities. IF several independently meaningful events share one invoice, payment, contract, workflow, or settlement, THEN that shared structure alone shall not justify Event Merge. IF tax advantage is the only material basis for Merge, THEN Merge shall be rejected. IF tax exposure is the only material basis for Split, THEN Split shall be rejected. IF Merge or Split remains ambiguous or conflicted, THEN the corresponding governance state shall remain visible. IF Merge or Split is approved, THEN source Event representations, resulting Event representations, relationship reassignment, and historical lineage shall remain reconstructable. IF the final relationship structure is sufficiently governed, THEN ERLMM shall produce the Governed Event Relationship Structure for TREDS. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum ERLMM implementation should support: Event Group Structure Reference The ERLGM output entering Merge & Split governance. Structural Review Identifier A stable identifier for the Merge/Split governance process. Review Type Merge, Split, Duplicate Consolidation, or No Structural Change. Candidate Event References The governed events under structural review. Merge Candidate State Whether Merge is under consideration. Split Candidate State Whether Split is under consideration. Formation Reference Relevant TREFS governance supporting or constraining structural change. Boundary Reference Relevant TREBS governance supporting or constraining structural change. Relationship Basis The TRERLS relationship information supporting structural review. Merge Basis The governed substantive basis for Merge where applicable. Split Basis The governed substantive basis for Split where applicable. Duplicate State Whether candidate records represent duplicated Event capture. Fragmentation State Whether artificial Event fragmentation has been identified. Aggregation State Whether artificial Event aggregation has been identified. Source Event References All Event representations preceding structural change. Resulting Event References All Event representations resulting from approved Merge or Split. Transformation Direction Many-to-one, one-to-many, partial Merge, partial Split, or other governed transformation. Relationship Reassignment Record How dependencies and other Event Relationships are reassigned. Sequence Reassignment Record How Event Sequence is affected. Grouping Reassignment Record How group membership is affected. Value Association Reference Any material TRVAS reference affected by the structural change. Historical Lineage Record The complete relationship between source and resulting Event representations. Merge/Split Justification Record The governed rationale for the decision. Decision State Approved, Rejected, Referred Upstream, Ambiguous, Conflicted, or Unresolved. Uncertainty State Any remaining structural uncertainty. Conflict State Any materially conflicting governance information. Reconsideration Reference Where a prior Merge or Split decision has been reopened. Supersession Reference Where a resulting Event representation supersedes an earlier representation. Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the full Merge/Split decision. Governance State The current ERLMM state. Handoff State Whether the Governed Event Relationship Structure is ready for TREDS. Governance Outputs ERLMM may produce: No Structural Change Determination; Merge Candidate Record; Split Candidate Record; Merge Qualification Record; Split Qualification Record; Merge Decision; Split Decision; Duplicate Event Consolidation Record; Artificial Fragmentation Correction; Artificial Aggregation Correction; Partial Merge Record; Partial Split Record; Source Event Mapping; Resulting Event Mapping; Merge Lineage Record; Split Lineage Record; Relationship Reassignment Record; Sequence Reassignment Record; Group Reassignment Record; Merge Uncertainty State; Split Uncertainty State; Merge Conflict State; Split Conflict State; Merge Reconsideration Record; Split Reconsideration Record; Supersession Record; Merge/Split Traceability Record; and the principal output: Governed Event Relationship Structure. Critical Distinctions Relationship Convenience ≠ Permission to Merge or Split Events. Merge Candidate ≠ Governed Event Merge. Split Candidate ≠ Governed Event Split. Merge ≠ Aggregation for Convenience. Split ≠ Fragmentation for Convenience. Additional Detail ≠ Split Requirement by default. Duplicate Record ≠ Additional Event. Technical Fragmentation ≠ Economic Event Fragmentation. Shared Record ≠ Permission to Merge. Desired Outcome ≠ Merge Basis. Desired Outcome ≠ Split Basis. Tax Advantage ≠ Event Merge Criterion. Tax Exposure ≠ Event Split Criterion. Event Merge ≠ Independent Formation Authority. Event Split ≠ Independent Formation Authority. Event Merge ≠ Independent Boundary Authority. Event Split ≠ Independent Boundary Authority. Many-to-One Representation ≠ Automatic Merge Justification. One-to-Many Representation ≠ Automatic Split Justification. Partial Relationship Overlap ≠ Full Merge by default. Partial Independence ≠ Full Event Split by default. Event Merge ≠ Historical Erasure. Event Split ≠ Historical Erasure. Structural Change ≠ Permission to Lose Relationship History. Split Result ≠ Automatically Governed Dependency. Reversal Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement. Refund Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement. Replacement Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement. Operational Phases ≠ Multiple Events by default. System Migration ≠ New Event Formation. Database Consolidation ≠ Event Merge. Database Separation ≠ Event Split. Accounting Aggregation ≠ Event Merge. Accounting Disaggregation ≠ Event Split. Invoice Consolidation ≠ Event Merge. Invoice Separation ≠ Event Split. Payment Aggregation ≠ Event Merge. Multiple Payments ≠ Event Split. Multiple Blockchain Transactions ≠ Event Split Requirement. Single Blockchain Transaction ≠ Event Merge Requirement. Smart-Contract Boundary ≠ Event Boundary. One Agent Workflow ≠ One Event by default. Machine Operation Count ≠ Event Count. Different Systems ≠ Different Events by default. Multiple Countries ≠ Multiple Events by default. Jurisdictional Tax Treatment ≠ TREGA™ Merge/Split Authority. Merge Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Merge. Split Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Split. Merge Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Consolidation. Split Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Fragmentation. Supersession ≠ Historical Deletion. Enterprise Application ERLMM provides the final structural-control layer of TRERLS. A typical enterprise path is: ERLIM — Governed Event Relationship Candidate Set → ERLDM — Governed Event Dependency Structure → ERLSM — Governed Event Sequence Structure → ERLGM — Governed Event Group Structure → ERLMM — Merge & Split Governance → Governed Event Relationship Structure → TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination This allows enterprises and digital infrastructures to correct duplicated, fragmented, or over-aggregated Event representations while preserving operational reality, historical lineage, and jurisdiction neutrality. Use Case 1 — ERP, Payment, and Marketplace Duplicate Event Reconciliation A marketplace, merchant ERP, and payment infrastructure each create separate records for the same purchase activity. Initial integration produces three apparent Tax-Relevant Events. Relationship governance later establishes that two of those records are duplicate representations of one underlying governed event, while the payment event remains independently constituted and related. ERLMM evaluates the Merge Candidate, coordinates the relevant Event Formation and Boundary references, consolidates the duplicate Event representations, preserves all source-record lineage, and retains the independent payment Event Relationship. The resulting structure corrects technical duplication without collapsing materially distinct activity. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Workflow Incorrectly Aggregated as One Event An autonomous industrial platform records an entire multi-stage service workflow as one event. Subsequent governance establishes that resource allocation, machine service delivery, and later digital settlement possess independent Formation, Boundaries, participants, and Value Associations. ERLMM establishes a Split Candidate and coordinates the required Formation and Boundary governance. The original over-aggregated Event representation is preserved historically while three independently governed Event representations are established and linked through dependency, sequence, and grouping relationships. The Split is justified by operational reality rather than tax treatment. Canonical Boundary ERLMM owns relationship-level governance of Merge Candidates, Split Candidates, duplicate consolidation, artificial-fragmentation correction, artificial-aggregation correction, Merge/Split qualification, decision structure, source-to-result mapping, relationship reassignment, lineage, uncertainty, conflict, reconsideration, supersession, and Merge/Split-specific traceability. ERLMM does not independently create Event Formation authority, redefine Event Boundaries without TREBS governance, determine Event Timing, Event Location, Event Participation, underlying Value governance, taxpayer status, tax aggregation, tax jurisdiction, Tax Base, Tax Liability, or another jurisdiction-specific legal consequence. Where Merge or Split changes Event Formation or Event Boundary, TREFS and TREBS remain authoritative. ERLMM governance ends when the final relationship structure among the relevant governed events is sufficiently represented for downstream Tax-Relevant Event Determination under TREDS. Canonical Handoff ERLGM — Governed Event Group Structure ↓ ERLMM — Governed Event Relationship Structure ↓ TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination Canonical Closing Statement ERLMM corrects the structure of related events when governance establishes that reality has been fragmented or aggregated incorrectly, while preserving every material step in the history of that correction. Events should be merged or split because the governed reality requires it — never because a technical system, reporting structure, or preferred tax outcome makes another representation more convenient. Event Merge ≠ Historical Erasure. Event Split ≠ Historical Erasure. Tax Advantage ≠ Event Merge Criterion. Tax Exposure ≠ Event Split Criterion.

title: OOF™ The Event Relationship Sequence Module (ERLSM) governs how
text: OOF™ The Event Relationship Sequence Module (ERLSM) governs how The Event Relationship Sequence Module (ERLSM) governs how OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ Parent Standard: TRERLS — Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard Module: ERLSM — Event Relationship Sequence Module Operational Layer: Event Relationship Sequence Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Event Relationship Sequence Origin ID: TREGA-TRERLS-ERLSM-003 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 1 September 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Event Relationship Sequence Module (ERLSM) governs how already-identified and dependency-qualified Tax-Relevant Events are ordered, sequenced, positioned, and related across temporal and operational progression. ERLSM determines whether events occur before, after, concurrently with, conditionally following, or otherwise in a governed sequence relative to one another. Its principal transition is: Governed Event Dependency Structure ↓ Event Sequence Governance ↓ Governed Event Sequence Structure ERLSM does not determine Event Timing itself, Event Dependency, Event Grouping, Event Merge, Event Split, causation, Event Identity, or tax consequence. The foundational distinction is: Event Sequence ≠ Event Identity. Operational Role Dependency alone does not fully explain how events unfold. Two events may be dependent without occurring immediately one after another. Several events may occur in parallel. A later event may depend on an earlier event but be separated from it by several intermediate events. One Event Network may contain multiple valid sequences. ERLSM provides the governance needed to represent how governed events progress relative to each other without converting chronology into causation or Event Identity. Internal Module Flow TRERLS operates through: ERLIM — Event Relationship Identification ↓ ERLDM — Event Relationship Dependency ↓ ERLSM — Event Relationship Sequence ↓ ERLGM — Event Relationship Grouping ↓ ERLMM — Event Relationship Merge & Split ↓ Governed Event Relationship Structure ERLSM receives the Governed Event Dependency Structure from ERLDM. Its output is passed to ERLGM. Operational Transition The canonical transition is: Governed Event Dependency Structure + Governed Event Timing Information ↓ Sequence Governance ↓ Governed Event Sequence Structure ERLSM uses already-governed timing information from TRETS. It does not redefine Event Timing. Operational Space ERLSM governs: sequence existence; sequence direction; predecessor relationships; successor relationships; concurrent sequence; parallel progression; conditional sequence; immediate sequence; deferred sequence; multi-stage sequence; branching sequence; converging sequence; interrupted sequence; resumed sequence; cyclic technical patterns where relevant; sequence qualification; sequence uncertainty; sequence conflict; sequence reconsideration; and sequence-specific traceability. Operational Scope ERLSM may govern sequence structures across: commerce; banking; payments; ERP; accounting; logistics; marketplaces; supply chains; blockchain systems; smart contracts; digital assets; AI agents; autonomous machines; industrial processes; energy systems; distributed digital infrastructure; cross-border operations; and machine-to-machine environments. Sequence Object A Sequence Object is a governed representation of the relative order between two or more governed events. It may identify: predecessor event; successor event; concurrent event; sequence branch; convergence point; sequence condition; interruption; resumption; or other materially relevant order structure. Sequence Object ≠ Event Timing Record. TRETS owns Event Timing. ERLSM owns the relationship among those governed times. Sequence Establishment A sequence may be established where governed information supports a meaningful order between events. The sequence may arise from: Event Timing; operational workflow; dependency structure; settlement progression; machine execution; contractual process; system state transition; or another materially relevant basis. Earlier Event ≠ Sequence Relationship by default. Chronological order alone does not always establish a materially relevant Event Relationship. Predecessor Relationship An event may act as a predecessor to another event. The canonical structure is: Event A ↓ Event B where Event A precedes Event B within the governed relationship. However: Predecessor ≠ Cause by default. Successor Relationship An event may follow one or more predecessor events. A successor relationship describes governed progression. It does not automatically mean the successor depends on every earlier event. Successor ≠ Dependent Event by default. ERLDM remains authoritative for dependency. Immediate Sequence Two events may occur directly next to one another in the governed process. For example: Authorization ↓ Settlement This may be represented as immediate sequence. However: Immediate Sequence ≠ Same Event. Deferred Sequence Events may be separated by significant time while still forming a governed sequence. For example: Purchase ↓ Annual Rebate Time distance does not invalidate sequence where a material structural relationship exists. Time Distance ≠ Sequence Absence. Concurrent Events Two or more events may occur at the same or overlapping time. ERLSM shall support concurrent sequence states. Concurrent Events ≠ Same Event. Concurrency does not remove separate Event Identities. Parallel Progression Several event paths may proceed simultaneously. Example: Purchase ↓ Payment and simultaneously: Purchase ↓ Fulfillment The two branches may later converge. ERLSM shall support parallel progression. Parallel Sequence ≠ Event Group by default. Grouping remains under ERLGM. Branching Sequence One event may lead into several sequence branches. The structure may be: A ↓ B A ↓ C A ↓ D This does not require the resulting events to be merged. Sequence Branching ≠ Event Fragmentation. Converging Sequence Several sequences may converge into one later event. Example: A ↓ D B ↓ D C ↓ D This is common in settlement, aggregation, production, and autonomous systems. Sequence Convergence ≠ Event Merge. Multi-Stage Sequence Complex activity may contain multiple governed sequence stages. Example: Order ↓ Authorization ↓ Fulfillment ↓ Delivery ↓ Settlement ↓ Refund Each event may remain distinct. ERLSM preserves the progression. Conditional Sequence An event may follow another only when a condition is satisfied. Example: Return Accepted ↓ Refund Event ERLSM may preserve that sequence condition. It does not govern authority or permission. Conditional Sequence ≠ Permission Governance. Sequence and Dependency Sequence and dependency must remain separate. An event may follow another without depending on it. An event may depend on another while several unrelated events occur between them. Therefore: Sequence ≠ Dependency. Sequence and Event Timing TRETS establishes Event Timing. ERLSM does not determine: Event Start; Event Completion; Event Duration; legal tax point; tax period. It consumes governed timing information to establish relative Event Sequence. Event Sequence ≠ Event Timing Determination. Temporal Sequence A temporal sequence represents order based on governed time. The form may be: Event A before Event B or: Event A concurrent with Event B Temporal sequence is one form of Event Sequence. Operational Sequence Operational order may differ from simple timestamp order. For example, a system may technically record settlement before another system finalizes a related fulfillment record. ERLSM may preserve operational sequence separately from raw system timestamps. System Timestamp Order ≠ Operational Sequence by default. Sequence and Causation Sequence is not proof of causation. Before ≠ Because Of. and: Event Sequence ≠ Causation. ERLSM does not determine legal, economic, or scientific causation. Sequence Direction Sequence shall preserve direction where material. A ↓ B is distinct from: B ↓ A Reversal of sequence may materially change event interpretation. Sequence Cardinality ERLSM shall support: one-to-one; one-to-many; many-to-one; many-to-many sequence structures. One-to-Many Sequence One event may precede several events. Example: Order ↓ Payment Order ↓ Fulfillment Order ↓ Logistics This does not mean the later events are one event. Many-to-One Sequence Several earlier events may precede one later event. Example: Multiple Sales ↓ Settlement ERLSM may represent the sequence without merging the source events. Many-to-Many Sequence Complex systems may contain several interacting sequence paths. ERLSM shall support those structures without forcing artificial linearization. Interrupted Sequence A process may stop after one event and resume later. ERLSM may preserve: A ↓ interruption ↓ B where the interruption is materially relevant. Interrupted Sequence ≠ Broken Event Relationship by default. Resumed Sequence A later event may resume a previously interrupted Event Relationship path. Resumption does not imply continuity of the same event. Sequence Resumption ≠ Same Event Continuity. TRECLS remains authoritative for Event Lifecycle continuity. Reversal Sequence A later reversal event may follow an earlier event or sequence. ERLSM may preserve: Original Event ↓ Reversal Event The sequence does not erase the original event. Reversal Sequence ≠ Historical Erasure. Refund Sequence A refund may occur after one or more earlier events. ERLSM governs the sequence relationship. It does not determine tax adjustment. Refund Sequence ≠ Tax Adjustment Determination. Replacement Sequence A replacement event may follow a failed, rejected, cancelled, or superseded event. ERLSM may represent the sequence. Replacement Sequence ≠ Original Event Invalidity by default. Correction Sequence A corrective event may follow an earlier event. The corrected relationship shall remain historically reconstructable. Correction Sequence ≠ Earlier Event Erasure. Sequence Across Systems Related events may be recorded in systems using different clocks, time zones, timestamps, or processing rules. ERLSM shall rely on governed Event Timing rather than blindly trusting raw technical timestamps. System Timestamp ≠ Governed Sequence by default. Sequence Across Organizations Different organizations may record related events independently. One system may show: A ↓ B while another reflects: B recorded before A ERLSM shall distinguish record order from governed Event Sequence. Record Order ≠ Event Sequence by default. Cross-Border Sequence Events may occur across multiple jurisdictions and time zones. ERLSM preserves their governed sequence without determining tax jurisdiction or tax period. Cross-Border Sequence ≠ Tax Period Determination. Blockchain Sequence Blockchain systems provide deterministic ledger ordering within particular technical contexts. However: Blockchain Order ≠ Complete Economic Event Sequence by default. Off-chain events may occur before, during, or after on-chain activity. ERLSM may integrate both governed forms. Smart-Contract Sequence One smart contract may trigger a series of technical actions. Those technical execution steps may inform sequence. They do not automatically define the sequence of Tax-Relevant Events. Smart-Contract Execution Order ≠ Tax-Relevant Event Sequence by default. AI-Agent Sequence AI agents may coordinate numerous actions concurrently. For example: Request ↓ Resource Search ↓ Allocation while another branch performs: Request ↓ Pricing ↓ Settlement Preparation ERLSM shall support branching, parallel, and converging agent sequences. Agent Action Order ≠ Event Identity. Machine Sequence Machine systems may execute events based on: sensor states; instructions; resource availability; control logic; completion signals. ERLSM may represent these sequences without assuming human participation. Sequence Qualification A sequence may be: direct; indirect; immediate; deferred; parallel; conditional; partial; qualified; ambiguous; conflicted. Qualification shall remain visible. Qualified Sequence ≠ Invalid Sequence. Sequence Uncertainty Available information may establish that events are related but not establish their exact order. ERLSM shall preserve uncertainty. Unknown Order ≠ Unrelated Events. Sequence Conflict Different systems may report incompatible ordering. ERLSM shall preserve the conflict until resolved. Sequence Conflict ≠ Permission to Select the Most Convenient Order. Sequence Reconsideration New governed timing or operational information may require sequence reconsideration. Prior sequence representations shall remain traceable. Sequence Reconsideration ≠ Historical Erasure. Sequence Stability Once governed sequence is established, technical migration or storage changes shall not alter it without materially relevant information. System Change ≠ Sequence Change by default. Sequence and Grouping ERLSM may produce sequence structures that later support Event Groups, Event Chains, or Event Networks. It does not itself create those structures. Sequence Structure ≠ Event Group. ERLGM remains authoritative. Sequence and Merge / Split Sequence complexity does not by itself justify event merge or split. Sequential Proximity ≠ Merge Criterion. Sequence Divergence ≠ Split Criterion by itself. ERLMM remains authoritative together with upstream TREFS and TREBS. Sequence and Taxation ERLSM does not determine: legal tax point; tax period; realization moment; accrual date; recognition date; tax aggregation; tax jurisdiction; Tax Base; Tax Liability; or another jurisdiction-specific legal consequence. Therefore: Governed Event Sequence ≠ Tax Timing Determination. Governance States ERLSM may represent: Sequence Governance Ready Sequence Under Governance Predecessor Established Successor Established Immediate Sequence Deferred Sequence Concurrent Sequence Parallel Sequence Branching Sequence Converging Sequence Conditional Sequence Interrupted Sequence Resumed Sequence Reversal Sequence Replacement Sequence Correction Sequence Sequence Qualified Sequence Ambiguous Sequence Conflicted Sequence Unresolved Governed Event Sequence Established Governance Requirements ERLSM implementations shall ensure that: sequence governance operates on governed Event Relationships; Event Timing remains under TRETS; predecessor and successor relationships can be represented; immediate and deferred sequence remain distinguishable; concurrent events can be represented; parallel progression can be represented; branching and convergence can be represented; conditional sequence can be represented; interrupted and resumed sequence can be represented; sequence remains distinct from dependency; sequence remains distinct from causation; operational sequence can be distinguished from raw timestamp order; one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, and many-to-many sequence structures can be represented; cross-system sequence can remain reconstructable; cross-organization sequence can remain reconstructable; cross-border sequence does not become Tax Period determination; blockchain ordering is not automatically treated as complete economic sequence; autonomous and machine-generated sequence can be governed; sequence uncertainty remains visible; sequence conflict remains visible; sequence reconsideration remains traceable; system changes do not automatically alter sequence; grouping remains under ERLGM; Merge & Split remains under ERLMM; and jurisdiction-specific tax timing remains downstream. Governance Logic IF ERLDM establishes a materially relevant Event Dependency Structure, THEN ERLSM shall evaluate the relative Event Sequence where required. IF Event A materially precedes Event B within the governed relationship, THEN a predecessor–successor relationship may be established. IF events occur concurrently, THEN concurrency shall be preserved rather than forcing artificial linear order. IF one event precedes multiple events, THEN branching sequence may be represented. IF multiple earlier events converge into one later event, THEN converging sequence may be represented without merging the earlier events. IF sequence depends on a condition, THEN the conditional state shall remain explicit. IF system timestamps conflict with governed operational information, THEN raw timestamp order shall not automatically determine sequence. IF sequence remains uncertain or conflicted, THEN the applicable governance state shall remain visible. IF sequence information suggests Event Formation or Boundary problems, THEN those issues shall be referred upstream rather than resolved inside ERLSM. IF the Event Sequence Structure is sufficiently governed, THEN it shall proceed to ERLGM for Event Relationship Grouping governance. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum ERLSM implementation should support: Dependency Structure Reference The ERLDM output entering sequence governance. Sequence Identifier A stable identifier for the governed sequence relationship. Primary Event Reference The event whose sequence relationship is being governed. Related Event Reference The event positioned relative to the primary event. Predecessor Event Reference Where a governed predecessor exists. Successor Event Reference Where a governed successor exists. Sequence Direction The governed directional order. Sequence Type Immediate, deferred, concurrent, parallel, conditional, branching, converging, interrupted, resumed, or other governed sequence type. Sequence Basis The governed information supporting sequence. Event Timing References The relevant TRETS outputs used in sequence governance. Operational Sequence Reference Where operational order differs from simple timestamp ordering. Sequence Condition Any governed condition controlling progression. Branch Reference Where the event belongs to a branching sequence. Convergence Reference Where multiple sequence paths converge. Sequence Cardinality One-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, or many-to-many. Sequence Extent The part of the relationship to which sequence applies. Sequence Confidence The qualified confidence in the sequence determination. Ambiguity State Whether exact ordering remains uncertain. Conflict State Whether materially conflicting ordering information exists. Prior Sequence Reference Where a prior governed sequence has been reconsidered. Correction / Reconsideration Reference The relevant change history. Sequence Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the sequence decision.
