EBIM — Event Boundary Identification Module Governs identification of the candidate structural Event Boundary and its basis. 2. EBSCM — Event Boundary Scope Module Governs the structural scope of the Event Boundary and what may legitimately fall within its governed extent. 3. EBEM — Event Boundary Exclusion Module Governs what must remain outside the Event Boundary while preserving relevant external associations. 4. EBSM — Event Boundary Separation Module Governs separation of adjacent, overlapping, composite, or otherwise distinguishable event structures where independent Event Boundaries are required. 5. EBRM — Event Boundary Revision Module Governs reconsideration and revision of established Event Boundaries when material new information or structural change requires modification. Together: EBIM ↓ EBSCM ↓ EBEM ↓ EBSM ↓ EBRM operationalize the TREBS governed space. Detailed internal governance belongs to the individual modules and is not duplicated within the Parent Standard. Transition from TREFS TREFS produces: Governed Formed Event TREBS receives that output. The architectural distinction is: TREFS asks: What governed event structure has been formed? TREBS asks: What is the legitimate governed extent of that formed event? Therefore: Event Formation ≠ Event Boundary. TREBS must not reopen Event Formation merely because boundary governance is difficult. Where a genuine formation deficiency is discovered, the issue may be returned to TREFS through governed reconsideration. Transition to TRETS Successful TREBS governance produces: Governed Bounded Event That event proceeds into: TRETS — Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard TRETS then governs its temporal position and structure. The transition is: Governed Formed Event → TREBS → Governed Bounded Event → TRETS → Governed Temporally Situated Event TREBS must not pre-empt that temporal governance. Foundational Principles Event Formation ≠ Event Boundary. Governed Formed Event ≠ Governed Bounded Event. System Boundary ≠ Event Boundary. Record Boundary ≠ Event Boundary. Contract Boundary ≠ Event Boundary. Accounting Boundary ≠ Event Boundary. Organizational Boundary ≠ Event Boundary. Association ≠ Boundary Inclusion by Default. Related Activity ≠ Event Membership. One Process ≠ One Event by Default. Multiple Technical Operations ≠ Multiple Events by Default. Aggregation ≠ Boundary Integrity by Default. Fragmentation ≠ Boundary Precision by Default. Shared Element ≠ Shared Event Boundary by Default. Distributed System Boundary ≠ Event Boundary. Machine Action Boundary ≠ Event Boundary by Default. Autonomous Decision Cycle ≠ Event Boundary by Default. Boundary Ambiguity ≠ Governance Failure. Event Boundary Revision ≠ Historical Erasure. Tax Rule Change ≠ Event Boundary Change by Default. Event Boundary ≠ Event Timing. Event Boundary ≠ Event Location. Event Boundary ≠ Event Participation. Event Boundary ≠ Event-to-Value Association. Event Separation ≠ Event Relationship Determination. Governed Bounded Event ≠ Determined Tax-Relevant Event. Event Boundary ≠ Tax Jurisdiction. Event Boundary Established ≠ Legal Taxability Established. TREGA™ governs the event. The jurisdiction governs the tax. Canonical Boundary TREBS governs the structural Event Boundary of a sufficiently formed event, including Event Boundary identification, scope, inclusion, exclusion, separation, ambiguity, conflict, uncertainty, revision, and readiness for subsequent Event Timing governance. TREBS does not govern Event Formation, legal tax point, tax period, Event Location, Tax Jurisdiction, Event Participation, taxpayer determination, value lifecycle, final Event-to-Value Association, Event Relationships, Event Determination, legal taxability, tax base, tax rate, exemptions, deductions, tax liability, reporting obligations, payment, collection, or enforcement. TREBS begins with: Governed Formed Event and ends with: Governed Bounded Event Canonical Closing Statement Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard establishes the governed structural extent of an event before temporal, spatial, participatory, value, relational, determination, and jurisdiction-specific taxation layers are applied. It prevents technical systems, records, contracts, accounting structures, organizational structures, machine operations, and downstream tax assumptions from silently defining where an event begins and ends. By separating Event Formation from Event Boundary, association from membership, technical granularity from event granularity, event separation from Event Relationships, and operational Event Boundary from Tax Jurisdiction, TREBS creates a stable jurisdiction-neutral boundary layer through which a Governed Formed Event becomes a Governed Bounded Event ready for subsequent TREGA™ governance. TREGA™ governs the event. The jurisdiction governs the tax.
