A digital event may have precise temporal information while its operational location remains distributed or unresolved. Therefore: Event Time ≠ Event Location. Event Location belongs to: TRELS — Tax-Relevant Event Location Standard. ------------------------------ Event Timing and Participation A timestamp may identify when an actor performed an action. It does not establish the actor's governed participation role. Therefore: Temporal Association ≠ Event Participation Determination. Participation belongs to TREPS. ------------------------------ Event Timing and Value A change in value may occur at or around a particular time. TRETS may preserve the temporal relationship but does not govern the value lifecycle or final Event-to-Value Association. Therefore: Event Time ≠ Value Recognition Determination. VFM® governs the value lifecycle. TRVAS governs Event-to-Value Association within TREGA™. ------------------------------ Event Timing and Event Relationships Chronological order may inform later relationship governance. However: Earlier Event ≠ Cause of Later Event by Default. Temporal Proximity ≠ Event Relationship by Default. Final Event Relationship governance belongs to TRERLS. ------------------------------ Operational Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point This is a foundational TRETS boundary. A jurisdiction may legally define a taxation point according to: supply delivery payment invoice transfer settlement acceptance realization accrual statutory deeming rule another jurisdiction-specific condition TRETS does not choose among these legal rules. TRETS establishes the governed operational temporal reality upon which such rules may subsequently operate. Therefore: Operational Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point. ------------------------------ Event Timing ≠ Tax Period Determination An event occurring on a particular date does not by itself determine the legal tax period to which a jurisdiction assigns the event. Tax period determination belongs to jurisdiction-specific taxation systems. Therefore: Event Timing ≠ Tax Period Determination. ------------------------------ Jurisdiction-Neutral Timing TRETS must remain jurisdiction-neutral. The same Governed Temporally Situated Event may subsequently be evaluated differently by multiple jurisdictions. Conceptually: One Governed Event ↓ One Governed Operational Temporal Representation ↓ Jurisdiction A ↓ Legal Tax Timing Rule A Jurisdiction B ↓ Legal Tax Timing Rule B Jurisdiction C ↓ Legal Tax Timing Rule C The operational temporal representation remains stable unless the underlying governed event information itself changes. ------------------------------ Temporal Governance States TRETS may represent Event Timing through states including: 1. Timing Ready 2. Timing Under Governance 3. Timing Qualified 4. Timing Conflicted 5. Timing Unresolved 6. Timing Established 7. Governed Temporally Situated Event These states allow downstream systems to distinguish established timing from qualified or unresolved timing. ------------------------------ Cross-Architecture Boundary TRETS may consume or interact with governed outputs from other OOF® architectures. ORA™ may establish operational reality from which temporal information originates. ADIT® may govern evidence and auditability associated with temporal records. VALIDOS™ may govern validation of relevant temporal claims or methods. INTEGROS® may govern broader integrity conditions. OBIDENITY® may govern identity and origin associated with temporal sources. VFM® may govern temporal states within the value lifecycle. TRETS remains responsible specifically for: the temporal governance of the Tax-Relevant Event within TREGA™. ------------------------------ Governance Requirements TRETS requires that: 1. Event Timing begins from a Governed Bounded Event. 2. relevant temporal signals are distinguished from unrelated system timestamps. 3. recorded timestamps are not automatically treated as governed Event Time. 4. temporal sources remain traceable. 5. Event Start is governed where structurally relevant. 6. Event Completion is governed where structurally relevant. 7. Event Duration is governed where structurally relevant. 8. temporal order is established where materially relevant. 9. point events and interval events remain distinguishable. 10. open events may remain temporally open where completion is not established. 11. continuous events are not automatically divided according to tax or accounting periods. 12. multi-stage timing does not automatically create multiple events. 13. distributed-system timestamps are reconciled without allowing one system clock to silently define operational reality. 14. machine-generated timestamp volume does not determine event multiplicity. 15. autonomous execution cycles do not automatically determine Event Timing. 16. original time-zone information remains traceable where relevant. 17. normalized time does not erase source temporal representation. 18. temporal precision does not exceed the governed information supporting it. 19. temporal ambiguity remains explicit. 20. temporal conflict remains explicit. 21. temporal uncertainty may be represented as a qualified range. 22. temporal correction preserves historical traceability. 23. Event Timing does not silently redefine Event Boundary. 24. Event Timing does not determine Event Location. 25. Event Timing does not determine Event Participation. 26. Event Timing does not govern value lifecycle. 27. chronological order does not automatically establish Event Relationships. 28. Operational Event Time remains distinct from Legal Tax Point. 29. Event Timing remains distinct from Tax Period Determination. 30. jurisdiction-specific taxation rules do not redefine operational Event Timing by default. 31. the resulting temporal representation is sufficiently governed before transfer to TRELS. ------------------------------ Governance Logic TRETS applies the following architecture-level logic: Has a Governed Bounded Event been established? If no: → Event Timing governance is not ready. If yes: → identify relevant temporal information. Can operational Event Time be sufficiently distinguished from technical, administrative, reporting, or downstream timestamps? If no: → preserve Timing Qualified, Conflicted, or Unresolved state. If yes: → establish the relevant temporal representation. Does the event require a governed Start? If yes: → govern Event Start. Does the event require a governed Completion? If yes: → govern Event Completion. Is duration materially relevant? If yes: → govern Event Duration. Is relative temporal order materially relevant? If yes: → govern Event Temporal Order. Are material temporal conflicts or uncertainties unresolved? If yes: → preserve the appropriate qualified state. If no: → establish the governed temporal representation. Is the event sufficiently temporally situated for subsequent TREGA™ governance? If yes: → produce Governed Temporally Situated Event. If no: → preserve the appropriate unresolved or qualified state. ------------------------------ Core Modules TRETS is operationalized through five Core Modules. 1. ETIM — Event Time Identification Module Governs identification and differentiation of temporal information relevant to the Governed Bounded Event. Primary question owned by the module: Which temporal signals legitimately describe the operational time of this event? ------------------------------ 2. ETSM — Event Start Module Governs establishment of the operational beginning of an event where a meaningful Event Start exists. Primary responsibility: Event Start governance. ------------------------------ 3. ETCM — Event Completion Module Governs establishment of the operational completion of an event where a meaningful completion state exists. Primary responsibility: Event Completion governance. ------------------------------ 4. ETDM — Event Duration Module Governs the temporal interval or duration of events for which duration is materially relevant. Primary responsibility: Event Duration governance. ------------------------------ 5. ETOM — Event Temporal Order Module Governs relative temporal ordering of the event against materially relevant events or operational structures. Primary responsibility: Event Temporal Order governance. ------------------------------ Internal Module Progression ETIM — What temporal information legitimately belongs to the event? ↓ ETSM — When did the event operationally begin? ↓ ETCM — When did the event operationally complete? ↓ ETDM — What governed temporal duration did the event occupy? ↓ ETOM — Where does the event stand in relevant temporal order? ↓ Governed Temporally Situated Event ------------------------------ Transition from TREBS TREBS provides: Governed Bounded Event TRETS receives that bounded event and governs its temporal representation. The architectural transition is: Event Boundary ↓ Event Timing TRETS must not reopen Event Boundary merely because multiple timestamps exist. Where temporal governance reveals a material structural defect in the Event Boundary, the issue must be returned to the appropriate TREBS governance process. ------------------------------ Transition to TRELS TRETS produces: Governed Temporally Situated Event This becomes the input to: TRELS — Tax-Relevant Event Location Standard The transition is: Governed Bounded Event ↓ TRETS — Event Timing ↓ Governed Temporally Situated Event ↓ TRELS — Event Location The next governance question becomes: Where did the temporally situated event occur operationally? Not: Which jurisdiction has the legal right to tax it? ------------------------------ Foundational Principles Recorded Timestamp ≠ Governed Event Time by Default. Event Time ≠ Single Timestamp by Default. Source Timestamp ≠ Authoritative Event Time by Default. Earliest Timestamp ≠ Event Start by Default. Operational Completion ≠ Legal Tax Recognition. Event Duration ≠ Tax Period. Temporal Order ≠ Causal Relationship by Default. Technical Timestamp Precision ≠ Operational Temporal Precision. System Clock ≠ Event Clock by Default. Machine Timestamp ≠ Independent Event Time by Default. Autonomous Execution Cycle ≠ Governed Event Timing by Default. Normalized Time ≠ Original Recorded Time. Temporal Ambiguity ≠ Permission for Arbitrary Timestamp Selection. Event Time Correction ≠ Historical Erasure. Event Timing ≠ Event Boundary Governance. Event Time ≠ Event Location. Temporal Association ≠ Event Participation Determination. Event Time ≠ Value Recognition Determination. Temporal Proximity ≠ Event Relationship by Default. Operational Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point. Event Timing ≠ Tax Period Determination. ------------------------------ Canonical Boundary TRETS governs the operational temporal representation of a Governed Bounded Event, including Event Time identification, Event Start, Event Completion, Event Duration, Event Temporal Order, temporal precision, ambiguity, conflict, uncertainty, distributed timing, machine-generated timing, autonomous timing, temporal correction, and readiness for subsequent Event Location governance. TRETS does not govern: Event Context Event Recognition Event Formation Event Boundary Event Location Tax Jurisdiction Event Participation taxpayer determination value lifecycle final Event-to-Value Association Event Relationship determination final Event Determination legal tax point tax period determination legal taxability tax base tax rate exemptions deductions tax liability reporting obligations payment collection enforcement TRETS begins with: Governed Bounded Event and ends with: Governed Temporally Situated Event ------------------------------ Canonical Closing Statement The Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard establishes a governed temporal representation of operational reality before jurisdiction-specific taxation rules interpret that reality. It ensures that timestamps, system clocks, accounting dates, settlement records, machine logs, autonomous execution cycles, and downstream tax assumptions do not silently become authoritative definitions of when an event occurred. A governed event may have a point in time, an interval, a duration, multiple temporal stages, distributed timing, or qualified temporal uncertainty. TRETS preserves the representation that operational reality legitimately supports. TRETS governs when the event occurred as governed operational reality — not when tax law decides that the event becomes taxable. TREGA™ governs the event. The jurisdiction governs the tax. Module Architecture → Event Time Identification Module (ETIM) → Event Start Module (ETSM) → Event Completion Module (ETCM) → Event Duration Module (ETDM) → Event Temporal Order Module (ETOM) Related Documents → About Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard (TRETS)

title: OOF™ Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard - (TRVAS)
text: OOF™ Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard - (TRVAS) Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard - (TRVAS) OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ Parent Standard: TRVAS — Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard Operational Layer: Tax-Relevant Value Association Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance Type: Parent Standard Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Value Association Origin ID: TREGA-TRVAS-008 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 1 September 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard (TRVAS) governs how value references, value states, value changes, and other governed value results are associated with a Governed Participatory Event so that the event can carry a sufficiently structured representation of value into subsequent Tax-Relevant Event governance. TRVAS establishes which governed value information legitimately belongs to the event, how that relationship is represented, how multiple value associations are distinguished, how value states and changes are connected to the event, and how those associations remain traceable. TRVAS does not determine the origin, emergence, development, degradation, nullification, restoration, extinction, ownership, economic meaning, or complete lifecycle of value. Those questions belong to VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism and other appropriate governance architectures. TRVAS also does not determine taxable value, Tax Base, consideration under law, customs value, transfer-pricing value, market value under a jurisdiction-specific rule, deductible amount, taxable income, taxable gain, tax rate, or Tax Liability. The foundational boundary is: VFM® determines what happened to value. TREGA™ determines which governed value result belongs to the event. Purpose Tax-relevant events frequently interact with value. An event may: create value; transfer value; exchange value; consume value; transform value; increase value; decrease value; temporarily hold value; redistribute value; destroy value; restore value; or affect several different values simultaneously. Yet the existence of value somewhere in an operational system does not establish that the value belongs to the specific event being governed. Likewise, a monetary amount appearing in a transaction record does not automatically represent the complete value structure of the event. TRVAS exists to establish a governed association layer between: Governed Participatory Event and: Governed Value Information without converting that association into a legal tax valuation. Core Question Which governed value results materially belong to the Tax-Relevant Event, and how can those relationships be represented without determining the jurisdiction-specific taxable value, Tax Base, ownership, entitlement, or legal tax consequence of that value? TREGA™ Governance Flow The complete TREGA™ Parent Standard governance sequence is: 1. TRECS — Tax-Relevant Event Context Standard → 2. TRERS — Tax-Relevant Event Recognition Standard → 3. TREFS — Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard → 4. TREBS — Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard → 5. TRETS — Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard → 6. TRELS — Tax-Relevant Event Location Standard → 7. TREPS — Tax-Relevant Event Participation Standard → 8. TRVAS — Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard ← CURRENT STANDARD → 9. TRERLS — Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard → 10. TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard → 11. TREGS — Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance Standard → 12. TRECLS — Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity Standard Position Within TREGA™ TRVAS operates after Event Participation has been governed and before relationships between multiple events are governed. Its architectural position is: Event Participation → Value Association → Event Relationships TREPS establishes: Who or what materially participated in the event? TRVAS establishes: Which governed value results materially belong to the event? TRERLS subsequently establishes: How does the event relate to other governed events? Governed Transition TRVAS receives: Governed Participatory Event together with relevant governed value information and produces: Governed Value-Associated Event The canonical transition is: Governed Participatory Event + Governed Value Results → TRVAS — Value Association Governance → Governed Value-Associated Event This output proceeds to TRERLS. Governed Space TRVAS governs the architecture-level space through which value is legitimately associated with a Tax-Relevant Event. This includes governance of: value-association identification; value references; event-value relationships; value-state association; value-change association; multiple value associations; participant-value-event distinctions; direct and indirect value association; value-association qualification; value-association uncertainty; value-association conflict; value-association traceability; and value-association readiness for downstream TREGA™ governance. TRVAS does not govern the internal lifecycle of the value itself. Value Association A Value Association represents the governed relationship between a value result and the specific Tax-Relevant Event. The existence of value does not automatically establish this relationship. Therefore: Value Existence ≠ Event Value Association A governed association requires sufficient support that the value information materially belongs to the event. Governed Value Result TRVAS may consume governed value results from VFM® or another legitimate upstream value-governance source. Such results may describe: value reference; value state; value change; value development; value degradation; value nullification; value restoration; or another governed value condition. TRVAS does not recalculate or redefine those results. Its question is narrower: Does this governed value result materially belong to this governed event? Value Reference A value associated with an event must be sufficiently referenceable so that the relationship can remain stable and reconstructable. A Value Reference may connect the event to an upstream governed value object or value result. The reference does not itself establish the association. Value Reference ≠ Value Association by Default. Monetary and Non-Monetary Value TRVAS shall not assume that relevant value must be expressed as money. Governed events may involve: monetary value; goods; services; digital assets; rights; access; resources; productive capacity; data-related value; computational resources; energy; economic benefits; obligations; or other governed forms of value. Therefore: Value ≠ Monetary Amount by Default TRVAS must remain capable of representing value associations before a jurisdiction determines which forms of value matter for taxation. Recorded Amount Versus Governed Value Operational systems frequently contain prices, balances, invoices, settlement amounts, accounting amounts, estimated values, and other numeric representations. These records may support Value Association. They are not automatically authoritative representations of governed value. Therefore: Recorded Amount ≠ Governed Value by Default. And: Invoice Amount ≠ Taxable Value by Default. Value Association Identification TRVAS shall establish whether available governed value information potentially belongs to the event. The purpose is to distinguish: Value information relevant to this event from: Value information merely present in surrounding operational systems. A value reference may enter association governance only where a plausible event relationship exists. Direct Value Association A governed value result may directly correspond to the event. For example, an event may directly produce, transfer, consume, or transform a governed value. Where sufficient support exists, TRVAS may establish a direct Value Association. However: Direct Value Association ≠ Taxable Consideration. The legal meaning remains downstream. Indirect Value Association Some value relationships may exist through intermediate operational structures. TRVAS may preserve indirect association where materially relevant. An indirect relationship shall not automatically be excluded merely because the value does not move directly between two participants. Therefore: Indirect Value Association ≠ Irrelevant Value by Default. Multiple Value Associations One event may legitimately interact with multiple values. The canonical model is: One Governed Event ↓ Value A + Value B + Value C + Value N Examples may include: goods and payment; service and digital entitlement; asset and consideration; energy and computational output; several currencies; multiple digital assets; or multiple value changes. Therefore: One Event ≠ One Value by Default TRVAS shall preserve materially distinct value relationships rather than forcing the event into one value field. One Value Across Multiple Events The same governed value may also relate to multiple events over time. TRVAS shall not assume that a value belongs exclusively to one event merely because an association exists. Therefore: Value Association ≠ Exclusive Event Ownership of Value. TRERLS may subsequently govern relationships among events where necessary. VFM® remains authoritative for the Value Lifecycle. Value State Association An event may be materially associated with a particular governed state of value. TRVAS shall preserve that relationship where relevant. However: Value State Association ≠ Value State Determination. VFM® governs the value state itself. TRVAS only establishes its relationship to the event. Value Change Association A governed event may be associated with a change in value. This may include increase, decrease, transfer, transformation, development, degradation, nullification, restoration, or another governed change. TRVAS shall establish whether the governed change materially belongs to the event. The boundary is: VFM® governs the Value Change. TRVAS governs the Event ↔ Value Change relationship. Therefore: Value Change Association ≠ Value Change Governance Value Without Transfer Value may be associated with an event even where no conventional transfer occurs. An event may: create value; consume value; destroy value; improve value; impair value; unlock value; restrict value; or transform value. Therefore: No Value Transfer ≠ No Value Association. This distinction is particularly important for digital, machine, infrastructure, and autonomous economies. Transfer Without Ownership Determination Where value is transferred, TRVAS may represent the relationship between the transfer result and the event. It does not determine legal ownership before or after the transfer. Therefore: Value Transfer Association ≠ Ownership Determination. OBIDENITY® remains authoritative for governed ownership where applicable. Participant and Value Association TREPS establishes Event Participation. TRVAS shall not assume that every participant owns, receives, supplies, controls, or benefits from every value associated with the event. Therefore: Event Participant ≠ Value Owner by Default and: Participation Role ≠ Value Entitlement An actor may materially participate without owning the associated value. Participant–Value Relationship Where materially relevant, TRVAS may preserve which value relationship is associated with which participant structure. However, such representation remains an event-value association structure. It shall not independently determine: legal ownership; beneficial ownership; legal entitlement; contractual entitlement; economic ownership under tax law; or liability for the value. Those conclusions remain outside TRVAS. Gross and Component Value Structures A single event may contain several value components. A total recorded amount may conceal materially different governed value relationships. TRVAS shall permit component-level associations where operationally justified. However: Total Recorded Amount ≠ Single Governed Value by Default. TRVAS does not prescribe a jurisdiction-specific gross/net or taxable/non-taxable decomposition. Positive, Negative, and Null Value Conditions Value association shall not be limited to positive economic amounts. A governed event may involve: positive value; negative value; zero-value state; value loss; value degradation; liability-like economic burden; or value nullification. TRVAS may associate such governed results with the event without determining their tax treatment. Zero Monetary Amount ≠ No Tax-Relevant Value Association by Default. Currency and Unit Representation Value may be expressed in different currencies, units, quantities, measures, or governed representations. TRVAS shall preserve the relevant upstream representation without assuming that one currency or unit constitutes the legally required tax measurement. Value Unit ≠ Tax Measurement Rule. Currency conversion, valuation methodology, and jurisdiction-specific tax measurement remain downstream unless governed by another appropriate architecture. Estimated Value Some operational events may contain estimated rather than directly observed value. TRVAS may associate a governed estimated value result where its status is clearly preserved. Therefore: Estimated Value ≠ Established Value. and: Estimated Value Association ≠ Tax Valuation. Value Association Confidence Value associations may possess different levels of support. TRVAS shall permit qualification where necessary. A Value Association may be: Established Qualified Partial Ambiguous Conflicted Unresolved A downstream requirement for a numeric amount shall not justify artificial certainty. Value Association Uncertainty Where it is unclear whether a governed value result belongs to the event, uncertainty shall remain visible. Therefore: Value Association Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Assign Convenient Value. The association shall not be created or rejected merely because one outcome produces a preferred tax result. Value Association Conflict Different operational or governed sources may associate different value results with the same event. TRVAS shall preserve material conflicts until sufficiently resolved. Therefore: Value Association Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Valuation Selection. TRVAS governs the conflict in association. It does not determine jurisdiction-specific legal valuation. Value Association Traceability Every material Value Association should remain sufficiently reconstructable. The governance structure should permit determination of: which event the value relates to; which governed value reference was used; which upstream value source produced the value result; which value state or change is associated; what basis supports the association; whether the association is direct or indirect; whether uncertainty existed; whether conflicting associations existed; and what governance state was assigned. Traceability must preserve the distinction between the value result and its association with the event. Value Association and Event Boundary TRVAS operates within the Event Boundary already governed by TREBS. Value information shall not silently expand the Event Boundary. Therefore: Value Association ≠ Event Boundary Expansion If value evidence indicates that the existing Event Boundary may be incorrect, the matter shall be referred to the appropriate upstream TREGA™ governance layer. TRVAS shall not redefine the Event Boundary independently. Value Association and Event Formation The presence of additional value does not automatically create another event. Likewise, multiple value changes may belong to one formed event. Therefore: Multiple Values ≠ Multiple Events by Default. If materially distinct event formation may exist, TREFS remains authoritative. Value Association and Event Timing A value may be recorded, recognized, transferred, settled, measured, or updated at a time different from the governed operational Event Timing. Therefore: Value Timestamp ≠ Event Time by Default. TRETS remains authoritative for Event Timing. TRVAS shall preserve relevant value timing only as part of the association where necessary. Value Association and Event Location A value may be recorded, stored, transferred, or represented in a location different from the governed Event Location. Therefore: Value Location ≠ Event Location by Default. Asset Location ≠ Tax Jurisdiction by Default. TRELS remains authoritative for Event Location. Value Association and Event Participation TRVAS receives the Governed Participatory Event from TREPS. It shall preserve participant structures without redefining them. A value relationship may provide additional evidence relevant to participation, but TRVAS shall not independently create or remove participants. Therefore: Value Association ≠ Participation Determination. TREPS remains authoritative for Event Participation. Value Association and Event Relationships The same value may appear across several related events. TRVAS shall preserve the association within the current event. TRERLS subsequently governs relationships among those events. Therefore: Shared Value Reference ≠ Same Event by Default. Relationship to VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism VFM® owns the governance of the Value Lifecycle. Its governed space includes what happens to value across: Value Context ↓ Value Origin ↓ Value Emergence ↓ Value Recognition ↓ Value State ↓ Value Change ↓ Value Development / Value Degradation ↓ Value Nullification ↓ Value Restoration / Value Extinction TRVAS shall not reproduce this lifecycle. The architectural boundary is: VFM® governs what happened to value. TRVAS governs which governed value result belongs to the Tax-Relevant Event. This separation allows TREGA™ to consume governed value information without becoming a second value-governance architecture. Relationship to OBIDENITY® TRVAS does not determine ownership merely because value is associated with an actor or event. OBIDENITY® governs origin-bound identity, ownership, authority, permission, provenance, transfer, continuity, and related identity-governance structures where applicable. Therefore: Value Association ≠ Ownership Governance. Relationship to Accountability and Liability Value association does not establish who is responsible for value creation, loss, transfer, degradation, or another outcome. Therefore: Value Association ≠ Accountability. Value Loss Association ≠ Liability Determination. AGA™ and HALIA™ remain authoritative for their respective governance spaces. Relationship to Tax Law TRVAS deliberately stops before jurisdiction-specific tax valuation. A jurisdiction may later determine whether an associated value constitutes: taxable consideration; taxable income; taxable gain; taxable benefit; customs value; transfer-pricing value; deductible amount; tax base; exempt value; or another legally defined amount. TRVAS does not make those determinations. Therefore: Governed Event Value ≠ Taxable Value and: Value Association ≠ Tax Base Determination Multi-Jurisdiction Governance One governed Value Association may legitimately support different tax interpretations across jurisdictions. The canonical model is: One Governed Event → One Governed Value Association Structure → Jurisdiction A Evaluation → Jurisdiction B Evaluation → Jurisdiction C Evaluation TRVAS shall therefore preserve operational value association independently from any single jurisdiction's valuation rules. Machine and Autonomous Economy Machine and autonomous events may produce value structures that do not resemble traditional human transactions. An AI agent may: allocate computational capacity; obtain a digital service; exchange digital assets; consume energy; generate operational output; trigger resource use; optimize production; or initiate another value-affecting action. TRVAS shall permit these governed value results to associate with the event without requiring a conventional invoice, human buyer, human seller, or monetary payment. Therefore: No Human Transaction ≠ No Value Association. Value Association States TRVAS may represent architecture-level states including: Value Association Ready Value Association Under Governance Value Association Established Multi-Value Association Direct Value Association Indirect Value Association Value State Associated Value Change Associated Value Association Qualified Value Association Ambiguous Value Association Conflicted Value Association Unresolved Governed Value-Associated Event These states describe Value Association only. They do not determine legal tax valuation. Governance Requirements A TRVAS-conformant implementation shall ensure that: value information is associated only where materially relevant to the governed event; governed value references remain distinguishable; monetary and non-monetary value can be represented; multiple values can be associated with one event; one value can remain associated with multiple events where legitimate; Value States can be associated without being redefined; Value Changes can be associated without being re-governed; direct and indirect associations can remain distinguishable; participant identity does not automatically determine value ownership; Participation Role does not automatically determine value entitlement; recorded amounts are not automatically treated as governed value; invoice amounts are not automatically treated as taxable value; uncertainty remains visible; conflicts remain visible; association traceability remains reconstructable; Value Association does not silently redefine Event Formation or Event Boundary; VFM® ownership of the Value Lifecycle remains preserved; ownership governance remains separate; tax valuation remains downstream; and Value Association does not determine Tax Base or Tax Liability. Governance Logic IF a Governed Participatory Event exists, THEN relevant governed value information may enter Value Association governance. IF a governed value result materially belongs to the event, THEN a Governed Value Association may be established. IF multiple materially distinct value results belong to the same event, THEN multiple Value Associations shall be preserved where necessary. IF a Value State or Value Change is governed upstream, THEN TRVAS may associate that result without redefining it. IF a value reference is merely present in surrounding operational data, THEN association shall not be established solely from that presence. IF Value Association remains uncertain or conflicted, THEN the relevant governance state shall remain visible. IF additional value information suggests that Event Formation or Event Boundary may be incorrect, THEN TRVAS shall refer the issue upstream rather than independently redefining the event. IF the event's value associations are sufficiently governed, THEN TRVAS may produce a Governed Value-Associated Event. TRVAS SHALL NOT convert Governed Event Value into jurisdiction-specific taxable value, Tax Base, or Tax Liability. Governance Outputs TRVAS may produce architecture-level outputs including: Governed Value Association; Governed Value Reference Structure; Governed Multi-Value Association Structure; Governed Direct Value Association; Governed Indirect Value Association; Governed Value State Association; Governed Value Change Association; Governed Participant–Value Relationship Reference; Value Association Confidence State; Value Association Ambiguity State; Value Association Conflict State; Value Association Traceability Structure; Value Association Governance State; and the principal output: Governed Value-Associated Event This output becomes the governed input to: TRERLS — Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard Critical Distinctions Value Existence ≠ Event Value Association Value Reference ≠ Value Association by Default Value ≠ Monetary Amount by Default Recorded Amount ≠ Governed Value by Default Invoice Amount ≠ Taxable Value by Default Direct Value Association ≠ Taxable Consideration Indirect Value Association ≠ Irrelevant Value by Default One Event ≠ One Value by Default Value Association ≠ Exclusive Event Ownership of Value Value State Association ≠ Value State Determination Value Change Association ≠ Value Change Governance No Value Transfer ≠ No Value Association Value Transfer Association ≠ Ownership Determination Event Participant ≠ Value Owner by Default Participation Role ≠ Value Entitlement Total Recorded Amount ≠ Single Governed Value by Default Zero Monetary Amount ≠ No Tax-Relevant Value Association by Default Estimated Value ≠ Established Value Estimated Value Association ≠ Tax Valuation Value Association ≠ Event Boundary Expansion Multiple Values ≠ Multiple Events by Default Value Timestamp ≠ Event Time by Default Value Location ≠ Event Location by Default Value Association ≠ Participation Determination Shared Value Reference ≠ Same Event by Default Value Association ≠ Ownership Governance Value Association ≠ Accountability Value Loss Association ≠ Liability Determination Governed Event Value ≠ Taxable Value Value Association ≠ Tax Base Determination Enterprise Application TRVAS provides the value-association layer between governed participation and subsequent Event Relationship governance: ERP / Commerce / Banking / Platform / AI Agent / Machine System → Governed Operational Event → TREPS — Governed Participatory Event VFM® / Governed Value Information → TRVAS — Governed Value-Associated Event → TRERLS — Event Relationship Governance → TREDS — Event Determination → Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record → Jurisdictional Tax Rules / Tax Engine This structure allows taxation systems to consume governed event-value relationships without requiring TREGA™ to determine the tax treatment of the value. Internal Module Architecture TRVAS is operationalized through five Core Modules: 1. VAIM — Value Association Identification Module Identifies governed value information that may materially belong to the event and determines which value references should enter Value Association governance. 2. VARM — Value Reference Module Establishes stable and traceable references between the governed event and relevant governed value objects or results. 3. VACM — Value Change Association Module Governs the association between the event and governed changes affecting value without re-governing the Value Change itself. 4. VASM — Value State Association Module Governs the association between the event and relevant governed Value States without determining those states independently. 5. VATM — Value Association Traceability Module Preserves reconstructable provenance, qualification, uncertainty, conflict, and history of the event-value association structure. Internal Module Flow VAIM — Value Association Identification → VARM — Value Reference → VACM — Value Change Association → VASM — Value State Association → VATM — Value Association Traceability → Governed Value-Associated Event Cross-Architecture Boundaries VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism Owns the Value Lifecycle and determines what happened to value. OBIDENITY® Owns governed identity, origin, ownership, authority, permission, provenance, and related structures. TREPS — Tax-Relevant Event Participation Standard Owns who or what materially participated in the event. TRVAS — Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard Owns which governed value results materially belong to the event. TRERLS — Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard Owns relationships among governed events. AGA™ Owns accountability governance. HALIA™ Owns the lifecycle of harm and liability. Jurisdiction-Specific Tax Systems Own legal tax classification, taxable value, Tax Base, Tax Liability, tax rates, exemptions, deductions, reporting, payment, collection, and enforcement. Canonical Boundary TRVAS governs the association of governed value references, Value States, Value Changes, and other legitimate governed value results with a specific Tax-Relevant Event. It does not govern the complete Value Lifecycle, determine the origin or ownership of value, redefine upstream governed Value States or Value Changes, determine Event Participation, redefine Event Formation or Event Boundary, establish accountability or liability, or determine jurisdiction-specific taxable value, Tax Base, taxable income, taxable gain, consideration, customs value, transfer-pricing value, tax rate, exemption, deduction, Tax Liability, filing obligation, collection, payment, or enforcement. TRVAS ends when the event possesses a sufficiently governed, traceable, and jurisdiction-neutral Value Association structure for subsequent TREGA™ governance. Canonical Closing Statement TRVAS establishes which governed value results belong to the event without allowing Event Value Association to become Value Lifecycle governance, ownership determination, or tax valuation. What happened to value and which part of that governed value reality belongs to an event are separate governance questions. What tax law subsequently does with that value is a third. VFM® governs what happened to value. TREGA™ governs which governed value result belongs to the event. Governed Event Value ≠ Taxable Value. TREGA™ governs the event. The jurisdiction governs the tax. Module Architecture → Value Association Identification Module (VAIM) → Value Reference Module (VARM) → Value Change Association Module (VACM) → Value State Association Module (VASM) → Value Association Traceability Module (VATM) Related Documents → About Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard (TRVAS)

title: OOF™ TREGA™ Architecture Map
text: OOF™ TREGA™ Architecture Map TREGA™ Architecture Map Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Layer TREGA™ serves as the official OOF® Tax-Relevant Event Governance reference map used to identify, define, classify, navigate, govern, evaluate, and understand governable Tax-Relevant Event spaces across physical transactions, digital services, financial systems, platforms, AI agents, autonomous systems, machine-to-machine environments, distributed systems, cross-border activity, organizations, and future taxation environments. The purpose of TREGA™ is not to define taxation itself. The purpose of TREGA™ is to identify, define, separate, and map the governable spaces through which a real-world, economic, operational, digital, transactional, machine-generated, autonomous, or value-affecting occurrence is contextualized, recognized, formed into a governed Event, bounded, temporally and spatially situated, associated with participants and Value, related to other Events, formally determined as tax-relevant, represented as a governed Event Record, and maintained throughout its lifecycle before jurisdiction-specific taxation rules are applied. TREGA™ serves as the official Tax-Relevant Event Governance reference map for: Physical Transactions Digital Transactions Digital Services Commercial Activity Financial Systems Banking Systems Commerce Platforms Digital Platforms Cross-Border Activity Distributed Systems Digital Assets AI Agents Autonomous Systems Machine-to-Machine Transactions Robotics and Machine Economies Industrial Systems Multi-Party Events Multi-Jurisdiction Environments Future Taxation Ecosystems Core Architectural Principle Every Tax-Relevant Event Governance space answers one primary governance question. No Tax-Relevant Event Governance space duplicates the purpose of another Tax-Relevant Event Governance space. Every Tax-Relevant Event Governance space has a defined beginning, a defined operational purpose, and a defined governance boundary. Every Tax-Relevant Event Governance space begins where the preceding Event Governance requirement has been sufficiently established. Together, these Tax-Relevant Event Governance spaces form the official Tax-Relevant Event Governance reference map of TREGA™. Official Tax-Relevant Event Governance Flow Real-World / Digital Event ↓ Event Context ↓ Event Recognition ↓ Event Formation & Root Association ↓ Event Boundary ↓ Event Timing ↓ Event Location ↓ Event Participation ↓ Value Association ↓ Event Relationships Event Determination ↓ Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record ↓ Event Continuity & Lifecycle ↓ Jurisdiction-Ready Tax-Relevant Event 1. Tax-Relevant Event Context Standard (TRECS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Context Core Question Within what governed operational, economic, digital, transactional, organizational, or machine context does the occurrence exist, and which contextual boundaries and relationships are relevant to its Event governance? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Context Standard (TRECS) defines the governance conditions under which the operational, economic, digital, transactional, organizational, machine, platform, infrastructural, or other materially relevant context surrounding an occurrence is formally identified, scoped, related, updated, and maintained as the contextual basis for Tax-Relevant Event Governance. Governance Boundary Begins when a real-world or digital occurrence requires a governed contextual basis before Tax-Relevant Event Recognition can legitimately proceed. Ends when the Event Context has been sufficiently identified, scoped, related, and governed to support recognition of whether the occurrence should enter Tax-Relevant Event Governance. 2. Tax-Relevant Event Recognition Standard (TRERS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Recognition Core Question Which occurrence should enter Tax-Relevant Event Governance, under what recognition conditions, and with what confidence, qualification, or escalation state? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Recognition Standard (TRERS) defines the governance conditions under which an occurrence is recognized as requiring Tax-Relevant Event Governance through explicit recognition rules, relevance screening, confidence assessment, qualification, and escalation where recognition remains uncertain. Governance Boundary Begins when an occurrence exists within a sufficiently governed Event Context and must be assessed for entry into Tax-Relevant Event Governance. Ends when the occurrence has been sufficiently recognized, qualified, rejected, or escalated to support Event Formation Governance. 3. Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard (TREFS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Formation Core Question How must a recognized occurrence be assembled into a governed Event, which components constitute it, and what operational root relationship supports its formation? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard (TREFS) defines the governance conditions under which a recognized occurrence is formed into a governed Event by identifying its constituent components, assembling their relevant relationships, establishing formation dependencies, associating the Event with its operational root, and maintaining Formation Integrity. Governance Boundary Begins when an occurrence has been sufficiently recognized as requiring Tax-Relevant Event Governance. Ends when the occurrence has been sufficiently formed into a governed Event with identifiable components, dependencies, assembly structure, and Root Association to support explicit Event Boundary Governance. Event Root ≠ Identity Origin. 4. Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard (TREBS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Core Question Where does the governed Event begin and end, what belongs inside or outside it, and how must it remain distinguishable from adjacent or related Events? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard (TREBS) defines the governance conditions under which the inclusion, exclusion, scope, separation, and revision boundaries of a Tax-Relevant Event are established so that the Event remains distinguishable from adjacent occurrences, related Events, supporting activity, and external operational conditions. Governance Boundary Begins when an Event has been sufficiently formed and its governed extent must be explicitly established. Ends when the Event Boundary has been sufficiently identified, scoped, separated, excluded where necessary, and governed to support Event Timing. 5. Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard (TRETS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Timing Core Question When does the Event begin, continue, complete, and relate temporally to other Events without converting operational Event Timing into a jurisdiction-specific legal tax point or Tax Period? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard (TRETS) defines the governance conditions under which the temporal identity, start, completion, duration, and temporal ordering of a Tax-Relevant Event are established and maintained as operational Event Timing. Governance Boundary Begins when a sufficiently formed and bounded Event requires explicit temporal positioning. Ends when Event Timing has been sufficiently established through Event Time identification, Start, Completion, Duration, and Temporal Order to support Event Location Governance. Operational Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point. Event Timing ≠ Tax Period Determination. 6. Tax-Relevant Event Location Standard (TRELS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Location Core Question Where does the Event occur physically, digitally, operationally, or across distributed environments without converting Event Location into Tax Jurisdiction determination? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Location Standard (TRELS) defines the governance conditions under which the physical, digital, distributed, operational, or correlated locations associated with a Tax-Relevant Event are identified, represented, related, and maintained without converting those locations into jurisdiction-specific tax conclusions. Governance Boundary Begins when Event Timing has been sufficiently established and the Event requires governed spatial or operational positioning. Ends when materially relevant physical, digital, distributed, and correlated Event Locations have been sufficiently established to support Event Participation Governance. Event Location ≠ Tax Jurisdiction. 7. Tax-Relevant Event Participation Standard (TREPS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Participation Core Question Which human, organizational, digital, machine, or autonomous actors materially participate in the Event, in what roles, and with what continuity without determining taxpayer status? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Participation Standard (TREPS) defines the governance conditions under which human, organizational, digital, machine, autonomous, or other actors are identified for Event Participation, associated with the Event, assigned materially relevant participation roles, and governed for participation continuity. Governance Boundary Begins when a sufficiently contextualized, recognized, formed, bounded, timed, and located Event requires identification of the actors materially participating in it. Ends when materially relevant Event Participants, their participation roles, actor associations, machine or autonomous participation, and participation continuity have been sufficiently governed to support Value Association. Participant ≠ Taxpayer. Identified Actor ≠ Governed Event Participant. 8. Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard (TRVAS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Value Association Core Question Which governed Value states, changes, transfers, or relationships belong to the Event, and how must they remain associated without duplicating Value lifecycle governance itself? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard (TRVAS) defines the governance conditions under which governed Value references, Value states, Value changes, and materially relevant Value relationships are associated with a Tax-Relevant Event and remain traceable as Event-specific Value Associations. Governance Boundary Begins when Event Participation has been sufficiently established and governed Value results must be associated with the Event. Ends when materially relevant Value references, states, changes, and traceability relationships have been sufficiently associated with the Event to support Event Relationship Governance. Value Association ≠ Value Governance. 9. Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard (TRERLS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Relationships Core Question How is the Event related to other Events through dependency, sequence, grouping, Merge, Split, or other materially relevant relationships? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard (TRERLS) defines the governance conditions under which Tax-Relevant Events are identified as related through dependency, sequence, grouping, Merge, Split, or other materially relevant Event relationships without collapsing distinct Events into one undifferentiated activity. Governance Boundary Begins when an Event has sufficient Context, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, and Value Association to determine materially relevant relationships with other Events. Ends when those relationships have been sufficiently identified and governed to support formal Event Determination. One economic activity ≠ necessarily one Event. Multiple technical operations ≠ necessarily multiple economically independent Events. 10. Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard (TREDS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Determination Core Question When is an Event sufficiently governed to be formally determined as tax-relevant and eligible for downstream taxation analysis without determining whether the Event is legally taxable? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard (TREDS) defines the governance conditions under which a governed Event is assessed for Determination Readiness, evaluated against Event Determination conditions, assigned a formal Tax-Relevant Event Determination, qualified for uncertainty where required, and reconsidered when materially relevant conditions change. Governance Boundary Begins when the Event has been sufficiently governed across Context, Recognition, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, Value Association, and Event Relationships. Ends when the Event has been sufficiently determined as tax-relevant, not tax-relevant, qualified, uncertain, or requiring reconsideration to support Event Record Governance. Event Determination ≠ Taxability Determination. 11. Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance Standard (TREGS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance Core Question How can a Determined Tax-Relevant Event be represented as a stable, identifiable, structured, linked, traceable, and interoperable governed record without allowing the record to redefine the Event or determine its legal tax consequence? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance Standard (TREGS) defines the governance conditions under which a Determined Tax-Relevant Event is transformed into an identifiable, structured, linked, traceable, and interoperable Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record while preserving the governed meaning established by preceding TREGA™ standards. Governance Boundary Begins when an Event has received a sufficiently governed Tax-Relevant Event Determination. Ends when the Determined Event has been sufficiently represented as a Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record capable of supporting lifecycle governance and downstream jurisdiction-specific taxation analysis. Governed Event Record ≠ Tax Assessment. 12. Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity Standard (TRECLS) Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity Core Question How can a governed Tax-Relevant Event remain continuous, reconstructable, correctable, and jurisdiction-ready throughout change without erasing historical reality or converting Event lifecycle governance into tax-law administration? Canonical Definition Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity Standard (TRECLS) defines the governance conditions under which a Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record remains methodologically continuous, historically reconstructable, and governably current as the Event is amended, corrected, superseded, maintained, closed, reopened, or referred for New Event Formation when continuity can no longer legitimately be preserved. Governance Boundary Begins when a Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record enters continuing use, maintenance, downstream reliance, lifecycle change, or closure consideration. Continues throughout the remaining Event lifecycle while the Event remains relevant for downstream taxation analysis, reporting, compliance, audit, reconstruction, or other legitimate use. Where material change invalidates the existing Event continuity basis, Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity Standard may trigger governed re-entry into the appropriate earlier TREGA™ governance space rather than forcing the existing Event to absorb a materially different occurrence. Event Continuity ≠ Tax Obligation Lifecycle. Core Governed Tax-Relevant Event Spaces Tax-Relevant Event Context Tax-Relevant Event Recognition Tax-Relevant Event Formation Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Tax-Relevant Event Timing Tax-Relevant Event Location Tax-Relevant Event Participation Tax-Relevant Value Association Tax-Relevant Event Relationships Tax-Relevant Event Determination Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity Recursive Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle TREGA™ does not end when a Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record is created. Once a governed Event remains in use, downstream reliance, reporting, analysis, maintenance, or jurisdictional processing, the architecture becomes recursive: Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record ↓ Event Continuity ↓ Event Amendment ↓ Event Correction ↓ Event Supersession ↓ Event Closure ↓ Jurisdiction-Ready Tax-Relevant Event Where materially relevant information emerges after Closure: Closed Event ↓ Reopening Review ↓ Lifecycle Re-Entry ↓ Updated Governed Event ↓ Reclosure Where Event continuity becomes materially invalid: Material Change ↓ Continuity Reassessment ↓ Continuity Break ↓ New Event Formation Referral ↓ Lifecycle Re-Entry Lifecycle re-entry occurs at the earliest materially affected governance space. A changed Event Context may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Context Standard. A previously unrecognized material occurrence may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Recognition Standard. A materially changed Event constitution may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard. A changed Event Boundary may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard. Changed operational Timing may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard. Changed or corrected Location may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Location Standard. Changed Participation may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Participation Standard. Changed Value Association may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard. A newly established dependency, sequence, Merge, Split, or grouping relationship may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard. A materially changed Event basis may require reconsideration under Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard. The architecture therefore supports targeted governed Event lifecycle re-entry rather than uncontrolled reconstruction of the entire Event. Architectural Position TREGA™ governs the complete Tax-Relevant Event Governance lifecycle before jurisdiction-specific tax determination begins. The architecture progresses through: Real-World / Digital Event ↓ Event Context ↓ Event Recognition ↓ Event Formation & Root Association ↓ Event Boundary ↓ Event Timing ↓ Event Location ↓ Event Participation ↓ Value Association ↓ Event Relationships Event Determination ↓ Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record ↓ Event Continuity & Lifecycle ↓ Jurisdiction-Ready Tax-Relevant Event Together, these Tax-Relevant Event Governance spaces govern how the context of an occurrence is established, whether the occurrence should enter Event Governance, how it becomes a governed Event, where its boundaries lie, when and where it occurs, which actors materially participate, which governed Value results belong to it, how it relates to other Events, when it becomes formally tax-relevant, how it is represented as a governed Event Record, and how that Event remains continuous, reconstructable, correctable, supersedable, closable, and jurisdiction-ready throughout its lifecycle. TREGA™ therefore provides a complete governance path from the first identification of the context in which something happened to the determination of whether the resulting governed Event is ready to enter jurisdiction-specific taxation analysis. What TREGA™ Defines TREGA™ defines: - where Tax-Relevant Event Governance begins, - how Event Context is identified and scoped, - which occurrences should enter Event Governance, - how a recognized occurrence is formed into a governed Event, - how Event components and Root Associations are established, - where the Event begins and ends, - what belongs inside and outside the Event Boundary, - when the Event begins, continues, and completes, - how Event Duration and Temporal Order are governed, - where the Event occurs physically, digitally, operationally, or across distributed environments, - which human, organizational, digital, machine, or autonomous actors materially participate, - what participation roles those actors hold, - which governed Value references, states, and changes belong to the Event, - how Event Value Associations remain traceable, - how Events relate through dependency, sequence, grouping, Merge, or Split, - when the Event is sufficiently governed for Tax-Relevant Event Determination, - how Event Determination uncertainty and reconsideration are governed, - how a Determined Tax-Relevant Event becomes an identifiable governed Event Record, - how Event Records remain structured, linked, traceable, and interoperable, - how Event Continuity is maintained, - how Events are amended, - how incorrect Event states are corrected without historical erasure, - how successor states supersede prior states without deleting history, - how Event Closure is governed, - when a Closed Event may require reopening, - when material transformation requires New Event Formation, - and when the Event becomes Jurisdiction-Ready for downstream tax-rule application. TREGA™ provides the official Tax-Relevant Event Governance language used for Event-space identification, lifecycle navigation, governance classification, structural diagnosis, jurisdiction-readiness, Event Record interoperability, and Tax-Relevant Event architecture design across complex physical, digital, distributed, autonomous, and cross-border environments. Critical Architectural Distinctions Operational Reality ≠ Tax-Relevant Event Governance Tax-Relevant Event ≠ Legally Taxable Event Event Recognition ≠ Taxability Determination Event Formation ≠ Event Boundary Event Root ≠ Identity Origin Operational Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point Event Timing ≠ Tax Period Determination Event Location ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Participant ≠ Taxpayer Participant Identification ≠ Event Participation Identified Actor ≠ Governed Event Participant Value Association ≠ Value Governance Event Relationship ≠ Event Identity Event Determination ≠ Tax Liability Determination Governed Event Record ≠ Tax Assessment Event Amendment ≠ Event Correction Correction ≠ Historical Erasure Record Correction ≠ Event Correction by default Supersession ≠ Historical Deletion Successor State ≠ New Event by default Event Continuity ≠ Tax Obligation Lifecycle Event Closure ≠ Tax Obligation Closure Jurisdiction-Ready ≠ Jurisdiction-Determined Cross-Architecture Governance Boundaries TREGA™ ↔ ORA™ — Operational Reality Architecture ORA™ — Operational Reality Architecture governs what exists and occurs in actual Operational Reality. TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs how occurrences from Operational Reality become structured and governed as Tax-Relevant Events. Operational Reality ≠ Tax-Relevant Event Governance. TREGA™ ↔ OBIDENITY® — Origin-Bound Identity Governance Architecture® OBIDENITY® — Origin-Bound Identity Governance Architecture® governs identity, origin, ownership, authority, permission, responsibility, provenance, transfer, and continuity. TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs whether and how an identified actor materially participates in a specific governed Event. Identity ≠ Event Participation. TREGA™ ↔ VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism governs what happens to Value throughout its lifecycle. TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs which governed Value state, change, reference, or relationship belongs to a specific Tax-Relevant Event. Value Governance ≠ Event Value Association. TREGA™ ↔ VALIDOS™ — Validation Governance Architecture TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ determines when an Event has become sufficiently governed to support downstream taxation analysis. VALIDOS™ — Validation Governance Architecture determines whether a complete validation basis is sufficient to support a Validation Determination and intended reliance. Event Determination ≠ Validation Determination. TREGA™ ↔ INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs Event-specific context, formation, boundary, timing, location, participation, Value Association, relationships, Determination, Record Governance, and lifecycle. INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture governs integrity across governed objects, structures, states, evidence, and processes. Tax-Relevant Event Governance ≠ General Integrity Governance. TREGA™ ↔ ADIT® — Audit in Real Time Architecture TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs the Event and its canonical Event Governance lifecycle. ADIT® — Audit in Real Time Architecture governs evidential observation, preservation, verification, traceability, examination, and auditability of what occurred where applicable. Event Governance ≠ Audit Governance. TREGA™ ↔ AGA™ — Accountability Governance Architecture TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs the methodological conditions under which an occurrence becomes and remains a governed Tax-Relevant Event. AGA™ — Accountability Governance Architecture governs who holds authority, responsibility, accountability, attribution, and decision ownership surrounding relevant actions, decisions, and failures. Event Methodology ≠ Accountability Governance. TREGA™ ↔ HALIA™ — Harm & Liability Architecture TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs the Tax-Relevant Event lifecycle. HALIA™ — Harm & Liability Architecture governs the lifecycle of harm and liability arising from relevant occurrences. Tax-Relevant Event Governance ≠ Harm or Liability Governance. TREGA™ ↔ Jurisdictional Tax Systems TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs the Event before jurisdiction-specific tax rules are applied. Jurisdictional Tax Systems determine what that Event legally means under applicable tax law. Tax-Relevant Event ≠ Legally Taxable Event. Jurisdiction-Ready ≠ Jurisdiction-Determined. Compatible OOF® Architectures GOA™ — Governance Architecture ORA™ — Operational Reality Architecture OBIDENITY® — Origin-Bound Identity Governance Architecture® VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism CLA® — Classification Architecture VALIDOS™ — Validation Governance Architecture INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture AGA™ — Accountability Governance Architecture HALIA™ — Harm & Liability Architecture AIG® — AI Governance Architecture ASGA™ — Autonomous Systems Governance Architecture ADIT® — Audit in Real Time Architecture Canonical Principle TREGA™ does not define legal Taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer determination, tax nexus, legal tax point, Tax Period, Tax Base, Tax Rate, exemptions, deductions, Tax Liability, filing obligations, payment, collection, enforcement, or other jurisdiction-specific legal tax consequences. TREGA™ governs the conditions under which a real-world or digital occurrence is contextualized, recognized, formed into a governed Event, bounded, temporally and spatially situated, associated with participants and Value, related to other Events, formally determined as tax-relevant, represented as a governed Event Record, and maintained through Continuity, Amendment, Correction, Supersession, Closure, and lifecycle re-entry until it becomes Jurisdiction-Ready for downstream tax-rule application. Canonical Closing Statement TREGA™ serves as the official Tax-Relevant Event Governance reference map for physical transactions, digital services, financial systems, platforms, AI agents, autonomous systems, machine-to-machine economies, distributed environments, cross-border activity, and future taxation ecosystems. By defining the primary governable spaces of the complete Tax-Relevant Event lifecycle, TREGA™ provides the architecture used to establish the context in which an occurrence exists, determine whether it should enter Event Governance, form and bound the Event, govern when and where it occurs, identify who or what materially participates, associate governed Value with the Event, establish relationships between Events, determine when the Event has become tax-relevant, convert that Event into a governed and interoperable Record, and preserve its continuity through Amendment, Correction, Supersession, Closure, reopening, and material lifecycle change. TREGA™ therefore establishes taxation-relevant Event Governance as a distinct methodological layer between Operational Reality and jurisdiction-specific taxation systems, enabling one governed Event Reality to remain structurally coherent, historically reconstructable, and Jurisdiction-Ready before different jurisdictions determine what that Event legally means under tax law.

However, the standards and modules listed below form the core structural backbone of TREGA™. 1. text: OOF™ TREGA™ TREGA™ Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Layer TREGA™ serves as the official OOF® tax-relevant event governance architecture used for Event Context governance, Event Recognition, Event Formation, Event Boundary governance, Event Timing, Event Location, Event Participation, Value Association, Event Relationship governance, Event Determination, Event Record Governance, and Event Lifecycle & Continuity governance across physical transactions, digital services, financial systems, commerce platforms, AI agents, autonomous systems, machine-to-machine environments, distributed systems, cross-border activity, organizations, and future taxation environments. Canonical Definition TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ is the jurisdiction-neutral governance architecture that establishes how real-world, economic, operational, digital, transactional, machine-generated, autonomous, and value-affecting occurrences are contextualized, recognized, formed into governed Events, bounded, temporally and spatially situated, associated with participants and value, related to other Events, formally determined as tax-relevant, recorded, and maintained throughout their lifecycle before jurisdiction-specific taxation rules are applied. CLA® — Classification Architecture governs classification of objects and states, while TREGA™ governs Event-specific tax-relevance determination and lifecycle. VALIDOS™ — Validation Governance Architecture governs whether a validation basis sufficiently supports a Validation Determination, while TREGA™ governs whether an Event is sufficiently structured and governed to enter downstream taxation analysis. INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture governs integrity across objects, states, evidence, and processes, while TREGA™ governs Event-specific structure, determination, representation, and lifecycle. ADIT® governs evidential observation, preservation, verification, examination, and auditability of what occurred, while TREGA™ governs the Event itself and the governed structures through which it becomes tax-relevant. AGA™ — Accountability Governance Architecture governs authority, responsibility, accountability, attribution, and decision relationships surrounding Event governance and downstream reliance. HALIA™ — Harm & Liability Architecture governs the lifecycle of harm and liability where Event consequences create relevant harm or liability relationships. TREGA™ serves as the common Tax-Relevant Event Governance architecture supporting the broader OOF® ecosystem by ensuring that operational occurrences become governed Events before jurisdiction-specific taxation systems determine their legal tax meaning. Architectural Position TREGA™ governs the complete Tax-Relevant Event lifecycle before jurisdiction-specific tax determination begins. The architecture progresses through: Real-World / Digital Event ↓ Event Context ↓ Event Recognition ↓ Event Formation & Root Association ↓ Event Boundary ↓ Event Timing ↓ Event Location ↓ Event Participation ↓ Value Association ↓ Event Relationships Event Determination ↓ Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record ↓ Event Continuity & Lifecycle ↓ Jurisdiction-Ready Tax-Relevant Event Together these standards govern how an occurrence is placed within context, recognized as requiring Event Governance, formed into a governed Event, bounded, situated in time and location, associated with participants and Value, connected to other Events, formally determined as tax-relevant, transformed into a governed Event Record, and maintained throughout its lifecycle until it becomes jurisdiction-ready. TREGA™ then hands the governed Event to downstream taxation infrastructure: Jurisdiction-Ready Tax-Relevant Event ↓ Jurisdictional Tax Rules / Tax Engine ↓ Tax Determination ↓ Reporting / Compliance Unlike a tax determination methodology, TREGA™ remains jurisdiction-neutral throughout the complete Event Governance lifecycle. The multi-jurisdiction model becomes: One Event ↓ One Governed Event Layer ↓ Multiple Jurisdictional Evaluations This enables one governed Event Reality to be consumed by multiple jurisdiction-specific taxation systems without requiring TREGA™ to redefine the Event separately for each jurisdiction. Core Governed Tax-Relevant Event Spaces TREGA™ establishes twelve distinct governable Tax-Relevant Event spaces: Tax-Relevant Event Context → within what operational, economic, digital, organizational, or machine environment the Event exists. Tax-Relevant Event Recognition → which occurrence should enter Tax-Relevant Event Governance. Tax-Relevant Event Formation → how the recognized occurrence becomes a governed Event and how its root association is established. Tax-Relevant Event Boundary → what belongs inside and outside the Event. Tax-Relevant Event Timing → when the Event begins, continues, completes, and relates temporally to other Events. Tax-Relevant Event Location → where the Event occurs physically, digitally, operationally, or across distributed environments. Tax-Relevant Event Participation → which actors materially participate in the Event and in what roles. Tax-Relevant Value Association → which governed Value results belong to the Event. Tax-Relevant Event Relationships → how the Event depends upon, sequences with, groups with, merges with, or splits from other Events. Tax-Relevant Event Determination → whether the Event is sufficiently governed to become a Determined Tax-Relevant Event. Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance → how the Determined Event becomes identifiable, structured, linked, traceable, and interoperable as a Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record. Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity → how the governed Event remains continuous, amendable, correctable, supersedable, closable, and jurisdiction-ready throughout its lifecycle. Each space answers a different methodological question. Each can fail independently. Their separation is therefore foundational to the TREGA™ architecture. Cross-Architecture Boundary Lock TREGA™ is intentionally bounded to prevent duplication with adjacent OOF® architectures and jurisdiction-specific tax systems. TREGA™ ↔ ORA™ ORA™: What actually happened in Operational Reality? TREGA™: How does that occurrence become a governed Tax-Relevant Event? Operational Reality ≠ Tax-Relevant Event Governance. TREGA™ ↔ OBIDENITY® OBIDENITY®: Who or what is the actor, under what origin, ownership, authority, permission, and provenance? TREGA™: Does that actor materially participate in this governed Event, and in what Event role? Identity ≠ Event Participation. Identified Actor ≠ Governed Event Participant. TREGA™ ↔ VFM® VFM®: What happened to Value throughout its lifecycle? TREGA™: Which governed Value result belongs to this Event? Value Governance ≠ Event Value Association. TREGA™ ↔ VALIDOS™ TREGA™: Has the Event been sufficiently governed to support downstream taxation analysis? VALIDOS™: Does the total validation basis sufficiently support a Validation Determination and intended reliance? Event Determination ≠ Validation Determination. TREGA™ ↔ INTEGROS® TREGA™: governs Event-specific context, recognition, formation, boundary, timing, location, participation, value association, relationships, determination, record, and lifecycle. INTEGROS®: governs integrity across objects, states, evidence, and processes. Tax-Relevant Event Governance ≠ General Integrity Governance. TREGA™ ↔ ADIT® TREGA™: governs the Event and its canonical governance lifecycle. ADIT®: governs evidential observation, preservation, verification, examination, and auditability of what occurred. Event Governance ≠ Audit of Event Governance. TREGA™ ↔ AGA™ TREGA™: governs the methodological Event lifecycle. AGA™: governs who holds authority, responsibility, accountability, and attribution for Event-related decisions, actions, and failures. Event Methodology ≠ Accountability Allocation. TREGA™ ↔ HALIA™ TREGA™: governs the Tax-Relevant Event lifecycle. HALIA™: governs the lifecycle of harm and liability arising from relevant occurrences. Tax-Relevant Event Governance ≠ Harm or Liability Determination. TREGA™ ↔ Jurisdictional Tax Systems TREGA™: determines whether an occurrence has become a sufficiently governed Tax-Relevant Event suitable for downstream analysis. Jurisdictional Tax System: determines what that Event legally means under applicable tax law. Tax-Relevant Event ≠ Legally Taxable Event. Jurisdiction-Ready ≠ Jurisdiction-Determined. Architectural Origin TREGA™ evolved from the foundational methodological problem that taxation systems require a reliable Event layer between operational reality and legal tax determination. Traditional taxation infrastructure often moves directly from: Transaction Data ↓ Tax Rules without explicitly governing what the underlying Event actually is.
