As digital platforms, distributed systems, autonomous agents, machine-to-machine activity, cross-border services, and future machine economies expand, the Event itself becomes increasingly difficult to identify, bound, locate, associate with participants and Value, relate to other Events, and preserve through time. TREGA™ therefore establishes a dedicated governance architecture between: Operational Reality and: Jurisdiction-Specific Tax Determination Its foundational principles are distributed primarily across: Event Context ↓ Event Recognition ↓ Event Formation ↓ Event Boundary ↓ Event Timing ↓ Event Location ↓ Event Participation ↓ Value Association ↓ Event Relationships ↓ Event Determination ↓ Event Record Governance ↓ Event Lifecycle & Continuity The architecture establishes the governed Tax-Relevant Event as an independent methodological object before downstream tax law determines legal consequence. Architectural Structure Architecture: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance Core Parent Standards: 12 Core Modules: 60 Architecture Model: Lifecycle-Based · Modular · Jurisdiction-Neutral Primary Governance Domain: Tax-Relevant Event Governance The architecture deliberately separates governable spaces that can independently fail. A taxation-relevant occurrence may: - be placed in the wrong Context; - fail to be recognized; - be incorrectly formed; - contain an incorrect Event Boundary; - have inaccurate Timing; - have incomplete or misleading Location information; - associate the wrong participants; - associate the wrong Value result; - be incorrectly related to other Events; - be prematurely determined as tax-relevant; - become an incomplete or semantically unstable Event Record; - lose lifecycle continuity through uncontrolled Amendment, Correction, Supersession, or Closure. TREGA™ treats these not as one generic tax data problem, but as distinct Event Governance spaces requiring distinct methodological controls. Recursive Lifecycle Principle TREGA™ does not end when a Tax-Relevant Event Record is first created. A governed Event may continue to change after its initial Determination and Record Governance. During that period: New information may emerge. Event attributes may require Amendment. Previously governed information may require Correction. A successor state may Supersede a prior state. Continuity may become uncertain. An Event may close. A Closed Event may require reopening. Material transformation may require New Event Formation. TREGA™ therefore closes recursively through TRECLS: Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record ↓ Event Continuity ↓ Event Amendment ↓ Event Correction ↓ Event Supersession ↓ Event Closure ↓ Jurisdiction-Ready Tax-Relevant Event Where materially relevant new information emerges: Closed Event ↓ Reopening Review ↓ Lifecycle Re-Entry ↓ Updated Governed Event ↓ Reclosure Where continuity can no longer legitimately be preserved: Material Transformation ↓ Continuity Break ↓ New Event Formation Referral This makes Event change part of Tax-Relevant Event Governance rather than an uncontrolled downstream data-maintenance problem. Foundational Architecture Principles TREGA™ governs the event. The jurisdiction governs the tax. Tax-Relevant Event ≠ Legally Taxable Event. Tax relevance means eligibility for taxation analysis, not legal taxability. Operational Reality must not become tax interpretation before the Event itself has been governed. Recognition ≠ Taxability Determination. Formation ≠ Boundary. Event Root ≠ Identity Origin. Operational Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point. Event Timing ≠ Tax Period Determination. Event Location ≠ Tax Jurisdiction. Participant ≠ Taxpayer. Identified Actor ≠ Governed Event Participant. Value Association ≠ Value Governance. Event Determination ≠ Tax Liability Determination. Governed Event Record ≠ Tax Assessment. Correction ≠ Historical Erasure. Amendment ≠ New Event by default. Material Transformation May Require New Event Formation. Event Continuity ≠ Tax Obligation Lifecycle. Jurisdiction-Ready ≠ Jurisdiction-Determined. One governed Event can support multiple legitimate jurisdictional evaluations without becoming multiple different Event realities. Canonical Principle TREGA™ does not govern legal Taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer determination, tax nexus, legal tax point, Tax Period, Tax Base, Tax Rate, exemptions, deductions, Tax Liability, filing obligations, payment, collection, enforcement, or other jurisdiction-specific legal tax consequences. TREGA™ governs the methodological conditions under which real-world and digital occurrences become contextualized, recognized, formed, bounded, temporally and spatially situated, associated with participants and Value, related to other Events, formally determined as tax-relevant, represented as governed Event Records, and maintained through Amendment, Correction, Supersession, Closure, and continuity governance until they become Jurisdiction-Ready for downstream tax-rule application. TREGA™ governs the event. The jurisdiction governs the tax.

title: OOF™ The Value Change Association Module (VACM) governs how governed changes
text: OOF™ The Value Change Association Module (VACM) governs how governed changes The Value Change Association Module (VACM) governs how governed changes OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ Parent Standard: TRVAS — Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard Module: VACM — Value Change Association Module Operational Layer: Value Change Association Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value Change Association Origin ID: TREGA-TRVAS-VACM-003 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 1 September 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Value Change Association Module (VACM) governs how governed changes affecting value are materially associated with a specific Tax-Relevant Event through the Governed Value References established by VARM. VACM determines whether a governed Value Change legitimately belongs to the event, how that relationship is qualified, and how multiple, partial, direct, indirect, sequential, or conflicting Value Change Associations are represented. VACM does not determine whether value actually changed, how the change occurred within the Value Lifecycle, or what economic, accounting, legal, or tax consequence follows from that change. VFM® remains authoritative for the underlying Value Change. Its principal task is: Governed Value Reference + Governed Value Change ↓ Governed Event–Value Change Association The foundational distinction is: Value Change Association ≠ Value Change Governance. Operational Role Events frequently coincide with changes in value. Value may be: created; increased; decreased; transferred; transformed; consumed; developed; degraded; impaired; nullified; restored; or otherwise materially changed. But temporal proximity between an event and a Value Change does not establish that the event and change belong together. VACM provides the governance mechanism for determining whether an already-governed Value Change is materially associated with the event. It therefore protects TREGA™ from making a common methodological error: observing a Value Change and automatically attributing that change to the event. Internal Module Flow TRVAS operates through: VAIM — Value Association Identification ↓ VARM — Value Reference ↓ VACM — Value Change Association ↓ VASM — Value State Association ↓ VATM — Value Association Traceability ↓ Governed Value-Associated Event VACM receives the Governed Value Reference Set from VARM together with relevant governed Value Change information. Its output proceeds to VASM. Operational Transition The canonical VACM transition is: Governed Value Reference Set + Governed Value Change Information ↓ Value Change Association Governance ↓ Governed Value Change Association Set VACM associates change with the event. It does not create the Value Change. Operational Space VACM governs: Event–Value Change Association; Value Change relevance; change-association basis; direct and indirect association; partial association; multiple Value Changes; sequential Value Changes; concurrent Value Changes; positive and negative changes; transfer-related changes; transformation-related changes; consumption-related changes; machine-generated changes; association materiality; association qualification; association uncertainty; association conflict; association correction; and Value Change Association readiness for downstream TRVAS governance. Operational Scope VACM may operate across Value Changes associated with: commercial events; payments; banking; digital assets; goods; services; rights; resources; energy; computational capacity; industrial production; marketplaces; blockchain systems; AI-agent activity; autonomous systems; machine-to-machine activity; infrastructure operations; and other governed economic or operational environments. The form of value does not determine the validity of the association. Governed Value Change A Governed Value Change is an upstream governance result describing a material change affecting a governed value. VACM may consume such a result. It does not recreate it. The architecture boundary is explicit: VFM® governs what changed in the value. VACM governs whether that governed change belongs to the event. Event–Value Change Association An Event–Value Change Association represents a sufficiently governed relationship between: a Governed Tax-Relevant Event; a Governed Value Reference; and a Governed Value Change. The existence of all three does not automatically establish the relationship. Event + Value + Change ≠ Established Value Change Association by default. The association itself requires governance. Association Basis VACM shall preserve the basis supporting the relationship between the event and the Value Change. The basis may derive from operational, transactional, temporal, participant-related, system-generated, contractual, technical, or other legitimate governed information. The existence of one indicator does not automatically establish the association. Association Evidence ≠ Association Determination by default. Direct Value Change Association A Value Change may occur directly through the governed event. For example, an event may directly transfer, consume, transform, increase, or decrease a governed value. Where sufficient support exists, VACM may establish a Direct Value Change Association. However: Direct Value Change Association ≠ Taxable Event Determination. Indirect Value Change Association A Value Change may be materially related through intermediate operations. For example: Governed Event ↓ Platform Operation ↓ Settlement Process ↓ Governed Value Change The presence of an intermediary does not automatically invalidate the relationship. Indirect Association ≠ Irrelevant Change by default. VACM shall preserve the actual association structure where sufficiently supported. Partial Value Change Association Only part of a governed Value Change may belong to the event. For example, one settlement may cover several events, or one resource-consumption record may aggregate several operations. VACM shall support partial association without forcing the entire change onto one event. Partial Association ≠ Complete Value Change Association. Multiple Value Changes One event may legitimately be associated with multiple Value Changes. For example: Event ↓ Payment Change + Asset Change + Service Value Change + Resource Consumption Change Therefore: One Event ≠ One Value Change by default. VACM shall preserve materially distinct changes. One Value Change Across Multiple Events A single governed Value Change may also relate to several events. For example, one settlement may resolve several transactions. VACM shall permit qualified multi-event association where operational reality supports it. One Value Change ≠ One Event by default. TRERLS remains authoritative for relationships among the events themselves. Sequential Value Changes An event may be associated with Value Changes occurring in a governed sequence. For example: Authorization ↓ Reservation ↓ Transfer ↓ Settlement ↓ Refund VACM may preserve the association sequence where materially relevant. However: Sequential Value Changes ≠ Separate Events by default. Whether separate events exist belongs to Event Formation, Boundary, and Relationship governance. Concurrent Value Changes Several Value Changes may occur simultaneously or within the same operational stage. VACM shall support concurrent associations without forcing an artificial sequence. Concurrent Value Changes ≠ Same Value Change. Value Increase Association An event may be associated with an increase in governed value. VACM may establish the association where the increase is already governed upstream. It does not determine the amount, cause, legal recognition, or tax consequence of the increase. Value Increase Association ≠ Taxable Gain. Value Decrease Association An event may be associated with a reduction in governed value. VACM may preserve this relationship without determining whether the decrease constitutes an expense, loss, deduction, impairment, or other legal or accounting category. Value Decrease Association ≠ Tax Deduction. Value Transfer Association A governed event may be associated with movement or transfer of value. VACM may establish the relationship between the event and the governed transfer result. However: Value Transfer Association ≠ Ownership Transfer Determination. Ownership remains outside VACM. Value Transformation Association Value may change form while remaining part of a governed lifecycle. An event may be associated with such transformation. VACM may represent the association without determining whether the transformed value constitutes a new asset, legal object, accounting item, or taxable category. Value Transformation Association ≠ Legal Reclassification. Value Consumption Association Events may consume value such as: energy; materials; computational capacity; machine time; service capacity; infrastructure resources; or other productive inputs. VACM may associate a governed consumption change with the event. Value Consumption ≠ Deductible Cost by default. Value Creation and Development Association An event may contribute to emergence or development of value. Where VFM® has governed the relevant result, VACM may associate that change with the event. VACM does not determine Value Origin or Value Development itself. Value Development Association ≠ Value Ownership. Value Degradation and Nullification Association An event may contribute to degradation, impairment, destruction, or nullification of value. VACM may associate the governed result with the event without determining responsibility or liability. Value Degradation Association ≠ Liability Determination. HALIA™ remains authoritative for harm and liability where applicable. Value Restoration Association An event may restore previously degraded or nullified value. VACM may preserve this relationship where the restoration result is governed upstream. Value Restoration Association ≠ Legal Compensation Determination. Reversal A Value Change may later be reversed. A payment may be reversed. A digital-asset transfer may be returned. A resource allocation may be cancelled. VACM shall preserve the relationship between the original and reversal-associated changes without assuming that the original event never occurred. Value Change Reversal ≠ Historical Erasure. Refund A refund may be associated with an earlier governed event or may itself participate in a separate event structure. VACM shall not automatically collapse the refund into the original Value Change. Refund ≠ Original Value Change Erasure. Whether the refund constitutes part of the same event or another related event belongs to the appropriate TREGA™ governance layers. Correction A Value Change Association may later be shown to be incorrect. VACM shall support governed correction while preserving reconstructability. Association Correction ≠ Historical Erasure. Value Change Timing A Value Change may occur, be recorded, recognized, settled, or observed at times different from the governed Event Timing. VACM shall not redefine Event Timing from a Value Change timestamp. Value Change Timestamp ≠ Event Time by default. TRETS remains authoritative for Event Timing. Value Change Location A Value Change may be recorded or technically executed in a location different from the governed Event Location. For example, a digital transfer may be processed through infrastructure in several countries. Therefore: Value Change Location ≠ Event Location by default. TRELS remains authoritative for Event Location. Value Change and Participation A participant may be associated with a Value Change. That relationship does not automatically establish ownership, entitlement, responsibility, or taxpayer status. Participant Associated with Value Change ≠ Value Owner. Participant Associated with Value Change ≠ Taxpayer. TREPS remains authoritative for Event Participation. Value Change and Ownership VACM does not determine whether ownership changes because value changes or transfers. Value Change ≠ Ownership Change by default. OBIDENITY® remains authoritative for ownership governance where applicable. Value Change and Accountability The association of a Value Change with an event does not establish which participant caused or is accountable for that change. Value Change Association ≠ Accountability Determination. AGA™ remains authoritative for accountability governance. Value Change and Liability A negative Value Change may represent loss, degradation, destruction, or impairment. VACM does not determine who is liable. Negative Value Change ≠ Liability by default. HALIA™ remains authoritative where applicable. Value Change and Taxation A governed Value Change may later be important to taxation. However, VACM does not determine whether the change constitutes: taxable income; taxable gain; deductible loss; taxable consideration; taxable benefit; realization; disposal; acquisition; taxable transfer; customs value; or another jurisdiction-specific tax concept. Therefore: Governed Value Change Association ≠ Taxable Value Change. A jurisdiction may later apply its own legal rules to the governed event-value structure. Multi-Jurisdiction Governance The same governed Value Change Association may support different interpretations across jurisdictions. The model is: One Governed Value Change Association ↓ Multiple Jurisdictional Evaluations Jurisdiction A may treat the change as taxable. Jurisdiction B may classify it differently. Jurisdiction C may not recognize a taxable consequence. TREGA™ preserves one governed operational reality while allowing legal interpretation to remain jurisdiction-specific. Machine and Autonomous Value Changes AI agents, robots, software systems, and autonomous machines may initiate or produce Value Changes without contemporaneous human execution. Examples include: autonomous asset transfer; resource consumption; energy allocation; computational exchange; machine-generated production; autonomous procurement; service execution; or digital settlement. VACM shall support association of such governed changes with the event. Machine-Generated Value Change ≠ Human Value Change by default. Likewise: Autonomous Value Change ≠ Autonomous Tax Liability. Association Materiality VACM shall determine whether the relationship between the governed Value Change and event is sufficiently material to require association. Materiality concerns the event-change relationship. It does not determine legal, accounting, audit, or tax materiality. Association Materiality ≠ Tax Materiality. Association Confidence A Value Change Association may possess different levels of support. VACM may represent the association as: Established · Qualified · Partial · Ambiguous · Conflicted · Unresolved A downstream need for a deterministic value shall not override governance uncertainty. Association Uncertainty It may be unclear whether the event caused, contributed to, coincided with, or merely preceded a Value Change. VACM shall preserve that uncertainty. Temporal Proximity ≠ Value Change Association. and: Association Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Assume Causation. VACM governs association, not universal causality. Association Conflict Different sources may disagree about whether a Value Change belongs to the event. VACM shall preserve materially relevant conflict until sufficiently resolved. Association Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Attribution. Governance States VACM may represent states including: Change Association Ready Change Association Under Governance Direct Change Association Indirect Change Association Partial Change Association Multi-Change Association Sequential Change Association Concurrent Change Association Change Association Qualified Change Association Ambiguous Change Association Conflicted Change Association Unresolved Governed Value Change Association Established These states describe Event–Value Change Association only. Governance Requirements VACM implementations shall ensure that: Value Changes are associated only through governed Value References; upstream governed Value Changes are consumed without being redefined; direct and indirect associations can be distinguished; partial association can be represented; multiple Value Changes can belong to one event; one Value Change can relate to multiple events where legitimate; sequential and concurrent changes can be represented; increases and decreases remain distinct from tax conclusions; transfers remain distinct from ownership determination; transformations remain distinct from legal reclassification; consumption remains distinct from deductibility; degradation remains distinct from liability; restoration remains distinct from compensation; reversals do not erase historical changes; refunds do not automatically erase original Value Changes; corrections remain traceable; Value Change timestamps do not redefine Event Timing; Value Change location does not redefine Event Location; participant association does not establish ownership or taxpayer status; accountability and liability remain separate; uncertainty remains visible; conflict remains visible; VFM® ownership of Value Change governance remains preserved; and tax determination remains downstream. Governance Logic IF VARM establishes a Governed Value Reference and a relevant governed Value Change exists, THEN VACM shall evaluate whether the change materially belongs to the governed event. IF the association is sufficiently supported, THEN a Governed Value Change Association may be established. IF only part of a Value Change belongs to the event, THEN partial association shall be preserved rather than assigning the complete change. IF multiple Value Changes belong to the event, THEN materially distinct associations shall remain separately governable. IF one Value Change relates to several events, THEN exclusivity shall not be assumed. IF a reversal, refund, or correction occurs, THEN historical Value Change Association shall remain reconstructable. IF the association remains uncertain or conflicted, THEN the corresponding governance state shall remain visible. IF information indicates a possible Event Formation, Event Boundary, Event Timing, or Event Relationship issue, THEN VACM shall refer the issue to the appropriate TREGA™ layer rather than redefining those spaces. IF Value Change Association is sufficiently governed, THEN the result shall proceed to VASM for Value State Association governance. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum VACM implementation should support: Governed Event Reference The governed event to which the Value Change may be associated. Governed Value Reference The VARM-governed value reference. Governed Value Change Reference The upstream governed Value Change being associated. Change Association Identifier The stable identifier for the Event–Value Change Association. Change Type Reference The relevant upstream governed change classification where available. Association Basis The basis supporting the relationship between event and change. Association Directness Direct, indirect, or otherwise qualified. Association Extent Complete, partial, or otherwise qualified. Sequence State Whether the change forms part of a materially relevant sequence. Concurrency State Whether the change occurs concurrently with another associated change. Reversal Reference Any materially relevant reversal relationship. Refund Reference Any materially relevant refund relationship. Correction Reference Any governed correction affecting the association. Association Confidence The qualified confidence attached to the association. Ambiguity State Whether the association remains ambiguous. Conflict State Whether materially conflicting associations exist. Traceability Reference The information required to reconstruct the association. Governance State The current VACM state. Handoff State Whether the result is ready for VASM. Governance Outputs VACM may produce: Governed Direct Value Change Association; Governed Indirect Value Change Association; Governed Partial Value Change Association; Governed Multi-Change Association Structure; Governed Sequential Value Change Association; Governed Concurrent Value Change Association; Value Transfer Association; Value Transformation Association; Value Consumption Association; Value Development Association; Value Degradation Association; Value Restoration Association; Value Change Reversal Relationship; Value Change Association Correction; Value Change Association Confidence State; Value Change Association Ambiguity State; Value Change Association Conflict State; and the principal output: Governed Value Change Association Set. Critical Distinctions Value Change Association ≠ Value Change Governance. VFM® governs what changed in value. VACM governs whether that governed change belongs to the event. Event + Value + Change ≠ Established Value Change Association by default. Association Evidence ≠ Association Determination by default. Direct Value Change Association ≠ Taxable Event Determination. Indirect Association ≠ Irrelevant Change by default. Partial Association ≠ Complete Value Change Association. One Event ≠ One Value Change by default. One Value Change ≠ One Event by default. Sequential Value Changes ≠ Separate Events by default. Concurrent Value Changes ≠ Same Value Change. Value Increase Association ≠ Taxable Gain. Value Decrease Association ≠ Tax Deduction. Value Transfer Association ≠ Ownership Transfer Determination. Value Transformation Association ≠ Legal Reclassification. Value Consumption ≠ Deductible Cost by default. Value Development Association ≠ Value Ownership. Value Degradation Association ≠ Liability Determination. Value Restoration Association ≠ Legal Compensation Determination. Value Change Reversal ≠ Historical Erasure. Value Change Timestamp ≠ Event Time by default. Value Change Location ≠ Event Location by default. Value Change ≠ Ownership Change by default. Value Change Association ≠ Accountability Determination. Governed Value Change Association ≠ Taxable Value Change. Temporal Proximity ≠ Value Change Association. Enterprise Application VACM enables businesses, banks, digital platforms, blockchain infrastructures, ERP systems, AI agents, and machine systems to connect governed Value Changes to the correct event without turning operational change into premature legal or tax conclusions. The operational path is: VARM — Governed Value Reference Set ↓ Governed Value Change Information ↓ VACM — Governed Value Change Association Set ↓ VASM — Value State Association ↓ VATM — Value Association Traceability ↓ Governed Value-Associated Event This enables downstream systems to understand not merely that value changed, but which governed event the change materially belongs to. Use Case 1 — Cross-Border Commerce with Settlement, Refund, and Multiple Value Changes A multinational marketplace processes a commercial event involving goods, platform services, payment processing, logistics, and currency conversion. The customer payment creates several operational records. The merchant later receives settlement after platform fees are deducted. A partial refund subsequently occurs. VFM® governs the relevant Value Changes. VACM determines which of those governed changes materially belong to the event, distinguishes direct, partial, sequential, and refund-related associations, and preserves the original change history. It does not determine whether the settlement constitutes taxable income, whether the refund creates a deduction, or which jurisdiction may tax any resulting amount. The result is a governed Event–Value Change structure suitable for subsequent tax analysis without rewriting operational value reality. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Infrastructure and Digital-Asset Settlement An autonomous industrial system obtains computational capacity and energy from distributed providers. AI agents coordinate allocation, machine systems consume resources, and settlement occurs through digital assets. Several governed Value Changes occur: resource consumption, service-value change, energy consumption, digital-asset transfer, and potentially later settlement adjustments. VACM associates the relevant governed Value Changes with the event while keeping the underlying Value Lifecycle under VFM®. It does not treat the blockchain transfer as the complete economic change, attribute ownership from wallet movement, or determine whether any change is taxable. The resulting association structure allows different jurisdictions to evaluate the same governed operational reality according to their own tax rules. Canonical Boundary VACM owns the association of already-governed Value Changes with a specific Tax-Relevant Event, including directness, indirectness, partial association, multiple changes, sequence, concurrency, reversals, refunds, correction, qualification, uncertainty, conflict, and association-specific traceability. VACM does not own Value Change creation or determination, the Value Lifecycle, Value Reference establishment, Value State governance, Value State Association, complete Value Association traceability, Event Formation, Event Boundary, Event Timing, Event Location, Event Participation, Event Relationships, ownership, entitlement, accountability, liability, taxable value, Tax Base, Tax Liability, or another jurisdiction-specific tax conclusion. Its governance ends when relevant governed Value Changes are sufficiently associated with the event for Value State Association governance. Canonical Handoff VARM — Governed Value Reference Set ↓ VACM — Governed Value Change Association Set ↓ VASM — Value State Association Governance Canonical Closing Statement VACM connects governed Value Change to governed Event Reality without taking ownership of the Value Change itself. A change in value may be real without belonging to the event, and a change belonging to the event may have different legal consequences across jurisdictions. Value Change Association ≠ Value Change Governance. Governed Value Change Association ≠ Taxable Value Change.

title: OOF™ The Value Association Identification Module (VAIM) governs how
text: OOF™ The Value Association Identification Module (VAIM) governs how The Value Association Identification Module (VAIM) governs how OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ Parent Standard: TRVAS — Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard Module: VAIM — Value Association Identification Module Operational Layer: Value Association Identification Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value Association Identification Origin ID: TREGA-TRVAS-VAIM-001 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 1 September 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Value Association Identification Module (VAIM) governs how value-related information potentially relevant to a Governed Participatory Event is discovered, distinguished, screened, qualified, and admitted into Tax-Relevant Value Association governance. VAIM establishes which available governed value results possess a sufficiently plausible and materially relevant relationship to the event to become Value Association Candidates. Its principal task is: Available Governed Value Information ↓ Governed Value Association Candidate Set VAIM does not establish the complete Value Association. It identifies the value results that are eligible to proceed through TRVAS governance. The foundational distinction is: Value Presence ≠ Event Value Association Operational Role Modern events may be surrounded by large quantities of value-related information. A single event may generate or interact with: prices; payments; invoices; accounting entries; asset transfers; balances; commissions; discounts; refunds; service values; resource consumption; digital assets; energy use; computational resources; rights; benefits; losses; and non-monetary value. Not all such information necessarily belongs to the event. VAIM prevents surrounding value data from being automatically absorbed into the governed event merely because it appears in the same system, transaction chain, account, ledger, platform, wallet, process, or operational environment. Internal Module Flow TRVAS operates through: VAIM — Value Association Identification → VARM — Value Reference → VACM — Value Change Association → VASM — Value State Association → VATM — Value Association Traceability → Governed Value-Associated Event VAIM is the entry point into this flow. Its output becomes the governed input to VARM. Operational Transition The canonical VAIM transition is: Governed Participatory Event + Available Governed Value Information → Value Association Identification Governance → Governed Value Association Candidate Set A Value Association Candidate is a governed value result or value-related reference whose potential relationship to the event is sufficiently supported to require further TRVAS governance. Value Association Candidate ≠ Established Value Association Operational Space VAIM governs: value-information discovery; potential value-association identification; candidate differentiation; value-source screening; event-relevance screening; material relevance; candidate inclusion; candidate exclusion; duplicate candidate detection; multi-value candidate identification; monetary and non-monetary candidate recognition; direct and indirect candidate recognition; candidate uncertainty; candidate conflict; and candidate readiness for subsequent Value Reference governance. VAIM does not determine the legal tax treatment of any candidate. Operational Scope VAIM may process value-related information originating from: ERP systems; accounting systems; banking infrastructure; payment systems; invoices; procurement systems; commerce platforms; marketplaces; blockchain networks; digital-asset systems; smart contracts; industrial systems; logistics systems; energy systems; AI agents; autonomous systems; machine networks; digital services; operational databases; or governed outputs from VFM®. The source of value information does not by itself establish event relevance. Value Association Candidate A Value Association Candidate is a sufficiently distinguishable value result or value-related reference that may materially belong to the governed event and therefore requires further Value Association governance. Candidate status means: Potentially relevant to the event. It does not mean: Established as belonging to the event. Therefore: Candidate Value ≠ Governed Event Value Candidate Identification VAIM shall identify value information only where a plausible relationship to the governed event exists. Possible indicators may include: event-generated value information; participant-linked value information; event-linked payment; asset movement; resource consumption; service delivery; value-state information; governed Value Change; contractual or operational value reference; machine-generated value activity; or another sufficiently supported event-value connection. These indicators initiate governance. They do not prove the final association. Event Relevance Value information may be economically real while still being irrelevant to the specific event. VAIM therefore distinguishes: Value existence from: Event relevance and: Established Event Value Association. The sequence is: Value Information ↓ Potential Event Relevance ↓ Value Association Candidate ↓ Subsequent TRVAS Governance Therefore: Economic Relevance ≠ Event Relevance by Default Material Relevance VAIM shall determine whether the potential relationship is sufficiently material to require governance. Material relevance concerns the relationship between the value information and the event. It does not determine whether the amount is materially significant under accounting, tax, audit, or securities law. Therefore: Value Association Materiality ≠ Legal Materiality. A small monetary amount may be operationally essential to an event. A large amount appearing nearby may be unrelated. Monetary Value Candidates VAIM may identify monetary value information including: payments; prices; fees; commissions; settlements; refunds; deposits; credits; debits; currency amounts; or other monetary records. However: Monetary Record ≠ Event Value Association by Default A payment record may relate to another event, several events, an earlier obligation, a later settlement, or a bundled economic structure. Non-Monetary Value Candidates VAIM shall support non-monetary value information. Candidates may include: goods; services; rights; access; resources; energy; computational capacity; productive capacity; digital assets; operational benefits; value loss; or other governed value results. Therefore: No Monetary Amount ≠ No Value Association Candidate This is essential for digital and machine economies. Governed Value Results Where VFM® or another legitimate governance source has already established a governed value result, VAIM may consume that result as an input. VAIM shall not independently recreate its Value Lifecycle governance. The boundary is: VFM® establishes what happened to value. VAIM establishes whether that governed value result should enter Event Value Association governance. Recorded Amount A numeric amount may be present in an operational system. Its presence alone does not establish that it belongs to the event. Therefore: Recorded Amount ≠ Value Association Candidate by Default. VAIM requires an event-relevance basis. Invoice Information An invoice may contain strong evidence of an economic relationship. But invoice information may contain: several items; several events; taxes; fees; discounts; bundled services; adjustments; historical charges; or later corrections. Therefore: Invoice Presence ≠ Complete Event Value. and: Invoice Amount ≠ Taxable Value. VAIM may identify individual value candidates without treating the invoice total as a single authoritative event value. Payment Information Payment information may support Value Association Identification. However, payment timing and economic-event timing may differ. One payment may settle several events. Several payments may settle one event. A payment may be reversed. A deposit may precede the event. Therefore: Payment ≠ Event Value by Default VAIM identifies the potential relationship. It does not resolve the complete Value Association. Digital-Asset Information Blockchain and distributed-ledger systems may expose highly visible asset movements. Visibility does not establish event meaning. A digital-asset transfer may represent: payment; internal transfer; collateral; settlement; exchange; liquidity movement; staking; protocol interaction; asset migration; or another activity. Therefore: On-Chain Transfer ≠ Tax-Relevant Event Value by Default VAIM may identify the transfer as a candidate while preserving the need for subsequent governance. Resource Consumption An event may consume economically relevant resources without generating a conventional transaction record. Examples include: energy; computing capacity; storage; bandwidth; machine time; production capacity; materials; or infrastructure resources. VAIM may identify such governed value information as candidates where materially related to the event. Resource Consumption ≠ Taxable Value by Default. Value Creation An event may create or develop value without an immediate payment or transfer. VAIM may identify governed value-creation results where they materially relate to the event. Therefore: No Transfer ≠ No Value Candidate. The existence and lifecycle of the value remain governed by VFM®. Value Loss and Degradation An event may be associated with value loss, degradation, impairment, destruction, or nullification. Such outcomes may be relevant even where the event contains no positive value transfer. Therefore: Value Loss ≠ Absence of Value Association. VAIM may admit the relevant governed value result as a candidate without determining liability or tax treatment. Direct Candidate Relationship A value result may possess an apparent direct relationship to the event. Examples include: payment specifically generated for the event; goods transferred during the event; service delivered through the event; or resource directly consumed by the event. Directness strengthens potential relevance. It does not establish final association. Therefore: Direct Value Connection ≠ Established Value Association. Indirect Candidate Relationship Some value results may relate through intermediate operations or systems. For example: Event ↓ Platform ↓ Settlement System ↓ Value Transfer The value may remain materially relevant despite the indirect path. Therefore: Indirect Value Connection ≠ Irrelevant Value by Default. VAIM may admit such information for subsequent governance. Participant-Linked Value Value information may be linked to an Event Participant. That linkage may support candidate identification. It does not establish ownership or final event association. Therefore: Participant-Linked Value ≠ Participant-Owned Value. and: Participant-Linked Value ≠ Event Value by Default. TREPS remains authoritative for Event Participation. Multiple Value Candidates One event may produce many legitimate candidates. VAIM shall not force them into a single value representation. The candidate structure may therefore be: Governed Event ↓ Candidate A + Candidate B + Candidate C + Candidate N Therefore: One Event ≠ One Value Candidate Subsequent TRVAS modules determine how those candidates are governed. One Candidate Across Multiple Events The same governed value reference may potentially relate to several events. VAIM shall not automatically assign exclusivity. Therefore: One Value Candidate ≠ One Event by Default. Event Relationship governance may later become relevant under TRERLS. Duplicate Candidate Detection Different systems may expose multiple references to the same underlying value result. For example: Invoice Record + Payment Record + ERP Record + Bank Record may represent overlapping information rather than four independent values. VAIM shall support detection of potential duplication. However: Multiple Value Records ≠ Multiple Values by Default VAIM shall not merge candidates where equivalence remains uncertain. Candidate Differentiation Conversely, similar amounts or descriptions do not prove that two records represent the same value. Therefore: Same Amount ≠ Same Value Same Currency ≠ Same Value Same Participant ≠ Same Value Similar Description ≠ Value Equivalence Candidate differentiation must remain evidence-based. Source Reliability A value candidate may originate from one or more sources. Source reliability may influence candidate qualification. However: Trusted Source ≠ Event Relevance by Default. A highly reliable bank record may still describe value unrelated to the event under governance. VAIM separates source quality from event relationship. Source Conflict Different sources may identify incompatible value information. VAIM shall preserve materially relevant conflicts. For example: ERP: CHF 10,000 Invoice: CHF 9,500 Settlement: CHF 9,200 VAIM does not select a taxable amount. It identifies and preserves the candidate structure and conflict for subsequent governance. Therefore: Value Data Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Value Selection Candidate Uncertainty A value relationship may remain uncertain. VAIM shall not convert uncertainty into artificial certainty merely because a downstream system requires a value field. Therefore: Required Value Field ≠ Permission to Invent Event Value Candidate uncertainty must remain visible. Candidate Exclusion Value information may be excluded from further TRVAS governance where sufficient evidence establishes that it does not materially relate to the governed event. Exclusion should itself remain traceable where materially relevant. Therefore: Candidate Exclusion ≠ Value Nonexistence. The value may exist but belong elsewhere. Candidate Reconsideration New information may justify reconsideration of previously included or excluded value information. VAIM shall permit governed reconsideration without silently rewriting historical decisions. Candidate Reconsideration ≠ Historical Erasure. Value Identification and Event Boundary VAIM operates inside the governed Event Boundary. Value information shall not automatically enlarge that boundary. Therefore: Value Candidate Discovery ≠ Event Boundary Expansion If candidate information indicates a possible Event Boundary problem, VAIM shall refer the issue to TREBS rather than redefine the event itself. Value Identification and Event Participation A value candidate may reveal information about an actor. VAIM shall not independently establish Event Participation from that information. Therefore: Value Candidate ≠ Participant Determination. TREPS remains authoritative for participation. Value Identification and Ownership VAIM does not determine who owns the candidate value. Therefore: Value Candidate ≠ Ownership Determination OBIDENITY® remains authoritative for governed ownership where applicable. Value Identification and Value Lifecycle VAIM does not determine: Value Origin; Value Emergence; Value State; Value Change; Value Development; Value Degradation; Value Nullification; Value Restoration; or Value Extinction. Those belong to VFM®. VAIM only determines whether available governed value information should enter TRVAS Value Association governance. Value Identification and Taxation Candidate identification occurs before jurisdiction-specific tax evaluation. VAIM does not determine: taxable value; Tax Base; taxable income; taxable gain; consideration under tax law; customs value; transfer-pricing value; deductible amount; exemption; or Tax Liability. Therefore: Value Association Candidate ≠ Taxable Value Machine and Autonomous Events Machine and autonomous systems may generate value information without traditional commercial records. Examples may include: autonomous resource allocation; machine-to-machine service exchange; computational consumption; energy exchange; autonomous procurement; digital-resource transfer; or machine-generated production. VAIM shall permit these value signals to enter candidate governance where materially relevant. Therefore: No Invoice ≠ No Value Candidate and: No Human Transaction ≠ No Value Candidate Candidate Governance States VAIM may represent states including: Value Information Detected Candidate Screening Candidate Qualified Candidate Included Candidate Excluded Candidate Duplicated Candidate Ambiguous Candidate Conflicted Candidate Unresolved Value Association Candidate Established These states govern admission into Value Association governance. They do not establish final Value Association. Governance Requirements VAIM implementations shall ensure that: available value information can be discovered; event relevance is evaluated before candidate admission; monetary and non-monetary value can be recognized; governed VFM® outputs can be consumed without being redefined; payments are not automatically treated as complete Event Value; invoice amounts are not automatically treated as taxable value; digital-asset transfers are not automatically treated as Event Value; resource consumption can be identified where materially relevant; value creation and value loss can enter candidate governance; direct and indirect relationships can be recognized; multiple candidates can exist for one event; one candidate can potentially relate to multiple events; duplicate records are not automatically treated as distinct values; similar records are not automatically merged; participant-linked value is not automatically treated as participant-owned value; source reliability remains distinct from Event Relevance; uncertainty remains visible; conflicts remain visible; exclusions remain traceable where required; candidate reconsideration does not erase governance history; Event Boundary remains protected; Event Participation remains governed by TREPS; ownership remains separate; the Value Lifecycle remains governed by VFM®; and tax valuation remains downstream. Governance Logic IF a Governed Participatory Event exists, THEN available governed value information may enter VAIM screening. IF value information has a plausible relationship to the event, THEN Event Relevance shall be evaluated. IF the relationship is sufficiently material to require further governance, THEN a Value Association Candidate may be established. IF multiple materially distinct candidates exist, THEN they shall remain distinguishable. IF multiple records may describe the same underlying value, THEN potential duplication shall be preserved until sufficiently resolved. IF a candidate relationship remains uncertain or conflicted, THEN the corresponding governance state shall remain visible. IF value information is sufficiently shown to be unrelated to the event, THEN it may be excluded without denying the existence of the value itself. IF candidate information indicates an Event Boundary problem, THEN VAIM shall refer the issue upstream rather than redefine the event. IF candidate status is sufficiently governed, THEN the candidate shall proceed to VARM for Value Reference governance. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum VAIM implementation should support: Governed Event Reference The Governed Participatory Event under Value Association governance. Candidate Identifier A stable identifier for the Value Association Candidate. Value Information Type The type of value-related information being evaluated. Value Source Reference The source from which the candidate information originates. Upstream Governed Value Reference The relevant VFM® or other governed value reference where available. Candidate Form Monetary, non-monetary, digital, resource-based, service-based, asset-based, or another governed form. Event Relevance Basis The basis supporting possible association with the event. Material Relevance State Whether the relationship is sufficiently material for further governance. Direct / Indirect State The apparent relationship path between candidate and event. Participant Link Reference Relevant TREPS participant reference where applicable. Duplicate State Whether the candidate may duplicate another value record. Candidate Confidence The qualified confidence attached to candidate identification. Ambiguity State Whether the candidate relationship remains ambiguous. Conflict State Whether materially conflicting value information exists. Inclusion / Exclusion State Whether the candidate proceeds through TRVAS governance. Traceability Reference The information required to reconstruct candidate identification. Governance State The current VAIM state. Handoff State Whether the candidate is ready for VARM. Governance Outputs VAIM may produce: Value Association Candidate; Monetary Value Candidate; Non-Monetary Value Candidate; Digital-Asset Value Candidate; Resource Value Candidate; Governed Value Result Candidate; Direct Value Candidate; Indirect Value Candidate; Multi-Value Candidate Structure; Potential Duplicate Value Candidate; Candidate Exclusion Record; Candidate Confidence State; Candidate Ambiguity State; Candidate Conflict State; Candidate Traceability Record; and the principal output: Governed Value Association Candidate Set This output proceeds to VARM. Critical Distinctions Value Presence ≠ Event Value Association Value Association Candidate ≠ Established Value Association Candidate Value ≠ Governed Event Value Economic Relevance ≠ Event Relevance by Default Value Association Materiality ≠ Legal Materiality Monetary Record ≠ Event Value Association by Default No Monetary Amount ≠ No Value Association Candidate Recorded Amount ≠ Value Association Candidate by Default Invoice Presence ≠ Complete Event Value Invoice Amount ≠ Taxable Value Payment ≠ Event Value by Default On-Chain Transfer ≠ Tax-Relevant Event Value by Default Resource Consumption ≠ Taxable Value by Default No Transfer ≠ No Value Candidate Direct Value Connection ≠ Established Value Association Indirect Value Connection ≠ Irrelevant Value by Default Participant-Linked Value ≠ Participant-Owned Value Participant-Linked Value ≠ Event Value by Default One Event ≠ One Value Candidate One Value Candidate ≠ One Event by Default Multiple Value Records ≠ Multiple Values by Default Same Amount ≠ Same Value Trusted Source ≠ Event Relevance by Default Required Value Field ≠ Permission to Invent Event Value Candidate Exclusion ≠ Value Nonexistence Value Candidate Discovery ≠ Event Boundary Expansion Value Candidate ≠ Participant Determination Value Candidate ≠ Ownership Determination Value Association Candidate ≠ Taxable Value No Invoice ≠ No Value Candidate No Human Transaction ≠ No Value Candidate Enterprise Application VAIM provides the first operational gateway into TRVAS: ERP / Banking / Commerce / Blockchain / Platform / AI Agent / Machine System → Available Value Information TREPS — Governed Participatory Event → VAIM — Value Association Identification → Governed Value Association Candidate Set → VARM — Value Reference Governance → VACM — Value Change Association → VASM — Value State Association → VATM — Value Association Traceability → Governed Value-Associated Event This allows organizations to separate potentially relevant value from surrounding operational data before downstream tax interpretation begins. Use Case 1 — Multi-System Commercial Event A multinational business processes a customer transaction through an ERP system, payment provider, marketplace, invoicing platform, and logistics system. The available records include a product price, platform commission, payment-processing fee, shipping charge, discount, currency-conversion amount, tax field, settlement amount, and later refund. Several systems contain overlapping records of the same underlying value relationships. VAIM identifies which value information plausibly belongs to the governed event, distinguishes materially different candidates, detects possible duplication, and excludes unrelated surrounding records. It does not decide which amount is taxable. The resulting Governed Value Association Candidate Set can proceed through TRVAS for structured Value Association governance. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Machine Economy An autonomous industrial system allocates excess computational and production capacity through a machine-accessible marketplace. An AI agent initiates the allocation, another autonomous system consumes the resource, energy is used, productive capacity is transferred, and settlement later occurs through a digital asset. There may be no conventional invoice when the operational event occurs. VAIM identifies computational capacity, energy consumption, service output, digital-asset movement, and other governed value results that plausibly belong to the event. It does not assume that the digital-asset transfer represents the entire event value and does not determine the tax treatment of any candidate. The resulting candidate structure allows subsequent TREGA™ governance to represent the economic event before jurisdiction-specific tax rules are applied. Canonical Boundary VAIM owns the discovery, differentiation, screening, qualification, inclusion, exclusion, duplicate detection, uncertainty, conflict, and readiness governance of value information that may materially belong to a Governed Participatory Event. VAIM does not establish the complete Value Association, create the definitive Value Reference, govern Value Change, govern Value State, own Value Association Traceability as a complete downstream mechanism, govern the Value Lifecycle, determine ownership or entitlement, redefine Event Participation or Event Boundary, determine accountability or liability, or establish taxable value, Tax Base, Tax Liability, or any jurisdiction-specific tax consequence. Its governance ends when the relevant value information has been sufficiently identified and qualified to enter Value Reference governance. Canonical Handoff Governed Participatory Event + Available Governed Value Information → VAIM — Governed Value Association Candidate Set → VARM — Value Reference Governance Canonical Closing Statement VAIM establishes which value information deserves to enter Event Value Association governance without treating the presence of money, assets, resources, or value records as proof that they belong to the event. Finding value and associating value are separate governance operations. Value Presence ≠ Event Value Association. Value Association Candidate ≠ Taxable Value.

title: OOF™ The Value Reference Module (VARM) governs how Value Association
text: OOF™ The Value Reference Module (VARM) governs how Value Association The Value Reference Module (VARM) governs how Value Association OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™ Independent Methodological Authority Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™ Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ Parent Standard: TRVAS — Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard Module: VARM — Value Reference Module Operational Layer: Value Reference Governance Layer Category: Governance & Enforcement Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance Type: Core Module Governed Space: Value Reference Origin ID: TREGA-TRVAS-VARM-002 Version: 1.0 Status: Canonical · Open Standard Effective Date: 1 September 2026 AI-Readable: Yes Authority: OOF® Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language Canonical Definition The Value Reference Module (VARM) governs how Value Association Candidates identified by VAIM are connected to stable, distinguishable, reconstructable, and interoperable value references within a Tax-Relevant Event. VARM establishes the reference structure through which TREGA™ can consistently identify which governed value object, value result, or value representation is being associated with the event without redefining the value itself. Its principal task is: Governed Value Association Candidate ↓ Governed Value Reference VARM does not determine what happened to value. It does not determine whether value increased, decreased, transferred, developed, degraded, was nullified, restored, or extinguished. It does not determine the legal or tax meaning of the referenced value. Its foundational distinction is: Value Reference ≠ Value DeterminationOperational Role Once VAIM identifies potentially relevant value information, TREGA™ requires a stable method for referring to that value throughout subsequent governance. Without a governed reference layer, the same value may appear under: different transaction identifiers; different invoice lines; different account entries; different currencies; different blockchain transaction references; different asset identifiers; different ERP records; different system-specific IDs; different machine-generated references; or different representations across organizations. Conversely, similar references may represent different values. VARM creates the governed reference structure needed to keep these representations distinguishable and traceable. Internal Module Flow TRVAS operates through: VAIM — Value Association Identification → VARM — Value Reference → VACM — Value Change Association → VASM — Value State Association → VATM — Value Association Traceability → Governed Value-Associated Event VARM receives the Governed Value Association Candidate Set from VAIM. Its output provides the stable reference structure required by the downstream TRVAS modules. Operational Transition The canonical VARM transition is: Governed Value Association Candidate Set → Value Reference Governance → Governed Value Reference Set A Governed Value Reference establishes which value object, result, or representation subsequent TRVAS governance is referring to. It does not establish the legal meaning or tax treatment of that value. Operational Space VARM governs: Value Reference establishment; reference differentiation; reference normalization; source-reference preservation; multi-source reference linkage; reference equivalence qualification; reference non-equivalence; reference hierarchy; reference granularity; reference stability; reference substitution; reference versioning; reference ambiguity; reference conflict; reference interoperability; and reference readiness for downstream TRVAS governance. Operational Scope VARM may govern value references originating from: VFM®; ERP systems; accounting systems; banking systems; payment infrastructure; invoices; procurement systems; marketplaces; digital platforms; blockchain networks; digital-asset systems; smart contracts; industrial systems; energy systems; logistics; AI agents; autonomous systems; machine networks; and other legitimate operational or governed sources. VARM remains neutral to the technology or data model producing the reference. Governed Value Reference A Governed Value Reference is a stable governance-level reference through which a specific value object, value result, or value representation can be distinguished within TRVAS. It permits subsequent governance to answer: Which value are we referring to? without answering: What is the final legal or tax meaning of that value? Therefore: Governed Value Reference ≠ Tax ValuationSource Value Reference Operational systems may already provide value identifiers. Examples include: transaction ID; invoice-line ID; asset ID; ledger-entry ID; payment ID; wallet transaction reference; token identifier; accounting reference; product reference; resource-allocation reference; or machine-generated value identifier. VARM may preserve these as Source Value References. However: Source Value Reference ≠ Governed Value Reference by Default A source identifier becomes part of the governed reference structure only through appropriate qualification. Canonical Reference Where several operational references describe the same governed value, VARM may establish a common governance-level reference through which those representations remain linked. The purpose is not to erase the source identifiers. The canonical reference provides a stable governance anchor while preserving the underlying source references. Therefore: Canonical Reference ≠ Source Reference Replacement. Reference Differentiation VARM shall distinguish separate value references where available information supports their independence. Similar numeric values or descriptions do not establish equivalence. Therefore: Same Amount ≠ Same Value Reference Same Currency ≠ Same Value Reference Same Participant ≠ Same Value Reference Same Timestamp ≠ Same Value Reference Similar Description ≠ Same Value Reference Reference equivalence must be governed rather than assumed. Reference Equivalence Multiple records may legitimately represent the same underlying value. VARM may establish governed reference equivalence where sufficient support exists. For example: ERP Record A Invoice Line B Bank Settlement C may refer to the same underlying value relationship. However: Multiple References ≠ Multiple Values by Default Equivalence must remain qualified where uncertainty exists. Reference Non-Equivalence Records that appear similar may represent distinct values. Two payments of the same amount may relate to separate events. Two identical digital assets may represent separate governed value objects. Two invoice lines may contain identical descriptions but refer to different economic components. Therefore: Reference Similarity ≠ Value Equivalence VARM shall preserve distinction where equivalence cannot legitimately be established. Reference Granularity Value may be represented at different levels. For example: Invoice → Invoice Component → Invoice Line → Line Component or: Digital Asset Portfolio → Asset Class → Asset → Asset Unit VARM shall preserve the level of reference necessary for the governed Value Association. Therefore: Aggregate Reference ≠ Component Reference A reference shall not be treated as more granular than the underlying information supports. Composite Value Reference One event may involve a value structure composed of several distinct components. VARM may establish a composite reference structure where the components legitimately belong together while remaining individually distinguishable. The canonical structure may be: Composite Value Reference → Component A → Component B → Component C However: Composite Reference ≠ Single Indivisible Value by Default. Reference Hierarchy Where value references exist at multiple levels, VARM may preserve their relationship. For example: Settlement Reference → Transaction References → Value Components or: Asset Bundle → Individual Asset References The hierarchy represents reference structure. It does not determine Value Ownership, Tax Base, or legal classification. Multi-Source Reference Linkage The same value may be represented across several systems. VARM shall permit governed linkage among those representations. Example: Commerce Platform Reference ↔ ERP Reference ↔ Payment Reference ↔ Bank Reference ↔ Governed Value Reference This can create interoperability without requiring every system to use the same internal identifier. Reference Normalization Different systems may use incompatible reference formats. VARM may normalize those representations for governance purposes while preserving their original forms. Normalization shall not alter the substantive meaning of the underlying value. Therefore: Reference Normalization ≠ Value TransformationReference Stability A Governed Value Reference should remain sufficiently stable throughout TRVAS governance. Changes in surrounding system identifiers shall not automatically create a new governed value reference. Therefore: Source Identifier Change ≠ New Governed Value by Default. The continuity of the reference must be assessed independently. Reference Substitution An operational source may replace one identifier with another. VARM shall preserve the relationship between prior and subsequent references where they represent the same underlying value. Therefore: Reference Substitution ≠ Value Replacement by Default. Historical reference paths should remain reconstructable. Reference Versioning Some value representations evolve. An estimate may later be updated. A provisional settlement reference may become final. A digital record may receive a subsequent version. VARM may preserve version relationships without treating every version as a separate value. Therefore: New Reference Version ≠ New Value by Default. Whether the underlying value itself changed belongs to the appropriate value-governance mechanism. Reference Correction A source reference may be corrected because of error. VARM shall support correction without silently erasing the prior reference history. Reference Correction ≠ Historical Erasure The corrected structure should remain reconstructable where governance requires it. Reference Ambiguity It may be unclear which value a source identifier represents. VARM shall preserve ambiguity rather than arbitrarily linking the reference. Therefore: Reference Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Assume Equivalence Where ambiguity cannot be sufficiently resolved, the governance state shall remain qualified or unresolved. Reference Conflict Different sources may assert incompatible reference relationships. For example: one system may associate a settlement with Invoice A while another associates it with Invoice B. VARM shall preserve material conflict until sufficiently resolved. Therefore: Reference Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient LinkageMissing Reference Economically relevant value may exist even where no usable operational identifier is available. VARM shall not assume that missing source identification means absence of value. Therefore: Missing Source Reference ≠ No Value Where permitted by governance, a governance-level reference may be established from sufficiently supported information while preserving the missing-source condition. Technical Identifier A technical identifier may assist reference governance. However, technical uniqueness does not establish economic uniqueness. Therefore: Unique Technical ID ≠ Unique Economic Value by Default This distinction is particularly important in blockchain, tokenized, machine-generated, and distributed systems. Blockchain References Blockchain systems may provide: transaction hashes; wallet addresses; token IDs; contract addresses; block references; output references; or protocol-specific identifiers. VARM may consume these references. However: Transaction Hash ≠ Economic Value Reference by Default. One transaction may contain several value relationships. One economic value relationship may also span multiple transactions. VARM therefore preserves the distinction between technical ledger references and governed value references. Token Reference A token identifier may identify a digital representation. It does not automatically establish the complete economic value being governed. Therefore: Token ID ≠ Governed Economic Value by Default. Likewise: Wallet Address ≠ Value Owner. Ownership remains outside VARM. Banking and Payment References Banks and payment systems may provide highly reliable transaction identifiers. VARM may use them as source references. However: Payment Identifier ≠ Complete Event Value Reference by Default. A payment may settle: one event; several events; part of an event; an earlier obligation; or a composite value structure. The reference relationship must therefore remain governed. Invoice References An invoice number may represent an aggregate commercial document rather than one value. VARM shall permit references below the invoice level where necessary. Therefore: Invoice Reference ≠ Single Value Reference by Default. Invoice lines and components may require separate governed references. Machine-Generated References Autonomous systems may create value-related references without human involvement. Examples include: resource-allocation IDs; machine-service IDs; compute-consumption references; autonomous procurement references; energy-exchange identifiers; agent transaction IDs; or machine settlement references. VARM shall support these references without requiring a human-created invoice or account entry. Therefore: Machine-Generated Reference ≠ Invalid Value Reference The reference must still satisfy normal governance requirements. Reference and Value State VARM establishes which value is being referenced. It does not determine the state of that value. Therefore: Value Reference ≠ Value State VASM owns Event–Value State Association within TRVAS. VFM® owns the underlying Value State governance. Reference and Value Change A stable Value Reference may persist while value changes. Therefore: Value Reference ≠ Value Change VACM governs the association between governed Value Changes and the event. VFM® owns the underlying Value Change governance. Reference and Event Participation A Value Reference may contain or be linked to participant information. VARM shall not infer participation solely from the reference. Therefore: Value Reference ≠ Participant Determination. TREPS remains authoritative for Event Participation. Reference and Ownership A Value Reference may be associated with an actor, account, wallet, organization, or machine. This does not establish legal ownership. Therefore: Value Reference ≠ Ownership OBIDENITY® remains authoritative for governed ownership where applicable. Reference and Event Boundary A Value Reference may reveal information outside the current Event Boundary. VARM shall not independently expand the event. Therefore: Reference Linkage ≠ Event Boundary Expansion. Potential Event Boundary issues shall be referred to TREBS. Reference and Event Relationship The same Value Reference may appear across several governed events. This does not establish that the events are identical. Therefore: Shared Value Reference ≠ Same Event TRERLS remains authoritative for Event Relationships. Reference and Taxation A governed reference identifies the value under subsequent governance. It does not determine its tax treatment. Therefore: Governed Value Reference ≠ Taxable Value Governed Value Reference ≠ Tax Base Governed Value Reference ≠ Tax Liability A jurisdiction may later interpret the referenced value according to applicable law. Multi-Jurisdiction Reference Stability A principal benefit of a jurisdiction-neutral Value Reference is that multiple taxation systems can evaluate the same governed value without TREGA™ redefining it for each jurisdiction. The model is: One Governed Value Reference → Jurisdiction A Evaluation → Jurisdiction B Evaluation → Jurisdiction C Evaluation The legal conclusions may differ. The governed reference remains stable. Reference Interoperability VARM should enable different operational systems to refer consistently to the same governed value structure without requiring identical internal data models. This supports: ERP integration; banking interoperability; payment reconciliation; blockchain integration; tax-engine integration; marketplace interoperability; AI-agent systems; machine economies; auditability; and cross-border data exchange. Interoperability concerns the reference. It does not require uniform legal interpretation. Reference Traceability VARM shall preserve sufficient information to reconstruct: where a reference originated; which source identifiers exist; how references were linked; which equivalence decisions were made; which hierarchy exists; whether normalization occurred; whether substitution occurred; whether versioning occurred; whether corrections occurred; whether ambiguity existed; and whether conflicts remain. VATM later governs the complete Value Association traceability structure. VARM owns traceability necessary specifically for the integrity of the Value Reference. Governance States VARM may represent states including: Reference Ready Reference Under Governance Reference Distinguished Reference Linked Reference Normalized Reference Equivalent Reference Non-Equivalent Reference Composite Reference Substituted Reference Versioned Reference Ambiguous Reference Conflicted Reference Unresolved Governed Value Reference Established These states describe reference governance only. Governance Requirements VARM implementations shall ensure that: every admitted Value Association Candidate can be referenceable; source references remain preserved; governance-level references can be distinguished from source identifiers; multiple source references can be linked where legitimate; reference equivalence is not assumed from superficial similarity; reference non-equivalence can remain visible; aggregate and component references can be distinguished; composite value structures can be represented; reference hierarchies can be preserved; normalization does not alter underlying value meaning; reference stability can survive source-identifier changes; substitutions remain traceable; version relationships remain reconstructable; corrections do not erase governance history; ambiguity remains visible; conflicts remain visible; missing source references do not automatically eliminate legitimate value; technical uniqueness is not treated as economic uniqueness; blockchain identifiers are not automatically treated as complete economic references; machine-generated references can be governed; Value State remains separate; Value Change remains separate; Event Participation remains separate; ownership remains separate; Event Boundary remains protected; Event Relationships remain separate; and tax valuation remains downstream. Governance Logic IF VAIM establishes a Value Association Candidate, THEN VARM shall determine how the relevant value can be stably referenced. IF a valid upstream governed Value Reference already exists, THEN VARM should preserve and consume that reference rather than unnecessarily recreate it. IF multiple source identifiers represent the same underlying governed value, THEN they may be linked under a common Governed Value Reference where equivalence is sufficiently supported. IF similar references cannot be shown to represent the same value, THEN they shall remain distinct. IF one aggregate reference contains materially distinct value components, THEN appropriate reference granularity shall be preserved. IF a source identifier changes while the underlying value remains continuous, THEN a new governed value shall not be created solely because of the identifier change. IF reference equivalence remains ambiguous or conflicted, THEN that state shall remain visible. IF a reference reveals a possible Event Boundary problem, THEN VARM shall refer the issue upstream rather than expand the event independently. IF the Value Reference is sufficiently governed, THEN it shall proceed to VACM for Value Change Association governance. Minimum Implementation Framework A minimum VARM implementation should support: Governed Event Reference The governed event to which the Value Reference structure relates. VAIM Candidate Reference The originating Value Association Candidate. Governed Value Reference Identifier The stable governance-level reference. Source Value Reference The original operational or governed identifier. Source System The system or governance source providing the reference. Reference Type The applicable reference category. Reference Granularity The level at which the value is being referenced. Parent Reference A higher-level reference where a hierarchy exists. Component Reference A lower-level reference where components exist. Equivalent Reference Set Other references governed as representing the same underlying value. Reference Equivalence State The qualification of equivalence. Normalization State Whether reference normalization occurred. Substitution State Whether one reference replaced another. Prior Reference The historical reference where substitution or versioning occurs. Version State The applicable reference version relationship.
